The provisions of the State Securities Law, the Local Government Securities Law, the
University Securities Law, or of any other general, special or local statute relating
to the issuance of public securities or other debt obligations do not apply to a trust
created for the benefit and furtherance of any public function.

2.

All bonds issued by any trust created for the benefit and furtherance of any public
function must:

(a)

Be sold at public or private sale, as determined by the trustees and approved by the
City Council. If the bonds are offered at public sale, but no satisfactory bids are
received from responsible bidders at the public sale, the bonds may be sold at private
sale.

(b)

Be secured:

(1)

By property, real or personal or both, having a market value equal to at least twice
the principal amount of the bonds sold; or

(2)

By gross revenues from an existing revenue producing facility equal to at least one
and one-half times the average annual debt service payable on the bonds.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412; A—Ch. 596, Stats. 1995 p. 2216)

heading: Section 7A.100 - Competitive bidding not required.
text:
Except as otherwise provided in section 7A.090, no statute, general, special or local, requiring competitive bidding applies to
a trust created for the benefit and furtherance of a public function.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412)

heading: Section 7A.110 - Termination of trust.
text:
Any trust created for the benefit and furtherance of a public function may be terminated
by agreement of the trustee, or if there is more than one, then all of the trustees,
and the governing body of the beneficiary, with the approval of the Governor of the
State of Nevada; but such trust shall not be terminated while there exists outstanding
any contractual obligations chargeable against the trust property, which, by reason
of such termination, might become an obligation of the beneficiary of such trust.

(Added—Ch. 694, Stats. 1975 p. 1412)

heading: Section 8.010 - Municipal taxes.
text:
1.

The City Council shall annually, at the time prescribed by law for levying taxes for
State and County purposes, levy a tax at a rate allowable under applicable provisions
of the Nevada Revised Statutes upon the assessed value of all real and personal property
within the City except as provided in the Local Government Securities Law and the
Consolidated Local Improvements Law, as amended from time to time. The taxes so levied
shall be collected at the same time and in the same manner and by the same officers,
exercising the same functions, as prescribed in the laws of the State of Nevada for
collection of state and county taxes. The revenue laws of the State shall, in every
respect not inconsistent with the provisions of this Charter, be applicable to the
levying, assessing and collecting of the municipal taxes.

2.

In the matter of equalization of assessments, the rights of the City and the inhabitants
thereof shall be protected in the same manner and to the same extent by the action
of the County Board of Equalization as are the State and County.

3.

All forms and blanks used in levying, assessing and collecting the revenues of the
State and counties shall, with such alterations or additions as may be necessary,
be used in levying, assessing and collecting the revenues of the City. The City Council
shall enact all such ordinances as it may deem necessary and not inconsistent with
this Charter and the laws of the State for the prompt, convenient and economical collecting
of the revenue.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 420; A—Ch. 266, Stats. 2013 p. 1217)

heading: Section 8.020 - Revenue ordinances.
text:
The City Council may pass and enact all ordinances necessary to carry into effect
the revenue laws in the City and to enlarge, fix and determine the powers and duties
of all officers in relation thereto.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 420)

heading: Section 9.010 - System of Civil Service.
text:
1.

There is hereby created a System of Civil Service, applicable to and governing the
employment of all employees of the City except Executive Officers, department directors,
senior department directors, division heads, assistant city attorneys, any other attorney
employed by the Office of the City Attorney, assistants to the City Manager, the Municipal
Court Administrator, any elected officer, any employee that reports directly to an
elected officer, any probationary employee, any temporary employee, and any other
employee excluded from the System by ordinance.

2.

The System of Civil Service must be administered by a Civil Service Board composed
of five persons appointed by the City Council.

3.

The Board shall prepare regulations governing the System of Civil Service to be adopted
by the City Council. The regulations must provide for:

(a)

Examination of potential employees.

(b)

Procedures for recruitment and placement.

(c)

Classification of positions.

(d)

Procedures for promotion, disciplinary actions and removal of employees.

(e)

Such other matters as the Board may deem necessary.

4.

Copies of the regulations governing the System of Civil Service must be distributed
to all employees of the City.

5.

An employee of the City who is included in the System of Civil Service and accepts
a position that is excluded from the System pursuant to subsection 1 does not retain
any rights or privileges within the System.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 421; A—Ch. 334, Stats. 1977 p. 630; Ch. 596, Stats. 1995
p. 2218; Ch. 108, Stats. 2003 p. 604; Ch. 266, Stats. 2013 p. 1217)

heading: Section 10.010 - Severability of provisions.
text:
If any portion of this Charter is held to be unconstitutional or invalid for any reason
by the decision of any court of competent jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect
the validity of the remaining portion of this Charter. The Legislature hereby declares
that it would have passed the Charter and each portion thereof, irrespective of the
portion which may be deemed unconstitutional or otherwise invalid.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 422)

heading: Section 10.020 - Effect of enactment of charter.
text:
1.

All rights and property of every kind and description which were vested in the City
prior to the enactment of this Charter shall be vested in the same municipal corporation
on the effective date of this Charter. No right or liability, either in favor of or
against such corporation existing at the time of becoming incorporated under this
Charter, and no action or prosecution shall be affected by such change, but it shall
stand and progress as if no change had been made.

2.

Whenever a different remedy is given by this Charter, which may properly be made applicable
to any right existing at the time of such City so becoming incorporated under this
Charter, such remedy shall be cumulative to the remedy before provided, and used accordingly.

3.

All ordinances and resolutions in effect in the City prior to the effective date of
this Charter shall, unless in conflict with the provisions of this Charter, continue
in full force and effect until amended or repealed.

4.

The enactment of this Charter shall not effect any change in the legal identity of
the City.

5.

The enactment of this Charter shall not be construed to repeal or in any way affect
or modify:

(a)

Any special, local or temporary law.

(b)

Any law or ordinance making an appropriation.

(c)

Any ordinance affecting any bond issue or by which any bond issue may have been authorized.

(d)

The running of the statute of limitations in force at the time this Charter becomes
effective.

(e)

Any bond of any public officer.

(Ch. 266, Stats. 1971 p. 422)

heading: Title 1 - GENERAL PROVISIONS
text: Chapters:

heading: Chapter 1.02 - ESTABLISHMENT AND EFFECT OF CODE
1.02.010 - Title.
text:
This Code shall be known as the "Henderson Municipal Code."

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.02.020 - Provisions deemed as continuations of existing ordinances.
text:
The provisions of this Code, insofar as they are substantially the same as legislation
previously adopted by the city relating to the same subject matter, shall be construed
as restatements and continuations thereof and not as new enactments.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.02.030 - Code does not affect prior offenses or rights.
text:
(a)

Nothing in this Code or the ordinance adopting this Code affects any offense or act
committed or done, any penalty or forfeiture incurred, or any contract or right established
before the effective date of this Code.

(b)

The adoption of this Code does not authorize any use or the continuation of any use
of a structure or premises in violation of any city ordinance on the effective date
of this Code.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.02.040 - Repealed ordinances not revived.
text:
Nothing in this Code or the ordinance adopting this Code shall revive, reordain, or
reinstate any ordinance that has been repealed.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.02.050 - Certain ordinances not affected by Code.
text:
Nothing in this Code or the ordinance adopting this Code affects the validity of the
city ordinances or any portion of a city ordinance not codified in this Code. Such
ordinances or portions of an ordinance continue in full force and effect to the same
extent as if published at length in this Code.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.02.060 - Supplementation of Code.
text:
Supplements to this Code shall be prepared and printed in the time and manner authorized
or directed by the city council.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: Chapter 1.03 - DEFINITIONS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION
1.03.010 - General definitions and rules of construction.
text:
The following definitions and rules of construction shall apply to this Code and to
all ordinances unless the context requires otherwise.

Generally.

(1)

When provisions conflict, the specific shall prevail over the general. All provisions
shall be liberally construed so that the intent of the city council may be effectuated.
The provisions of this Code and all proceedings under it are to be liberally construed
to affect its purposes and to promote justice.

(2)

Words and phrases shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of
the language, but technical words, technical phrases and words and phrases that have
acquired peculiar and appropriate meanings in law shall be construed according to
such meanings.

(3)

Grammatical errors shall not vitiate, and a transposition of words and clauses may
be resorted to when the sentence or clause is without meaning as it stands.

(4)

Scrivener's errors shall be ignored.

Charter. The term "charter" means the charter of the City of Henderson, Nevada.

City. The term "city" means the City of Henderson, Clark County, Nevada.

City council. The terms "city council" and "council" mean the City Council of the City of Henderson,
Nevada.

Code, ordinance. The term "ordinance" means city ordinance. The term "Code" means the Henderson Municipal
Code, as designated in this section. References to the Code are to the Code, as amended.
References to ordinances are to ordinances as amended.

Computation of time. In computing any period of time prescribed or allowed the day of the act, event,
or default from which the designated period of time begins to run shall not be included.
The last day of the period so computed shall be included, unless it is a Friday, a
Saturday, a Sunday, or a legal holiday day, in which event the period runs until the
end of the next day which is not a Friday, Saturday, a Sunday, or legal holiday, or,
when the act to be done is the filing of a paper with the city, a day on which weather
or other conditions have made the city office in which the paper is to be filed inaccessible,
in which event the period runs until the end of the next day which is not one of the
aforementioned days. When the period of time prescribed or allowed is less than 11
days, intermediate Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays shall be excluded
in the computation.

Conjunctions. In a provision involving two or more items, conditions, provisions or events, which
items, conditions, provisions or events are connected by the conjunction "and," "or"
or "either….or," the conjunction shall be interpreted as follows unless the context
clearly required that the words "and" and "or" be interchangeable:

(1)

"And" indicates that all the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply.

(2)

"Or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events apply singly
or in any combination.

(3)

"Either...or" indicates that the connected terms, conditions, provisions or events
apply singly but not in combination.

County. The term "county" means Clark County, Nevada.

Delegation of authority. A provision that authorizes or requires a city officer or a city employee to perform
an act or make a decision authorizes such officer or employee to act or make a decision
through subordinates.

Gender. The masculine gender includes the feminine and neuter genders.

Health department. The term "health department" means the Southern Nevada Health District.

Includes. The term "includes" does not limit a term to a specified example.

Joint authority. Words giving a joint authority to three or more persons give such authority to a
majority of all such persons.

May. The term "may" confers a right, privilege or power.

May not. The term "may not" states a prohibition and has a prohibitory effect and abridges
or removes a right, privilege or power.

Must. The term "must" is to be construed as imposing a requirement.

NRS. The abbreviation "NRS" refers to the Nevada Revised Statutes, as now or hereafter
amended.

Number. Words in the singular include the plural. Words in the plural include the singular.

Oath. A solemn affirmation is the equivalent to an oath and a person shall be deemed to
have sworn if such person makes such an affirmation.

Officers, departments, etc. References to officers, departments, boards, commissions, committees or employees
are to city officers, city departments, city boards, city commissions, city committees
and city employees.

Owner. The term "owner," as applied to property, includes any part owner, joint owner, tenant
in common, tenant in partnership, joint tenant or tenant by the entirety of the whole
or part of such property.

Person. The term "person" means any natural person, any form of business or social organization
and any other nongovernmental legal entity including, but not limited to, a corporation,
partnership, association, trust or unincorporated organization. The term does not
includes a government, governmental agency or political subdivision of a government
to the maximum extent permitted by law.

Personal property. The term "personal property" means any property other than real property.

Premises. The term "premises," as applied to real property, includes land and structures.

Property. The term "property" includes real property, personal property and mixed property.

Public place. The term "public place" includes any street, sidewalk, park, cemetery, school yard,
body or water or watercourse, public conveyance, or any place for the sale of merchandise,
public accommodation or amusement.

Real property. The term "real property" or "real estate" means property consisting of land and all
appurtenances to the land, including buildings and other improvements, fixtures and
vegetation erected upon, affixed to, planted in or growing upon the land, and any
interest, estate, benefit, right or privilege in such property.

Sale. The term "sale" includes any sale, exchange, barter, or offer for sale.

Shall. The term "shall" imposes a duty to act.

Shall not. The term "shall not" imposes a prohibition against acting.

Sidewalk. The term "sidewalk" means that portion of the street between the curb line and the
adjacent property line intended for the use of pedestrians.

Signature of subscription by mark. The term "signature" or "subscription by mark" include a mark when the signer or
subscriber cannot write, such signer's or subscriber's name being written near the
mark by a witness who writes his own name near the signer's or subscriber's name;
but a signature or subscription by mark can be acknowledged or can serve as a signature
or subscription to a sworn statement only when two witnesses so sign their own names
thereto.

State. The term "State" means the State of Nevada.

Street. The term "street" shall mean the entire width between the boundary line of every
way publicly maintained when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for
vehicular traffic.

Tenant or occupant. The terms "tenant" and "occupant," as applied to premises, include any person holding
a written or oral lease, or who actually occupies the whole or any part of such premises,
alone or with others.

Tenses. The present tense includes the past and future tenses. The future tense includes
the present tense.

Week. The term "week" means a period of seven consecutive days.

Will. The term "will" imposes a duty to act.

Writing. The term "writing" includes any form of recorded message capable of comprehension
by ordinary visual means.

Year. The term "year" means a calendar year.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.03.020 - Title, chapter and section headings.
text:
Title, chapter and sections headings contained in this Code shall not be deemed to
govern, limit, modify or in any manner affect the scope, meaning or intent of the
provisions of any title, chapter or section.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.03.030 - History notes, state law references and other footnote material.
text:
(a)

The history of source notes appearing in parentheses after sections in this Code are
not intended to have any legal effect but are merely intended to indicate the source
of matter contained in the section. State law references that appear after sections
or subsections of this Code or which otherwise appear in footnote form are provided
for the convenience of the user of this Code and have no legal effect.

(b)

Editor's notes, charter references, cross references and state law references that
appear in this Code after sections or subsections or that otherwise appear in footnote
form are provided for the convenience of the user of the Code and have no legal effect.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.03.040 - References to Code.
text:
Unless otherwise specified:

(1)

All references in this Code to titles, chapters, sections or subsections are to titles,
chapters, sections or subsections of this Code.

(2)

All references in this Code to titles, chapters, sections or subsections of this Code
are to titles, chapters, sections or subsections of this Code, as amended.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.03.050 - Effect of repeal of ordinances.
text:
(a)

Unless specifically provided otherwise, the repeal of an ordinance does not revive
any previously repealed ordinance.

(b)

The repeal or amendment of an ordinance does not affect any punishment or penalty
incurred before the repeal took effect, nor does such repeal or amendment affect any
suit, prosecution or proceeding pending at the time of the amendment or repeal.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.03.060 - Severability.
text:
If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase, provision or portion of this
Code, or the application thereof to any person or circumstances, is for any reason
held to be invalid or unconstitutional by the decision of any court of competent jurisdiction,
such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions or provisions
of this Code or their applicability to distinguishable situations or circumstances.
In enacting this Code, it is the desire of the city council to validly regulate to
the full measure of its legal authority in the public interest, and to that end, the
city council declares that it would have adopted this Code and each section, subsection,
sentence, clause, phrase, provision, or portion thereof, irrespective of the fact
that any one or more sections, subsections, sentences, clauses, phrases or portions
thereof might be declared invalid or unconstitutional in whole or in part, as applied
to any particular situation or circumstances, and to this end the provisions of this
Code are intended to be severable.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.04.010 - Authorized—Service.
text:
Except when otherwise expressly directed by law or ordinance, upon any violation of
any ordinance of the City of Henderson, the city manager, the police chief, the fire
chief and authorized assistants, the managing inspector and authorized assistants,
and all other authorized officers, inspectors and employees charged with the enforcement
of city ordinances may prepare, sign and serve on the accused person a written citation
to appear in the municipal court to answer such charge or complaint. For criminal
matters, a citation may be served in lieu of arresting the person committing the violation.
All such citations shall be personally served on the person accused or his representative.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014; Code 1976, § 1.04.010; Ord. 236 § 1, 1958)

heading: 1.04.020 - Form.
text:
The citation provided for in the preceding section shall be substantially, in form
and content, as set forth in NRS 171.1774. When the issuance of a citation is appropriate,
a single citation that includes all charges arising out of the same incident shall
be issued unless, due to the high number of offenses charged, it is not possible to
include all such charges on a single citation, in which case more than one citation
may be issued.

(Ord. No. 3326, § 1, 1-19-2016; Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014; Code 1976, § 1.04.020; Ord. 236 § 2, August 18, 1958)

heading: 1.04.030 - Time for appearance.
text:
The time specified in such citation for the accused to appear must be not less than
five days after service, unless an earlier hearing is demanded by the accused. If
more than one offense is charged in connection with the same incident, all such charged
offenses shall be heard at the same time and as part of the same case.

(Ord. No. 3326, § 1, 1-19-2016; Code 1976, § 1.04.030; Ord. 236 § 3, August 18, 1958)

heading: 1.04.040 - Failure to appear.
text:
In the event any person willfully fails to appear in court as required by such citation,
the court shall issue a bench warrant and may deem the person in contempt of court,
which is punishable by a fine not exceeding $500.00 or term of imprisonment not exceeding
25 days, or both.

(Ord. No. 3549, § 1, 12-8-2018; Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014; Code 1976 § 1.04.040; Ord. 236 § 4, August 18, 1958)

heading: Chapter 1.05 - PENALTIES AND REMEDIES FOR CODE VIOLATIONS
1.05.010 - Definition.
text:
(a)

In this chapter "violation of this Code" means any of the following:

(1)

Doing an act that is prohibited or made or declared unlawful, an offense, a violation
or a misdemeanor by ordinance or by rule or regulation authorized by ordinance.

(2)

Failure to perform an act that is required to be performed by ordinance or by rule
or regulation authorized by ordinance.

(3)

Failure to perform an act if the failure is prohibited or is made or declared unlawful,
an offense, a violation, or a misdemeanor by ordinance or by rule or regulation authorized
by ordinance.

(b)

In this chapter "violation of this Code" does not include the failure of a city officer
or city employee to perform an official duty unless it is specifically provided that
the failure to perform the duty is to be punished as provided in this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.05.020 - Authorized punishment; penalties.
text:
(a)

Except as otherwise provided by law or ordinance, a person convicted of a violation
of this Code shall be guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in the Henderson
Detention Center for not more than six months, and/or by a fine of not more than $1,000.00.

(b)

In lieu of all or part of the punishment which may be imposed pursuant to subsection
(a), the convicted person may be sentenced to perform a fixed period of community
service pursuant to the conditions prescribed in NRS 176.087.

(c)

In all cases where a corporation is convicted of a violation of this Code, the corporation
is punishable by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 unless otherwise provided by law or
ordinance.

(d)

A person violating any administrative provision of any chapter of this Code may be
assessed a civil penalty not exceeding $500.00, or as otherwise provided in such chapter.

(e)

The commission of any act within the corporate limits of the city or the failure to
perform any act within such corporate limits which is made a civil infraction by the
laws of the state of Nevada is declared to be and shall constitute a civil infraction
under this Code. Furthermore, all procedures and administrative protocol provided
by specific statute as it relates to civil infractions is hereby enacted and in effect.

(f)

A person who is found to have committed a civil infraction shall be punished by a
civil penalty of not more than $500.00 per violation unless a greater or lesser civil
penalty is authorized by specific statute.

(Ord. No. 4152, § 1, 3-17-2026; Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.05.030 - Separate offenses.
text:
Except as otherwise provided by law or ordinance:

(1)

With respect to violations of this Code that are continuous with respect to time,
each day that the violation continues is a separate offense.

(2)

With respect to violations of this Code that are not continuous with respect to time,
each act is a separate offense.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.05.040 - Injunctive relief.
text:
Violations of this Code that are continuous with respect to time are a public nuisance
and may be abated by injunctive or other equitable relief. The imposition of a civil
penalty does not prevent equitable relief.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 1.05.050 - Other remedies.
text:
The imposition of a civil penalty or equitable relief does not prevent suspension
or revocation of a license, permit or franchise or other administrative remedies.

(Ord. No. 3173, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: Chapter 2.01 - COUNCIL SALARIES
text: Sections:

heading: 2.01.010 - Salary for councilmembers from Wards I, II, III and IV.
text:
Commencing on July 1, 1999, the councilmembers representing Wards I, II and IV shall
receive as compensation for their services an annual salary of $34,250.00.

Commencing on July 1, 2001, the councilmember representing Ward III shall receive
as his/her compensation for his/her services an annual salary of $34,250.00 plus the
proportion that the index figure of the National Consumer Price Index for all Urban
Consumers for All Items, U.S. City Average (1967 = 100) that is published by the Bureau
of Labor Statistics, United States Department of Labor, (hereafter "CPI Index") for
March 2001 has increased above the CPI Index for March of 2000.

(Ord. 2054, § 1, 2001; Ord. 1831, § 1 (part), 1998)

heading: 2.01.020 - Salary for mayor.
text:
Commencing on July 1, 2001, the mayor of the City of Henderson shall receive as compensation
for his/her services an annual salary of $42,250.00.

(Ord. 1831, § 1 (part), 1998)

heading: 2.01.030 - Salary for councilmen and mayor—Automatic increase.
text:
The salaries of the mayor and members of the city council that are provided for in
sections 2.01.010 and 2.01.020 of this chapter shall automatically be increased:

A.

On July 1, 2000, in the same proportion that the CPI for March of 2000 has increased
above such index figure for March of 1999; and

B.

On July 1 in each year thereafter, in the same proportion that such index figure for
March of that year has increased above such index figure for March of the previous
year.

(Ord. 2054, § 2, 2001; Ord. 1831, § 1 (part), 1998)

heading: 2.01.040 - Vehicle allowance.
text:
Inasmuch as the mayor and members of the city council are required to use their personal
vehicles for the conduct of city business and travel within the State of Nevada, a
monthly reimbursement in the amount of $900.00 for mayor and $600.00 for each member
of the city council shall be paid as follows: Effective on July 1, 1999, for Wards
I, II and IV; effective on July 1, 2001, for the mayor and Ward III. This amount is
to be considered total reimbursement for vehicle fuel, maintenance, repair, wear and
tear, and liability insurance for vehicles used.

(Ord. 1831, § 1 (part), 1998)

heading: 2.01.050 - Benefits.
text:
In addition to the salaries set forth in sections 2.01.010 and 2.01.020, the mayor and each member of the city council shall receive all benefits for which
he/she is eligible under the elected officials benefit package.

(Ord. 1831, § 1 (part), 1998)

heading: 2.04.010 - Date and time of meetings.

heading: 2.04.020 - Place of meetings.
text:
The city council herewith designates as its council chambers, for the conduct of all

heading: 2.04.030 - Special meetings.

Special meetings of the city council may be called by the mayor or a majority of the

text:

heading: 2.04.050 - Reserved.
text:

heading: 2.04.060 - Executive sessions and closed meetings.

The written minutes approved by the city council shall act as the permanent record

heading: 2.04.080 - City council rules of procedure.
text:

that shall apply to city council meetings. The city council rules of procedure and
any amendments thereto shall be adopted by city council resolution. A current copy
of the city council rules of procedure shall be held by the city clerk's office.

(Ord. No. 3174, § 1, 6-17-2014; Ord. No. 3368, § 1, 11-1-2016)

heading: 2.04.090 - Recordings or transcripts of meetings held by order of city attorney.

Upon order of the city attorney, any audio or video recordings or transcripts of city

text:
Any audio or video recordings or transcripts of city council meetings held as records
of the city may be destroyed in accordance with the City of Henderson Records Retention
Schedule, provided that all retention requirements of NRS chapter 241 have been met.

presently being held" to "Recordings or transcripts of meetings." The historical notation
has been preserved for reference purposes.

Effective the first pay period of fiscal year 2016 by an additional three percent;
and

On July 1 in each year thereafter, in the same proportion that such index figure for

heading: 2.05.030 - Benefits.
text:
In addition to the salary set forth in section 2.05.010, the elected municipal court judges shall receive all benefits for which he/she is

heading: 2.05.031 - Professional allowance for municipal court judge.
text:

heading: Chapter 2.06 - MUNICIPAL COURT
text: Sections:

heading: 2.06.010 - Court of record.
text:
Effective January 2, 1996, the Henderson Municipal Court shall be a court of record.

(Ord. 1609, § 1, 1995)

heading: 2.06.020 - Administrative fee exceptions.
text:
A.

When a defendant pleads guilty, guilty but mentally ill or is found guilty of a misdemeanor,
including the violation of any municipal ordinance, the municipal judge shall include
in the sentence the sum of $10.00 as an administrative assessment for the provision
of court facilities and render a judgment against the defendant for the assessment.

B.

This section does not apply to an ordinance regulating metered parking or an ordinance
which is specifically designated as imposing a civil penalty or liability pursuant
to NRS 268.019.

C.

The money collected for an administrative assessment for the provision of court facilities
must not be deducted from the fine imposed by the municipal judge but such must be
taxed against the defendant in addition to the fine. The money collected for such
an administrative assessment must be stated separately on the court's docket and must
be included in the amount posted for bail. If the defendant is found not guilty or
the charges are dismissed, the money deposited with the court must be returned to
the defendant. If the judge cancels a fine because the fine has been determined to
be uncollectible, any balance of the fine and the administrative assessment remaining
unpaid shall be deemed to be uncollectible and the defendant is not required to pay
it. If a fine is determined to be uncollectible, the defendant is not entitled to
a refund of the fine or administrative assessment he has paid and the municipal judge
shall not recalculate the administrative assessment.

D.

If the municipal judge permits the fine and administrative assessment for the provision
of court facilities to be paid in installments, the payments must be applied in the
following order:

1.

To pay the unpaid balance of an administrative assessment imposed pursuant to NRS
176.059;

2.

To pay the unpaid balance of an administrative assessment for the provision of court
facilities pursuant to this section; and

3.

To pay the fine.

E.

The money collected for administrative assessments for the provision of court facilities
in municipal courts must be paid by the clerk of the court to the director of finance
on or before the fifth day of each month for the preceding month. The director of
finance shall deposit the money received in a special revenue fund. The city may use
the money in the special revenue fund only to:

1.

Acquire land on which to construct additional facilities for the municipal court;

2.

Construct or acquire additional facilities for the municipal court;

3.

Renovate or remodel existing facilities for the municipal court;

4.

Acquire furniture, fixtures and equipment necessitated by the construction or acquisition
of additional facilities or the renovation of an existing facility for the municipal
court. This paragraph does not authorize the expenditure of money from the fund for
furniture, fixtures or equipment for judicial chambers;

5.

Acquire advanced technology for use in the additional or renovated facilities;

6.

Pay debt service on any bonds issued pursuant to subsection 3 of NRS 350.020 for the
acquisition of land or facilities or the construction or renovation of facilities
for the municipal court.

Any money remaining in the special revenue fund after five fiscal years must be deposited
in the municipal general fund for the continued maintenance of court facilities if
it has not been committed for expenditure pursuant to a plan for the construction
or acquisition of court facilities or improvements to court facilities. The finance
director shall provide, upon request by a municipal court, monthly reports of the
revenue credited to and expenditures made from the special revenue fund.

(Ord. 1723, § 1, 1997)

heading: Chapter 2.08 - ELECTIONS
text: Sections:

heading: 2.08.010 - Elective officers.
text:
The following officers shall be elected: mayor, four councilmen, and three municipal
judges.

(Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

heading: 2.08.020 - Terms of office of mayor, councilmen and municipal judges elected by voters.
text:
For term of office of councilmen and the mayor see City Charter section 2.010 subsection 4 and section 5.020 subsection 1.

For term of office of municipal judge see City Charter section 5.020 subsection 1.

(Ord. No. 3060, § 1, 9-17-2013; Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

heading: 2.08.030 - Vacancies in elective offices.
text:
Upon the occurrence of a vacancy in the offices of mayor, councilmen or municipal
judge, the city council may, by majority vote, appoint a qualified person to fill
the vacancy within 60 days after the occurrence of the vacancy. In lieu of appointment,
the city council may, by resolution, order a special election to be held no later
than 90 days after the occurrence of the vacancy.

(Ord. No. 3060, § 1, 9-17-2013; Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3060, § 1, adopted September 17, 2013, changed the title of section 2.08.030 from "Special
elections" to "Vacancies in elective offices." The historical notation has been preserved
for reference purposes.

heading: 2.08.040 - Date of entry upon duties.
text:
A councilman, mayor, or municipal judge elected into office during the primary or
general municipal election shall take office at the second regular meeting of the
city council held in June of the year of the general municipal election. See City
Charter section 5.100.

(Ord. No. 3060, § 1, 9-17-2013; Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

heading: 2.08.050 - Qualifications for elective offices—Filing and fees.
text:
All candidates for the office of mayor or municipal judge must be qualified electors
within the City of Henderson and must have been bona fide residents thereof for a
period of at least 12 months immediately preceding the last day for filing a declaration
of candidacy for the office.

All candidates for councilmen must be qualified electors within the respective ward
for which they seek the office of councilman, must have been a resident of that ward
for at least 30 days immediately preceding the last day for filing a declaration of
candidacy for the office (except that changes in ward boundaries pursuant to City
Charter section 1.040 do not affect the rights of any elected councilmen to continue in office for the
term for which they were elected), and must have been a bona fide resident of the
City of Henderson for a period of at least 12 months immediately preceding the last
day for filing a declaration of candidacy for the office.

At the time for filing as a candidate for office, all candidates for the office of
mayor, councilman or municipal judge shall pay to the city clerk a filing fee of $100.00.

(Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

heading: 2.08.060 - Vote centers.
text:
A.

The city clerk may propose to the city council a plan for the establishment of vote
centers. The plan must include the following:

1.

The total number of vote centers to be established.

2.

The location by street address of each vote center and the ward in which the vote
center is located. The locations may be presented by map or other graphic depiction.

3.

A description of hardware, firmware or software that will be used:

a.

To create an electronic poll list of voters and precincts that can vote at the vote
center.

b.

To establish a secure connection between the county election board and the vote centers.

4.

A certification that the proposed vote centers comply with the accessibility requirements
applicable to polling places under NRS 293C.281.

5.

A proposed layout for each vote center indicating how the vote center will be set
up for use by election officials and voters for early voting periods and on election
day.

6.

Whether the vote centers will also be designated as polling places for early voting
pursuant to NRS 293C.355 to 361.

B.

The vote center locations must be approved by ordinance of the city council to be
enacted at least 60 days prior to the time established for early voting in any municipal
election.

C.

The city clerk upon approval shall publish the location of each vote center.

D.

The city clerk shall administer an election conducted at vote centers in accordance
with applicable federal, state and local laws and the plan submitted to the city council
under HMC [section] 2.08.060A.

E.

Notwithstanding any other law, a registered voter who resides in the city is entitled
to cast a ballot at any vote center established in the city without regard to the
precinct or ward in which the voter resides.

(Ord. 2513, § 2, 2006)

heading: 2.08.070 - Ward boundaries.
text:
The city council may modify the boundaries of wards pursuant to Section 1.040 of the Henderson City Charter. However, modification shall not take place, except
to accommodate an annexation of territory to the city, during any year in which a
general election is held and within the six months prior to the deadline for a candidate
to file a declaration of his or her candidacy.

(Ord. No. 3060, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 2.10.010 - City manager authority.
text:
A.

Pursuant to Section 3.020 of the City of Henderson Charter, the city manager is the chief executive officer
of the city and shall be responsible for administering the government of the city.
The city manager shall have general supervision and oversight over all departments
and offices of the city, excluding the municipal court and the offices of executive
officers appointed by the city council pursuant to the Henderson City Charter.

B.

The city manager shall also perform such administrative and executive duties as the
city council may designate through the Henderson City Charter, this chapter, other
ordinances or resolutions, a city manager's employment agreement and other city council
action.

C.

The city manager shall also perform such duties required by a city manager or chief
executive officer of a city as may be set forth in the Nevada Revised Statutes.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

heading: 2.10.020 - City manager organizational duties.
text:
A.

The city manager shall have general supervision and oversight over all departments
and offices of the city, excluding the municipal court and the offices of executive
officers appointed by the city council pursuant to the Henderson City Charter.

B.

From time to time the city manager may:

(1)

Establish new departments, combine existing departments, or make other adjustments
to the departments. Any such action by the city manager shall be effective immediately
or when directed by the city manager.

(2)

Establish and adjust divisions, offices or other units within the various departments
of the city, as well as offices and other units that are independent of those departments.

C.

Pursuant to Henderson City Charter, Section 1.090(3), the city manager shall appoint the following executive officers, subject to ratification
of the city council:

(1)

Chief of police.

(2)

Assistant city manager.

(3)

Fire chief.

(4)

Chief financial officer.

D.

Pursuant to Henderson City Charter, Section 1.090(2), the city manager must appoint any newly established executive officer not otherwise
listed in the Henderson City Charter that the city council may establish as it deems
necessary for the operation of the city.

E.

The city manager shall appoint all department directors and senior directors. All
appointed executive officers set forth in subsections (C), (D), and all department
directors and senior directors serve at the pleasure of the city manager.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

heading: 2.10.030 - City manager financial duties.
text:
A.

The city manager shall have charge and supervision over all accounts and records of
the city, and may inspect, or cause to be inspected, all financial records or accounts
required to be kept in any of the offices or departments of the city. The city manager,
or his designee, shall examine or cause to be examined, and report to the city council
upon, all bills, accounts and payrolls of the city.

B.

The city manager shall direct the department of finance to develop a city financial
management policy that is approved by the city council. The financial management policy
shall include the elements to design, maintain and administer a reliable revenue system
to support desired city services pursuant to state and federal laws.

C.

In coordination with the city attorney, the city manager shall submit to the city
council for approval a city fiscal signature policy. The city fiscal signature policy
shall include the signatory requirements for agreements and payments approved and
executed by either the city council, the city manager, department directors or other
city employees depending on the type of agreement or payment.

D.

The city manager shall direct the department of finance to develop an annual budget
for the city each fiscal year, pursuant to state law.

(1)

Once the annual budget is approved and appropriated by the city council, the city
manager has the authority to manage the city budget within the appropriated amounts
approved by the city council.

(2)

The city manager has the ability to re-direct funds within the appropriated budget
unless the re-direction would require the appropriated budget to be augmented with
additional funds outside the appropriated budget. The city manager shall manage all
city funds pursuant to all state and federal laws and any rules or ordinances applicable
to a particular city fund.

(3)

Any augmentation to the approved annual budget requires city council approval.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

heading: 2.10.040 - City manager human resources and benefits duties.
text:
A.

The city manager shall develop and maintain an administrative personnel policy manual
that includes certain city personnel policies that establish an orderly system of
personnel administration within the city.

(1)

The city manager may issue administrative personnel policies and directives in consultation
with the director of human resources and the city attorney.

(2)

All city administrative personnel policies and directives shall comply with state
and federal employment laws, the City of Henderson Charter, and where applicable,
Henderson civil service rules or the terms of any collective bargaining agreement
entered into by the city.

B.

The city manager or their designee shall act as the city's management representative
for any collective bargaining units recognized by the city pursuant to NRS Chapter
288.

C.

The city manager shall manage and administer the benefit plans and programs of the
city including, but not limited to, any: city funded health plans; paid time off and
or sick leave programs for employees; disability and life insurance benefits for employees,
and; any other benefits that city may provide. The city manager shall administer the
benefit plans and programs of the city in compliance with state and federal employment
laws, the City of Henderson Charter, and where applicable, Henderson civil service
rules or the terms of any collective bargaining agreement entered into by the city.

(1)

The city manager may make additions or modifications to city benefit plans if the
costs of such additions or modifications do not require augmentation of the city council
approved annual budget.

(2)

If a city manager addition or modification to city benefit plans require an augmentation
to the city council approved annual budget the augmentation must be approved by the
city council before the addition or modification becomes effective.

D.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, may make modifications
to city job descriptions.

E.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, may make modifications
to the salary ranges or classification of city job positions pursuant to state and
federal law.

F.

The city manager, in consultation with the director of human resources, the chief
financial officer and the city attorney, may approve any change in salary, compensation
or benefits for any city employee.

G.

The city manager, with the approval of the city attorney, may approve and execute
any employment related settlement or severance agreement, including any agreement
related to a city council approved reduction-in-force, early retirement or enhanced
severance program.

H.

The city manager may approve any new positions within the city, or other modifications
to the city employee staff compliment, if such changes do not require augmentation
of the city council approved annual budget.

(Ord. No. 3123, § 1, 2-18-2014)

heading: 2.24.010 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter:

Coordinator means the emergency management coordinator for the city.

Disaster means a severe or prolonged emergency for which assistance is, or may be, needed
to supplement the efforts and capabilities of the city to protect or avert the threat
of damage to life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure.

Emergency means a natural or human-caused incident or set of incidents, occurring or threatened
to occur, that requires responsive action by the city to protect or avert the threat
of damage to life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure.
An emergency includes, but is not limited to, an incident involving a(n) active assailant,
air quality issue, chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, or explosives hazard,
oil spill, civil disturbance, cybersecurity, drought, fire, flood, landslide, debris
flow, geohazard, infectious disease, impact on infrastructure, severe weather, terrorism,
and/or impact on transportation.

Emergency management means the management and coordination of prevention, mitigation, preparedness, response,
and recovery activities for emergencies and disasters, other than functions for which
military forces are primarily responsible.

Emergency operations plan means the emergency response plan for the city that complies with any applicable
requirements in NRS 239C.250 and NRS chapter 414, is prepared at the direction of
the city manager, with input from the Henderson emergency management council in accordance
with section 2.24.040, and is adopted by city council.

Human-caused means caused by human activity, including but not limited to incidents of a chemical,
biological, radiological, nuclear, explosive, or technological (including cyber) nature,
whether accidental or intentional.

Local organization for emergency management has the same meaning as the term "local organization for emergency management" in
NRS chapter 414.

Mitigation means activities designed to reduce or eliminate risks to persons, property, the
environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure or to lessen the actual or potential
effects or consequences of an emergency or disaster.

Next lawful meeting means the first regular or special meeting of the city council at which the desired
action may be duly noticed and taken in accordance with NRS chapter 241, without utilizing
the emergency provisions under such chapter.

Preparedness means the range of deliberate, critical tasks and activities necessary to build,
sustain, and improve the operational capability to prevent, protect against, mitigate
against, respond to, and recover from emergencies and disasters.

Prevention means actions to avoid an incident or to intervene to stop an incident from occurring,
including but not limited to actions to protect lives, property, the environment,
critical systems, and infrastructure.

Recovery means the development, coordination, and execution of plans or strategies to restore
impacted communities and city operations and services.

Response means efforts to minimize the short-term direct effects of an incident threatening
or harming life, property, the environment, critical systems, and/or infrastructure.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 1, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 2, 1993)

heading: 2.24.020 - Emergency management coordinator—Appointment and authority.
text:
The emergency management coordinator for the city shall be appointed by the city manager
and shall be responsible for emergency management in accordance with the state's plan
and program for emergency management and for the organization, administration and
operation of the local plan for emergency management subject to the direction and
control of the city manager. Under that direction and control, the coordinator shall
be empowered to function with the duties and responsibilities described in section
2.24.030.

(Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 3, 1993)

heading: 2.24.030 - Emergency management coordinator—Duties and responsibilities.
text:
A.

The emergency management coordinator shall be the "director" of the local organization
for emergency management established by the city pursuant to NRS 414.090 and shall
take the oath required pursuant to NRS 414.150 upon assuming the duties of emergency
management coordinator. In the absence of the emergency management coordinator or
vacancy in that position, each person designated under section 2.24.110 to fill the position of emergency management coordinator shall take the oath required
pursuant to NRS 414.150 before that person assumes the duties of emergency management
coordinator.

B.

The emergency management coordinator is authorized to petition, acquire and accept
funds from the United States Government or any agency or office thereof, or from the
State of Nevada, for emergency management purposes, as provided in the provisions
of NRS 414.130.

C.

The emergency management coordinator, in collaboration with other public and private
agencies within the state, may develop or cause to be developed, agreements for mutual
aid or assistance in case of emergency or disaster for which the city requires such
assistance. Those agreements shall be approved by the city council, shall be consistent
with the state's plan and program for emergency management, and shall provide that
in time of emergency or disaster each local organization for emergency management
shall render assistance in accordance with the provisions of such agreements.

D.

The emergency management coordinator shall perform and exercise other such functions,
powers and duties as are necessary to promote and secure public safety and protection
within the territorial limits of the city and, in addition, shall conduct such functions
outside the territorial limits of the city as may be required pursuant to the provisions
of NRS chapter 414.

E.

The emergency management coordinator is responsible for responding to emergencies
and disasters as they may occur at any time. The police communications dispatch center
will be advised when the emergency management coordinator will not be available during
off hours, annual leave and holidays. In order to relieve the emergency management
coordinator and to temporarily assume the continuous coverage of responsibility, qualified
back up employees are designated by title in section 2.24.110, Continuity of government. In order for the emergency management coordinator to respond
at all hours, the emergency management coordinator shall be assigned a city take-home
vehicle, in which all necessary emergency equipment, radios, publications, check lists,
marked clothing, etc., will be available and ready for use. The vehicle will be used
solely by the emergency management coordinator and operated in accordance with the
applicable city directive. The vehicle will be used solely by the emergency management
coordinator and operated in accordance with all applicable city policies and directives.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 2, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, §§ 4—7, 1993)

heading: 2.24.040 - Emergency management council—Created—Members.
text:
A.

There is created the Henderson emergency management council ("EMC") which shall consist
of the following:

1.

The emergency management coordinator, or their designee, who shall serve as chair
of the EMC;

2.

The emergency management officer, who shall serve as vice chair of the EMC and act
as chair in the absence of the emergency management coordinator; and

3.

Department heads of various departments, as appointed by the city manager, who may
have key emergency responsibilities to the city government.

B.

The emergency management coordinator may invite organizations that may provide support
or information during an emergency to be members of the EMC. That organization shall
designate one or more people to represent it on the EMC. Those organizations and representatives
shall keep all confidential information disclosed to them confidential, shall not
disclose confidential information in any manner to any individual or business entity
without prior written authorization from the emergency management coordinator, and
are presumed to agree to these confidentiality obligations by virtue of the organization
being a member of the EMC. "Confidential information" means oral or written information
concerning (1) the city's emergency planning, operations or preparedness provided
to the EMC, (2) the emergency operations plan, other confidential emergency response
plan(s), and any confidential incident response plan(s), and/or (3) drafts of those
plans.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 3, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3580, § 1, 5-21-2019; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 8, 1993)

heading: 2.24.050 - Emergency management council—Powers and duties.
text:
The EMC is established for the purpose of making recommendations to the city manager
with respect to matters involving emergency management. The EMC shall make recommendations
for the adoption of an emergency operations plan in compliance with the requirements
of NRS chapters 239C and 414 and the adoption or approval of any and all mutual aid
plans and agreements that are deemed necessary for the implementation of such emergency
operations plan. The duties of such EMC shall also include a continuing study of the
need for revisions to the emergency operations plan. The EMC shall meet upon the call
of the chair.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 4, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 9, 1993)

heading: 2.24.060 - Declaration of state of emergency.
text:
A.

In accordance with NRS 241.020(2) and (5), charter sections 2.050 and 3.010, and the emergency operations plan, the mayor, mayor pro tempore, or a majority of
the members of the city council may call an emergency meeting. If it is determined
that an emergency or disaster exists, the city council shall declare in writing that
a state of emergency exists and shall publicize, by a method deemed appropriate by
city council, the existence of the emergency or disaster. If circumstances prohibit
timely action by the city council, then the mayor, mayor pro tempore, city manager,
or emergency management coordinator may issue a declaration of state of emergency
and seek the ratification of that declaration by a majority of a quorum of the city
council at the next lawful meeting. If the city council fails to ratify that declaration
of state of emergency at the next lawful meeting, then that declaration shall automatically
terminate when that next lawful meeting adjourns.

B.

The city council or city manager shall terminate the declaration of state of emergency
when the emergency or disaster no longer exists or the threat of an emergency has
passed.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 5, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 10, 1993)

heading: 2.24.070 - Operational emergency management organization.
text:
The operational emergency management organization of the city shall consist of officers
and employees of the city designated by the emergency management coordinator, as well
as all volunteer workers. The functions and duties of this organization shall be distributed
among such divisions, services and special staff as the city manager shall prescribe.
The operational emergency management organization is the "local organization for emergency
management" established pursuant to NRS 414.090.

The emergency management coordinator, with the approval of city manager, shall set
forth the form of organization, establish and designate divisions and services, assign
functions, duties and powers, and designate officers and employees to carry out the
provisions of this chapter. Insofar as possible, the form of organization, titles
and terminology shall conform to the recommendations of the federal government and
the recommendations of the emergency management agency of the State of Nevada. A specific
directive creating this organization by name will be developed by the emergency management
coordinator, approved by the city manager, and updated periodically in the emergency
operations plan as necessary.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 6, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 11, 1993)

heading: 2.24.080 - Emergency powers of city manager and emergency management coordinator.
text:
A.

At the inception of and during a disaster or emergency, the city manager or the emergency
management coordinator:

1.

Shall implement the city's emergency operations plan and may direct and control such
other city employees as are required to implement the plan from the emergency operations
center (EOC) or other designated location(s);

2.

May, through requisition or contract with private parties or other government entities,
obtain necessary services, supplies and equipment needed to protect life and property
and implement the plan; and may bind the city for the value thereof without being
required to comply with the normal purchasing procedures, if compliance with those
procedures would unreasonably hamper or impair the implementation the plan; and

3.

May suspend the licensing requirements for persons whose services are required for
implementation of the emergency operations plan.

B.

The emergency powers granted the city manager and emergency management coordinator
under this section may be revoked, limited or restricted by order of the city council.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 7, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 12, 1993)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3862, § 7, adopted April 5, 2022, changed the title of section 2.24.080 from "Emergency
powers of city manager" to "Emergency powers of city manager and emergency management

heading: 2.24.090 - Measures to maintain peace and order.
text:
If a declared state of emergency exists within the city, the city council may, if
it deems it necessary to maintain peace and protect the public, take action and order
and enforce the measures listed in this section. If circumstances prohibit the timely
action of the city council, the city manager, mayor, mayor pro tempore, or emergency
management coordinator may, under the same circumstances, order measures and take
actions consistent with the items listed below and shall report their actions to the
city council at its next lawful meeting. During the existence of a state of emergency,
to the full extent permitted by law, including in the exercise of any delegation of
authority by the Governor of the State of Nevada, the city council or, if authorized
by the city council or in the event that circumstances prohibit the timely action
of city council, the city manager, mayor, mayor pro tempore, or emergency management
coordinator may:

A.

Establish a curfew for the area designated as an emergency area which fixes the hours
during which persons other than officially authorized personnel may be upon the public
streets or other public places;

B.

Prohibit or limit the number of persons who may gather or congregate upon any public
street, public place or any outdoor place within the area designated as an emergency
area;

C.

Barricade streets and roads, as well as access points onto streets and roads, and
prohibit or restrict vehicular or pedestrian traffic in the area;

D.

Enter into contracts and incur obligations necessary to combat such an emergency or
disaster, protect the health and safety of persons and property and provide emergency
assistance to the victims of such an emergency or disaster to the full extent permitted
under NRS chapter 332, NRS chapter 414, or other applicable law;

E.

Redirect funds for emergency use to the full extent permitted under NRS chapter 414
or other applicable law;

F.

Suspend standard procurement procedures to obtain necessary services or equipment
to the full extent permitted under NRS chapter 332, NRS chapter 414, or other applicable
law;

G.

Commit to mutual aid agreements; and

H.

Take such other actions and perform and exercise such other functions, powers and
duties as are necessary to promote and secure the safety and protection of the civilian
population.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 8, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 13, 1993)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3862, § 8, adopted April 5, 2022, changed the title of section 2.24.090 from "Emergency
measures to maintain peace and order" to "Measures to maintain peace and order." The
historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

heading: 2.24.100 - Public works director—Duties and responsibilities.
text:
A.

To the extent necessary during or after the existence of a declared emergency or disaster
and under the direction of the city manager, the director of the city's public works
department may remove debris which threatens the public health or safety. Any action
taken by the director under this section shall be reported by the city manager to
the city council at its next lawful meeting. Under the direction and control of the
city manager, the director may:

1.

Use the city departments, mutual aid agreements with other governmental entities or,
if necessary, private resources; and

2.

Accept funds from the federal government or the state and utilize those funds for
the purpose of removing such debris.

B.

Debris which exists on city-owned property may be removed at city expense, provided
that the expense of removing any debris caused by the negligent or intentional act
of any person may be recovered from that person.

C.

The public works director may order that debris which exists on privately owned property
be removed by the owner of the property or the person responsible for the property
at the owner's or other person's expense. Each order must specify the nature of the
threat to the public and the minimum quantity of debris which must be removed to eliminate
the threat. During an emergency, the order is effective when orally conveyed to the
owner or other person responsible for the property.

D.

Upon the failure of a person to comply with an order described in this section, the
public works director may remove or cause the removal of the debris. The owner of
the property or the person responsible for the property is liable to the city for
the costs incurred.

E.

When immediate emergency measures are determined necessary for protection of public
health and safety, or public or private property, and oral or written authorization
cannot be obtained from the owner or other person responsible for the property, the
public works director may authorize the entry upon the public or private lands or
waters and perform such tasks necessary to the emergency removal or clearance operations.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 9, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 1431, § 14, 1993)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3862, § 9, adopted April 5, 2022, changed the title of section 2.24.100 from "Public works,
parks and recreation director—Duties and responsibilities" to "Public works director—Duties
and responsibilities." The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

heading: 2.24.110 - Continuity of government.
text:
A.

Catastrophic events can interrupt, paralyze and/or destroy the ability of local governments
to carry out their legislative, executive and judicial functions. Therefore, it is
imperative that a "continuity of government" (COG) be structured with the capability
to preserve, maintain, and/or reconstitute its ability to function under the threat
or occurrence of any emergency that could disrupt local government and public services.

B.

In order to continue governmental functions, it is necessary to establish replacements
for key positions through three levels where possible. The following positions are
considered key positions in emergency management, and any absences and vacancies will
be filled by the person holding the title indicated or, if the title indicated does
not correspond with an existing position, by the person holding the functionally equivalent
position under a different title, in order as follows:

1.

City manager. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Chief operating officer/Deputy city manager;

b.

Chief infrastructure officer/Assistant city manager;

c.

Chief strategy officer/Assistant city manager;

d.

Chief of police.

2.

Mayor. In accordance with the charter section 3.010, mayor pro tempore performs the duties of mayor during the absence or disability
of the mayor and acts as mayor until the vacancy is filled pursuant to charter section 1.070. Absence or vacancy of mayor or mayor pro tempore filled by:

a.

Most senior member of the city council, as shown by the city clerk's records.

3.

City council. Absence not filled. Vacancy filled in accordance with charter sections 1.060 and 1.070.

4.

Chief of police. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Deputy chief of police (operations);

b.

Deputy chief of police (support);

c.

Most senior captain.

5.

Fire chief. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Deputy fire chief (operations);

b.

Deputy fire chief (support);

c.

Most senior battalion chief.

6.

Director of public works. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director;

b.

City engineer;

c.

Facilities maintenance manager.

7.

Emergency management coordinator. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Emergency manager;

b.

Emergency management officer;

c.

Emergency management specialist;

d.

Safety manager;

e.

Environmental manager.

8.

City attorney. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Senior assistant city attorney (civil division);

b.

Senior assistant city attorney (criminal division);

c.

Assistant city attorney who primarily supports city's emergency management division.

9.

Chief financial officer. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director;

b.

Business operations manager;

c.

Budget manager.

10.

Director of economic development and tourism. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Manager of business operations and tourism;

b.

Most senior economic development officer;

c.

Economic development officer.

11.

Assistant director—Building and fire safety. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Manager of inspection services;

b.

Manager of plans examining services;

c.

Assistant manager of inspection services.

12.

City clerk. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Archives and records manager;

b.

Manager of council and commission services.

13.

Municipal court judge. Absence not filled. Vacancy filled in accordance with charter sections 1.060 and 1.070.

14.

Director of government and public affairs. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Government affairs manager;

b.

Marketing and public relations manager.

15.

Utility services director. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Most senior deputy director;

b.

Deputy director;

c.

Most senior manager of water/wastewater operations.

16.

Director of information technology. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director of information technology;

b.

Information technology manager (information systems);

c.

Information technology manager (infrastructure);

d.

Information technology manager (service center).

17.

Director of community development and services. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director community development and services;

b.

Assistant director building and fire safety;

c.

Planning manager.

18.

Human resources director. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director;

b.

Chief labor negotiator;

c.

Manager of organizational effectiveness.

19.

Director of parks and recreation. Absence or vacancy filled by:

a.

Assistant director;

b.

Administrative manager;

c.

Recreation superintendent.

20.

Other departments. Vacancies to be filled by appointment as necessary.

When not part of a person's official title, "senior" refers to the person who has
held the applicable position for the longest period of time, and information in parenthesis
refers to the division or operations the referenced person manages or oversees. Any
person filling a vacancy pursuant to this section shall hold such position as "acting
[title]" until the position is duly filled in accordance with any applicable law.

(Ord. No. 3862, § 10, 4-5-2022; Ord. No. 3580, § 2, 5-21-2019; Ord. No. 3403, § 1, 5-2-2017; Ord. No. 3021, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. No. 1431, § 15, 1993)

heading: 2.27.010 - Purpose.
text:
To regulate the use of city-owned and/or operated parks, trails, recreation facilities
and public plazas hosting cultural activities in order that all persons may enjoy
and make use of the parks, trail, recreation facilities and public plazas to protect
the assets and resources of these community properties.

(Ord. No. 3753, § 1, 1-19-2021; Ord. No. 3396, § 1, 4-11-2017; Ord. No. 3190, § 2, 7-1-2014)

heading: 2.27.020 - Definitions and interpretation.
text:
As used in this chapter, the following definitions shall apply. Words and phrases
shall be construed according to the common and approved usage of the language, but
technical words, technical phrases and words and phrases that have acquired peculiar
and appropriate meanings in law shall be construed according to such meanings. A park
event permit shall be requested in writing.

Amplified sound means speech, music, or other sound projected or transmitted by electronic equipment
(including, but not limited to, amplifiers, loud speakers, bull horns or similar devices),
which is intended to increase the volume or range of the sound.

Applicant means any person or entity who submits a request to the director under this chapter
in order to obtain the necessary permission to conduct certain activities as described
in HMC 2.27.030 at or within a park, recreation facility or trail.

Cultural activity means an activity dedicated to performing arts, history or education, or the promotion
of activities related to sporting events.

Director means the director of the city's parks and recreation department or his or her authorized
representative or designee.

Electric bicycle has the meaning as described in NRS 484B.017 and means a device upon which a person
may ride, having two or three wheels, or every such device generally recognized as
a bicycle equipped with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750
watts, and is categorized by the following:

Class 1 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling,
and that ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 20 miles
per hour;

Class 2 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that may be used exclusively to propel the bicycle, and
that is not capable of providing assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 20
miles per hour; and

Class 3 electric bicycle is equipped with a motor that provides assistance only when the rider is pedaling,
and that ceases to provide assistance when the bicycle reaches a speed of 28 miles
per hour. This bicycle is equipped with a speedometer.

Electric motorcycle means device upon which a person may ride, having two or three wheels which is not
covered by Nevada Revised Statute as a motor vehicle and is not defined as an electric
bicycle in this Code which is propelled by one or more electric motors.

Electric scooter has the meaning described in NRS 484B.018 and means that it has a maximum speed of
not more than 20 miles per hour.

HMC means the Henderson Municipal Code, as the same may be amended or modified from time-to-time.

Off-road vehicle or off-highway vehicles has the meaning as described in NRS 480.420. This term is inclusive of all internal
combustion motor vehicles and electric motor driven vehicles.

Park means a parcel of land owned, operated or maintained by the city and specifically
set apart for the recreational use of the public, either temporarily or permanently.
This term also includes any land identified as a trail.

Participate means, for purposes of HMC 2.27.030(N), to take a direct role or part in communicating the permittee's message, as opposed
to merely being present at the permittee's use. By way of illustration, every person
marching in a parade is an expressive unit, the sum of which constitutes the expressive
message attributed to the parade's organizer, whereas a spectator who is merely present
along the parade's route and who expresses his or her own contrary message is not
a "participant" because his or her message could not reasonably be perceived as part
of the message he or she protests.

Permittee means any person who received the necessary permission to conduct certain activities
as described in HMC 2.27.030 at or within a park, recreation facility or trail.

Public plaza means an open outdoor area that is:

A.

Water Street Events Plaza, located on Water Street and Atlantic Avenue;

B.

Any other outdoor area that is:

1.

Owned and operated by or on behalf of the city;

2.

Designed for use as a gathering place for the public or the public enjoyment of cultural
activities; and

3.

Designated as a public plaza by resolution of the city council.

Recreation facility means those structures, amenities, or apparatus located in a park or trail which
aid or make easier the recreational use of the park or trail, including, but not limited
to, recreation centers.

Trail means an improved or unimproved pathway designed primarily for outdoor recreational
purposes that generally connects elements, spaces, or facilities.

Trailhead means a location having an information kiosk for a trail.
