heading: 4.05.130 - Apartment house.
text:
A.

For the purposes of this section, the following definitions shall apply:

1.

"Apartment house" is defined as a building, or group of buildings, which contains
multiple dwelling units designed for residential purposes and occupied by multiple
households. This definition excludes multi-family dwelling units which qualify as
a townhouse, residence hotel, or condominium.

2.

"Manager" is defined as a licensee, an employee of a licensee, a property manager,
or an employee of a property manager or any other person designated by a licensee
who has primary responsibility for the day to day operations of an apartment house,
including such activities as negotiating lease and rental terms, managing lease and
rental transactions, maintaining accounting records, and overseeing building and grounds
maintenance.

3.

"Landlord training program" is defined as the training program provided to apartment
managers by the police department or the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department
in connection with the Henderson Crime Free Multi-Housing Program.

4.

"Property manager" is defined as an individual or a property management company that
is licensed by the Nevada Department of Business and Industry Real Estate Division
to operate as a property manager.

B.

Every person operating an apartment house with five or more units must obtain, and
thereafter maintain, an apartment house business license and shall pay a semiannual
license fee as set forth in the following schedule:

Less than five apartments

No license required

Five to ten apartments

$35.00

Excess of ten

$35.00 plus $2.50 for each additional apartment in

excess of ten

C.

For purposes of this section, units located on contiguous sites or on the same street
or adjacent streets may, at the discretion of the city, be combined to determine total
units for a license.

D.

In addition to the semiannual fees set forth in subsection 4.05.130(B), an apartment house renting to transient guests, as that term is defined in chapter 4.48, is also subject to the transient lodging taxes as set forth in chapter 4.48.

E.

To obtain and maintain a valid apartment house business license, the licensee must
identify its designated manager(s), as defined in this section, and provide proof
to the department and the police department that said manager(s) has completed the
landlord training program within 90 days of the issuance of the license.

F.

A person licensed as the operator of an apartment house shall notify the department
of any change to the designated manager of the apartment house within 30 days of when
the change occurs. Newly hired or designated managers must complete the landlord training
program within 90 days of the date of hire.

G.

A certificate of completion of the landlord training program shall be maintained on
the premises of each apartment house containing proof that the current manager has
completed a landlord training program or evidence that the current manager has been
employed in that capacity for fewer than 90 days.

H.

All apartment house licensees and applicants with applications currently on file with
the city as of the effective date of the ordinance codified in this section shall
have until 180 days from the effective date of the ordinance to provide proof to the
division that they are in compliance with the landlord training program requirement.

I.

The division, at its sole discretion, may extend any compliance period set forth in
this section up to an additional 90 days upon a showing of good cause as to why the
licensee was unable to satisfy the compliance period; or upon notification from the
police department that the available landlord training programs offered could not
accommodate the number of managers requiring certification within the time period
for compliance.

J.

Failure to comply with any provision of this subsection constitutes a violation of
this title and shall subject the licensee to the penalties available under this title.

(Ord. No. 3521, § 1, 9-18-2018; Ord. No. 3291, § 1, 10-6-2015)

(See subsection 4.04.060(B)). No person shall be issued a license to practice astrology unless such person
meets all the qualifications provided for below:

professional offices or any commercial or industrial use, and provided that the use

license based on the finding of suitability and the application submitted; and

astrological columns.

during the course and scope of employment. Every licensee shall accordingly use adequate

heading: 4.05.280 - Locksmith and safe mechanic.
text:
A.

or renumbered the license fee shall be $100.00 semiannually. In addition to completing
a regular application, each applicant for a locksmith or safe mechanic's license shall
present himself to the police department for fingerprinting and furnish the police
department any other information necessary to conduct an investigation pursuant to
chapter 4.03. Upon completion of the investigation, the director shall prepare and submit to the
council a report containing the finding of suitability and a recommendation of approval
or disapproval of the license.

B.

If it shall appear to the council that the applicant is of such character and reputation
that the issuance of a locksmith's or safe mechanic's license to him will not prejudice
or be detrimental to the public safety or welfare, the council shall approve the application,
and the division shall therefor issue the license upon payment of the required fee.

C.

In the event the applicant is a firm, partnership, or corporation, the director shall
identify the responsible party(ies) who shall complete an application. Upon completion
of the investigation(s), the director shall prepare and submit to the council a report
containing the finding(s) of suitability and a recommendation of approval or disapproval
of the license.

D.

A locksmith and safe mechanic license is a privileged license and may be suspended,
limited or revoked, or other disciplinary action taken with respect thereto for the
failure of the licensee to comply with the requirements of this section.

E.

Each licensee shall be responsible for the acts of his employees and agents committed
during the course and scope of employment. Each licensee shall accordingly use adequate
care in the selection of his employees and agents. In any license suspension, limitation
or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge
of the events complained of shall be no defense and every licensee accepts his license
subject to said condition.

heading: 4.05.345 - Psychic arts practitioner.
text:
A.

For every person who carries on, practices, or professes to practice the business
of palmistry, phrenology, life reading, fortunetelling, cartomancy, clairvoyance,
clairaudience, crystal gazing, mediumship, prophecy, augury, divination or necromancy,
and demands or receives a fee for the exercise or exhibition of his respective arts,
directly or indirectly, or incidental to the conduct of any other business, either
as a gift, donation, or otherwise, or who gives an exhibition thereof at any place
where an admission fee is charged the license fee shall be $100.00 semiannually.

B.

Application for a psychic arts practitioner license shall be made to the division
accompanied by a nonrefundable investigation fee deposit, as set forth in chapter 4.03, to conduct a police department criminal background investigation of the applicant.
(See subsection 4.04.060(B)). No person shall be issued a psychic arts practitioner license unless such person
meets all the qualifications provided for below:

1.

A psychic arts practitioner license shall be limited to areas permitting professional
offices or any commercial or industrial use, and provided that the use is operated
in compliance with title 19;

2.

A background investigation shall be conducted; and the results shall be furnished
to the director who will make a determination on the finding of suitably of the applicant;
and

3.

The division shall forward a recommendation to the council to approve or deny the
license based on the finding of suitability and the application submitted; and

4.

The applicant shall be at least 18 years of age.

C.

No employee or other person shall assist the licensee in any audience or reading,
except psychic healings, nor shall any mechanical device of any description whatsoever
be used by the licensee in the conduct of any interview, audience or reading.

D.

A psychic arts practitioner license is a privileged license and may be suspended,
limited or revoked, or other disciplinary action taken with respect thereto for the
failure of the licensee to comply with the requirements of this section.

E.

Each licensee shall be responsible for the acts of their employees and agents committed
during the course and scope of employment. Each licensee shall accordingly use adequate
care in the selection of their employees and agents. In any license suspension, limitation
or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge
of the events complained of shall be no defense and every licensee accepts their license
subject to said condition.

F.

This section shall not be construed to apply to doctors, dentists, or other medical
practitioners licensed by the appropriate board under Nevada Revised Statutes or to
a person employed by such doctors, dentists, or other medical practitioners acting
under their direction and control, who use any psychic arts as an aid in the treatment
or as a supplementary form of treatment in the course of their profession.

G.

This section shall not be construed to apply to astrologers licensed under section
4.05.140.

(Ord. No. 3583, § 6, 6-4-2019; Ord. No. 3291, § 1, 10-6-2015)

text:

one temporary sales or service permit per calendar quarter.

days prior to the event:

1.

Written permission of the property owner or, in the case of a retail location, the
written authorization of the store management;

2.

Proof of a State of Nevada sales tax permit, if applicable;

3.

Approval of the community development and services department; and

state, or the federal government.

calendar days prior to the scheduled event may be waived at the director's discretion.

2.

a.

For purposes of this chapter an arts, crafts and business trade show is an event with
a minimum of 20 vendors wherein at least 50 percent of the vendors provide only handmade
items, including, but not limited to, decorative items, clothing and food that has
been created for sale by the craftsman.

b.

service permit per calendar quarter pursuant to subsection 4.05.375(C)(2) be granted more than 16 temporary sales or service permits in a single calendar
year, and no more than two temporary sales or service permits in any single month.

3.

calendar year.

heading: Chapter 4.06 - POLICY AND PROCEDURE SHOW CAUSE, LICENSE SUSPENSION, LIMITATION, REVOCATION[5]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (5) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3302, §§ 1, 2, adopted October 20, 2015, repealed and reenacted chapter 4.06 in its entirety
to read as herein set out. Formerly, chapter 4.06, §§ 4.06.010—4.06.300, pertained
to similar subject matter, and derived from Ord. No. 2950, § 2, adopted December 20, 2011, and Ord. No. 3084, § 1, adopted November 5, 2013;

heading: 4.06.010 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter, words and terms shall have the meaning ascribed to them pursuant
to title 4, unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning.

References to days in this chapter shall refer to calendar days and time shall be
computed pursuant to Rule 6 of the Nevada Rules of Civil Procedure.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.020 - Investigation and reporting of violations.
text:
The director is responsible for the enforcement of business license regulations and
ordinances and the investigations thereof. Those violations that the director deems
necessary for additional disciplinary action, in addition to the action taken by the
division, shall be referred to the city attorney for appropriate action.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.030 - Division to cooperate with other regulatory agencies.
text:
A.

The division shall cooperate with other public agencies concerned with the regulation
and control of business licenses, and to that end may exchange with such agencies
any and all types of confidential information, including, without limitation, information
regarding licensees, their independent contractors, operations, agents and employees.
When dealing with any gaming matter, the division may immediately inform the state
gaming agencies of any investigation, hearing or other actions that the division,
its officers or the director intends to take or is considering taking against a licensee.

B.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with the state gaming agencies
such that duplication of effort shall be kept to a minimum; provided, however, that
if the apparent violation is of such a character that action should be taken and if
the state gaming agencies fail, refuse or decline to assume control of the investigation
and hearing, then the division shall promptly investigate.

C.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with liquor and gaming boards in
the incorporated and unincorporated cities and towns of Clark County so that overall
regulation and control may be more effectively maintained.

D.

The division may enter into one or more agreements with state professional and/or
occupational licensing boards so that overall regulation and control may be more effectively
maintained.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.040 - Complaint against license—Determination by city attorney.
text:
In addition to any action taken by the division for a violation of this title, the
city attorney, or his designee, may investigate the violation(s) to determine whether
there is cause for additional disciplinary action, such as suspension or revocation
of the license, or suspension or revocation of a conditional use permit pursuant to
title 19.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.041 - Administrative action.
text:
If the city attorney is satisfied that based upon the requirements of title 4 grounds exist for the revocation or suspension of a license or permit or for discipline
of a licensee or permittee, the city attorney shall draft a complaint and notice of
hearing, both of which shall be filed with the city clerk and served on the licensee,
permittee, or registered agent either personally or by registered or certified mail,
return receipt requested, at the address on file with the division. The complaint
and notice of hearing shall be served at least 20 days prior to the hearing.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.042 - Hearing notice.
text:
The notice of hearing shall be in substantially the following form, but may include
other information:

YOU ARE HEREBY NOTIFIED that a hearing will be held before a duly appointed hearing
officer at (insert place of hearing) on the (insert day) of (insert month), (insert
year) at (insert time), upon the charges made in the complaint served upon you herewith.
You may be present at the hearing and may be represented by counsel. You may present
any relevant evidence, call witnesses and cross-examine all witnesses testifying against
you.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.050 - Complaint.
text:
The complaint shall be a written statement of charges that shall set forth the facts
and/or omissions with which the licensee or permittee is charged. The complaint shall
specify the code sections, regulations and/or provisions of law that the licensee
or permittee is alleged to have violated or the hazard or threat to the public health,
safety or welfare allegedly attributable to the licensee or permittee and the facts
supporting such allegations.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.060 - Form of answer—Filing deadline.
text:
A.

The licensee or permittee must, at least ten days prior to the scheduled hearing,
file with the city clerk its answer responding to the charges made in the complaint
and set forth any defenses it intends to raise, and serve a copy of the answer upon
the city attorney and the appointed hearing officer.

B.

The answer to the complaint shall be signed and verified by the licensee or permittee,
or his agent. The complaint and answer shall form the pleadings for the hearing. In
connection with the complaint and hearing process, the licensee or permittee is the
"respondent".

C.

The answer shall include the following:

To the hearing officer for the city council:

1.

The respondent admits the following facts set forth in the complaint.

2.

The respondent denies the following facts set forth in the complaint.

3.

The respondent believes the following defenses and explanations should be considered
by the hearing officer for the city council.

4.

The respondent raises the following legal defenses.

5.

Upon the filing of an answer, the respondent shall be entitled to a hearing on the
merits upon the issues denied by the answer.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.070 - Representation.
text:
In any case pursuant to this title, the respondent may appear on his or her own behalf
or the respondent may be represented by an attorney licensed to practice law in this
state. A respondent is responsible for all costs, including, without limitation, attorneys'
fees, related to the presentation of his or her defense.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.080 - Failure of respondent to answer charges deemed admission of guilt.
text:
A.

Failure of the respondent to answer within the time specified shall be deemed an admission
of the allegations in the complaint. Thereupon, the hearing officer shall impose such
disciplinary action as requested in the complaint, and shall give notice of such disciplinary
action by mailing a true copy thereof by United States certified mail in a sealed
envelope with postage thereon fully prepaid, addressed to the respondent at respondent's
latest address of record.

B.

Failure to file an answer within the time designated shall further constitute a waiver
of respondent's right to a hearing.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.090 - Hearing officers.
text:
The city council may appoint hearing officers to act on its behalf in conducting hearings
under this title.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.100 - Hearing officers—Appointment, qualifications, conflict of interest, disqualification.
text:
A.

A hearing officer shall be appointed with regard to his or her qualifications to conduct
administrative or quasi-judicial hearings and must:

1.

Be a resident of the State of Nevada;

2.

Be licensed to practice law in the State of Nevada and have at least ten years of
experience practicing law;

3.

Have significant experience in the practice of administrative law or as a hearing
officer or administrative law judge in contested cases;

4.

Not be affiliated or associated with the city in any other manner, such as for example,
as agent, employee, fiduciary officer, or any other type of representative of the
city.

B.

No person may act as a hearing officer in a matter in which he or she has a direct
or substantial financial interest or other conflict of interest. For purposes of this
chapter, "conflict of interest" means a pecuniary or personal interest sufficient
to affect his or her independent judgment and the objective exercise of his or her
public duty.

C.

Either the city or the respondent may move to disqualify a hearing officer prior to
any hearing by filing a written motion and supporting affidavits of conflict of interest.
Such a motion shall be served upon the city clerk, the non-moving party, and the city
manager's office. The city manager or his designee shall rule upon the motion.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.110 - Hearing officers—Appointment to list and compensation.
text:
The city council may appoint individuals to a list of hearing officers based on their
qualifications. Hearing officers shall be entitled to compensation from the city for
the time reasonably expended in the process of preparing for, hearing and deciding
the case at a rate to be set by the city manager with a maximum chargeable time of
20 hours per hearing. In the event that a hearing officer serves more than 20 hours
on any given hearing, he may submit to the city manager a written statement requesting
additional compensation and setting forth reasons therefor. The city manager may authorize
such additional compensation at the set rate if the city manager is satisfied that
the additional hours of service were justified and necessary. As a condition to receiving
payment, the hearing officer must submit an itemized invoice for services rendered
to the city manager within 30 days after the hearing officer's decision is served
upon the parties.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.120 - Hearing officers—Assignment to matter.
text:
Upon the filing of a complaint by the city attorney:

A.

The city manager or designee on behalf of the city council shall select a hearing
officer from the appointed list, or engage an attorney to act as a hearing officer
if there is not a current list or the number of attorneys on the list is insufficient
for any reason, and provide the selected hearing officer with a copy of the complaint.

B.

The city manager or designee shall obtain written verification from the selected hearing
officer that there is no conflict of interest or other reason precluding the hearing
officer from serving on the particular matter assigned.

C.

If a hearing officer is able to serve on the case, the city manager or designee shall
obtain a hearing date and other information to be included in the notice of hearing
pursuant to section 4.06.140. If the selected hearing officer cannot hear the case within the time parameters
set forth in section 4.06.140, the city manager shall select another hearing officer and follow the procedure set
forth in subsections (1) and (2) of this section.

D.

If a hearing officer does not accept the appointment within five days of his selection,
the hearing officer shall be discharged and another hearing officer selected pursuant
to the provisions of this section. A hearing officer discharged pursuant to this section
will not be entitled to be compensated for any costs or fees associated with the case
from which the hearing officer was discharged.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.130 - Hearing officers—Powers and duties.
text:
The hearing officer shall preside over hearings determining allegations of violations
of title 4 and possess all the powers of the city council in determining such matters including
but not limited to:

A.

Coordinating with the city manager's office to set the time and date of the hearing.

B.

Hearing any motions, stipulations or orders upon which the parties agree and addressing
any administrative details.

C.

Continuing a hearing based on good cause shown by one of the parties to the hearing
or if the hearing officer independently determines that good cause exists.

D.

Issuing a subpoena for witnesses, documents, and other evidence as requested by the
parties and in accordance with chapter 4.06.

E.

Imposing disciplinary action, including but not limited to suspension or revocation
of the business license or permit.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.140 - Hearing—Time, date and place.
text:
A.

All hearings shall be held at city hall or other city-owned facility within the city
of Henderson.

B.

Upon the appointment of a hearing officer to hear the case, the hearing officer shall
coordinate with the city manager's office to set the time and date for the hearing
which will be included in the notice of hearing to be served upon the respondent with
the complaint. The hearing date set by the hearing officer shall not be set later
than 45 days from the date of the hearing officer's appointment.

(Ord. No. 3417, § 1, 7-11-2017; Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.150 - Subpoena and compensation of witnesses.
text:
The hearing officer shall issue subpoenas upon receipt of a written request from a
party that is submitted a minimum of ten business days before the hearing. All witnesses
appearing pursuant to subpoena, other than parties, officers or employees of the city,
shall receive fees and mileage in the same amounts and under the same circumstances
as provided by law for witnesses in civil actions in the district court. Such fees
shall be paid by the party at whose request the witness is subpoenaed.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.160 - Discovery.
text:
No discovery may be conducted in the case. A party may not serve any interrogatories
or other written discovery or take any depositions relating to the case.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.170 - Witness—Affidavit or declaration—Service.
text:
Affidavits or declarations made under penalty of perjury may be received in evidence
at any hearing. The party wishing to use such affidavit or declaration shall, not
less than ten days prior to the day set for the hearing, serve upon the opposing party
or counsel, either personally or by mail, a copy of the affidavit or declaration which
that party proposes to introduce in evidence.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.180 - Restriction on communications.
text:
Neither the city nor the respondent (nor their respective counsel) may communicate
with the hearing officer regarding the merits of the case, except in the presence
of the other party or their counsel.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.190 - Hearing procedure.
text:
The following procedures shall apply at all hearings conducted pursuant to this title:

A.

The proceedings at the hearing shall be reported either stenographically and/or by
audio recorder.

B.

Oral evidence shall be taken upon oath or affirmation administered by the hearing
officer.

C.

Each party to a hearing shall have the right:

1.

To call and examine witnesses;

2.

To introduce exhibits relevant to the issues of the case;

3.

To cross-examine opposing witnesses on matters relative to the issues of the case;

4.

To impeach any witness regardless of which party called the witness to testify; and

5.

To offer rebuttal evidence.

D.

If the respondent does not testify on respondent's own behalf, respondent may be called
and examined as if under cross-examination.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.200 - Hearing—Admission of evidence.
text:
A.

The hearing need not be conducted according to technical rules relating to evidence
and witnesses. Any relevant evidence may be admitted, subject to the provisions of
this section.

B.

Irrelevant, immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence must be excluded. Effect shall
be given to the rules of privilege recognized by law. Objections to evidentiary offers
may be made and must be noted in the record. Subject to the requirements of this subsection,
when a hearing will be expedited and the interests of the parties will not be prejudiced
substantially, any part of the evidence may be received in written form.

C.

Every witness shall declare, by oath or affirmation, that he or she will testify truthfully.

D.

Notice may be taken of judicially cognizable facts and of generally recognized technical
or scientific facts within the specialized knowledge of the city's departments and
divisions. Parties must be notified of the material noticed and afforded an opportunity
to contest the material so noticed. The experience, technical competence and specialized
knowledge of the city's departments and divisions may be utilized in the evaluation
of the evidence.

E.

The hearing officer shall have the authority to regulate the course of the hearing,
hold conferences for the settlement or simplification of issues, dispose of procedural
requests, and rule upon offers of proof and questions of relevance.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.210 - Hearing—Order of hearing.
text:
A.

Except as otherwise provided in this section, in any hearing pursuant to this title,
the hearing must proceed as follows:

1.

The hearing officer shall call the hearing to order.

2.

The parties and their representatives shall be introduced for the record.

3.

The hearing officer shall consider any preliminary motions, offers of settlement,
stipulations or orders and shall address any administrative details regarding the
hearing.

4.

The hearing officer:

a.

Shall ask the parties if they want any witness excluded from the hearing.

b.

Shall instruct any witness who is excluded from the hearing not to discuss the case
during the course of the hearing.

c.

Shall allow the respondent to remain in the hearing.

d.

May, on its own motion, exclude any witness from the hearing.

5.

The city may present a brief opening statement of the charges, explaining the theory
of the case and what the evidence will show;

6.

The respondent or respondent's attorney may present a brief opening statement;

7.

The city will present evidence, subject to cross-examination by the respondent's counsel
and the hearing officer;

8.

The respondent or respondent's counsel may present evidence, subject to cross-examination
by the city and the hearing officer;

9.

The hearing officer may question a witness at any time during the hearing. If a witness
is questioned by the hearing officer, the party who called the witness may request
permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by the hearing
officer. When the party who called the witness has asked those questions, the other
party may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed
by the hearing officer.

10.

After the city and respondent have presented their cases, the hearing officer may
allow the city and respondent to call rebuttal witnesses. If the city or respondent,
or both, call one or more rebuttal witnesses, each rebuttal witness must be sworn
in and questioned in the same manner as other witnesses.

11.

Closing statements may be made at the conclusion of the evidence by both parties.
These statements may include summaries of the evidence and legal arguments. The city
will present its closing statement first, and then the respondent may present its
closing argument. If the respondent makes a closing statement, the city may make a
final closing argument.

12.

Either party may recommend specific disciplinary action to the hearing officer at
the appropriate time.

B.

The hearing officer may deviate from the order of the hearing set forth in subsection
(1) if the hearing officer:

1.

Upon a showing of good cause, deems it appropriate; or

2.

Deems it necessary to expedite or ensure the fairness of the hearing.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.211 - Record of the hearing.
text:
The hearing shall be reported and/or recorded by any means determined appropriate
by the hearing officer. If any party desires the hearing transcribed by a certified
court reporter, that party must make the necessary arrangements and bear the costs
thereof.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.220 - Burden of proof.
text:
The city has the burden of proof in any hearing pursuant to this title. The standard
of proof in such a hearing is substantial evidence.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.230 - Failure of respondent to appear at hearing.
text:
If the respondent fails to appear at a scheduled hearing, and a continuance has not
been scheduled or granted, the city may make an offer of proof that the absent respondent
was given sufficient legal notice of the hearing. Upon a determination by the hearing
officer that the respondent was given sufficient legal notice, the hearing officer
may proceed to consider and dispose of the case without the participation of the respondent
and may accept the allegations against the respondent in the charging document as
true, deem the violations proven and impose discipline.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.240 - Amendment—Filing of amended pleadings.
text:
The hearing officer may, in the hearing officer's discretion, before submission of
the case for decision, permit the filing of amended or supplemental pleadings and
shall notify all parties thereof, and provide a reasonable opportunity for objections
thereto.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.250 - Hearing security.
text:
At the request of either the hearing officer, city, or respondent, a city police officer
or marshal shall be present at the hearing to provide security and help maintain order.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.260 - Written decision of hearing officer.
text:
The hearing officer shall render a written decision within ten calendar days from
the last day of the hearing. The hearing officer is empowered to extend the time period
for rendering a decision up to 30 days when additional information is required for
the hearing officer to render a decision or due to the complexity of the issues presented.
The written decision shall contain findings of fact, conclusions of law, a determination
of the alleged violations presented and the disciplinary action to be imposed. Copies
of such order shall be served on the parties or their counsel either personally or
by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested. The decision shall take
effect upon service of the order and shall be a final decision.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.270 - Attorney's fees and costs incurred by city.
text:
A.

The hearing officer may order respondent to pay reasonable attorney's fees and costs
that are incurred by the city as part of its investigative, administrative and disciplinary
proceedings against the respondent if the hearing officer enters a final order in
which it finds that the respondent has violated any provision of this title.

B.

As used in this section, "costs" means:

1.

Costs of an investigation.

2.

Costs for photocopies, facsimiles, long distance telephone calls and postage and delivery.

3.

Fees for court reporters at the hearing.

4.

Fees for expert witnesses and other witnesses at the hearing.

5.

Fees for necessary interpreters at the hearing.

6.

Fees for service and delivery of process and subpoenas.

7.

Expenses for research, including, without limitation, reasonable and necessary expenses
for computerized services for legal research.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.06.280 - Aggrieved party—Petition for reconsideration.
text:
A.

Within ten days after service of an order of the hearing officer, any party aggrieved
may petition for reconsideration. Such petition shall not be granted except upon a
showing that:

1.

There is additional evidence that is material, unavailable at the time of the original
hearing, necessary and reasonably calculated to change the decision of the hearing
officer; or

2.

Granting the petition is necessary to correct a manifest error of law or fact; or

3.

Granting the petition is necessary to prevent manifest injustice.

Any petition based on the unavailability of evidence shall be supported by an affidavit
or declaration of the moving party or the moving party's counsel showing with particularity
the materiality and necessity of the additional evidence and the reason why it was
not introduced at the hearing.

B.

The petition shall be served upon the non-moving party and the hearing officer. The
hearing officer shall provide the non-moving party an opportunity to respond to the
petition either in writing or at a hearing scheduled by the hearing officer.

C.

After the granting of a petition, the hearing officer may modify his or her decision
and order. Any such modification must be made in writing within 30 days of the filing
of the petition for rehearing and must be served on the parties, either personally
or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested.

(Ord. No. 3302, § 2, 10-20-2015)

heading: Chapter 4.07 - ALTERNATIVE TO CRIMINAL PROSECUTION[6]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (6) ---

Editor's note—
Prior to the reenactment of chapter 4.07 by Ord. No. 3303, § 1, adopted October 20, 2015, Ord. No. 3132, § 1, adopted April 1, 2014, repealed the former chapter 4.07, §§ 4.07.010—4.07.030
in its entirety, which pertained to business impact consideration, and derived from
Ord. No. 1978, § 1, adopted in 2000.

heading: 4.07.010 - Generally.
text:
As an alternative to criminal prosecution for a violation of any provision of title 4, the city may impose a civil penalty in accordance with the provision of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.020 - Notice of violation—Required information.
text:
A.

A civil penalty under this chapter shall be imposed by the issuance of a notice of
violation by the city. The notice of violation must contain, at a minimum, the following
information:

1.

The name and address (if known) of the person or entity responsible for the violation;

2.

A brief description of the violation and a reference to the applicable ordinance or
code citation(s);

3.

The location, date and time of the violation;

4.

The name of the person issuing the notice of violation;

5.

The amount of the civil penalty; and

6.

Information advising of the manner and time for responding to the notice of violation.

B.

No error concerning, or omission of, any of the above-described information is grounds
for the dismissal of a proceeding relating to a notice of violation unless the person
requesting the dismissal demonstrates substantial prejudice from the error and/or
omission.

C.

Where the notice of violation data is entered into and stored in a computer or similar
device, any printout or other output readable by sight that accurately reflects such
data is an original notice of violation for purposes of a proceeding under this chapter.
Any such data entry that is moved or copied into another computer or similar device
is intended to constitute an additional or replacement of the record of the data by
the issuing officer or employee and is also an original notice of violation for purposes
of a proceeding under this chapter.

D.

Any notice of violation issued pursuant to this chapter shall constitute a declaration
which is subject to the penalty of perjury.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.030 - Notice of violation—Issuance.
text:
The notice of violation may be issued by any peace officer or by any authorized officer
or employee of the division.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.040 - Notice of violation—Filing.
text:
An original notice of violation, or a facsimile thereof, must be filed with and retained
by the business operations division. A notice of violation is prima facie evidence
of the facts which are alleged therein. The notice of violation must be served on
the person responsible for the violation or, in the case of an entity, an officer,
key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. A notice of violation
may be served on the person responsible for the violation either personally or by
registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, at the address on file with
the division.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.050 - Notice of violation—Response—Hearings.
text:
A.

The individual or licensee, referred to herein as the "person" per section 4.04.010, cited must respond to a notice of violation within the time prescribed by section
4.07.060 of this chapter in one of the following ways:

1.

Admit responsibility for the commission of the violation and liability by paying the
amount of the civil penalty; or

2.

Appeal the notice of violation, or civil penalty by submitting a written request for
an administrative hearing to the division. The request for hearing must contain the
following information:

a.

The name of the person on the notice of violation;

b.

The current address and contact telephone number of the person;

c.

The notice(s) of violation(s) which the person wishes to dispute at the hearing;

d.

The basis or facts supporting the appeal; and

e.

The requested relief.

B.

After receipt of a person's written request for a hearing, the division shall set
a hearing date and provide notice of the hearing to the person requesting it at least
14 days before the date of the hearing, unless a shorter time period is agreed to
in writing by the division and the individual. The notice shall state the date, time,
and location of the hearing, and shall include a short explanation of the hearing
process.

C.

The business operations manager of the department, or authorized designee (the "presiding
officer"), shall preside over hearings conducted pursuant to this chapter except under
the following circumstances:

1.

If the city attorney initiates a disciplinary action for suspension or revocation
of a business license, an appeal hearing under this chapter may be held in conjunction
with the disciplinary action hearing, presided over by a hearing officer appointed
pursuant to chapter 4.06;

2.

If the business operations manager determines that the circumstances so warrant, the
business operations manager may refer an appeal under this chapter to the city manager's
office. Upon receiving a referral, the city manager may appoint an assistant city
manager or the director (or designee) of another city department as the presiding
officer for the referred appeal hearing.

D.

The presiding officer shall conduct the hearing, direct the order of the proceedings,
and hear all evidence presented relevant to the subject notice of violation and appeal.
The hearing shall be conducted informally and shall not be constrained by evidentiary
or procedural rules applicable to public hearings or judicial proceedings. The hearing
shall provide an opportunity for the parties to present witness statements or testimony
and other evidence regarding the subject notice of violation for the purpose of dispensing
a fair and speedy resolution. The presiding officer may question witnesses, allow
rebuttal testimony, limit the time of the hearing to a reasonable length, limit the
presentation of immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence, and record the hearing.

E.

If the person requesting a hearing fails to appear at the hearing without having first
sought and obtained a continuance of the hearing, the presiding officer may enter
a decision upholding the violation and the full amount of the civil penalty scheduled
to be reviewed. The burden of proving any defense shall be upon the person raising
such defense.

F.

Upon the conclusion of the hearing, the presiding officer shall consider all evidence
presented and shall issue a decision to uphold, reverse, or modify the disputed violation
and/or citation. Written notice of the decision shall be issued no later than 30 days
following the conclusion of the hearing. The decision shall clearly state one of the
following:

1.

That the notice of violation is upheld, including a short statement of findings explaining
the basis for the decision, and providing a deadline and any conditions for the payment
of any civil penalty;

2.

That the notice of violation is reversed, including a short statement of findings
explaining the basis for the decision; or

3.

That the notice of violation and/or penalties are modified, including a short statement
of findings explaining the basis for the decision, and providing a deadline and any
conditions for any modified compliance obligations and payments of any civil penalty.

G.

Any decision by the presiding officer pursuant to this chapter shall be a final determination.

H.

The city attorney may file a petition in a court of competent jurisdiction, including
the Henderson municipal court for the entry of a civil judgment against the person
in an amount equal to that stated in the written decision if the city attorney determines
this action to be necessary to enforce the decision. Service of such petition on the
defendant must be made by certified mail, return receipt requested, restricted delivery,
addressed to the defendant at the defendant's last known address, or in any other
manner which is authorized by law. An affidavit or declaration of mailing, a signed,
returned receipt, or other evidence of service of the civil judgment shall be filed
upon such service of the petition.

(Ord. No. 3936, § 1, 1-3-2022; Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.060 - Notice of violation—Response period.
text:
A.

A response to a notice of violation, as provided in section 4.07.050, must be made within 30 calendar days after the date on which the notice of violation
is served. If no response is received during such 30-day period, an additional civil
penalty which is equal to the amount of the original civil fine may be assessed.

B.

If a person does not respond to a notice of violation within the 30-day response period,
the director, or an authorized designee, shall send a notice of delinquency by mail
to the person responsible for the violation or, in the case of an entity, an officer,
key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity at the address
on file with the division.

C.

The notice of delinquency shall contain the original date of the violation, the amount
of the civil fine and the amount of any late penalty which is associated therewith.
The person responsible for the violation or, in the case of an entity, an officer,
key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity has 15 calendar
days after the date of the notice of delinquency in which to respond to the division.
If no response is made to the notice of delinquency within such additional 15-day
period, an additional civil penalty may be assessed equal to the original civil penalty
imposed and the matter may be referred to the city attorney's office to initiate proceedings
to suspend and/or revoke the business license or permit.

D.

If a person fails to respond to a notice of violation or a notice of delinquency in
accordance with this chapter, the city is entitled to collect the amount of any fines
and penalties by means of any remedy available under applicable law, including without
limitation referring the matter to a collection agency and initiating proceedings
to suspend and/or revoke the person's business license or permit.

E.

If a person fails to respond to the notice of violation or a notice of delinquency
and the violation continues to exist, said action shall be considered a public nuisance
as described in section 4.07.080 and the city may seek injunctive relief pursuant to section 1.05.040.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.070 - Collection fees.
text:
In addition to the civil penalties assessed pursuant to this chapter, the person responsible
for any violation shall be liable for an additional collection fee where the collection
of the penalties provided for herein is referred for collection. The amount of such
fee shall be 25 percent of the outstanding indebtedness or $250.00, whichever is less.
The amount of any such collection fee shall accrue and become due and payable at the
time the indebtedness is referred for collection to the collection agency, and that
amount may be added by the collection agency to the amount sought to be collected.
Any judgment or amended judgment entered under this chapter may include the amount
of the collection fee authorized herein.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.07.080 - Public nuisance abatement.
text:
Any continuous violation of title 4 is a threat to the public health, safety, and morals and constitutes a public nuisance
to the general public. In addition to any civil penalties provided herein, the city
may abate the nuisance or apply for other equitable relief pursuant to HMC 1.05.040.

(Ord. No. 3303, § 1, 10-20-2015)

heading: Chapter 4.08 - AUCTIONS AND AUCTIONEERS[7]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (7) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3242, § 1, adopted January 6, 2015, amended chapter 4.08 in its entirety to read as herein
set out. Formerly, chapter 4.08, §§ 4.08.010—4.08.210 pertained to similar subject
matter, and derived from Ord. No. 838, § 2, adopted in 1982, and Ord. No. 1301, §
6, adopted in 1992.

heading: 4.08.010 - Definitions.
text:
For the purpose of this chapter, the following words and terms, when used in this
chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, unless the context
clearly indicates otherwise:

Auction sale. The term "auction sale" shall mean a sale of property by public outcry to the highest
bidder.

Auctioneer. The term "auctioneer" shall mean any person who shall, by public outcry, sell or
offer to sell to the highest bidder at public offering, when bids are called for,
any goods, wares, merchandise, livestock, vehicles, fruits, stocks, bonds and other
securities, or any personal property of whatever nature, or any real estate or interest
therein, at any store, stand or other place within the city where any and all persons
who choose so to do are permitted to attend and offer bids, or any person who shall
advertise or in any other manner hold himself out as an auctioneer for public patronage,
or receive fees or compensation for service as such.

Jewelry. The term "jewelry" shall mean any goods, ware and merchandise customarily kept in
retail jewelry stores for sale, including, but not limited to, precious and semiprecious
stones and imitations thereof, whether sold or offered for sale with or without settings,
rings, bracelets, articles made in whole or in part of gold, silver, platinum or other
precious or semiprecious metal whether solid, plated or overlaid.

Property. The term "property" shall mean real property and personal property of whatever nature.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.020 - License required—Exceptions.
text:
A.

An auctioneer license is a privileged license. It shall be unlawful for any person
or firm to act as an auctioneer or to hold or carry on any auction within the city
without first obtaining a license as herein required and paying the license fee as
set forth in chapter 4.05.

B.

No license shall be required of any individual who furnishes proof of holding a valid
license as an auctioneer in any political subdivision or entity of Clark County, Nevada.
Each such auctioneer shall be required to obtain a permit according to section 4.08.030 prior to each auction sale.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.030 - Permit required.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to advertise for disposal, offer for sale, dispose
of, sell, cause or permit to be advertised for disposal, offered for sale, disposed
of or sold at public auction within the city, or in any manner carry on or conduct,
or cause or permit to be carried on or conducted, within the city a public auction
of any property, whether the same shall be his own property or the property of others,
without first complying with the provisions of this chapter and obtaining a permit
to do so as herein required.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.040 - Investigation fees—Required—Fees charged.
text:
Any person applying for an auctioneer license is required to submit to the city an
investigation fee as set forth in chapter 4.03, for each person required to be investigated.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.050 - License—Application.
text:
All applications for licenses required by section 4.08.020 shall be filed by the person(s) who as auctioneer(s) will carry on or conduct any
auction sale and shall be on forms as provided by the division. All applications shall
set forth at least the following information:

A.

Name and address of the applicant.

B.

Whether applicant is the holder of a valid license as an auctioneer in any jurisdiction
in the State of Nevada.

C.

Whether applicant has ever made an application for an auctioneer's license and has
been refused same.

D.

Whether applicant has ever been convicted of a felony.

E.

Any other information as needed by the division to determine the license suitability
of the applicant.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.060 - Permit—Application—Conditions.
text:
All applications for permits required by section 4.08.030 shall be filed with the division by the person(s) who, as auctioneer(s), will carry
on or conduct any auction sale. Such application shall be submitted not less than
20 nor more than 40 calendar days before the date of commencement of any auction sale.
Applications shall be on forms as provided by the division. No application for a permit
shall be acted on until the applicant has complied with section 4.08.020. All applications shall set forth at least the following information:

A.

Name and address of the applicant.

B.

Whether applicant is the holder of a valid and subsisting license as an auctioneer
in any jurisdiction in the State of Nevada.

C.

The location of the place where the auction sale will be conducted.

D.

The length of time for which the permit is desired and the date when the applicant
desires to commence such auction.

E.

The name and address of the owner of the property proposed to be sold at such auction.

F.

A list of all items to be auctioned, including a description and quantities of each
item so listed.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.070 - Permit—Exception.
text:
No permit will be required for any auction sale carried on or conducted in the city
by an auctioneer licensed pursuant to section 4.08.020 and whose principal place of business is located within the city limits when the
auction is conducted at the licensed business establishment. Auctions held within
the city but away from the licensed premises are subject to the permit requirements
set forth in section 4.08.030.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.080 - Permit—Fee.
text:
A fee of $50.00 shall be paid for each permit required by section 4.08.030. Such fee shall be paid at the time of filing of application.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.090 - Bond required.
text:
As a condition precedent to the issuance or renewal of an auctioneer's license, the
applicant shall file a two-year non-revocable surety bond with the division in the
sum of $20,000.00 from a company authorized to do business in the State as a surety.
Such bond must be conditioned to be paid to the city or to any person who suffers
any damage by reason of any fraud, dishonesty, misstatement, misrepresentation, deceit,
unlawful acts or omissions, or violation of the provisions of this Code by the licensee,
his agents and employees. Such bond shall not be void upon the first recovery, but
may be sued and recovered upon from time to time by any person aggrieved, in his own
name, until the whole penalty is exhausted.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.100 - Restriction to private places.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any auctioneer or other person to offer for sale or sell
at public auction or public outcry any property upon any street or public place in
the city.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.110 - Consignment and auction records.
text:
Each licensee or permittee shall keep a permanent record of all items taken for sale
or consignment for sale and shall contain the following information:

A.

An accurate description of each item including any model number, style, and serial
number(s);

B.

The name, age, sex, residence address (not a post office box), and telephone number
of the person consigning said items;

C.

Each licensee or permittee shall keep a permanent record of all sales, the name and
address of the purchaser, the amount paid, and the date of each sale. Each permanent
record, as herein described, shall be open at all times for inspection by the police
department and the division.

D.

Any other information as the division may deem necessary.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.120 - No private sale during auction.
text:
No property shall be sold at private sale at the place for which a permit has been
granted for the conduct of an auction sale during the progress of such auction or
on any day when such property is advertised for sale at public auction, other than
by public outcry and to the highest bidder.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.130 - Conditions for auction sale.
text:
All auction sales shall be conducted as follows:

A.

Each day before the commencement of the auction, the licensee or permittee shall announce
the terms of the sale.

B.

The licensee or permittee, at each time a bid is announced or accepted, shall give
some description of the person making the bid, and also point out or designate the
location of the bidder on the premises.

C.

No licensee or permittee, his agents, employees, or the owner, or other person on
his behalf, shall make any false or misleading statement concerning the ownership
kind, character, quality, condition, make, size, price, or other fact pertaining to
any article sold or offered for sale.

D.

No licensee or permittee, his employee, or the owner, or other person on his behalf,
shall act as a by-bidder, or what is commonly known as a "capper" or "booster," or
make or accept any false or misleading bid, or falsely pretend to buy or sell any
article, or conspire with any person to make a false or fictitious bid; and no licensee
or permittee, his employee, or the owner of the articles, or other person acting on
his behalf, shall bid or purchase at such sale, unless, at the time such bid is made,
the permittee shall announce, in such tone and manner as to be plainly heard and understood
in all parts of the room in which the sale is being conducted, that such bid is for
the benefit of the permittee, his employee or owner, as the case may be.

E.

Each article offered for sale shall be sold as offered, if a bid be made by more than
one bona fide bidder, before another article is offered for sale, and without any
unreasonable delay. There shall be no reserved price on any article unless, at the
time the article is offered for sale, the licensee or permittee shall announce the
reserved price in such tone and manner as to be plainly heard and understood in all
parts of the room in which the sale is being conducted. If any article is offered
for sale and two or more bids are made thereon, and such article is afterwards withdrawn
from sale for the reason that the highest bidder did not equal the reserved price
as announced, there shall not be the same or another article of the same kind or class
offered for sale until four other sales have been made, or for one hour, whichever
is the longer time.

F.

No free drawing shall be conducted, nor gifts be given, nor any form of entertainment
be given for the encouragement of attendance at such sale, or for any other purpose.

G.

Upon request of any person who has bid upon an article offered for sale, the licensee
or permittee shall allow such bidder a reasonable opportunity to examine such article,
and such bidder may thereafter withdraw his bid at any time before the licensee or
permittee declares the article sold.

H.

The licensee or permittee shall allow any police officer, the director or his designee,
during regular business hours, to examine any article held for sale by auction or
offered for sale, at any time before such article is delivered to the purchaser.

I.

No person other than the licensee or permittee shall cry the sale of any article at
said auction sale.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.140 - Licensee and permittee responsible for the acts of employees.
text:
Every licensee and permittee shall be responsible for the acts of his employees and
agents committed during the course and scope of employment. Every licensee shall accordingly
use adequate care in the selection of his employees and agents. In any license suspension,
limitation or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual
knowledge of the events complained of shall be no defense and every licensee accepts
his license subject to said condition.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.150 - Jewelry—Special conditions.
text:
No licensee or permittee shall make at any time prior to or during any auction sale
any statement in regards to the quality, content, construction, plating, size or weight
of any precious or semiprecious stones or imitations thereof, type of metal, the grade
of fineness thereof, of any item of jewelry, as herein defined, unless the licensee
or permittee has a notarized authentication of such claim by a jeweler or appraiser
licensed to do business in any political subdivision or entity located in Clark County,
Nevada.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: 4.08.160 - Exempted sales—Conditions.
text:
The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to auctions of the following:

A.

Property owned by, or in the lawful possession, custody or control of banks, trust
companies, trustees in bankruptcy, assignees for the benefit of creditors, executors
and administrators, selling or disposing of such property under the laws of the United
States or the State of Nevada;

B.

Property sold at judicial sales;

C.

Unclaimed or undelivered property held by common carriers or public warehousemen,
selling or disposing of the same for freight or storage charges;

D.

Property being sold solely for charitable or benevolent purposes or for any church,
fair, festival or bazaar; and

E.

Property held by licensed pawnbrokers, selling or disposing of the same as unredeemed
pledges in the manner provided by NRS Chapter 646 and HMC chapter 4.64.

(Ord. No. 3242, § 1, 1-6-2015)

heading: Chapter 4.12 - DOOR-TO-DOOR SOLICITORS, PEDDLERS AND CANVASSERS[8]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (8) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3067, § 1, adopted September 17, 2013, amended chapter 4.12 in its entirety to read as
herein set out. Formerly, chapter 4.12, §§ 4.12.010—4.12.180 pertained to similar
subject matter, and derived from Ord. No. 2382, § 1, adopted in 2005, and Ord. No.
2855, § 1, adopted June 1, 2010.

heading: 4.12.010 - Definitions.
text:
The following words, terms, and phrases, and their derivations, when used in this
chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the
context clearly indicates a different meaning:

A.

Canvasser means any natural person who is not in the business of selling goods and who makes
or attempts to make personal contact with a resident at his residence, without prior
specific invitation or appointment from the resident, for the primary purpose of (1)
distributing or attempting to distribute a handbill or flyer advertising a noncommercial
item, cause, event or service or (2) making or attempting to make noncommercial surveys
for research purposes, analysis, opinion polls and any similar work.

B.

Charitable purpose is defined to mean any benevolent, philanthropic, patriotic, religious or eleemosynary
group, partnership, association or corporation which solicits and collects funds for
charitable purposes and is classified in one of the categories defined in Section
501 of the United States Internal Revenue Code as being exempt from payment of federal
income tax as evidenced by the organization's 501 registration number or is duly organized
pursuant to Nevada Revised Statutes Chapters 81, 82, 84 or 86.

C.

Peddler means any natural person other than a mobile food vendor who goes upon the premises
of any private residence in the city, not having been invited by the resident or occupant
thereof, carrying or transporting goods, wares, merchandise or personal property of
any nature and offering or attempting to offer the same for sale. "Peddler" does not
include a natural person who distributes handbills or flyers for a commercial purpose,
advertising an event, activity, good, or service that is offered to a resident for
purchase at a location away from his residence or at a time different from the time
of visit.

D.

Solicitor means any natural person other than a mobile food vendor who goes upon the premises
of any private residence in the city, not having been invited by the resident or occupant
thereof, for the primary purpose of taking or attempting to take orders for the sale
of goods, merchandise, wares or other personal property of any nature for future delivery,
or for services to be performed in the future. "Solicitor" includes any natural person
who distributes a handbill or flyer advertising a commercial event, good, or service.
This definition also includes any natural person who, without invitation, goes upon
private residential property for the primary purpose of requesting a donation for
political, charitable, religious purposes or other noncommercial purpose, even if
incidental to such purpose the solicitor offers or provides goods or services.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.020 - License requirements.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any natural person 18 years of age or older to engage in
any peddling or solicitation activities within the city without first obtaining a
license issued by the division.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.030 - License fee.
text:
At the time the application is filed, the applicant shall pay a license fee of $25.00.
The application fee in section 4.04.065 shall not be required.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.040 - License application.
text:
Every natural person required to obtain a license pursuant to section 4.12.020 shall, in person, file with the director an application in writing on a form to be
furnished by the division, which shall provide the following information:

A.

Proof of age, address and identification of the applicant;

B.

A brief description of the business or activity to be conducted;

C.

If employed, contracted, or otherwise engaged by another person to engage in the activities
regulated in this chapter, the name, address and telephone number of such person;

D.

A statement as to whether or not the applicant has been convicted of a crime within
the past ten years, and, if so, the nature of the offense or violation, the penalty
or punishment imposed, and the date when and place where such conviction occurred;

E.

Proof of possession of any license which, under federal, state or local laws or regulations,
the applicant is required to have in order to conduct the proposed business or activity,
or which, under any such law or regulation, would exempt the applicant from the licensing
requirements of this chapter; and

F.

One passport photograph of the applicant's face which shall have been taken within
12 months immediately prior to the date of filing of the application. The photograph
shall measure approximately two inches by two inches and be on a white background.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.050 - Application review and license issuance.
text:
A.

Unless there is, pursuant to section 4.12.060, a reason to deny the license, the director shall approve the license.

B.

The license shall show the name and address of the licensee and the licensee's employer,
if applicable, and the date of issuance.

C.

Licenses shall be issued promptly, but in all cases within three business days of
personal hand-delivery of the application, unless the application is not complete
or the license is denied for any of the reasons set forth in section 4.12.060. Failure to approve or deny the license within the time periods referenced in this
chapter shall result in the license being granted.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.060 - Denial of license.
text:
A.

Upon the director's review of the application, the director shall refuse to issue
a license to the applicant for any of the following reasons:

1.

The applicant has been convicted of any felony, gross misdemeanor, or a misdemeanor
involving a sex offense, trafficking in controlled substances, or any violent act
against a person or property, such conviction having being entered within the ten
years preceding the date of application;

2.

The applicant is a person against whom a judgment based upon, or conviction for, fraud,
deceit or misrepresentation has been entered within the ten years immediately preceding
the date of application.

B.

The license application may also be denied for good cause as set forth in subsection
4.04.150(A).

C.

The director's disapproval and the reasons for disapproval shall be noted on the application,
and the applicant shall be notified that his application is disapproved and that no
license will be issued. Notice shall be delivered personally or mailed to the applicant
at the address shown on the application form, or at the applicant's last known address.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.070 - License exhibition.
text:
Every natural person required to obtain a license under the provisions of this chapter
shall keep the license in his possession at all times while the licensee is soliciting
or peddling in the city, and shall allow inspection of the license upon request by
any prospective customer, business license officer in the division or police officer.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.080 - Transfer prohibited.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any person other than the licensee to use any license issued
under the provisions of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.090 - Licensee responsible for acts of employees and agents.
text:
Any person or entity who employs, contracts, or otherwise engages another to conduct
soliciting, peddling, or canvassing activities, is responsible for the acts or omissions
of his employees or agents committed during the course of employment or performance
of activities governed by this chapter. In any suspension, limitation, or revocation
proceeding, the fact that the distributing service or person who employed, contracted,
or engaged another did not have actual knowledge of the violation shall be no defense.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.100 - Entry upon posted premises unlawful.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any natural person, while canvassing, peddling or soliciting,
to enter upon any residential premises or to knock on the door, window or any other
part of the residential structure, or ring the bell of any residential premises, or
to do any other act calculated to attract the attention of anyone inside of the premises,
where the owner, resident, occupant or person legally in charge of the premises has
posted, at the entry, or any of the points of ingress to the premises, a sign with
visible and legible letters at least three-fourths of an inch in height bearing the
words "No Trespassers," "No Canvassers," "No Peddlers," "No Solicitors," or words
of similar import. A sign containing any of these or similar phrases is deemed to
prohibit all activities governed by this chapter. This regulation shall apply to all
groups of structures or complexes such as apartments, condominiums or private gated
communities, which have posted such a sign or signs with letters at least one and
one-half inches in height at the entrance(s) or other point(s) of ingress regardless
of whether any individual particular residence is posted.

This section shall not apply, however, when the solicitor, peddler or canvasser has,
despite the signage, been specifically invited by the owner, resident, occupant or
person legally in charge of the premises.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.110 - Hours of solicitation.
text:
No person, while conducting the activities of a canvasser, peddler or solicitor, shall
enter upon any private property, knock on doors, ring any bells, or otherwise disturb
persons in their residences between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.120 - Posting on public ways, structures, vehicles, vacant premises.
text:
No peddler, solicitor or canvasser shall post or cause any other person to post any
handbill, flyer, or any other similar poster, paper or device calculated to attract
the attention of the public or any member thereof, on any public property or on anything
situated on public property, or upon premises which are vacant.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.130 - Handbills and flyers must be securely fastened without causing damage.
text:
A handbill, flyer, or similar item left at a residence must be placed on the doorknob
or similar place with a rubber band or similar means so as to secure it as far as
practicable from being blown away. No handbill, flyer or similar item shall be left
at, or attached to, any property in a manner that causes damage to such property.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.140 - License denial or revocation.
text:
Any license issued under this chapter may be revoked, limited or suspended by the
director, for any of the reasons set forth in sections 4.12.060 or 4.04.150 and may be subject to sections 4.06.040 et seq.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: 4.12.150 - Appeals—Judicial review.
text:
Appeal rights are the same as those set forth in section 4.04.210. Procedures for judicial review of final decisions are the same as those set forth
in section 4.06.300.

(Ord. No. 3067, § 1, 9-17-2013)

heading: Chapter 4.18 - ALARM SYSTEMS
text: Sections:

heading: 4.18.010 - Definitions.
text:
Whenever used in this chapter, the words and terms shall have the meaning ascribed
to them pursuant to title 4, unless a different meaning clearly appears in the definitions or context:

Activated alarm system means an alarm system which has been set, or turned on; in which condition it will
emit a noise, turn on lights, dial a telephone or send a signal to a monitoring station,
or any other means of signaling, when the alarm has been activated.

Alarm condition means that a situation exists, determined by an alarm monitoring business, or other
means, which is used to summon emergency response personnel.

Alarm system means any mechanism, equipment or device which is designed to detect an unauthorized
entry into any building or onto any property, or to direct attention to a crime in
progress, or to signal an emergency of any kind, and to signal the above occurrence
either by a local or audible alarm or by a silent or remote alarm. Alarm systems shall
not include alarms installed in motor vehicles.

Alarm systems business means any person engaging in the business of planning, installing, servicing, maintaining,
repairing or replacing, or monitoring alarm systems in the city. "Alarm systems business"
shall also mean any person acting as a contractor or subcontractor for or with an
alarm systems business as described.

Applicant means any person who has requested, or is about to request, licensing as an alarm
systems business, or any person who has requested, or is about to request, a building
permit to install an alarm system at a particular location in the city.

Building director means the director of the building department of the city or his designee.

Emergency response personnel means, but is not limited to, the police and fire departments and ambulance services.

Employee means a person who is employed by an alarm systems business and who plans, sells,
installs, services, maintains, repairs, monitors or replaces alarm systems in the
city. (See [section] 4.18.190.)

False alarm means an actual alarm signal transmitted in the absence of an alarm condition which
results in emergency response personnel being dispatched to the location of the alarm.

Local or audible alarm means an alarm, which, when activated, emits a loud noise at or near the protected
area without notifying an alarm monitoring station.

Manually activated alarm means an alarm system which is activated manually, and which transmits a signal to
an alarm monitoring station indicating an emergency or a crime in progress.

Responder means a private patrol business, licensed in accordance with the provisions of NRS
and the city, or the owner of the home, business, structure or facility experiencing
an alarm condition.

User means a person, who owns, or is in control of the premises protected or intended
to be protected by an alarm system.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

heading: 4.18.020 - Legislative intent.
text:
As the city's population has grown, more residential and commercial property owners
are turning to privately monitored security alarm systems to provide additional protection
for their properties. Commensurate with the growth in the number of private alarm
systems installed within the City of Henderson there has been a corresponding increase
in the number of false alarm reports received by the police department. In response
to the proliferation of alarm systems and the city council's concern for the public's
best interest from a safety standpoint as it relates to the increased incidents of
false alarms, it is necessary that rules and regulations be adopted to control the
licensing and operation of alarm systems businesses and the establishment of a process
whereby the city can recoup the expenses incurred in responding to the ever increasing
number of false alarms.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

heading: 4.18.030 - Regulation.
text:
All persons, except an alarm user as defined in this chapter, shall be licensed and
subject to regulation, and the license may be suspended, limited, or revoked for violation
of the provisions of this chapter, the laws of the State of Nevada, other ordinances
of the city, or for any other cause deemed sufficient by the council in the exercise
of its sole discretion. In conformity with the policy of this chapter, the following
persons are declared not to be qualified to hold a license under the provisions of
this chapter:

(1)

A person who has been convicted of a crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving
or possessing stolen property, any narcotics violation whatsoever or any sex offense;

(2)

A person whose license, whether issued under the provisions of this chapter, or those
ordinances or statutes of any other agency lawfully engaged in the licensing or regulation
of alarm systems businesses, has been revoked for cause;

(3)

A person who, at the time of renewal of any license issued under this chapter, would
not be eligible for such license upon a first application;

(4)

A partnership, limited partnership or association, unless all of the members of such
partnership, limited partnership or association are qualified to obtain a license;

(5)

A corporation, unless it is incorporated in the State of Nevada, or unless it is a
foreign corporation which is qualified under Nevada law to transact business in Nevada;

(6)

A corporation, if an officer or director thereof would not be eligible to receive
a license for any reason which would disqualify an individual applicant.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

heading: 4.18.040 - Unlawful to operate without license.
text:
It is unlawful for any person to conduct any alarm systems business as described in
this chapter without first having obtained a license therefor.

(Ord. 1343, § 1 (part), 1992)

heading: 4.18.050 - License—Application—Contents—General.
text:
Whenever a person desires to conduct any alarm systems business in the city, such
person shall make application in writing to the division to obtain a license therefor;
and, such application shall contain the following:

(a)

The name and residence address of the applicant; and

(b)

The classification of the license sought, the business address for which the license
is sought where the operation will be conducted; and

(c)
