heading: 4.68.010 - Definitions.
text:
The following definitions are in addition to the definitions set forth in chapter 4.04 of this title. Unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning, the definitions
below shall govern the construction, meaning, and application of words and phrases
used in this chapter:

Antique means a unique object of personal property that is not less than 60 years old and
has special value primarily because of its age, or as otherwise defined by NRS Chapter
647.

Collectible means an object of personal property that has special value primarily because of
its unique characteristics and the high level of demand for the object.

Drop-off center means a collection site where recyclable materials may be taken by persons and deposited
into designated containers.

Jewelry means merchandise customarily kept in retail (including estates) jewelry stores for
sale, including, but not limited to, precious and semiprecious stones; watches; clocks;
rings; bracelets; articles made in whole or in part of gold, silver, platinum or other
precious or semiprecious metal and, in addition thereto, shall also include art objects.

Net assets means the book value of current assets less applicable liabilities, represented by
a capital investment unencumbered by a lien or other encumbrance, and subject to a
claim by a general creditor. Such capital investment must be represented by common
or preferred shares and capital or earned surplus, if the business is a corporation;
or a substantial equivalent of items, as determined by generally accepted accounting
principles, if the business is not a corporation.

New merchandise means all commodities which merchants normally sell, whether at wholesale or retail,
and which have never entered into common market place for sale or distribution to
a consumer.

Recyclable materials or recyclables has the same meaning as that term is defined in the health department regulations
governing recycling centers, as amended.

Recycling center has the same meaning as that term is defined in the health department regulations
governing recycling centers, as amended.

Scrap metal means:

1.

Nonferrous metals, scrap iron, stainless steel or other material or equipment which
consists in whole or in part of metal and which is used in construction, agricultural
operations, electrical power generation, transmission or distribution, cable, broadband
or telecommunications transmission, railroad equipment, oil well rigs or any lights
maintained by the state or a local government, including, without limitation, street
lights, traffic-control devices park lights, or ball park lights; and

2.

Catalytic converters.

3.

The term does not include waste generated by a household, aluminum beverage containers,
used construction scrap iron or materials consisting of a metal product in its original
manufactured form which contains not more than 20 percent by weight nonferrous metal.

Scrap metal processor means any person who:

1.

Engages in the business of purchasing, trading, bartering or otherwise receiving scrap
metal; or

2.

Uses machinery and equipment for processing and manufacturing iron, steel or nonferrous
scrap into prepared grades, and whose principal product is scrap iron, scrap steel
or nonferrous metallic scrap, not including precious metals, for sale for remelting
purposes.

Secondhand dealer means any person having a place of business in the city for purchasing, trading or
dealing in any secondhand personal property. Establishments conducting the business
of recyclables, or of a drop-off center, are included in this definition.

Secondhand dealer, Category A, means:

1.

A person whose principal business practices and transactions are primarily in new
merchandise, with used, or secondhand, merchandise constituting a maximum of 30 percent
of the total gross revenues from the business activities.

2.

This category of secondhand dealer license includes license classifications I or II,
as set forth in section 4.68.025.

Secondhand dealer, Category B, means:

1.

A person whose principal business practices and transactions are primarily in used
or secondhand merchandise.

2.

This category of secondhand dealer license includes license classifications I, II,
and III, as set forth in section 4.68.025.

Secondhand dealer, Category C, means a person whose business practices and transactions are in furs, currency or
stamps.

Secondhand dealer, Category D, means:

1.

A person whose business practices and transactions are limited to those set forth
in category C and jewelry; and maintaining net assets of at least $250,000.00 that
are used or readily available for use in the business of the licensed location.

2.

If the director cannot verify that an applicant meets the net assets requirement of
this section, the director may require the applicant to submit a finding, including
a current balance sheet, by an independent certified public accountant that the accountant
has reviewed the applicant's books and records, and the applicant meets the net assets
requirement.

3.

This category of secondhand dealer license is included in secondhand dealer, class
II.

4.

With the exception of a license issued for a change of ownership for a business holding
a valid secondhand dealer, category D license issued on or before November 29, 2011,
no new secondhand dealer, category D licenses will be issued.

5.

Any valid, existing category D license issued on or before November 29, 2011, shall
be deemed nonconforming and may continue to operate so long as it is in compliance
with the provisions of this title.

6.

Any change of ownership relating to a valid, existing category D license must be approved
by council in order for the establishment to continue to operate as a nonconforming
business.

7.

A change of location of a business holding a valid, existing category D license approved
pursuant to section 4.68.175 shall continue to be deemed a nonconforming business.

Secondhand dealer, Category E, means a recycling center permitted to operate by the health department.

1.

This category excludes scrap metal processors.

2.

Any valid, existing category E license issued to a secondhand dealer that was engaged
in the business of scrap metal processing as of January 1, 2018, shall be deemed nonconforming.
Such a nonconforming license may continue to operate so long as it is in compliance
with the provisions of this title, including the scrap metal processor provisions
set forth in this chapter, without obtaining a separate category F license.

Secondhand dealer, Category F, means a scrap metal processor permitted to operate by the health department.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.020 - Statement of legislative intent—Regulation.
text:
It is found and declared that the public health, safety, morals and welfare of the
inhabitants of the city require the regulation and control of persons engaged in the
secondhand dealer business, or in the operation of secondhand shops. All secondhand
dealers, as defined in this chapter, shall be licensed and regulated so as to protect
the public health, safety, morals, good order and general welfare of the inhabitants
of the city and to safeguard the public. It is further found and declared that the
right to obtain such license is a privilege and that the operation of a secondhand
dealer business, when authorized by such license, is a privileged business subject
to regulations, and that the license may be revoked for violation of the conditions
of this chapter. In conformity with the policy of this chapter, the following persons
are declared not qualified to hold a license under the provisions of this chapter:

A.

A person who has been convicted of a crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving
or possessing stolen property, any controlled substance violation whatsoever, or any
sex offense;

B.

A person whose license, issued pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, or those
ordinances or statutes of any other agency lawfully engaged in the licensing or regulation
of secondhand dealer businesses, has been revoked for cause;

C.

A person who, at the time of renewal of any license issued under this chapter, would
not be eligible for such license upon a first application;

D.

A partnership, limited partnership or association, unless all of the members of such
partnership, limited partnership or association are qualified to obtain a license;

E.

A corporation, unless it is incorporated in the State of Nevada, or unless it is a
foreign corporation which is qualified under Nevada law to transact business in Nevada;

F.

A corporation or limited liability corporation, if an officer or director thereof
would not be eligible to receive a license for any reason which would disqualify an
individual applicant.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.025 - Secondhand dealer classifications.
text:
Classifications include the following:

A.

Secondhand dealer, Class I, which includes all secondhand dealers who handle, or deal
in secondhand motor vehicles or trailers for sale or for the purpose of dismantling,
wrecking, disassembling and selling the dismantled, wrecked or disassembled parts
or accessories; and, secondhand motor vehicles or trailers, or parts and accessories
thereof; and, secondhand dealers who dismantle, wreck, or disassemble motor vehicles
or trailers, and who possess the appropriate State of Nevada, Department of Motor
Vehicles dealers license this class also includes ATV's, boats and dirt bikes.

B.

Secondhand dealer, Class II, which includes all secondhand dealers who handle, or
deal in one or more of, but not limited to, the following: metals, scrap metals, rags,
paper, furs, furniture, fixtures, household goods, radios, televisions, office supplies
and equipment, pictures, paintings, watches, gold, silver and other precious metals,
diamonds and other precious stones, recyclables, and dealers who smelt gold or wrought
gold, or other wrought metals. The business of consignment may also be included in
this classification based on the nature of the goods being placed on consignment with
the establishment.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.030 - License required.
text:
It is unlawful for any person to operate, conduct, carry on, or maintain any secondhand
dealer business as described in this chapter within the city without first obtaining
and thereafter maintaining the license herein required and paying the license fee
as set forth in chapter 4.05.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.035 - License exemptions.
text:
A.

This chapter does not apply to the following persons licensed pursuant to chapter 4.05 or chapter 4.64 as specified elsewhere in this title:

1.

Pawnbrokers licensed pursuant to chapter 4.64;

2.

Dealers in antiques;

3.

Dealers in used books and/or periodicals;

4.

Dealers in coins which are not a part of jewelry;

5.

Dealers in collectibles; or

6.

Dealers in used firearms or any antique parts, accessories or other equipment relating
to those firearms if:

a.

The person engages in that business at a show that:

i.

Is held at:

1.

A convention facility which is owned or operated by and located on the premises of
a resort hotel; or

2.

A recreational facility which is owned or operated by a county fair and recreation
board; and

ii.

Is conducted for not more than seven days during any six-month period; and

b.

The person has been issued a license as a manufacturer, importer, dealer or collector
pursuant to the provisions of 18 U.S.C. § 923;

B.

A business licensed pursuant to this title may take in used items on trade for store
credit or for the purchase of store merchandise without the requirement to obtain
a secondhand dealers license.

C.

Nonprofit organizations recognized as such by the Internal Revenue Code of the United
States which are registered pursuant to chapter 4.04.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.040 - Limit on number of secondhand dealer licenses.
text:
There shall be allowed one category B, class II license for each 20,000 population
in the city as determined and reported by the State of Nevada, Department of Taxation,
pursuant to the provisions of NRS 360.283, and as certified by the governor, pursuant
to the provisions of NRS 360.285.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.050 - Land use—Compliance with title 19.
text:
Every secondhand dealer licensed in the city must comply with the provisions of title
19 of this Code.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.070 - License—Application—General.
text:
Whenever a person desires to conduct any secondhand dealer business in the city, or
engage in the business thereof, such person shall make application in writing to the
division to obtain a license therefor.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.080 - Special provisions of secondhand dealer license.
text:
A.

All applicants for a secondhand dealer, category A, license shall, in addition to
the application for a secondhand dealer license, make application, be issued, and
shall maintain, a gross revenue business license for new merchandise as defined in
section 4.05.010, during all times the category A license is to remain valid; and

B.

In all cases, to obtain, and maintain, a secondhand dealer, category A, license, the
business so licensed shall derive a minimum of 70 percent of its gross revenues from
the sale of new merchandise during any six-month period of time.

C.

To obtain and maintain a secondhand dealer, category E, license, the business so licensed
shall maintain a valid permit to operate a recycling center issued by the health department.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.130 - Investigation fees—Required—Fees charged.
text:
Any person applying for a secondhand dealer license, is required to submit to the
city an investigation fee as set forth in chapter 4.03, for each person required to submit to a background investigation.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.170 - License issuance—Assignment—City council approval required—License nontransferable.
text:
A.

Upon receipt of the results of the background investigation from the police department,
the director will submit the application to the city council for consideration. If
approved by the council, the division may be directed to issue the license; provided,
however, that all other conditions, restrictions, payment of fees, and compliance
with all applicable state statutes and city ordinances have been met.

B.

A secondhand dealer license shall not be transferable and shall not be assignable
to any other person, or place of business, without council approval.

C.

Any assignee, or transferee, of a valid secondhand dealer license shall be required
to obtain a separate license prior to engaging in the business of a secondhand dealer.

D.

It is unlawful for any licensee to permit the licensed premises to be managed or utilized
by a lessee, or other transferee, who has not first obtained a separate secondhand
dealer license.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.175 - License—Change of location.
text:
A.

No secondhand dealer license is transferable to a new location unless such proposed
change of location complies with all requirements of this title and title 19; and

B.

Location changes are subject to council approval. Such approval may be withheld for
any reason deemed sufficient by the council; and

C.

Location changes are subject to an administrative fee as set forth in chapter 4.04.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.190 - Closure or non-operational status—Responsibility of licensee to maintain use.
text:
A.

In the event a secondhand dealer licensee holding a category B, class II license or
a secondhand dealer licensee holding a category D license desires to close or discontinue
his business operations for any period of time in excess of three months, he must
submit a written notification to the division within 30 calendar days of the closure
or discontinuance requesting approval for non-operational status beyond the initial
three-month period. The notification must include a closure plan detailing the length
of closure or period of non-operational status and the licensee's plans for reopening,
relocating, selling, or otherwise divesting themselves of the business. The licensee
may not discontinue operation of the business for more than a three-month period and
maintain a valid license without council approval. The council may approve non-operational
status of the business beyond the initial three-month period in time increments not
to exceed one year but in no event shall the council approve any non-operational status
beyond a maximum of two years. A license shall be automatically revoked at the expiration
of the time periods provided by this section unless council approval has been granted
pursuant to this section. All semiannual license fees must be paid notwithstanding
the licensee's non-operational status. Failure to maintain the fees will result in
automatic revocation of the license and termination of the established use.

B.

All other secondhand dealer licensees must continue business operations in order to
maintain licensing at the specified business location.

C.

It shall be the responsibility of the licensee to maintain, extend, or renew any necessary
land use approvals.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.200 - Display of sign.
text:
Every secondhand dealer holding a class II license shall maintain and display at all
times during the period of his license, in a conspicuous place at the public entrance
to the licensed premises, a sign in letters not less than six inches in height, bearing
the name of such licensee and the words "Secondhand Dealer."

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.210 - Purchase from minors and juveniles—Prohibitions—Exceptions—Conditions.
text:
A.

It is unlawful for any class I secondhand dealer, whether acting for himself as licensee,
or whether by an employee or agent of the licensee, to purchase any secondhand merchandise
as defined herein from any person under 18 years of age, unless the person has title,
free and clear, for the motor vehicle, ATV, boat, dirt bike or parts, to be purchased,
except with the written consent or direction of the parent or guardian of such person.
Said written permission shall be maintained as part of the records as specified in
section 4.68.230.

B.

It is unlawful for any secondhand dealer, whether acting for himself as licensee,
or whether by an employee or agent of the licensee, to purchase any secondhand merchandise
as defined herein, from any person under 18 years of age.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.220 - Time period merchandise to be retained.
text:
Except for class I secondhand dealers, every dealer in secondhand merchandise as defined
herein must keep, without concealment, for a period of 30 days, subject to inspection
by any police officer or license agent, all merchandise purchased or received a from
any person, before selling, shipping, or otherwise disposing of the same.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.230 - Record of transactions—Inspection of records and goods—Record retention.
text:
A.

Every secondhand dealer or scrap metal processor shall keep appropriate recordation
of each transaction at the time of purchase or receipt, in the English language in
a format approved by the chief of police, and retained in accordance with the provisions
of NRS Chapter 647.

B.

The record and all goods received must at all times during the ordinary hours of business
be open to inspection by the director, his designee, or the police department.

C.

Each secondhand dealer shall make the necessary reports to the police department in
accordance with the provisions of NRS 647.120 and shall be in a form acceptable to
the chief of police.

D.

The provisions of subsection C of this section do not apply to any transaction which
involves business activities identified as exempt in section 4.68.035.

E.

The records required to be kept per subsection A of this section are required to be
kept and maintained on the premises for a minimum of three years from the date of
original transaction.

F.

Every secondhand dealer having good cause to believe that any property in his or her
possession has been previously lost or stolen shall forthwith report that fact to
the chief of police, together with the name of the owner if known, and the date when
and the name of the person from whom the secondhand dealer received the property.

G.

It is unlawful for any person to purchase scrap metal unless the scrap metal has been
transported to the purchaser by means of a motor vehicle, and not by means of a shopping
cart or on a walk-up basis.

H.

It is unlawful for any person to purchase scrap metal in the form of metallic wire
that has been burned in whole or in part to remove insulation unless the purchaser:

1.

Obtains from the seller written evidence identifying the seller and documenting that
the wire was lawfully acquired and burned; and

2.

Complies with the documentation and retention requirements of NRS 647.030 and 647.035
that pertain to the purchase of burned metallic wire.

I.

It is unlawful for any person to purchase scrap metal unless:

1.

Payment is made either by check or electronic transfer of money; and

2.

Such payment is not mailed, delivered or electronically transmitted sooner than ten
days after the purchase transaction.

a.

The ten-day time period set forth in subsection (I)(2) above does not apply to any
transaction in which the seller is the holder of, or a principal of the holder of,
a State of Nevada business license, any other state-level licenses necessary to engage
in such a transaction, and a city business license issued under title 4.

J.

For any payment made by check under subsection (I) to a seller who represents a business,
the check must be made payable to the business, and not the representative, employee
or agent of the business.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.233 - Record of scrap metal purchases—Photographic or video documentation required—Inspection of records.
text:
A.

Each scrap metal purchase shall be conducted in compliance with NRS 647.094.

B.

Each scrap metal processor shall maintain and make available for inspection all records
as required pursuant to NRS 647.094.

C.

Each scrap metal processor shall make the necessary reports to the police department
in accordance with the provisions of NRS 647.094 and shall be in a form acceptable
to the chief of police.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.235 - Daily reports.
text:
Every secondhand dealer shall submit reports in compliance with NRS 647.120.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.240 - Licensee responsible for the acts of employees.
text:
Every licensee shall be responsible for the acts of his employees and agents committed
during the course and scope of employment. Every licensee shall accordingly use adequate
care in the selection of his employees and agents. In any license suspension, limitation
or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge
of the events complained of shall be no defense, and every licensee accepts his license
subject to said condition.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.260 - License—Suspension—Revocation—Limitation.
text:
The council, its designee, or the director may deem that any activity on the part
of the licensee or employees, or a person previously found suitable, which is contrary
to the public health, safety, morals, good order, or general welfare of the residents
of the city or the state is grounds for disciplinary action which may result in a
suspension, limitation or revocation of the secondhand dealer license pursuant to
chapter 4.06. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, each of the following reasons
is declared to be a basis for disciplinary action:

A.

Conviction of the licensee of any crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving
or possessing stolen property, any narcotics violation or any sex offense; or

B.

Conducting a secondhand dealer business in an unlawful manner or in a manner detrimental
to the public health, safety or welfare; or

C.

Each licensee who violates any provision of title 4; or

D.

Each licensee who knowingly fails to report or conceals a full disclosure of the names
of all persons having an interest in the ownership of or having an equitable or beneficial
right to the profits under a license in which he has an interest; or

E.

Each licensee who knowingly fails to report or conceals from proper authority any
information which it is his duty to supply under any statute, ordinance or regulation
of the state or the city; or

F.

Each licensee who, for conduct subsequent to the issuance of a license, becomes ineligible
to hold a secondhand dealer license as set out in the statutes, ordinances and regulations
of the state or city; or

G.

Each licensee who made a misrepresentation of a material fact in his application to
obtain a license; or

H.

Each licensee whose secondhand dealer license in any place in the state, or in any
state or municipality which is empowered to issue a license or permit for the business
of secondhand dealer, has been revoked for cause; or

I.

In the case of a category D secondhand dealer, failure to maintain the minimum net
assets requirement.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.270 - Application of Nevada Revised Statutes.
text:
The terms, conditions and requirements of this chapter are in addition to those imposed
under NRS 647.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: 4.68.290 - Violation—Penalty.
text:
Any person who violates any provision of this chapter, including the requirements
of NRS Chapter 647, shall be punished:

1.

For the first offense, by a fine of not more than $500.00.

2.

For the second offense, by a fine of not more than $1,000.00.

3.

For the third offense, by a fine of not more than $2,000.00 and by revocation of the
license of the secondhand dealer.

(Ord. No. 4041, § 1, 10-15-2024)

heading: Chapter 4.72 - MOBILE FOOD VENDORS[16]
text:
Sections:

Footnotes:

Prior ordinance history: 1782 and 1302.

heading: 4.72.010 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, or the words are otherwise
defined below, the words and terms used in this chapter have the following meanings:

A.

Department means the department of finance business license division.

B.

Director means the administrator of purchasing and licensing or his designee in the business
license division of the department of finance.

C.

Mobile food vendor means, but is not limited to, any person or employee or agent thereof carrying on
or conducting the business of selling ice cream, fruit, candy, vegetables, meats or
any other edible foods, raw, prepared, loose or packaged, from a motor vehicle, or
other type of food service conveyance, approved or required to be approved, by the
statutes or ordinances of the Clark County Health District governing such vehicles,
conveyances and sales practices.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.020 - Statement of purpose and intent—Regulation.
text:
It is found and declared that the public health, safety, morals, good order and general
welfare of the residents of the city require the regulation and control of all mobile
food vendors. All mobile food vendors shall be licensed and regulated so as to protect
the public health, safety, morals, good order and general welfare of the inhabitants
of the city and to safeguard the public. It is further found and declared that the
right to obtain such a license is a privilege and that the license may be suspended,
limited or revoked for violation of the conditions of this chapter. In conformity
with the policy of this chapter, the following persons are declared not to be qualified
to hold a license under the provisions of this chapter:

A.

A person who violates, or has violated, the provisions of this chapter despite notice
by the city;

B.

A person who has been convicted of a crime involving theft, fraud, dishonesty, receiving
or possessing stolen property, any controlled substance violation or any sex offense;

C.

A person whose license, issued under the provisions of this chapter, or those ordinances
or statutes of any other agency lawfully engaged in the licensing or regulation of
businesses as defined in this chapter, has been denied, suspended or revoked for cause;

D.

A person who, at the time of renewal of any license issued under this chapter, would
not be eligible for such license upon a first application;

E.

A partnership, limited partnership association, limited liability company, or other
business entity unless all of the members of such partnership, limited partnership
association, limited liability company, or business entity are qualified to obtain
a license;

F.

A corporation, unless it is incorporated in the State of Nevada, or unless it is a
foreign corporation which is qualified under Nevada law to transact business in Nevada;
or

G.

A corporation, if an officer or director thereof would not be eligible to receive
a license for any reason which would disqualify an individual applicant.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.030 - Unlawful to operate without license.
text:
It is unlawful for any mobile food vendor to engage in the business of mobile food
vending within the city without first obtaining a license therefor in compliance with
the provisions of this chapter.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.040 - License—Application—Consent to investigation.
text:
Whenever a person desires to conduct any of the activities of a mobile food vendor
in the city, such person shall completely execute the following:

A.

The application specified in section 4.04.060(A);

B.

Applicant's request to release information (HPD INV 40 [Rev. 1/01] or as may be amended)
the contents of which are incorporated herein by reference; and

C.

Henderson police department personal history questionnaire (HPD INV 41 [2/01], or
as may be amended) the contents of which are incorporated herein by reference and
any other pertinent documents or information which the department may require in order
to corroborate the information provided in the form.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.050 - Investigation fees—Employees or agents to qualify the same as the applicant.
text:
An applicant is required to pay to the department the investigation fee as set forth
in chapter 4.03, for each person required to be licensed as well as for each driver.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.060 - No refund on investigation fee.
text:
Even though an applicant is denied a license after investigation, no part of the investigation
fees deposited shall be returned to the applicant.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.070 - Withdrawal of application—Refund.
text:
If any applicant withdraws his application prior to the beginning of an investigation,
all investigation fees deposited shall be returned to the applicant.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.080 - Investigation and issuance.
text:
A.

Upon receipt of the application, the department shall refer the applicant or employee
or agent thereof to the Henderson police department which shall cause a background
investigation of the applicant's and driver's local criminal history and the Nevada
Sex Offender Registry.

B.

Upon the director's review of the application, the director shall refuse to issue
a license to the applicant for any of the following reasons:

1.

The applicant has been convicted of any felony, gross misdemeanor, or a misdemeanor
involving a sex offense, trafficking in controlled substances, or any violent act
against a person or property, such conviction having being entered within the ten
years preceding the date of application;

2.

The applicant is a person against whom a judgment based upon, or conviction for, fraud,
deceit or misrepresentation has been entered within the ten years immediately preceding
the date of application.

C.

The license application may also be denied for good cause as set forth in section
4.04.150(A), or because the applicant is not qualified as set forth in section 4.72.020.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.090 - Fees—Further regulations.
text:
A.

Mobile food vendors shall be subject to the fees set forth in section 4.05.010.

B.

Each mobile food vendor shall be in compliance with the regulations enacted by the
Clark County Health District, and shall show written evidence of the same, prior to
issuance of a license by the department.

C.

No licensee hereunder may lease, rent, or otherwise hire a vehicle to another for
use as a mobile food vendor's vehicle. Every driver shall be a licensee hereunder,
or the direct employee of such licensee.

D.

Each licensee shall further be subject to regulation of section 8.99.030(G).

E.

During the hours that schools are in session and during the period of one-half hour
before or after the times posted on the applicable school zone signs, no mobile food
vendor shall sell or solicit, or attempt to sell or solicit, or park a vehicle (1)
within 500 feet in any direction from the extreme outside perimeter of any school
and/or adjacent park grounds, (2) within a posted school zone, or (3) on the opposite
side of the street which runs next to the front of a school.

F.

No mobile food vendor shall enter on private property, knock on doors, ring any bells,
or otherwise disturb persons in their residences between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and
8:00 a.m. This section shall not apply, however, when the mobile food vendor has been
specifically invited by the owner, resident, occupant or person legally in charge
of the premises.

(Ord. 2831, § 5, 10-20-2009; Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.100 - Exhibition of license.
text:
All mobile food vendors are required to exhibit their licenses at the request of any
customer or potential customer, business license officer or peace officer.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.110 - Signs denying approach.
text:
A.

It is unlawful for any mobile food vendor to knock on the door, or ring the bell of
any residence whereon a sign with visible and legible letters at least three-fourths
of an inch in height bearing the words "No Trespassers," "No Peddlers," "No Canvassers,"
"No Mobile Food Vendors," "No Solicitors," or other words of similar import are painted,
affixed or exposed to public view, or to attempt to gain admittance thereto.

B.

This regulation shall apply to all groups of structures or complexes such as apartments,
condominiums, or private gated communities which have posted signage pursuant to subsection
A of this section at the entrance(s) or other points of ingress to such property regardless
of whether any individual residence is individually posted, provided that the sign
has letters at least 1½ inches in height.

C.

The provisions of this section shall not apply to a mobile food vendor who knocks
at any door, or rings any bell, at the specific invitation of the owner, resident,
occupant or person legally in charge of the premises.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.120 - Transfer prohibited.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any mobile food vendor to transfer his license to any other
person.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.130 - License—Suspension—Revocation—Limitation.
text:
Any license issued under this chapter may be revoked, limited, or suspended by the
director for any of the reasons set forth in sections 4.72.080 or 4.04.150.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.140 - Licensee responsible for the acts of employees.
text:
Every licensee shall be responsible for the acts of his employees and agents committed
during the course of employment or licensed activity. In any license suspension, limitation
or revocation proceedings, the fact that the licensee did not have actual knowledge
of the events complained of shall be no defense, and every licensee hereunder accepts
his license subject to said condition.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.150 - Licensee's agreement to conform to law.
text:
Acceptance of a license constitutes an agreement on the part of such licensee to be
bound by all of the regulations of the city as the same now are, or may hereafter
be amended or promulgated. It is the sole responsibility of the licensee to keep himself
informed of the content of all such rules and regulations, and ignorance thereof will
not excuse violations.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.160 - Right of appeal.
text:
Appeal rights of applicants are set forth in section 4.04.210.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.170 - Judicial review.
text:
Procedure for judicial review of final decisions and order of the council are set
forth in section 4.06.160.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.72.180 - Penalty for violation of chapter.
text:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor;
and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as the law allows for a misdemeanor
crime. Whenever in this chapter any act is prohibited, or is made or declared to be
unlawful, or an offense or a misdemeanor, or whenever in such chapter the doing of
any act is required, or the failure to do any act is made or declared to be unlawful,
or an offense or misdemeanor, the doing of any such prohibited act, or the failure
to do any such required act, shall constitute a violation of this chapter. Every day
of violation of this chapter constitutes a separate offense. Any person being adjudged
guilty of a violation of this chapter or any of the provisions or prohibitions thereof
may, in the discretion of the council, be denied a license thereafter.

(Ord. 2382, § 2 (part), 2005)

heading: 4.75.010 - Definitions.
text:
Whenever used in this chapter, the following words must have the meanings ascribed
in this section, unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning:

Applicant shall have the same meaning as set forth in chapter 4.04, as may be amended.

Conveyance means, without limitation, a pushcart, stand, display, pedal driven cart, wagon,
showcase, or rack that is used by a sidewalk vendor for purposes of selling food or
beverages.

Entertainment district means a contiguous area zoned/customarily used for commercial purposes that contains
a combination of restaurants, bars, entertainment establishments, music venues, theaters,
art galleries, dance studios, or sports stadiums.

Food means any substance whether processed, semi-processed or raw, which is intended for
human consumption and includes non-alcoholic drinks.

Food establishment means a city-licensed establishment that operates in the capacity of a restaurant
or has an alcoholic beverage license that includes the operation of a restaurant or
tavern.

Health district means the Southern Nevada Health District.

Nonstationary sidewalk vendor means a sidewalk vendor utilizing a mobile conveyance such as a pushcart, pedal-driven
cart, or wagon.

Open-air vendor means a vendor that operates on private commercial property and who sells food from
a conveyance, including, without limitation, a pushcart, stand, display, pedal-driven
cart, wagon, showcase, or rack, as otherwise defined or amended by NRS Chapter 268.

Religious assembly means a religious institution, place of worship, and/or similar facilities for religious
worship and incidental religious functions and education, but not including schools
as defined by title 19.

Sidewalk vendor means a person who sells food upon a public sidewalk or other pedestrian path from
a conveyance, including, without limitation, a pushcart, stand, display, pedal-driven
cart, wagon, showcase, or rack, as otherwise defined or amended by NRS Chapter 268.
The term includes, without limitation, a nonstationary sidewalk vendor and a stationary
sidewalk vendor.

Stationary sidewalk vendor means a sidewalk vendor utilizing a nonmobile conveyance such as a stand, display,
showcase, or rack.

Vend means to sell or offer to sell food products from a vending conveyance as either
a nonstationary sidewalk vendor or open-air food vendor.

Water Street entertainment district is an entertainment district and means the area of Water Street bordered by Ocean
Street to the South and Lake Mead Parkway to the North, including Purple Heart Street,
Market Street and West Army Street between Water Street and Market Street.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.020 - Statement of purpose and intent.
text:
It is found and declared that the public health, safety, good order, and general welfare
of the residents of the city require the regulation and control of all sidewalk vendors
operating in the city. All sidewalk vendors shall be licensed and regulated so as
to protect the public health, safety, good order, and general welfare of the residents
of the city.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.030 - License requirement and fee.
text:
It shall be unlawful to operate, conduct, carry on, or maintain any sidewalk vendor
business, as described in this chapter, without first having obtained and thereafter
maintaining the license as herein required. Each sidewalk vendor shall pay an annual
license fee of $150.00. The application fee in section 4.04.065 shall not be required.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.040 - License application.
text:
Every person required to obtain a license pursuant to this chapter shall file, with
the division, an application, on a form to be furnished by the division, providing,
without limitation, the following information:

1.

The name, mailing address, and telephone number of the applicant;

2.

A brief description of the business or activity to be conducted including, without
limitation:

A.

A description of the products the applicant intends to sell;

B.

The number and type of conveyance(s) that will be utilized pursuant to the license,
and a drawing or photograph identifying the height, width, and length of each conveyance;

3.

If employed, contracted, or otherwise engaged by another individual, company, partnership,
or corporation to engage in the activities regulated in this chapter, the name, address
and telephone number of the principal office of such individual, company, partnership,
or corporation;

4.

A certification by the sidewalk vendor that, to the best of the applicant's knowledge
and belief, the information submitted to the division is true; and

5.

All licenses, permits, or evidence of compliance required by applicable laws or regulations
of a state or local agency, including without limitation, a state business license,
a health district permit, etc. as may be applicable.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.045 - Licensee's agreement to conform to law.
text:
Acceptance of a license under this chapter constitutes an agreement on the part of
such licensee to be bound by all of the regulations of the city as the same now are,
or may hereafter be amended or promulgated. It is the sole responsibility of the licensee
to keep himself informed of the content of all such rules and regulations, and ignorance
thereof will not excuse violations.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.050 - Display of license and equipment requirements.
text:
1.

Each sidewalk vendor licensed in the city shall keep the license in their possession
at all times while the licensee is operating in the city, and shall allow inspection
of the license and health district permit upon request by any compliance agent, code
enforcement officer, police officer or other compliance personnel of the city, state,
or county regulatory agencies, including the health district.

2.

Each conveyance shall prominently display any sidewalk vendor decal issued under a
multi-jurisdictional business license issued by a neighboring jurisdiction, if applicable.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.055 - General liability insurance required.
text:
Each sidewalk vendor as defined by this chapter shall file with the division and thereafter
maintain a general liability insurance policy issued by an insurance company authorized
to do business in the State of Nevada in accordance with applicable sections of NRS
Title 57. The general liability insurance policy shall name the City of Henderson
as an additional insured and the certificate of insurance must be made available upon
request of the division. The policy limits of each insurance policy shall not be less
than:

1.

For bodily injury or the death of one person in any one accident, $250,000.00;

2.

Subject to the limitations of paragraph 1., for bodily injury to or death of two or
more persons in any one accident, $500,000.00; and

3.

For injury to or destruction of property in any one accident, $50,000.00.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.060 - Operating regulations—Nonstationary sidewalk vendors—Residential.
text:
1.

Sidewalk vendors are subject to the following requirements:

A.

Maintain sanitary conditions and comply with all applicable health district regulations
and permit requirements including but not limited to cleanliness and food safety standards;

B.

Sidewalk vendors may only vend items authorized by a valid health district permit
as applicable;

C.

Ensure that the conveyance and vending area are free from trash, debris, rubbish,
refuse, or waste. Including but not limited to trash created by the vendor's customers
and drips and spills of liquid waste from the conveyance;

D.

A sidewalk vendor must comply with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities
Act of 1974 (ADA), as amended, including requirements related to clear paths of travel.
A sidewalk vendor may not operate in a manner that will impede pedestrian traffic
or other normal use of the public sidewalk or pedestrian path, or otherwise hinder
accessibility or otherwise operate:

a.

Within 25 feet of any ADA sidewalk access point; or

b.

From a public sidewalk or pathway if such operations do not allow for a clear path
of travel of at least 36 inches.

2.

A sidewalk vendor shall not:

A.

Lease, rent, loan, or otherwise hire a conveyance to another for use as a sidewalk
vendor in the city. Each sidewalk vendor operating from a conveyance in the city shall
be a licensee under this chapter, or the direct employee of such licensee;

B.

Enter on private property, knock on doors, ring any bells, or otherwise disturb persons
in their residences between the hours of 9:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. This section shall
not apply when the sidewalk vendor has been specifically invited by the owner, resident,
occupant, or person legally in charge of the premises;

C.

Have any exclusive right to operate from any location upon public sidewalks, pathways,
or alleys;

D.

Utilize temporary signs except for menu boards located on or adjacent to the conveyance.
Illuminated signs are prohibited;

E.

Operate from any public street, including marked or unmarked crosswalks or in any
manner that may impede or interfere with the orderly flow of traffic on the street;

F.

Ring bells, play chimes, play an amplified musical system, or make any other noise
to attract attention to its business while operating within city limits; or

G.

Provide tables or seating areas for customers.

3.

Limitations on locations of operation from the property line of the protected use.
A sidewalk vendor shall not operate:

A.

Within 1,500 feet of:

a.

A resort hotel defined in NRS 463.01865; or

b.

A professional sports event facility with a seating capacity for 5,000 people.

B.

Within 500 feet of:

a.

An entertainment district, including the Water Street entertainment district, unless
otherwise permitted under a special event permit issued by the city;

b.

Any city park, community center, recreational facility, trail, or convention center,
unless otherwise permitted under a special event permit issued by the city;

c.

A childcare facility in commercially zoned areas during operating hours;

d.

A polling place during election operations;

e.

Religious assembly or place of worship during operating hours;

f.

In the immediate vicinity of a farmer's market during operating hours; or

g.

In the immediate vicinity of an area designated for a temporary special event throughout
the duration of the temporary special event.

C.

Within 150 feet of or immediately adjacent to:

a.

A licensed food establishment during the hours the establishment is open for business,
unless the vendor is operating as part of a special event approved by the city;

b.

A nonrestricted gaming establishment as defined in subsection 1 or 2 of NRS 463.0177;

c.

A privately funded community center or recreational facility, including facilities
that offer youth sports;

d.

A school (public, private, charter, etc.) during the hours the school is in session
and the 30-minute period before sessions begin and after sessions end; or

e.

Any public safety stations or substations (police and fire).

4.

Stationary sidewalk vendors are prohibited from operating in residential areas.

5.

Sidewalk vendors shall not operate from any single location for more than 30 minutes,
unless:

A.

The sidewalk vendor is operating under a special event permit issued by the city to
the vendor;

B.

The sidewalk vendor is operating at a temporary special event pursuant to a prior
arrangement made with the event holder (and the event holder has a valid special event
permit); or

C.

The sidewalk vendor is operating on private property when specifically invited by
the owner, resident, occupant, or person legally in charge of the premises, and subject
to the provisions of section 4.75.065.

6.

Exemptions.

A.

The following persons are exempt from the location restrictions:

a.

The location restrictions set forth in subsection 4.75.060(3) shall not apply to nonstationary sidewalk vendors operating in areas zoned exclusively
for residential use, unless the area is on a public sidewalk or pedestrian path that
is immediately adjacent to (visible from) the restricted location.

b.

Persons operating on private property pursuant to section 4.75.065.

B.

This chapter does not apply to charitable solicitations conducted in compliance with
the provisions of chapter 4.12.

7.

A map of the areas where a person may engage in the act of sidewalk vending in the
city may be viewed on the city's internet website.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.065 - Operating regulations—Open-air vendors—Private property.
text:
1.

Open-air vendors are subject to the following requirements:

A.

Maintain sanitary conditions and comply with all requirements applicable to sidewalk
vendors set forth in subsections 1 and 2 of 4.75.060;

B.

Open air vendors may only vend items authorized by a valid health district permit;

C.

May only operate on private commercial property with written permission of the property
owner or responsible party for the property or from the immediately adjacent business.
The written permission required by this subsection must be available for inspection;
and

D.

Must comply with the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1974,
as amended, including requirements related to clear paths of travel.

2.

Open-air vendor shall not:

A.

Block entrances and exits to existing commercial businesses on the property;

B.

Operate within 150 feet of a licensed food establishment or another open-air vendor;

C.

Sell merchandise; or

D.

Operate during hours in which the business granting permission to the property is
not operating or from 12:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., whichever is more restrictive.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.070 - Transfer prohibited.
text:
No sidewalk vendor license issued or renewed under the provisions of this chapter
may be transferred or assigned.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.090 - Licensee responsible for acts of employees and agents.
text:
Any person or entity who employs, contracts, or otherwise engages another to conduct
sidewalk vendor activities, is responsible for the acts or omissions of his employees
or agents committed during the course of employment or performance of activities governed
by this chapter. In any suspension, limitation, or revocation proceeding, the fact
that the distributing service or person who employed, contracted, or engaged another
did not have actual knowledge of the violation shall be no defense.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.100 - Electrical cords, chains, wires, or hoses.
text:
Except as otherwise expressly allowed by state law or city code, electrical cords,
chains, wires, or hoses shall not be strung across or along public sidewalks or public
pedestrian easements, nor may electrical generators or batteries be placed upon such
sidewalks or easements in the restricted area.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.110 - License does not provide defense for noncompliance with other laws.
text:
1.

The provisions of this chapter and the statutory provisions related to sidewalk vendors
set for in NRS Chapter 268 shall not be construed to:

A.

Exempt a person from complying with any state or local law or regulation; or

B.

Provide a defense to any criminal charge unrelated to the act of sidewalk vending.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.140 - Enforcement authority and disciplinary action.
text:
1.

The director, agents, or officers of the division, code enforcement, the police department,
or any state or county regulatory agency shall be entitled to enforce the provisions
of this chapter and impose disciplinary action as set forth in this section:

A.

Civil penalties. Any activity by a sidewalk vendor licensed under this chapter that
violates any provisions of this chapter, state law, or other governmental regulation
applicable to sidewalk vendors is grounds for disciplinary action including, but not
limited to, notices of violation of this chapter, civil penalties of $100.00 to $500.00
for each violation for each day the violation occurs or continues, notices of correction,
stop work orders, or the suspension or revocation of licenses pursuant to chapter 4.06.

a.

Pursuant to NRS 446.883, a city license issued under this chapter shall be automatically
revoked in the event the sidewalk vendor's permit is revoked by the health district,
and no new license may be issued until such person again possesses an unrevoked (valid)
permit from the health district.

b.

If any meat, seafood, poultry, vegetable, fruit, or other perishable articles which
are unsound, or contain any filthy, decomposed or putrid substance, or that may be
poisonous or deleterious to health or otherwise unsafe is found, the same having been
declared to be a nuisance, agents may condemn or destroy the same, or in any other
manner render the same unsalable as human food.

B.

Criminal penalties. The persons identified in subsection A of this section, and otherwise
authorized by law, shall also have the authority to issue misdemeanor citations to
enforce the following:

a.

Vending within 1,500 feet of a resort hotel per subsection 4.75.055(1)(a), a conviction
under this subjection does not constitute a crime of moral turpitude; or

b.

A violation of any state or local law otherwise punishable by misdemeanor citation,
if the violation is otherwise unrelated to the sidewalk vendor provisions set forth
in this chapter or NRS Chapter 268, including any legal prohibition on unlicensed
business activities.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: 4.75.150 - Enforcement—Appeal rights.
text:
Appeal rights for civil penalties issued under this chapter are the same as those
set forth in chapter 4.07.

(Ord. No. 4033, § 1, 6-18-2024)

heading: Chapter 4.80 - EMERGENCY MEDICAL SERVICES[18]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (18) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3292, §§ 1, 2, adopted October 6, 2015, repealed and reenacted chapter 4.80 in its entirety
to read as herein set out. Formerly, chapter 4.80, §§ 4.80.010—4.80.120, pertained
to private ambulance services, and derived from Ord. No. 1750, § 2, adopted in 1997;
Ord. No. 1895, §§ 1, 2, adopted in 1999; Ord. No. 2779, §§ 1—4, adopted in 2008, and
Ord. No. 2847, § 1, adopted January 19, 2010.

heading: 4.80.010 - Declaration of policy.
text:
The provision of pre-hospital emergency medical services is an essential public safety
function of government, made available in support of community health, security and
general welfare. In order to successfully support this function, various emergency
medical services components must be integrated and managed by the city to further
the optimal provision of such services for the inhabitants of the city.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.020 - Purpose of provisions.
text:
The provisions of this chapter shall govern the franchising, licensing and regulation
of an integrated emergency medical services system, including but not limited to ambulance
services, community para-medicine, and special event medical services in the city,
so that the general public has access to a safe, dependable, efficient, and integrated
emergency medical services system in the case of medical/traumatic injury emergencies.

(Ord. No. 3856, § 1, 3-1-2022; Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.030 - Chief of the department.
text:
It shall be the duty of the chief of the fire department to manage the IEMS in accordance
with the provisions of this chapter, unless otherwise provided herein. Nothing contained
in this chapter shall be construed to limit or otherwise apply to any function or
service provided by the fire department except as specifically set forth in this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.040 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter, the following definitions shall apply. Unless otherwise expressly
stated, words not defined herein shall be given their common and ordinary meaning:

Advanced life support or ALS, whether used alone or as a modifier of other nouns, means medical procedures for
sustaining life, including the advanced diagnosis and protocol-driven treatment of
a patient in the field such as defibrillation, airway management, and administration
of medications, that are provided by a paramedic.

Advanced emergency medical technician or AEMT or advanced EMT has the same meaning as the term "advanced emergency medical technician (AEMT)" in
the health district regulations, as may be amended.

Air ambulance has the same meaning as the term "air ambulance" in the health district regulations,
as may be amended.

ALS ambulance has the same meaning as the term "dedicated advanced life support ambulance" in the
health district regulations, as may be amended.

Advanced life support intervention has the same meaning as the term "Advanced life support (ALS) intervention" in 42
CFR 414.605, as may be amended.

Ambulance means a motor vehicle which is specially designed, constructed, equipped and staffed
to provide basic, intermediate, advanced, or critical/specialty care for one or more:

(1)

Sick or injured persons; or

(2)

Persons whose medical condition may require special observation during transportation.

For the purposes of this chapter, the term "ambulance" specifically excludes vehicles
for special event medical service vehicles.

Ambulance service has the same meaning as the term "ambulance service" in the health district regulations,
as may be amended. The term "ambulance service" does not include the use of vehicles
for special event medical service.

Applicant means a person who submits a completed application for a franchise as set forth in
this chapter.

Application means all written documentation, statements, representations and warranties provided
to the city by an applicant, in accordance with this chapter, to be relied upon by
the city council in making its determination of whether to grant or withhold a franchise.

Basic life support or BLS, whether used alone or as a modifier of other nouns, has the same meaning as the
term "basic life support (BLS)" in 42 CFR 414.605, as may be amended.

CFR means the Code of Federal Regulations, as may be amended, which is the codification
of the general and permanent rules published in the Federal Register by the departments
and agencies of the Federal Government.

CFO means the chief financial officer of the city, or their designee.

City council means the governing body of the city.

City manager means the city manager appointed by the city council to perform such administrative
functions of the city government as may be required of them by the city council, or
their designee.

Computer-aided dispatch or CAD means dispatching of emergency vehicles through computer technology to calls for
ambulance service.

Commission on Accreditation of Ambulance Service or CAAS means an independent commission that establishes a comprehensive series of standards
for the ambulance service industry.

Community para-medicine means the delivery of patient-centered healthcare in the out-of-hospital environment
utilizing technology and mobile pre-hospital professional resources to address the
needs of the community, including the following services:

(1)

Utilization of a medical professional for advice for low acuity 911 calls.

(2)

Patient-centered healthcare navigation.

(3)

Community risk-reduction strategies.

(4)

Medication reconciliation.

(5)

Provision of preventative care, health screening, and education.

(6)

Provision of alternative yet appropriate responses for low acuity calls to the PSAP
center.

(7)

Provision of alternative modes of transport.

(8)

Post-discharge healthcare navigation.

(9)

Post-discharge follow up and disease management.

(10)

Hospital readmission avoidance.

(11)

Hospice care support and collaboration.

(12)

Long-term care facility support and collaboration.

(13)

Chronic disease management.

(14)

Coordination of outpatient care.

(15)

Fall-reduction strategies.

CPI-MCS means the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for all Urban Consumers: U.S. City Average,
Series CUUR0000SAM2, Medical Care Services, as published by the U.S. Department of
Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Washington, D.C.

Critical care transport or CCT has the same meaning as the term "critical care transport" in the health district
regulations, as may be amended. CCT can also mean SCT.

Department means the business operations division of the finance department of the city, responsible
for the administration of this chapter as set forth herein.

Director means the business license supervisor of the business operations division of the
finance department of the city, or their designee.

Emergency has the same meaning as the term "emergency" in the health district regulations,
as may be amended.

Emergency medical care means medical care given to a patient in an emergency situation before the patient
arrives at a hospital or other medical facility, and until responsibility for the
patient is assumed by the medical staff at such facility.

Emergency medical service system or EMS means a system consisting of a chain of services linked together to provide emergency
medical care for the patient at the scene of an emergency, during transport, and upon
entry to a hospital or other medical facility.

Emergency medical technician or EMT has the same meaning as the term "emergency medical technician (EMT)" in the health
district regulations, as may be amended.

Emergency medical technician paramedic or EMT-Paramedic or paramedic has the same meaning as the term "paramedic" in the health district regulations,
as may be amended and in accordance with the health district regulations is authorized
to administer additional advanced life support interventions and medications.

Emergency response has the same meaning as the term "emergency response" in 42 CFR 414.605, as may be
amended.

EMS priority dispatch means a dispatch system:

(1)

Whereby emergency medical dispatchers, certified by the health district, give lifesaving
pre-arrival instructions to person(s) requesting the same; and

(2)

Which provides for the dispatch of the appropriate level of emergency vehicle response,
as determined by use of a priority card or computer program, based on the severity
of the medical emergency.

Financial statements means financial statements of the local operation of a business licensed, or licensed
and franchised, under this chapter. Financial statements are to include: balance sheet,
income statement, statements of cash flows, and statement of retained earnings prepared
in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

Fire department means the fire department of the city.

Franchise means the authorization granted to a person, firm, partnership, corporation or company
by the city council to provide services in support of the IEMS within the public rights-of-way
and all highways, streets, roads and alleys within the jurisdictional limits of the
city. The terms and conditions of such authorization will be described in a franchise
agreement specific to such purpose.

Franchise agreement means the written agreement entered into between the city and a franchisee evidencing
the city's authorization for a franchisee to provide services in support of the IEMS
and requiring the franchisee to comply with the terms of this chapter, and incorporating
such other reasonable terms, conditions, and provisions as the city council deems
appropriate.

Franchise service area or service area means the geographic area within the city specified in a franchise agreement, wherein
a franchisee is authorized and required to provide services in support of the IEMS.

Franchisee means the person, firm, partnership, corporation or company to whom a franchise is
granted by the city council pursuant to this chapter.

Health district means the Southern Nevada Health District, its officers and authorized agents.

Health district regulations means the applicable EMS regulations, manuals and protocols adopted by the health
district, as they may be amended from time to time.

Health officer means the chief health officer of the health district.

HIPAA means the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, as amended,
and regulations related thereto.

Hospital has the same meaning as the definition of that term in NRS 439B.110, as amended.

Incident commander means the city fire officer or fire paramedic in charge at the scene of an incident
where patient care is being provided by fire department personnel.

Inter-facility ambulance transport service means an emergency transport or a nonemergency transfer of a patient by ambulance
that originates and terminates at previously designated medical facilities or locations.

Integrated emergency medical service system or IEMS means a system of components that provides for the receipt and notification of calls
for service, arrangement of personnel, facilities, training, quality improvement,
equipment, and management of the system components for the effective and coordinated
delivery of health care services under emergency/nonemergency conditions within the
city.

Life threatening emergency is an event or situation where immediate death or disability could be reasonably
inferred to occur if immediate emergency medical care and transport is not provided.

Loaded mileage has the same meaning as the term "loaded mileage" in 42 CFR 414.605, as may be amended.

Maximum ambulance service rate means the maximum amount that a franchisee may bill a patient or other payer for
the level of ambulance service provided to the patient, as established in this chapter,
including all ancillary services and supplies used in providing ambulance service.

Mutual aid means ambulance service provided within the franchise service area in response to
a request through the city PSAP for assistance.

Non-emergency ambulance service means prearranged non-911 dispatched ambulance service provided to patients with
non-life-threatening conditions, including without limitation non-emergency ambulance
service requested at special events and other non-911-dispatched ambulance service
requests that would be categorized as nonemergency transfers or level 33-A calls (as
that term is approved and endorsed by the health district) when processed through
EMS priority dispatch protocol.

Public safety answering point or PSAP means the 911 call answering point which is administered by the City of Henderson,
or other agency designated by the city.

Rights-of-way means public property dedicated to, granted to, or held or prescriptively used by
the city for public street, alley, road and highway purposes, except public streets
predominantly used for public freeway or expressway purposes.

Service category means the type or level of ambulance service that is specified in a franchise granted
pursuant to this chapter.

Special event means an activity that occurs on a specific date and time at a specific location,
such as, but not limited to, sporting events, off-road vehicle races, speedway races,
concerts, fairs and parades.

Special event medical service or SEMS means the providing of medical care to the participants and members of the public
in attendance at a special event pursuant to a contractual arrangement between a special
event medical service provider or a franchisee and the special event owner, operator,
promoter, organizer or any other person authorized to enter into such contractual
arrangements on behalf of the special event.

Special event medical service provider or SEMS provider means a person who has obtained a special event medical service provider business
license pursuant to this chapter and the special purpose ambulance service permit
required pursuant to health district regulations.

Special event medical service vehicle means the special purpose vehicle permitted by health district regulations which
for the purposes of this chapter may be used for the sole purpose of providing medical
care at a special event. Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the term does
not include a vehicle which provides ambulance service over city rights-of-way.

Specialty care transport or SCT has the same meaning as the term "specialty care transport (SCT)" in 42 CFR 414.605,
as may be amended.

Street means the surface of the full width of the right-of-way, including alleys, sidewalks
and thoroughfares, places or ways of any kind used by the public or open to the public
as a matter of right for the purpose of vehicular traffic or vehicular and pedestrian
traffic.

Sub-zone means a portion of a franchise service area as defined in a franchise agreement.

Transfer means the scheduled or unscheduled movement of a patient located within the geographic
area within the city by ambulance from one medical facility to another medical facility,
from a home to a medical facility, from a medical facility to a home or from another
location to a medical facility.

Transport has the same meaning as the term "transport" in the health district regulations,
as may be amended.

(Ord. No. 3856, § 2, 3-1-2022; Ord. No. 3379, § 1, 1-3-2017; Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.050 - Ambulance services—Business license required.
text:
A.

No person shall engage in the business of operating an ambulance service upon the
rights-of-way of the city without first obtaining, and thereafter maintaining a valid
unexpired business license, as required by this chapter.

B.

Each ambulance service licensed in the city under this chapter shall pay, in advance,
a semiannual business license fee as set forth in section 4.05.124.

C.

A person is not required to obtain a business license pursuant to this section if
such person is licensed in another jurisdiction to provide ambulance services and
does not provide cross-jurisdictional transport or transfer services originating inside
the city.

(Ord. No. 3379, § 1, 1-3-2017; Ord. No. 3352, § 2, 7-5-2016; Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.060 - Ambulance services—Franchise requirements.
text:
A.

Except as provided in subsection B of this section, it is unlawful for any person
to provide ambulance service in support of the IEMS in the city without first obtaining
and thereafter maintaining an ambulance service franchise and paying the franchise
fee as required by this chapter.

B.

A person is not required to obtain an ambulance service franchise pursuant to this
chapter if the services such person provides in the city are limited to the following:

1.

Providing cross-jurisdictional transport or transfer services originating outside
the city;

2.

Responding to requests for emergency mutual aid in accordance with subsection 4.80.160(A);

3.

Responding to requests for CCT/SCT services when a franchisee is not available to
respond; or

4.

Responding to requests for aid from a franchisee pursuant to an aid agreement authorized
by the city between the franchisee and the ambulance service.

(Ord. No. 3379, § 1, 1-3-2017; Ord. No. 3352, § 2, 7-5-2016; Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.070 - Ambulance services—Franchise fee determination.
text:
A franchise fee shall be the amount imposed for the grant or extension of a franchise,
as set forth in a franchise agreement. Franchise fees shall be paid according to the
provisions of the franchise agreement, and shall be accompanied by such supporting
documentation as required therein and as the CFO deems necessary.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.080 - Ambulance services—Solicitation of bids.
text:
The city council, in its sole discretion, may solicit qualifications for ambulance
service franchises and, the requirements for application stated in section 4.80.120 notwithstanding, establish such requirements for qualifications as it deems appropriate.
Qualifications received shall be reviewed and investigated by the department, and
the results of such investigation shall be reported to the city council. After receiving
the department's report, the city council may grant a franchise, not grant a franchise
or take any other action it may deem appropriate.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.090 - Ambulance services—Limitation of number of franchises.
text:
The city council may, in its sole discretion, specify by resolution a fixed number
of ambulance service franchises, including their service levels, types and categories,
to be granted within the city. If the city council has not specified by resolution
a fixed number of ambulance service franchises to be granted within the city, then
prior to accepting a new application for an ambulance service franchise, the city
council in its sole discretion, shall make a determination by resolution of whether
a new ambulance service franchise will serve the public convenience and necessity.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.100 - Ambulance services—Grant of franchise.
text:
An ambulance service franchise shall grant permission to the franchisee to provide
ambulance services in support of the IEMS for the service level, type and category
so authorized in the service areas specifically described in the franchise agreement,
according to the terms and conditions contained in the franchise agreement.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.110 - Ambulance services—Right of property not granted by franchise.
text:
Any franchise granted pursuant to this chapter is a privilege conferred by the city
council and shall not impart to the franchisee any right of property in any city rights-of-way
or other city property. The franchise agreement shall be construed to have granted
permission and authority to operate within the city under the terms and conditions
of the franchise agreement.

(Ord. No. 3292, § 2, 10-6-2015)

heading: 4.80.120 - Ambulance services—Application for franchise.
text:
A.

Whenever the number of ambulance service franchisees within the city is less than
the maximum number established by the city council pursuant to this chapter, or if
the city council has not established a maximum number of such franchises but has determined
that a new ambulance service franchise will serve the public convenience and necessity
as provided in section 4.80.090, a person may apply for a new franchise by submitting an application with the department
on such form or in such format as the department shall require.

B.

The application shall be in writing and shall include, at a minimum, the following:

1.

For a sole proprietor:

a.

The name and business and residence addresses of the applicant; and

b.

A list of any other businesses in which the sole proprietor has a five percent or
greater ownership interest.

2.

For a corporation:

a.

The corporate name, date and place of incorporation, the address of its principal
place of business, and identification of the ownership and control of the applicant,
including:

(i)

A list of the officers and directors and persons who may otherwise control the operations
of the corporation;

(ii)

A list of all shareholders of five percent or more of the shares of the corporation;

(iii)

A list of any businesses in which any of the persons listed in item 2(a)(i) and (ii)
have a five percent or more ownership interest;

b.

A copy of the articles of incorporation and all effective amendments certified by
the appropriate officer of the state of incorporation; and

c.

A certificate of good standing from the Nevada Secretary of State.

3.

For a limited liability company:

a.

The limited liability company name, date and place of organization, the address of
the principal place of business and the ownership and control of the limited liability
company, including:

(i)

Whether the limited liability is managed by member(s) or manager(s);

(ii)

A list of the managers, members, officers and persons who may otherwise control the
operations of the limited liability company;

(iii)

A list of any businesses in which any of the persons listed in item 3(b) have a five
percent or more ownership interest;

b.

A copy of the articles of organization.

4.

For a partnership or, association:

a.

The names of the owners, partners or the persons comprising the partnership or association,
the names and percentage of ownership of each owner, partner or person, and the business
and residence addresses of each owner, partner or person.

b.

A list of any businesses in which any of the persons listed in item 4(a) have a five
percent or more ownership interest; and

c.

A copy of the partnership agreement or articles of association.

5.

A statement with such references as may be acceptable to the department describing
the qualifications and experience of the applicant and the personnel who will manage
the ambulance service franchise; all geographic areas and all other jurisdictions
currently or previously provided ambulance service by the applicant, including performance
standards achieved and levels of service provided. This section shall not be deemed
to preclude an application from a new business entity; provided that the principals
in such entity are able to demonstrate to city council, in city council's sole discretion,
that the new entity can satisfy the requirements for a franchise set forth in this
chapter.

6.

A letter of intent from an insurance carrier stating that, if a franchise is granted,
an insurance policy will be issued for liability insurance in the amount and under
the conditions stated in this chapter.

7.

A letter of commitment from a qualified institution acceptable to the department stating
