club, then in the area of such facility dedicated to the use of the massage establishment;

I.

Transferring or attempting to transfer or assign a license issued under this chapter;
or

J.

Failure to comply with any of the requirements specified in this chapter or NRS Chapter
640C, as may be amended or renumbered.

(Ord. No. 3301, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.84.190 - Obtaining a license after revocation—Prohibition.
text:
No massage establishment license shall be granted, and any existing massage establishment
license may be revoked, limited or suspended, with respect to any person whose business
license, massage establishment license, massage therapy license or other similar license
was revoked, limited or suspended in any jurisdiction, for the period of two years
following the date of such revocation or suspension. The prohibition on granting a
license, and the potential revocation, limitation or suspension of an existing license,
shall also apply to the spouse, family member, or business associate of, or any person
who holds more than a ten percent ownership interest in, such business whose license
was suspended, limited or revoked.

(Ord. No. 3301, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.84.200 - Enforcement authority.
text:
A.

The director, agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, the police department,
or any state or county regulatory agency shall be entitled to enforce the provisions
of this chapter.

B.

Such enforcement power shall include, but not be limited to, the power to issue notices
of violation of this chapter, impose civil penalties up to $500.00 for each violation
for each day or any portion thereof during which the violation occurs or continues,
declare nuisances, serve notices of correction, issue red tag/stop work orders, initiate
suspension or revocation of licenses pursuant to chapter 4.06, and to perform all other duties relating to licensing enforcement as provided in
this title. In addition, those persons identified in subsection A of this section
shall have the authority to prepare, sign and serve misdemeanor citations pursuant
to NRS Chapter 171, as may be amended or renumbered, to enforce the provisions of
this title.

C.

The director or his designee shall also have the authority to issue a "red tag/stop
work order" for the following reasons:

1.

No manager in charge present on the premises during business hours;

2.

No massage therapist on the premises;

3.

Refusal of the manager in charge, employee or other person to allow agents or officers
of the division, code enforcement, the police department, or any state or county regulatory
agency onto the premises for inspection to verify compliance with the provisions of
this chapter;

4.

Occurrence of a crime on the premises of the massage establishment related to the
operations of the massage establishment or actions of an employee or independent massage
therapist;

5.

Existence of a threat to the public health, safety, welfare or morals;

6.

A third violation of the provisions of this chapter by any employee, independent massage
therapist or the massage establishment, or any combination thereof, in a six-month
period;

7.

Failure to comply with a plan of correction established between the division and the
massage establishment or massage therapist during the time provided for in the plan
of correction; or

8.

Upon notice to the division or city from the board or other governmental agency of
discipline against a massage establishment or its employees or independent massage
therapists if the discipline is an indication that continued operation of the massage
establishment or provision of massage therapy services may be a threat to the safety,
welfare, health or morals of the city.

The "red tag/stop work order" shall direct the massage establishment employees, independent
massage therapist, or unlicensed person performing massage to cease and desist from
the activity, or activities designated in the "red tag/stop work order". The "red
tag/stop work order" shall be given in writing by the director or his designee to
the massage establishment, its agents, or employees, or to unlicensed persons providing
services in violation of this chapter, clearly stating the violation(s) being committed.
The director or his officers shall affix a copy of the "red tag/stop work order" to
the public entrance(s) of the massage establishment in a prominent location. It shall
be unlawful for any person to remove the "red tag/stop work order" from the public
entrance(s) of the establishment without the express written authorization of the
director or one of his officers.

D.

Any violation of a "red tag/stop work order," issued pursuant to subsection C of this
section, shall be deemed a separate violation of this chapter and shall be cause to
suspend, limit and/or revoke the massage establishment or independent massage therapist
license. A notice of violation and civil penalty may be issued for each violation,
for each and every day of continued violation.

E.

When, in the course of enforcing the provisions of this title relative to emergency
suspension or a "red tag/stop work order," the division shall have the authority to
lock and seal the premises where the massage therapy services are being provided.

F.

Any agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, the police department, or
any state or county regulatory agency shall have access to every part and portion
of the massage establishment or location where massage services are being provided
at any time when a massage establishment is open for the transaction of business or
massage therapy services are being provided, and after regular business hours if business
is still being conducted, for the purpose of determining compliance with the provisions
of this chapter and title 19 of the development code.

G.

Failure of the director or agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, the
police department, or any state or county regulatory agency to discover violations
and/or take action to enforce any provision of this chapter shall not constitute a
forfeiture or waiver of such person's right to take appropriate action at any time
thereafter. Nothing in this chapter shall be construed as requiring the director or
agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, the police department, or any
state or county regulatory agency to impose any penalty on a massage establishment
or massage therapist, if the division, police department, or relevant agency deems
the matter giving rise to a notice of violation has been corrected.

H.

This section is supplemental to, and not exclusive of, enforcement measures available
to other officials regarding this title.

(Ord. No. 3301, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: Chapter 4.85 - REFLEXOLOGY[20]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (20) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3304, §§ 2, 3, adopted October 20, 2015, repealed and replaced chapter 4.85 in its entirety
to read as herein set out. Formerly, chapter 4.85, §§ 4.85.010—4.85.200, pertained
to similar subject matter, and derived from Ord. No. 2844, § 4, adopted January 19,
2010; Ord. No. 2947, §§ 5, 6, adopted December 6, 2011, and Ord. No. 3068, § 1, adopted October 1, 2013.

heading: 4.85.010 - Definitions.
text:
The following definitions are in addition to the definitions set forth in chapter 4.04 of this title. Unless the context clearly indicates a different meaning, the definitions
below shall govern the construction, meaning, and application of words and phrases
used in this chapter:

Advertising means the intentional placement or issuance of any sign, card or device, or the permitting
or allowing of any sign or marking on a motor vehicle, in any building, structure,
newspaper, magazine, handout, flyer or other publication, any airway transmission,
on the Internet or in any directory under the listing of "reflexologist" or "reflexology."

Ancillary employee means any employee of a reflexology establishment or of an independent reflexologist
that is not a reflexologist.

Control means the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of
a reflexology establishment, reflexologist, employee or agent in any way.

Employee means any of the following: (i) a reflexologist employed by a reflexology establishment
to provide reflexology, but who is not an independent contractor of the reflexology
establishment; (ii) a manager in charge and (iii) an ancillary employee.

Independent reflexologist means (i) a reflexologist who is a sole practitioner or independent contractor; or
(ii) a person otherwise providing reflexology services as described in this chapter
who is not an employee of a reflexology establishment.

Outcall reflexology means any reflexology performed by a reflexologist or independent reflexologist upon
a patron at a location other than a location licensed as a reflexology establishment.

Patron means any person who receives reflexology services at a reflexology establishment
or from an independent reflexologist.

Reflexologist means a person who uses special pressure techniques on the reflexes in the human
feet, hands, and ears and who has studied the principles of reflexology, anatomy and
physiology generally included in a regular course of study of reflexology. While the
provisions of this chapter apply to anyone performing reflexology or operating a reflexology
establishment, regardless of whether such person or place is licensed as such, nothing
in this chapter shall be construed to allow the practice of reflexology without all
appropriate licenses and permits. Reflexologist means both independent reflexologists
and reflexologists who are employees of a reflexology establishment unless otherwise
specified.

Reflexology means the application of specific pressure by the use of the licensed practitioner's
hands, thumbs, and fingers to reflex points in the client's hands, feet, or ears using
alternating pressure, and such techniques as thumb walking, finger walking, hook and
back up, and rotation on a reflex. This practice does not involve the removal of any
clothes other than shoes and socks.

Reflexology establishment means any fixed place of business where any individual, firm, association, partnership,
corporation, or combination of individuals, engages in, conducts, carries on, or permits
to be engaged in or conducted, for money or any other consideration, any reflexology
services. For purposes of this chapter, including, without limitation, responsibility
for compliance with the provisions of this chapter and penalties for failure to so
comply, the term shall include the owners, managers, members, partners, directors,
or shareholders of the business entity operating as a reflexology establishment.

Sexual activity means:

1.

Sexual intercourse;

2.

Examining or touching any specified anatomical area of a patron;

3.

Rubbing against a patron for sexual gratification;

4.

Kissing a patron;

5.

Hugging, touching, fondling or caressing a patron in a romantic or sexual nature;

6.

Removing the patron's clothing, except as may be necessary in a medical emergency;

7.

Dressing or undressing in the presence of a patron;

8.

Showing a patron sexually explicit photographs or videos;

9.

Encouraging masturbation or any other sex act in the presence of the reflexologist,
an employee of the reflexology establishment or any other person;

10.

Discussing the sexual history, preference or fantasies of the reflexologist in the
presence of a patron;

11.

Masturbation or any other sex act by the reflexologist or an employee of the reflexology
establishment or any other person in the presence of the patron;

12.

Any behavior, gesture or expression by a reflexologist or an employee of a reflexology
establishment that may reasonably be interpreted as seductive or sexual;

13.

Making statements regarding the patron's body, appearance, sexual history or sexual
orientation other than for legitimate health care purposes;

14.

Sexually demeaning behavior including any verbal or physical contact which may reasonably
be interpreted as demeaning, humiliating, embarrassing, threatening or harming a patron;
or

15.

Photographing or filming the body or any body part of a patron.

Specified anatomical area means the human genitals, pubic region, anus, or perineum of any person, or the breasts
of a female.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.015 - Statement of legislative intent—Regulation.
text:
The public health, safety, morals and welfare of the inhabitants of the city require
the regulation and control of all persons engaged in the business of reflexology.
All such persons shall be licensed in order to help protect the public health, safety
and general welfare of the residents of the city and to safeguard the public.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.020 - Exemptions.
text:
This chapter does not apply to the activities or services of physicians, chiropractors,
physical therapists, cosmetologists, registered nurses, or members of other professions
licensed, certified, or registered by the state who may, on occasion, apply pressure
to the reflex points in the hands, feet, and ears in the course of their work, so
long as the activities or services are provided in connection with the practice for
which the person is licensed, certified, or registered.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.025 - Owner-Employees.
text:
A.

Each reflexology establishment shall be operated under the lawful control of a manager
in charge as defined in section 4.85.060. Each reflexologist working at a reflexology establishment who is not an actual owner
or independent contractor of the establishment shall be deemed an employee of said
establishment.

B.

Every reflexology establishment and manager in charge shall be responsible for the
conduct of the reflexology establishment employees, agents, representatives, or other
persons, who are on the premises of the reflexology establishment regardless of whether
such person is providing reflexology services, and the reflexology establishment,
reflexologist and/or manager in charge shall be subject to disciplinary action including,
notices of violation, civil penalties, and criminal citations, and the reflexology
establishment license shall be subject to suspension, revocation or limitation, based
upon such conduct, regardless of any actual or constructive knowledge of the conduct
by the reflexology establishment or manager in charge. In any license suspension,
limitation, or revocation proceedings, the fact that the reflexology establishment
did not have actual knowledge of the events complained of shall be no defense and
every reflexology establishment accepts his or her license subject to said condition.

C.

Any reflexology establishment that contracts with reflexologists as independent contractors
for the purpose of having the reflexologist perform reflexology shall be jointly responsible
for the conduct and business operations of the independent reflexologist. Any misconduct
by the independent reflexologist shall be attributable to both the independent reflexologist
and the reflexology establishment and shall subject the reflexology establishment,
manager in charge and independent reflexologist to disciplinary action including notices
of violation, civil penalties, and criminal citations, and shall subject the reflexology
establishment to suspension, limitation and/or revocation of the reflexology establishment
license based upon the conduct of the independent reflexologist, regardless of any
actual or constructive knowledge of the conduct by the reflexology establishment or
manager in charge. In any license suspension, limitation, or revocation proceedings,
the fact that the reflexology establishment or manager in charge did not have actual
knowledge of the events complained of shall be no defense and every reflexology establishment
accepts its license subject to said condition.

D.

Reflexology establishments shall train their employees and shall ensure their independent
reflexologists have training regarding how to address patrons who initiate, request
or suggest sexual activity.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.030 - Unlawful to operate without a license—License application requirements.
text:
It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a reflexology establishment, or provide
services as a reflexologist, within the city without first having obtained a valid
reflexology establishment or reflexologist license as herein required and paying the
license fees as set forth in chapter 4.05.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.033 - Investigation fees—Required—Fees charged.
text:
Any person applying for a reflexology establishment license or a reflexologist license
is required to submit to the city an investigation fee as set forth in chapter 4.03, for each person required to be investigated. Persons who are required to be investigated
include, without limitation, reflexologists and, with respect to reflexology establishments,
owners, managers in charge, officers, directors, managers, members, and partners.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.035 - License—Location subject to conditional use permit and massage establishment license if massage performed at location.
text:
All applicants for a license for a reflexology establishment that will be located
within the city and that will also provide massage therapy (as that term is defined
in chapter 4.84) shall submit to the community development and services department an application,
in the manner specified by that department, for a conditional use permit in accordance
with title 19 of the development code. Disciplinary actions imposed under this chapter
or chapter 4.84 in connection with any massage therapy services provided may include revocation of
the conditional use permit.

Any reflexology establishment that wishes to offer massage therapy services pursuant
to chapter 4.84 must separately obtain a massage therapy establishment license.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.040 - Minimum educational and certification requirements.
text:
Applicants for a reflexologist license shall submit the following at the time of application:

A.

A diploma or certification for the practice of reflexology, issued by a duly licensed
school of reflexology or massage therapy, the curriculum of which includes at least
110 hours of instruction, covering reflexology theory, history, and hands on work;
anatomy and physiology correlated to reflexology; anatomy and physiology specifically
focused on the study of the lower leg and foot; business practice which involves ethics
and business standards and knowledge of local and state laws and ordinances pertaining
to the practice of reflexology; and 90 hours of practicum; or

B.

Certification from an independent national reflexology testing entity which is not
aligned with any school, training program, or membership.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.045 - License—Changes in ownership.
text:
In the case of a corporation, partnership, association, limited liability company,
or any other form of ownership of a reflexology establishment other than a sole proprietor,
any and all changes in the officers, partners, managers, members or directors of such
legal entity shall be reported to the division within 30 days of the change. Any new
officers, partners, managers, members, or directors shall be required to pass the
investigation and pay the related fees therefore in accordance with chapter 4.03. Failure of any of the aforementioned persons to pass the investigation or pay the
fees may result in revocation, suspension, or limitation of the reflexology establishment
license.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.050 - License issuance.
text:
Upon receipt of the results of the background investigation required by section 4.85.033 from the police department, the director will make a determination on the finding
of suitability of the applicant for a reflexology establishment license. The division
will submit the recommendation for approval or denial of the application for a reflexology
establishment license to the city council for consideration. All license applicants
are required to submit an affidavit or declaration, on a form provided by the division,
to the city council at the time the city council considers whether to approve or deny
the license affirming their willingness to abide by the provisions of this chapter.
If the applicant is approved by the city council, the division may be directed to
issue the license; provided, however, that all other conditions, restrictions, payment
of fees, and compliance with all applicable state statutes and city ordinances have
been met.

(Ord. No. 3623, § 1, 9-18-2019; Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.055 - Advertising.
text:
A.

No person shall advertise that such person provides services as a reflexologist operating
in the city unless, in the case of a natural person, the person is licensed by the
city as a reflexologist, and in the case of a business, is licensed by the city as
a reflexology establishment.

B.

No reflexology establishment or reflexologist shall place, publish or distribute or
cause to be placed, published or distributed any advertisement, picture, or statement
which is known or, through the exercise of reasonable care, should be known to be
false, deceptive or misleading or which would reasonably suggest to prospective patrons
that sexual stimulation or sexual gratification will be provided in order to induce
any person to purchase or utilize any reflexology services of the reflexology establishment
or reflexologist.

C.

All advertising by a reflexologist must include his or her legal name, license number,
if any, and the name of the reflexology establishment where he/she performs reflexology
services. All advertising by a reflexology establishment must include the business
name and license number(s) of the reflexology establishment.

D.

In the event a reflexology establishment or manager in charge becomes aware of any
advertising that: (i) directs the viewer of the advertisement to the reflexology establishment,
either by name or address; and (ii) violates the provisions of this section, the reflexology
establishment or manager in charge shall take reasonable steps to have such advertising
removed or taken down, or in the case of flyers or handbills, shall cease distribution
thereof. With respect to internet advertising or posting, reasonable efforts shall
include, but not be limited to, requesting the host of the website on which the advertising
is located, or the person posting the advertisement, to remove or delete the advertisement
or post.

E.

Two or more violations of section 4.85.055 within a six-month period may subject the reflexology establishment or reflexologist
license to suspension, limitation, or revocation pursuant to chapter 4.06 and the reflexology establishment, reflexologist, manager in charge or other party
responsible for the advertising to civil penalties as provided for in chapter 4.07.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.060 - Operating requirements.
text:
The operating requirements of all reflexology establishments licensed pursuant to
this chapter are as follows:

A.

A person designated as the manager in charge shall be on the premises at all times
of operation. The manager in charge shall also be responsible for accepting citations,
written correspondence, and any other communications from the city. The manager in
charge shall be a key employee subject to the requirements of section 4.04.180.

A reflexology establishment may have more than one manager in charge provided, however,
that: at least one manager in charge must be present on the premises of the reflexology
establishment at all times while the reflexology establishment is open for business.
Each person identified as a manager in charge shall be required to obtain an approval
letter issued by the division which shall not be issued until the person meets the
following requirements to the satisfaction of the director:

1.

The manager in charge shall be at least 18 years old;

2.

The manager in charge shall be a citizen of the United States or a non-citizen eligible
to work in the United States, with proper documentation of same;

3.

The manager in charge shall not be a registered sex offender or required by law to
register as a sex offender;

4.

The manager in charge shall not, within ten years before requesting an approval letter,
have been convicted of (or offer a plea of nolo contendere to) an offense in a case
involving sexual misconduct with a child, including sexual abuse, sexual assault,
sexual conduct, sexual molestation, or sexual exploitation;

5.

The manager in charge shall not, within ten years before requesting an approval letter,
be convicted of prostitution (or offer a plea of nolo contendere), or of operating
an unlawful prostitution enterprise;

6.

The manager in charge shall not, within ten years before requesting an approval letter,
be convicted of (or plead nolo contendere to) a felony or crime of moral turpitude
not otherwise specified herein; and

7.

The record of the manager in charge shall be free of all reasons to deny, suspend,
limit or revoke an application under this section, section 4.04.150, and section 4.85.100 of this title.

B.

A list of services available and prices for all services shall be prominently posted
in the reception area in a location available to all prospective customers and shall
be written in English.

C.

Every reflexology establishment, and all licensed reflexologists, shall post the license
required by this chapter in a prominent place in the reception area of the establishment.

D.

The manager in charge shall be responsible for ensuring that all persons performing
reflexology at the reflexology establishment have a valid, unexpired reflexology license
issued by the division. The manager in charge shall maintain a list of all employees
and independent contractors working at the reflexology establishment each day and
their license numbers. Such list shall be available for viewing by agents or officers
of the division, code enforcement, police department or state or county regulatory
agencies at all times the establishment is open for the conduct of business.

E.

All reflexologists, employees, and managers in charge shall at all times while working
in a reflexology establishment or providing reflexology services, either carry on
their person or otherwise have present at the location where they are working, government-issued
identification. It shall be unlawful for any employee, independent reflexologist or
manager in charge to refuse to, or otherwise fail to, present his or her identification
to agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, police department or state
or county regulatory agencies if he or she is asked to do so during business hours.

F.

It is unlawful for any person in a reflexology establishment to place his/her hand
or hands upon, to touch with any part of his/her body, or to fondle in any manner,
a specified anatomical area of any patron.

G.

All reflexology establishments shall be responsible for ensuring that their establishment
remains closed to the public, with no signage indicating the establishment is open
for any purpose, if at any time an appropriately licensed reflexologist is not on
the premises to perform reflexology services.

H.

No person shall operate a reflexology establishment or administer reflexology services
for money or any other consideration between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.

I.

If an agent or officer of the division, code enforcement, police department or state
or county regulatory agency, while on the premises of a reflexology establishment,
observes that an establishment has failed to comply with any of the above-listed operating
requirements, the agent may take action as described in section 4.85.200 of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.065 - Facilities and clothing requirements.
text:
A.

Every portion of the reflexology establishment, and all chairs, towels, water basins
and seating areas used for reflexology services shall be kept clean and operated in
a sanitary condition.

B.

Exterior windows of the reflexology establishment shall not be tinted, covered or
blocked so as to impede a view inside the establishment from the exterior. Tint shall
be no lower than 50 percent with a maximum of ten percent exterior reflectance not
including the glass.

C.

All front reception, hallway and front exterior doors (except back or rear exterior
doors used only for employee entrance to and exit from the reflexology establishment
and patron restroom doors) shall be kept unlocked during business hours. No electronic,
automatic, combination, or other locking device may be utilized on any interior door
which is required to remain unlocked.

D.

Reflexology establishments shall only provide or permit reflexology services in an
unenclosed area within the reflexology establishment. If walls, barriers, or structures,
whether temporary, movable or permanent, are used to separate or divide portions of
the reflexology establishment, such wall, barrier or structure shall not be taller
than three feet in height, as measured from the finished floor of the reflexology
establishment.

E.

All reflexology establishments shall ensure that all employees, independent reflexologists,
agents or representatives are completely clothed at all times while on the premises
of a reflexology establishment, regardless of whether such person is providing reflexology
services. Outer garments must be clean, must not be torn, must be opaque and must
be in good repair.

For purposes of this subsection, the term "completely clothed" means:

1.

With respect to the upper body:

a.

For women, wearing undergarments;

b.

For men and women, wearing either a blouse or shirt with sleeves and which shall cover
the entire torso from the neck to the waist.

2.

With respect to the lower body for both men and women, wearing appropriate undergarments
plus either pants or a skirt which must cover from the waist down to a point at least
two inches above the knee.

3.

Undergarments shall not be exposed to a patron or other person on the premises of
a reflexology establishment at any time.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.070 - Unlawful acts.
text:
It shall be unlawful for:

A.

A reflexologist to use lotions, creams, or mechanical devices in the application of
reflexology.

B.

A reflexologist to diagnose or treat for specific diseases, practice spinal or other
joint manipulations, prescribe or adjust medication, or prescribe or administer vitamins.

C.

Reserved.

D.

Any individual that is not a customer, employee, independent contractor or owner of
the licensed establishment to be present in any area of the business identified as
designated for employees only or intended for patron services.

E.

Any person to possess any alcoholic beverages on the premises of any reflexology establishment.

F.

Gaming (as defined in this title) to occur on the premises wherein the practice of
business of reflexology is conducted.

G.

Subsections E and F shall not apply in cases where the reflexology establishment is
located within a facility such as, but not limited to, a hotel, a hotel/gaming establishment,
athletic club, etc. where alcohol or gaming are legally permitted. This prohibition
of alcoholic beverages and gaming shall only apply to the area of the primary facility
dedicated to the use of the reflexology establishment.

H.

A reflexology establishment, employee, independent reflexologist, agent, representative
or patron thereof, to engage in or solicit sexual activity from any person, at any
time within a reflexology establishment, whether or not the sexual activity occurs
during the course of performing reflexology on a person, even if the person consents
to the sexual activity. It shall also be a violation if the, employee, independent
reflexologist, agent, or representative, initiates sexual activity with or encourages
sexual activity from a patron, regardless of whether the sexual activity actually
occurs.

I.

Any employee, owner or any other person to use the reflexology establishment premises
as a residence or sleeping quarters.

J.

Any person affiliated with the reflexology establishment to fail to allow any agent
or officers of the division, code enforcement, police department or state or county
regulatory agency access to the premises for administrative inspections or to hinder
such agent or officer while performing such inspection.

K.

A reflexology establishment to employ any person who is not legally qualified to work
in the United States.

L.

Any reflexology establishment owner or manager in charge to fail to report to the
division any arrest that occurs on the premises of the reflexology establishment of
which it has actual or constructive knowledge, within three calendar days of the arrest,
regardless of whether the person arrested is an employee, independent contractor,
patron or other person if the arrest is related to activities that occurred on the
premises of the reflexology establishment.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.075 - License not transferable—Change of location.
text:
A.

No reflexology establishment license is transferable for any reason. A reflexology
establishment license is conferred only to the licensee named therein. Upon the sale
or transfer of any interest in a reflexology establishment, other than as described
in section 4.85.045, the business license for that reflexology establishment shall be null and void.
A new application pursuant to this chapter shall be made by any person who, by reason
of such sale or transfer, desires to own or operate the establishment.

B.

A reflexology establishment that has undergone a sale or transfer of ownership may
continue to operate while the new owner(s) are going through the approval process
provided that the new owner applies for and receives a temporary license in accordance
with section 4.04.025. In order for the reflexology establishment to operate pursuant to this section,
a reflexology establishment must have an approved manager in charge on the premises
at all times the reflexology establishment is open for business. Allowing an applicant
to continue to operate pending approval of the applicant's license shall in no way
guaranty that an applicant will be granted a license if the applicant does not satisfy
the license requirements or is otherwise disqualified from being licensed. Any costs
or expenses incurred by an applicant prior to issuance of its license are solely at
the applicant's risk.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.080 - Outcall treatment.
text:
There shall be no outcall reflexology services. There shall be no outcall massage
therapy services provided on the premises of a reflexology establishment.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.100 - Disciplinary action—License suspension, revocation or limitation.
text:
Any activity on the part of a reflexologist or reflexology establishment, manager
in charge, or the employees, agents, or representatives or any of the foregoing, which
is contrary to the public health, safety, morals, good order, or general welfare of
the residents of the city or that violates any city ordinance, state law or regulation
may be grounds for the issuance of criminal citations, notices of violation, civil
penalties, and/or the suspension, limitation or revocation of the relevant license
or suitability classification. Disciplinary action may also be imposed for any of
the following:

A.

Doing or failing to do any act which would make one unqualified to hold a license
under the provisions of this chapter;

B.

Performing reflexology or operating a reflexology establishment in an unlawful manner
or in a manner detrimental to the public health, safety or welfare, or in violation
of any of the provisions of this chapter;

C.

Knowingly failing to report or concealing from proper authority any information which
it is the licensee's duty to supply under this chapter or any statute, ordinance or
regulation of the state or the city;

D.

Becoming ineligible to hold a reflexology license as set out in the statutes and ordinances
of the state or city after a reflexology license has been issued;

E.

Making a misrepresentation of a material fact in his application to obtain a license;
or

F.

Conduct on the part of any person that results in a person being charged with solicitation
of prostitution on the premises of any reflexology establishment, within the preceding
three-year period.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.110 - Obtaining a license after revocation—Prohibition.
text:
No reflexology establishment or reflexologist license shall be granted, and any existing
reflexology establishment or reflexologist license may be revoked, suspended, or limited,
with respect to any person whose reflexologist, reflexology establishment, business
or other similar license was revoked or suspended in any jurisdiction, for the period
of two years following the date of such revocation or suspension. The prohibition
on granting a license, or revoking or suspending an existing license, shall also apply
to the spouse, family member, or business associate of, or any person who holds more
than a ten percent ownership interest in, such business whose license was revoked
or suspended.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.85.200 - Enforcement authority.
text:
A.

The director and agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, police department
or state or county regulatory agencies shall enforce the provisions of this chapter.

B.

Such enforcement power shall include, but not be limited to, the power to issue notices
of violation of this chapter and civil penalties up to $500.00 for each violation
for each day or any portion thereof during which the violation occurs or continues,
and the power to serve notices of correction, issue orders of suspension or limitation,
declare nuisances, prohibit unlawful business activities, prevent activities in contravention
of the licensing ordinances, initiate suspension, revocation or limitation of licenses
pursuant to chapter 4.06 and to perform all other duties relating to licensing enforcement as provided in
this title. In addition, those persons identified in subsection A of this section
shall have the authority to prepare, sign and serve misdemeanor citations pursuant
to NRS Chapter 171, as may be amended or renumbered, to enforce the provisions of
this title.

C.

The director or his designee shall have the authority to issue a "red tag/stop work
order" for the following reasons:

1.

No manager in charge is present on the premises during business hours;

2.

No licensed reflexologist is on the premises during business hours;

3.

Refusal of the manager in charge, owner or employee to allow agents or officers of
the division, code enforcement, police department or state or county regulatory agencies
onto the premises for inspection to verify compliance with the provisions of this
chapter;

4.

Occurrence of a crime on the premises;

5.

Existence of a threat to the public health, safety, welfare or morals;

6.

A third violation of this chapter by any reflexologist, employee or the reflexology
establishment (or combination thereof) in a six-month period;

7.

Failure to comply with a plan of correction established between the division and the
reflexology establishment or reflexologist during the time provided for in the plan
of correction; or

8.

Upon notice from a governmental agency of discipline against the reflexology establishment,
its employees or independent reflexologists that indicate continued operation may
be a threat to the safety, welfare, health or morals of the city.

The "red tag/stop work order" shall direct the unlicensed person, the reflexologist
or reflexology establishment or its or their employees that are providing services
in violation of this chapter to cease and desist from the activity or activities designated
in the order. The "red tag/stop work order" shall be given in writing by the director
or its designee to the reflexology establishment, its manager in charge, agents, independent
reflexologists or employees, clearly stating the violation(s) being committed. The
director or its designee shall affix a copy of the "red tag/stop work order" on the
public entrance(s) of the establishment in a prominent location. It shall be unlawful
for any person to remove the "red tag/stop work order" from the public entrance(s)
of the establishment without the express written authorization of the director or
its designee.

D.

Any violation of a "red tag/stop work order" in subsection C of this section shall
be deemed a separate violation of this chapter and shall be cause to suspend, limit
and/or revoke the reflexology establishment or reflexologist license and a citation
and/or civil penalty may be issued for each violation, for each and every day of continued
violation.

E.

When, in the course of enforcing the provisions of this title relative to emergency
suspension or a "red tag/stop work order," the division shall have the authority to
lock and seal the premises where the reflexology services are being provided.

F.

Any agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, police department or state
or county regulatory agencies authorized pursuant to this chapter, chapter 4.04 or
any state statute or regulation shall have access to every part and portion of the
premises on which reflexology services are provided at any time when such business
is open for the transaction of business, and after regular business hours if business
is still being conducted, for the purpose of determining that the provisions of this
chapter are being complied with. It shall be unlawful for any person to fail to allow
any such agents or officers of the division, code enforcement, police department or
state or county regulatory agencies access to the premises or to hinder such representative
in any manner.

G.

Failure of the director or the officers or agents of the division, code enforcement,
police department or state or county regulatory agency to discover violations and/or
take action to enforce any regulation shall not constitute a forfeiture or waiver
of the right to take appropriate action at any time thereafter. Nothing in this chapter
shall be construed as requiring the officers or agents of the division, code enforcement,
police department or any state or county regulatory agency to impose any penalty on
a reflexology establishment or reflexologist, if the division deems the matter giving
rise to a notice of violation has been corrected.

H.

This section is supplemental to, and not exclusive of, enforcement powers available
to other officials regarding this title.

(Ord. No. 3304, § 3, 10-20-2015)

heading: 4.110.010 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, or the words are otherwise
defined below, the words and terms used in this chapter have the definitions set out
in chapter 4.04.

Adult bookstore, adult novelty business, or adult video store means an establishment having as a significant portion of its stock in trade in any
one or more of the following:

1.

Books, film, digital video discs, compact discs, video cassettes, slides, magazines,
and other periodicals or other written, oral, or visual representations that are distinguished
or characterized by an emphasis on depicting or describing sexual conduct or specified
anatomical areas; or

2.

Instruments or devices that are designed for or marketed primarily for stimulation
of human genital organs or for sadomasochistic use or abuse of self or others.

A "significant portion of its stock in trade" exists where the establishment maintains
greater than 30 percent of its floor space for the display, sale, and/or rental of
said items.

Adult club means a public or private establishment, which may charge admission for entrance,
that regularly features nude or topless entertainers, bottomless entertainers, strippers,
exotic dancers, or other live performances that are distinguished or characterized
by the exposure of specified anatomical areas or that advertises, or holds out to

that a separation and/or barrier that prevents physical contact between performers
and customers is maintained at all times during each performance.

Adult motion picture theater means an enclosed building, or a portion thereof, used for presenting motion pictures,
films, video cassette, compact disc or digital video disc recordings, slide photographs,
or other motion or still pictures, that are distinguished or characterized by an emphasis
on depicting or describing sexual conduct or specified anatomical areas.

Adult video arcade means any establishment, or any portion thereof, containing any manually operated,
coin or slug operated, or electrically or electronically operated or controlled, still,
motion picture, film, compact disc, digital video disc, or video cassette machines,
projectors, players, or other image producing devices that are maintained to display
images to one or more persons per machine or per viewing room at any one time, and
where the images so displayed are distinguished or characterized by an emphasis on
depicting or describing sexual conduct or specified anatomical areas.

Attendant means a natural person, who is employed by or who received any monetary consideration
from an adult club for soliciting the sale or purchase of any product or service,
including but not limited to beverages, and/or who collects entry fee, admission or
cover charge.

Commercial adult establishment means any establishment other than an adult club that provides the performance of
any lawful service, or any other lawful business activity, profession or calling,
to include, but not be limited to, car washes, cosmetology or barber services, maid

written, oral or otherwise, that their services, professions or callings are to be
performed in clothing such as, but not limited to, nude, topless, lingerie, g-strings,

Escort means any person who, for any form of consideration or gratuity, or no fee, dates,

or similar service personnel whose relationship with their patron is characterized

who provide a service not principally characterized as dating or socializing. This

as singing telegrams, birthday greetings or similar activities characterized by appearances
in a public place, contracted by a party other than the person for whom the service
is being performed and of a duration of no longer than one hour.

Escort service means an individual or entity, which, for any form of consideration or gratuity,
or for no fee, furnishes or offers to furnish escorts, or provides or offers to introduce
patrons to escorts.

Film, compact disc, digital video disc, video cassette or other media viewing device means, but is not limited to, any digital, electric, electronic, mechanical, magnetic,
optical, laser, holographic, virtual reality, or other technology that, through a
controlled viewing or projection device, produces a controlled visible image that
is either still or in motion, to patrons, the temporary use of which is contingent
upon the payment of some consideration and which use is to occur upon the premises.

Fondle or caress means the conduct or affectionate touching that is intended to sexually arouse (may
include "sexual conduct").

Governmental offices means any building that is used by the federal, state or local government, and is
open to the general public.

Nude modeling agency means any person, agency, firm, corporation, partnership, or any other entity or
individual that furnishes, books or otherwise engages or offers to furnish, book or
otherwise engage the service of a person for performance or appearance at an establishment
licensed pursuant to this chapter as an adult club, commercial adult establishment,
or nude modeling studio.

Nude modeling studio means any place where, for any form of consideration or gratuity, figure models,
who display specified anatomical areas, are provided to be observed, sketched, drawn,
painted, sculptured, photographed, or similarly depicted by persons paying such consideration
or gratuity. This section excludes "arts" classes sanctioned by the Board of Regents
of the University of Nevada or any other postsecondary educational institution that
is licensed by a federal or state agency and is accredited by a nationally recognized
educational accrediting association.

An offer to provide acts of sexual conduct means to offer, propose or to solicit to provide sexual conduct to a patron. Such
definition includes all conversations, publications, advertisements, handbills and
acts which would lead a reasonably prudent person to conclude that such acts were
to be provided even if such acts are illegal or are purported to be illegal or unlawful.

Operation means the conduct of any business regulated or licensed by this chapter.

Patron means any person who contracts with or employs any escort services or escort, outcall
promoter or outcall entertainer, or the customer of any other business licensed pursuant
to this chapter.

Outcall means the business procedures whereby one or more persons are sent or referred to
a location by another person or business entity for any form of consideration or gratuity,
or no fee.

Outcall entertainer shall have the same meaning as escort.

Outcall promoter shall have the same meaning as escort service.

Prostitution means engaging in sexual intercourse, oral-genital, oral-anal, or anal-genital contact,
or any touching of the sexual organs, pubic region or male or female breast of a person

for a fee, monetary consideration, or other thing of value.

Public park means a tract of land maintained by federal, state or local government for the recreation

Religious assembly means a building in which persons regularly assemble for worship, intended primarily
for purposes connected with faith, or, for propagating a particular belief form.

School means a licensed child care facility, grades preschool through grade 12, together
with the playgrounds, dormitories, stadiums, and other structures or grounds used

Server means a natural person who is employed by or who receives any monetary consideration
from an adult club for soliciting the sale or purchase of any product or service,
including but not limited to beverages.

Sexual conduct and specified anatomical areas as used in this chapter means:

1.

"Sexual conduct" includes the following:

The fondling or other touching of human genitals, pubic region, buttocks, or male
or female breasts;

b.

Ultimate sex acts, normal or perverted, actual or simulated, including intercourse,
oral copulation and sodomy;

c.

Masturbation;

d.

Excretory functions, alone, as part of, or in connection with, any of the activities
set forth in paragraphs a., b. and c. of this subsection; and

e.

Flagellation or torture by or upon a person clad in undergarments, a mask or bizarre

2.

"Specified anatomical areas" include the following:

a.

above the top of the areola;

b.

Human male genitals in a discernibly turgid state, even if completely covered.

Sex club means any establishment that is operated and maintained for the purpose of allowing
one or more persons to view or participate in live sexual conduct for consideration
or a gratuity. A sex club is prohibited and is a public nuisance per se.

Note—
This definition shall not be construed to apply to the non-obscene presentation, showing
or performance of any play, dance, erotic dance, drama, ballet, concert, or similar
performance in any theater, concert hall, fine arts academy, school, institution of
higher education, business or similar establishment as a form of expression of opinion
