heading: Chapter 5.28 - TREES AND PLANTS
text: Sections:

heading: 5.28.010 - Duties of abutting landowners.
text:
It shall be the duty of any person growing a tree, plant or shrub on his property
to keep such tree, plant or shrub from encroaching upon or obstructing the abutting
or adjacent streets, sidewalks and public parks, buildings and grounds by:

A.

Trimming or removing his tree, plant or shrub so as not to constitute, in the opinion
of the building director or his code enforcement officer, a hazard to any member of
the public or render unsafe in any manner whatsoever any public place and/or right-of-way;

B.

Treating or removing any tree, plant or shrub so diseased or insect-ridden as to constitute
a hazard to the public or to any tree, plant or shrub in public places.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: 5.28.020 - Authority to order the treatment, trimming or removal of trees, plants and shrubs.
text:
The building director or his code enforcement officer shall have the authority to
order the treatment, trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub upon private
property when he shall find such action necessary to public safety and/or health or
to prevent the spread of disease or insects to public trees, plants or shrubs or any
public place.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: 5.28.030 - Procedure upon order to treat, trim or remove.
text:
When the building director or his code enforcement officer shall find it warranted
to order the treatment, trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub, as authorized
in section 5.28.020, he shall serve a written order to correct the dangerous or unsafe condition upon
the owner, lessee or occupant of the private property by one of the following methods
of service:

A.

By making personal delivery of the order to the owner, lessee or occupant of the private
property where the dangerous or unsafe condition exists or originates;

B.

By leaving the order with some person of suitable age and discretion upon the premises;

C.

By affixing a copy of the order to the door at the premises in violation;

D.

By mailing a copy of the order to the last known address of the owner of the premises,
by certified mail, return receipt requested;

E.

Only if the above four methods of service are impractical, by publishing a copy of
the order in a local newspaper once a week, for three consecutive weeks.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: 5.28.040 - Action upon noncompliance.
text:
When a person to whom an order is directed shall fail to comply within five days of
service of the order, the building director may remedy the condition or contract with
others for such purpose and charge the cost thereof to the person to whom the order
is directed. The person remedying a condition hereunder shall be authorized to enter
the premises for that purpose.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: 5.28.050 - Collection of delinquent charge.
text:
When the city or other person with whom the city has contracted has effected the treatment,
trimming or removal of any tree, plant or shrub pursuant to this chapter, the cost
thereof, plus accrued interest at the rate of ten percent per annum from the date
of the completion of the work shall be charged to the owner of the private property.
Such charge shall constitute a lien upon the real property of such owner until such
charge is paid, as well as constitute a debt of the record owner of the property and
of the person occupying such premises to the city. The city may bring a civil action
in any court of competent jurisdiction to recover such charge, or follow the lien
procedures set forth in section 15.12.060(N)(3)(e).

(Ord. No. 3082, § 1, 11-5-2013; Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: 5.28.060 - Penalty.
text:
Any person who, having been served with a written order as provided in HMC [section]
5.28.030, and fails to comply therewith, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor. Each day
such a violation is committed or permitted to continue shall constitute a separate
offense.

(Ord. 1234 (part), 1991)

heading: Title 6 - CIVIL SERVICE RULES[1]
text:
Footnotes:
--- (1) ---

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3267, §§ 1, 2, adopted May 19, 2015, repealed and reenacted title 6 in its entirety to
read as herein set out. Formerly, title 6, chapters 6.04—6.44, pertained to civil
service, and derived from Ord. No. 2147, § 1, adopted in 2003, and Ord. No. 2745,
§ 1, adopted in 2008.

Note—
For benefits for unclassified employees, see chapter 2.34, Unclassified Employees.

heading: 6.01.010 - Purpose.
text:
The purpose of these rules is to establish methods, practices and procedures to ensure
fair and effective human resources administration. The terms and conditions of employment
for covered positions shall be governed by the civil service rules. As provided by
the Henderson City Charter, the civil service rules set forth provisions that concern:

A.

Examination of potential employees;

B.

Procedures for recruitment and placement;

C.

Procedures for reductions in force;

D.

Procedures for disciplinary actions against, and the discharge of, employees; and

E.

Procedures for hearing employee appeals and taking final action.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.020 - Persons covered under the civil service rules.
text:
A.

Pursuant to the Henderson City Charter, the civil service rules are applicable to
and govern the employment of certain non-represented full-time employees of the city
who have successfully completed their probationary period. Pursuant to Section 24
and 26 of Senate Bill No. 440, a person holding any of the positions below, before,
on or after October 1, 2013, is not covered by the civil service rules:

1.

Executive officers;

2.

Senior department directors;

3.

Department directors;

4.

Division heads (including assistant directors);

5.

Assistant city attorneys;

6.

Any other attorney employed by the office of the city attorney;

7.

Assistants to the city manager;

8.

The municipal court administrator;

9.

Any elected officer;

10.

Any employee that reports directly to an elected officer;

11.

Any probationary employee;

12.

Any employee covered under a collective bargaining agreement, unless otherwise stated
in the collective bargaining agreements;

13.

Any seasonal or temporary employee;

14.

Any part-time employee;

15.

Volunteers (including but not limited to, reserve fire officers, reserve police, reserve
marshals, who receive no regular salary from the city); and/or

16.

Independent contractors.

B.

Employees covered under the civil service rules have classified positions. The employees
identified in subsection A. are considered to hold unclassified positions.

C.

The rules and regulations adopted in this title shall be made available to each employee
holding a classified position. The civil service rules are maintained with the human
resources department and the city clerk's office.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.030 - Amendments to the civil service rules.
text:
A.

The city manager, (or designee) and director of human resources (or designee) shall
review the civil service rules on an annual basis. Proposed amendments shall be submitted
to the civil service board who will then review and recommend the proposed amendments
to the Henderson city council.

B.

The civil service rules are codified in the Henderson Municipal Code ("HMC"), title 6. The Henderson city council must adopt the civil service rules and any amendments
thereto. If not otherwise specified, the civil service rules and amendments thereto,
are effective after they are approved by the Henderson city council and published
in accordance with the Henderson City Charter.

C.

The civil service rules are subject to change at any time pursuant to this section.
These rules do not constitute a contract between employees in a classified position
and the city.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.040 - Other city policies and procedures.
text:
A.

Employees covered under the civil service rules are required to follow all City of
Henderson policies, procedures and directives, including the Henderson City Charter
and all applicable sections of the HMC, unless a policy, procedure, or directive specifically
excludes classified positions. If there is an inconsistency between the civil service
rules and any of the City of Henderson policies, procedures and/or directives, then
the civil service rules shall prevail.

B.

A department may establish rules regarding employee conduct and performance to promote
the efficient and orderly operation of the department, as long as such rules are not
inconsistent with the City of Henderson policies, procedures and directives, the HMC,
the Henderson City Charter, or the civil service rules.

1.

Department rules and amendments related to employment practices must be approved by
the director of human resources (or designee).

2.

Department rules shall be made available to the employees in the affected department.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.050 - Equal opportunity policy.
text:
The City of Henderson is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions
on the basis of merit. In accordance with applicable law, the city prohibits discrimination
based on race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, age, national origin or ancestry,
disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, status as HIV positive, genetic information,
gender identity and expression, or any other consideration protected by federal, state
or local laws. All such discrimination is prohibited. The city's commitment to equal
opportunity employment applies to all persons involved in the operations of the city
and prohibits discrimination by any employee or agent of the city. For additional
information, please refer to the City of Henderson's policies regarding its commitment
to equal employment opportunities.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.060 - Accommodation requests.
text:
To comply with applicable laws ensuring equal employment opportunities to qualified
individuals with disabilities, the city will make reasonable accommodations for the
known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified individual with a disability
who is an applicant or an employee, unless undue hardship or a direct threat would
occur as a result.

Any applicant or employee who requires an accommodation in order to perform the essential
functions of the job they hold or desire to hold should contact human resources and
request such an accommodation in accordance with the city's policies and procedures.
Once an accommodation has been requested, the city will investigate these barriers
or limitations and then identify what possible accommodations, if any, will help to
eliminate the barrier(s) or limitation(s). If the requested accommodation is reasonable
and will not impose an undue hardship or a direct threat, the city will make the accommodation
in accordance with applicable law. The city may propose an alternative to the requested
accommodation or substitute one reasonable accommodation for another, but the city
retains the ultimate discretion to choose between reasonable accommodations.

The accommodation process is interactive, and it may take multiple conversations between
the city and the requesting individual before an accommodation is reached. Employees
are expected to fully cooperate in the accommodation process, including making every
effort to provide management with current medical information. Employees who do not
meaningfully cooperate in the accommodation process waive the right to accommodation.
For additional information, please refer to the City of Henderson's policies and procedures
that relate to accommodation requests.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.070 - Prohibited harassment.
text:
The city maintains a policy strictly prohibiting sexual harassment and harassment
because of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, age, national origin or ancestry,
disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, status as HIV positive, genetic information,
gender identity and expression, or any other consideration protected by federal, state
or local laws. This policy applies to all persons involved in the operations of the
city and prohibits such harassment by any employee or agent of the city, including
supervisors and co-workers. The city's policies and procedures also prohibit harassment
by visitors, clients, vendors or other service providers at our facilities. Prohibited
harassment will not be tolerated. The city is committed to taking all reasonable steps
to prevent such harassment from occurring. For additional information, please refer
to the City of Henderson's policies on maintaining a harassment free workplace.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.01.080 - Prohibited retaliation.
text:
Applicable law and the City of Henderson's policies and procedures prohibit retaliation
against any employee for opposing, reporting or threatening to report prohibited discrimination
or harassment, or for participating in any manner in an investigation, proceeding
or hearing regarding prohibited discrimination or harassment. The city will not retaliate
against employees who complain of prohibited discrimination or harassment and will
not permit such retaliation by its employees. Complaints of prohibited retaliation
should immediately be reported to the employee's supervisor and/or human resources
in accordance with the City of Henderson's policies and procedures.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.02.010 - Civil service board selection and composition.
text:
A.

The civil service board shall be composed of five persons appointed by a majority
vote of the city council.

B.

Members of the civil service board shall be appointed by vote of the City Council
at a public meeting to serve for staggered terms lasting up to three years and may
serve no more than three terms.

C.

The civil service board shall meet annually (or additionally, as needed), and by majority
vote, select a chairperson and vice-chairperson for that calendar year or until the
first meeting of the Board in the following year.

D.

A member of the civil service board may be removed immediately for good cause prior
to the expiration of the term by a majority vote of the city council. Removal for
good cause means that the basis for removal is not for any arbitrary, capricious,
or illegal reason and is based on facts (1) supported by substantial evidence, and
(2) reasonably believed to be true. City Council has the sole discretion to determine
if good cause exists.

E.

A member of the civil service board shall automatically be removed if they miss more
than two meetings in one calendar year period. A member may be removed by a majority
vote of the city council if they fail to respond to communications related to their
responsibilities on the civil service board.

F.

A member of the civil service board may resign from their position by submitting a
written resignation letter to the director of human resources. The civil service board
member should provide at least two weeks' notice to the director of human resources
in order to allow for the city council to find a replacement.

G.

The director of human resources (or designee) will serve as secretary to the civil
service board. The secretary of the board (or designee) shall have the authority to
set the time and place of the annual regular meeting, and shall provide notice of
such meeting in accordance with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws (set forth in Nevada Revised
Statutes Chapter 241). The secretary does not have any voting authority.

H.

Special meetings may be convened at the call of the chairperson, the secretary of
the board, or by any two members of the civil service board after reasonable public
notice and notice to the remaining members of the civil service board (in compliance
with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws set forth in Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 241).

I.

The civil service board shall have the authority to hear appeals in the method provided
by these rules from an employee who has requested an appeal that is receivable under
these rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.02.020 - Meetings.
text:
A.

The chairperson, or in the absence of the chairperson, the vice-chairperson, shall
preside at all meetings of the civil service board. If neither the chairperson nor
the vice-chairperson is present, the secretary shall preside over the meeting.

B.

No business may be transacted and no action may be taken unless a quorum is present.
A quorum shall consist of a minimum of three members.

C.

Notice of all meetings shall be given in accordance with Nevada's Open Meeting Laws
(set forth in Nevada Revised Statutes Chapter 241).

(Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.02.030 - Recusal of a civil service board member.
text:
A.

Civil service board members are responsible for complying with the HMC chapter 2.40, including the provisions regarding disclosing conflicts of interest and recusing
themselves where appropriate.

B.

In compliance with HMC section 2.40.060, Civil service board members, even if they do not intend to recuse themselves, shall,
prior to the beginning of the hearing, disclose on the record any facts that could
reasonably create the appearance that their impartiality could be affected.

C.

Pursuant to HMC section 2.40.060, a civil service board member who has a conflict of interest in regard to a particular
matter that would materially affect the independence of judgment of a reasonable person
in their situation shall recuse themselves and abstain from voting on the matter.

D.

The employee or the city, prior to the beginning of a hearing, may ask for the disqualification
of any civil service board member(s). The request may be based on the disclosures
of a civil service board member, if any, or other facts relating to the particular
civil service board member. If the employee or the city is relying on evidence from
a third party, the evidence shall be presented in an affidavit.

E.

Before a civil service board member may be disqualified, upon the request of the employee
or the city, the board must vote and approve of the disqualification. A member may
be disqualified from the hearing by at least two votes from the civil service board
members who have not been challenged.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.03.010 - Job descriptions.
text:
A.

All classified positions are assigned an appropriate job description. The human resources
department and department directors are responsible for the content of each job description.

B.

At a minimum, each job description shall include a reference to the following: (1)
the job title; (2) essential functions; (3) minimum qualifications including physical
requirements, education, training, experience, licenses, certifications, and/or special
requirements; and (4) knowledge, skills and abilities. Job descriptions shall be deemed
a summary of the essential work required but will not necessarily include all duties
to be performed in a particular position.

C.

All new and revised job descriptions are effective upon the approval of the director
of human resources (or designee).

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.03.020 - Compensation plan.
text:
A.

The director of human resources shall recommend a compensation plan to the city manager.
The city reserves the right to alter the compensation plan in accordance with the
City Charter and the HMC, and any other relevant laws, policies and procedures.

B.

Compensation modifications that differ from the approved budget are subject to available
funding.

(Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.03.030 - Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation.
text:
A.

Employees who have not been subject to a performance improvement plan or a return-to-work/last
chance agreement in the previous 12 months and/or issued disciplinary action consisting
of a suspension, may be eligible for an annual pay adjustment and general increase,
provided said compensation is approved by the city and funded in the city's annual
budget.

B.

If approved by the city, annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation is
still subject to funding availability and is in no way guaranteed. Annual pay adjustment
and general increase compensation may be paid in the form of a salary increase or
as a one-time lump sum payment or both.

C.

Salary assignments, adjustments, and/or lump-sum bonus payments are not subject to
appeal through these rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.03.030 from "Pay-for-performance"
to "Annual pay adjustment and general increase compensation." The historical notation
has been preserved for reference purposes.

heading: 6.04.010 - Job postings.
text:
A.

Vacancies may be filled from an existing eligibility list. If there is no eligibility
list or the list is expired, the vacancy may be posted to create an eligibility list.

B.

The director of human resources (or designee) may elect to post internally/departmentally,
city-wide, or as permitted in subsection 6.04.070(B) or externally, based upon the business needs of the city. The vacancy shall be
posted for a minimum of seven calendar days or limited by a predetermined number of
applications. Application materials must be completed in their entirety and submitted
by the posted closing date and time.

C.

The posted vacancy shall specify the title and salary range of the vacant position,
a brief summary of the position's essential duties, the minimum qualifications and
the final date upon which employment applications shall be accepted, unless the posting
is open and continuous.

D.

Probationary employees shall be eligible to apply for vacancies for which they are
qualified. However, a new probationary period will apply if selected to fill the vacancy.

E.

The director of human resources (or designee) may choose to consider applicants who
have applied to job postings for classifications within the same job series or job
family (as determined by human resources), or for classifications in which the qualifications
are sufficiently similar to conclude that the applicant on the eligibility list are
likely to be competent for the vacancy in question. These classifications must be
within the same or lower pay level as the posted position. The candidate must meet
the minimum qualifications of that classification and may be required to pass any
applicable assessments. Eligibility for consideration extends up to one year from
the date of application or the date the eligibility list expires (whichever is later).

F.

Upon approval, a temporary and part-time employee who has worked at least 988 continuous
hours (with no separation of employment) in that classification, meets the minimum
qualifications of the position, and was hired through a competitive process into that
temporary or part-time classification may have their position converted to a full-time
position or may be placed into a vacant full-time position in the same classification,
without the requirement to post the position. These transactions require approval
from the director of human resources (or designee). If the change affects the staff
complement (i.e., position conversions), additional approvals may be required.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Note—
Former section 6.04.030.

heading: 6.04.020 - Employment application process.
text:
A.

For every posted vacancy, each candidate must complete the employment application
materials and may be required to provide evidence of education, training, relevant
experience or other requirements and certifications for the relevant classification.

B.

The city may reject application materials for any of the reasons below, including,
but not limited to:

1.

The candidate does not have a legal right to work in the United States;

2.

The application materials are incomplete;

3.

The application materials are not submitted by the job posting deadline;

4.

The application materials do not demonstrate that the candidate meets minimum qualifications;

5.

The candidate was previously terminated for-cause (the city may consider the circumstances
surrounding the for-cause termination and the time that has passed before making a
hiring decision); and

6.

The candidate previously applied and was denied the position because they failed the
background review process (the city shall consider the circumstances pertaining to
the background failure, the time that has passed, and city policy before making a
hiring decision).

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Note—
