heading: 6.04.030 - Application materials review and assessment process.
text:
A.

Application materials will be reviewed for completeness, timeliness, and to determine
if the candidate meets the minimum qualifications for the classification for which
they applied.

B.

Assessment processes will be conducted and administered at the discretion of the city.
The city reserves the right to modify the selection and assessment process in accordance
with accepted legal, ethical and professional standards.

C.

The purpose of the assessment process is to evaluate candidates in order to identify
those who are best qualified to continue in the recruitment process. Candidates will
be evaluated on the information supplied in their application materials and may be
given any combination of written, oral, physical agility or performance skills assessments
in accordance with applicable federal and state laws and standards. Only the best-qualified
candidates will be invited to move forward.

D.

The human resources department shall have full responsibility for the design, development,
and administration of the assessment process to include contracting with a third party
as required by statute or normal course of business.

E.

Candidates with disabilities who require accommodation in the assessment process shall
contact the human resources department to request assistance prior to the closing
date of the recruitment. Requests may be submitted in writing, by phone, or through
another accessible method.

F.

Applicants may be disqualified if:

1.

The applicant fails to be on time for a scheduled assessment or complete an assessment
by an established deadline. Exceptions may be made for emergency situations as determined
by the human resources department;

2.

The applicant fails to follow instructions;

3.

The applicant has made a false statement or omission of any material fact, or attempted
to or practiced any deception, misrepresentation or fraud in the application, assessment,
and/or background process; and/or

4.

The candidate exhibited dishonesty, unacceptable and/or unprofessional behavior at
any time during any part of the application, assessment, and/or background process
as outlined in city policy.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.04.030 from "Application
review and assessment process" to "Application materials review and assessment process."
The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

Note—
Former section 6.04.020.

heading: 6.04.040 - Eligibility lists.
text:
A.

Eligibility lists may be created through an application materials review and/or an
assessment process.

B.

Candidates who pass either process shall be placed on an eligibility list, which may
be ranked or unranked. Candidates who have successfully completed a scored assessment
process shall be ranked in descending order based upon their overall performance.
A hiring authority may elect to interview any candidate on the eligibility list(s).

C.

Eligibility lists shall be certified by the director of human resources (or designee).
The director of human resources (or designee) may abolish an eligibility list for
legitimate business purposes, such as but not limited to: an insufficient number of
qualified candidates, and/or the job description, salary, and/or assessment for the
position has significantly changed since the position was posted.

D.

The city may elect to consider candidates from an eligibility list for a period of
12 months from the date they were placed on the list.

E.

Eligibility lists may be extended upon approval of the director of human resources
(or designee).

F.

Any person may be removed from an eligibility list for reasons listed below, or under
extenuating circumstances as determined by the director of human resources:

1.

At the candidate's request;

2.

Separation from the city;

3.

Failure to respond to inquiries or notices from the city;

4.

Failing the background review process;

5.

If an offer has been rescinded;

6.

Falsification of their application materials; and/or

7.

If the city is aware of any factual information that indicates a person is unable
or incapable of performing the functions of the job for which the person is applying
(e.g., not attaining a certification as required by the minimum qualifications for
the position).

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 4018, § 1, adopted April 2, 2024, changed the title of section 6.04.040 from "Certification
of eligibility list" to "Eligibility lists." The historical notation has been preserved
for reference purposes.

heading: 6.04.050 - Selection, offers, and appointment of employment.
text:
A.

Employment with the city is at the sole discretion of the city.

B.

Employment offers, whether to an internal or external candidate, shall be contingent
upon the successful and timely completion of a background review process, which, depending
on the position may include, but is not limited to, completion of employer forms and
documents, a criminal background check, DMV records review, education and experience
verifications, reference checks, credit check, drug screening, and physical and/or
psychological examination.

C.

Candidates who fail to respond to the city's offer of employment within three business
days shall be deemed to have declined the offer of employment; at which time it may
be rescinded.

D.

Any person whose job offer has been rescinded by the city per this section shall be
removed from an eligibility list, unless the candidate presents an explanation to
the director of human resources (or designee) deemed to be satisfactory.

E.

Any person who declines a formal offer of employment per this section may request
to remain on the eligibility list.

F.

A conditional offer may be rescinded if a candidate fails to fully cooperate with
or fails any part of the background review process.

G.

If an individual who was previously employed with the city has an interest in being
rehired to a previously held position, similar position of equal or lower pay, or
lower-level position within the same job series, they may submit a request in writing
to the director of human resources (or designee) within one year of their date of
separation from the city. Rehires may be considered if there is a current vacancy,
and if approved by the department director and the director of human resources. Rehired
employees must meet the minimum qualifications of the position and may be required
to take assessments. Rehires may be required to submit to background screenings prior
to reemployment and a probationary/qualifying period may be required and/or adjusted
based on prior time in service.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 4142, § 1, adopted January 6, 2026, changed the title of section 6.04.050 from "Selection
and appointment of employment" to "Selection, offers, and appointment of employment."
The historical notation has been preserved for reference purposes.

heading: 6.04.060 - External candidates subject to a probationary period.
text:
A.

Upon initial hire or rehire, an employee will be subject to a six-month probationary
period. Probationary periods may be extended up to a period of six additional months
upon the recommendation of a department director and approval of the director of human
resources (or designee). If an employee is on any type of leave during their probationary
period (exceeding four workdays) or is temporarily assigned to a light-duty position
(exceeding four workdays, whether consecutive or inconsecutive), the city may also
extend the probationary period.

B.

During the probationary period, a department director may recommend termination. The
director of human resources (or designee) shall have the authority to approve or deny
all recommended terminations. An employee who is terminated during the probationary
period does not have appeal rights under these civil service rules.

C.

If an employee is transferred to or selected for a different city position while serving
a probationary period, then the employee must start a new probationary period (the
full six months, subject to extension) for the new position. The employee's original
date of hire will remain their city seniority date.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.04.070 - Internal classification changes, promotions and the qualifying period.
text:
A.

Insofar as practicable and consistent with the best interest of the city, vacancies
in a classified position may be filled by internal candidates from within the city.

B.

The city manager, in conjunction with the director of human resources, may authorize
alternative internal recruitment and/or selection processes (e.g., assigning or appointing
employees to a classified position, for which they are qualified) to facilitate modifications
to the organizational structure, to enhance operational efficiencies, or to address
any other legitimate operational concerns.

C.

With approval from the director of human resources (or designee), the city may elect
to establish and utilize a transfer list to fill vacancies.

1.

Full-time non-probationary employees who are interested in transferring to the same
classification in a different department who meet the requirements of the new position
may elect to place themselves on the transfer list.

2.

Employees who are no longer eligible for transfer will be removed from the eligibility
list.

D.

Employees who meet the minimum qualifications and want to compete in the recruitment
process must submit completed application materials within the established timeframe.

E.

The application materials review and/or assessment process set forth in section 6.04.030 shall be used to determine which employees are eligible for selection, unless the
vacancy is filled as a result of an alternative internal selection process as permitted
by subsection 6.04.010(E), 6.04.010(F), or 6.04.070(B).

F.

Upon promotion, voluntary or involuntary demotion or transfer, employees will serve
a six-month qualifying period. The qualifying period may be extended for up to six
additional months upon the recommendation of the department director and approval
of the director of human resources (or designee). If an employee is on any type of
leave during their qualifying period (exceeding four workdays, whether consecutive
or inconsecutive) or is temporarily assigned to a light-duty position (exceeding four
workdays, whether consecutive or inconsecutive), the city may extend the qualifying
period.

G.

An employee who has been promoted, voluntarily or involuntarily demoted, or laterally
transferred shall be subject to the applicable performance standards of the new position.
Failure to meet performance standards during the qualifying period may result in disciplinary
action, up to and including suspension, a return to their former classification (if
such a position is available), a demotion or transfer, or termination.

H.

An employee who is suspended or terminated for failure to meet performance standards
during the qualifying period shall have the appeal rights afforded by these Rules
and set forth in chapter 6.08. However, an employee who is offered the opportunity to return to their former classification
or a similar classification (i.e., demoted), as a result of being issued disciplinary
action for failure to meet the performance standards during a qualifying period, does
not have any appeal rights under these rules.

I.

An employee who transfers from a classified position to an unclassified position or
to a position covered under a collective bargaining agreement does not retain any
rights or privileges under the civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 4018, § 1, adopted April 2, 2024, changed the title of section 6.04.070 from "Internal
transfers, promotions and the qualifying period" to "Internal classification changes,
promotions and the qualifying period." The historical notation has been preserved
for reference purposes.

heading: 6.04.080 - Recruitment concerns/complaints regarding violations of this chapter.
text:
A.

If a candidate covered under the civil service rules believes that the city violated
chapter 6.04 of these rules, they may report such violations to the director of human resources,
in writing, within seven calendar days from the date the candidate is notified of
the hiring decision. The candidate's complaint must specifically identify the civil
service rule allegedly violated and explain the reason why the candidate believes
the rule was violated. Upon timely receipt of the complaint to the director of human
resources, the director of human resources (or designee) will investigate the complaint.
A decision by the director of human resources (or designee) shall be made within 14
calendar days of receipt of the complaint. If the investigation requires additional
time, the candidate must be notified within 14 calendar days of receipt of the complaint
that the complaint has been received but that the investigation will require additional
time to conduct.

B.

If a candidate is submitting a complaint regarding the selection for a position within
the human resources department, the complaint may be submitted directly to the city
manager (or designee). The procedures for submitting a complaint to the city manager
(or designee) are the same as for submitting a complaint directly to the director
of human resources.

C.

The decision of the director of human resources (or designee) or the city manager
(or designee) shall be final.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.010 - Job abandonment.
text:
A.

An employee shall have abandoned their job if the employee fails to directly notify
their supervisor of an absence from work for three consecutive workdays. Job abandonment
shall also occur when an employee fails to return to work for three consecutive workdays
after the employee's approved leave has expired without directly notifying their supervisor
of the continuing absences and without satisfactory explanation.

B.

Before the city makes a determination that the employee has abandoned their job, the
city shall attempt to contact the employee on two separate days using either the employee's
last known home telephone number, cell phone number or email address provided to the
city by the employee. If the attempts to reach the employee are unsuccessful, the
city can conclude that the employee has abandoned their job, and the employee shall
be immediately terminated.

C.

Employees who are terminated for job abandonment do not have appeal rights under these
rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.020 - Resignation or retirement.
text:
A.

An employee's notice of resignation or retirement shall be in writing and shall be
submitted to their supervisor and/or department director. The notice shall indicate
the effective date of resignation or retirement. The notice should be submitted at
least two weeks prior to the effective date of the resignation or retirement.

B.

The notice of resignation or retirement shall be deemed accepted by the city upon
receipt by the employee's supervisor and/or department director. The supervisor and/or
department director will forward an employee's notice of resignation or retirement
to the human resources department. Once a notice is received by the employee's supervisor
and/or department director, the notice may not be withdrawn without the written approval
of the director of human resources or designee.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.030 - Reduction-in-force procedures.
text:
A.

A department director may make recommendations to the city manager regarding a reduction-in-force
if the department director believes layoffs are necessary by reason of shortage of
work or funds, the elimination of a position, organizational changes, or for any other
legitimate business or operational purposes.

B.

The city manager must approve all reductions-in-force.

C.

The city council must approve a reduction-in-force involving layoffs of five or more
non-vacant positions.

D.

After a reduction-in-force has been approved by the city manager, the city manager
(or designee) must inform the director of human resources as to the number of employees
to be laid-off within each of the affected departments and classifications, and identify
the reason (e.g., shortage of work, lack of funds, position elimination, organizational
changes or any other legitimate business reason) for the lay-offs. Once this information
is provided to the director of human resources, the human resources department shall
administer the reduction-in-force according to city seniority within the following
limitations:

1.

All probationary employees in the affected classification(s) shall be laid-off before
employees covered under the civil service rules may be impacted by the reduction-in-force.
Probationary employees shall not have displacement rights under these civil service
rules.

2.

Once all probationary employees have been laid-off in the impacted classification(s)
and department(s), then employees shall be selected for inclusion in the reduction-in-force
in the inverse order of their city seniority within the affected classification(s)
and department(s), with the last employee hired being the first selected for the reduction-in-force.
An employee loses their city seniority status for the purposes of a reduction-in-force
if they have received active discipline (as defined in HMC 6.07.050) in the form of a demotion, suspension, performance improvement plan and/or return-to-work/last
chance agreement.

3.

Employees, other than employees serving their probationary period, selected for inclusion
in the reduction-in-force shall have displacement rights.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.040 - Displacement rights.
text:
A non-probationary employee selected for inclusion in a reduction-in-force is considered
a displaced employee and shall have displacement rights. The displacement procedure
shall be administered as follows:

A.

A displaced employee may displace an employee with the least city seniority within
the same classification. Under no circumstances is a displaced employee entitled to
displace an employee with greater city seniority than the displaced employee.

B.

If the displaced employee's classification does not exist outside of their department,
or if the displaced employee does not have more seniority than a person in that classification
in a different department, then the displaced employee may displace the least senior
employee holding the same previously held classification that the displaced employee
held within the prior ten years, as long as the displaced employee is still qualified
to perform the previously held classification and the position is covered under the
Civil Service Rules. If the displaced employee has held multiple previously held classifications
during the prior ten years, they will displace the employee with the least city seniority
status (as long as the displaced employee is still qualified to perform the previously
held classification), in order of the most recently held job covered under the Civil
Service Rules.

C.

A non-probationary employee holding a classified position who is displaced pursuant
to this procedure, has the same displacement rights as a displaced employee.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.050 - Lay-offs.
text:
A.

If a displaced employee does not have a previously held classification with the city,
or has the least city seniority in the previously held classification, or is no longer
qualified or eligible to hold the previously held classification, or the classification
no longer exists, the displaced employee shall be laid-off and placed on a reinstatement
list.

B.

The director of human resources (or designee) will advise the affected employees,
within at least 30 calendar days (or the appropriate period of time required by law)
of the employees' effective lay-off date. If the city is unable to provide timely
notice, then the city shall pay the affected employees one month's wages (two pay
periods) based upon the employee's base rate of pay for their regular work schedule
earned in the prior two pay periods.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.05.060 - Reinstatement list.
text:
A laid-off employee shall be placed on a reinstatement list for the classification
they held at the time of lay-off. The laid-off employee shall remain on a reinstatement
list for the applicable classification for a period of 24 months or a period equal
to the laid-off employee's length of employment, whichever is less.

A.

Laid-off employees on a reinstatement list will be ranked in order by their city seniority
date for the classification they held at the time of being laid-off. Vacancies will
then be offered to individuals on the reinstatement list for a particular classification
in descending order of city seniority. A person must still be qualified to perform
the essential functions of the job with or without an accommodation to be eligible
for the position.

B.

A reinstatement list will have precedence over all other eligibility lists.

C.

An employee who is placed in a previously held classification as a result of being
selected from the reinstatement list must meet the minimum qualifications as listed
on the job description and successfully complete the background review process prior
to beginning the previously held classification. Once the employee starts working
with the city again, they may be required to serve a qualifying period of six months.

D.

Laid-off employees on a reinstatement list will be considered eligible for internal
recruitments, for classified positions for which they are qualified, for a period
of 24 months or a period equal to the employee's length of employment, whichever is
less. Employees selected for a classified position as a result of the internal recruitment
process, must successfully complete the background review process prior to beginning
the new classified position. Once the employee starts working with the city again,
they must serve a qualifying period of six months.

E.

Laid-off employees placed on a reinstatement list waive their reinstatement privileges
if they fail to respond to a re-employment offer within 15 calendar days after the
notice is mailed to the last known address. It is the laid-off employee's responsibility
to update the city, in writing, of any changes to their contact information.

F.

Once a laid-off employee is removed from the reinstatement list, the laid-off employee
no longer has rights under the civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.06.010 - Employee obligations.
text:
A.

Employees are required to adhere to the rules and procedures set forth in the civil
service rules, as well as to applicable regulations or policies set forth in the City
Charter, administrative policies and procedures, ethics rules, employee agreements,
department rules and any other official city rules.

B.

Employee responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

1.

Learning their official job duties and performing accordingly;

2.

Completing assigned training, and/or acquiring and/or maintaining any license(s) registration(s),
and/or certifications that are required of their position;

3.

Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with supervisors, fellow
employees and the public;

4.

Learning and adhering to city and departmental rules, regulations, and policies;

5.

Maintaining the ability to perform the essential functions of their position with
or without a reasonable accommodation;

6.

Maintaining the level of performance required of their position;

7.

Communicating any concerns regarding their employment to their supervisor and/or human
resources;

8.

Timely completion of all required self-evaluations;

9.

Attending work as scheduled, unless authorized to be absent, and taking responsibility
for initiating and obtaining any necessary authorization for such absences;

10.

Obtaining approval from their immediate supervisor, department director, and the director
of human resources to work a secondary job, including employment for third parties
or self-employment, while employed by the city; and

11.

Participating and cooperating in investigations conducted by the city.

C.

In addition to the above, employees in supervisory positions are responsible for:

1.

Providing instruction and guidance to employees in the performance of job functions;

2.

Monitoring employee performance and timely completing performance evaluations;

3.

Maintaining an open-door policy with employees, which includes being accessible to
their employees' concerns and questions;

4.

Communicating with employees about positive and negative performance;

5.

Documenting employee disciplinary matters and employee complaints; and

6.

Participating, cooperating, and potentially coordinating investigations related to
employee disciplinary matters, employee complaints, and other personnel related matters.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.06.020 - Performance evaluations.
text:
A.

Performance evaluations are meant to be beneficial to both the employer and the employee.
In addition to regular work related discussions and/or informal coaching and feedback,
supervisors shall conduct formal performance evaluations for each employee under their
supervision. All formal performance evaluations shall be completed in a timely manner,
and in a manner approved by the director of human resources (or designee). The purpose
of the performance evaluation is to review the employee's work performance, achievements,
challenges, development goals, and/or define and set clear performance expectations
where support is needed. Additionally, the performance evaluation will explain how
the employee's job duties aligns with strategic and operational goals and initiatives
for both the department and the organization. The performance evaluation also provides
an opportunity for the employee to communicate any support they need from their supervisor
and ask specific questions to help clarify their role or work.

1.

Supervisors should ensure newly hired employees understand the duties and performance
expectations for the position and provide regular feedback during a new hire's probationary
period or qualifying period. For employees who are not on a probationary period or
qualifying period, supervisors shall conduct performance evaluations on an annual
basis.

2.

Performance evaluations should recognize all aspects of an individual's job performance,
including exceptional, acceptable and substandard performance. Supervisors should
provide regular coaching and feedback to employees throughout the year and refer to
such discussions in the formal performance evaluation.

3.

Employees subject to a performance improvement plan may require additional performance
evaluations. Employees subject to a performance improvement plan will have clear actions
and accountabilities detailed in the plan, which must be satisfied during the stated
time period to avoid potential disciplinary action.

4.

Annual pay adjustment increases, general increases, and lump sum performance bonuses
are not tied to the employees' yearly performance evaluations. An employee is not
eligible for an annual pay adjustment increase, general increase or lump-sum performance
bonus if they have received active discipline (as defined in subsection 6.07.050) in the form of a demotion, suspension, performance improvement plan and/or return-to-work/last
chance agreement.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.06.030 - Recognition of exceptional performance.
text:
A.

If an employee is performing above and beyond their supervisor's expectations, the
department director (or designee) may recognize such performance in writing.

B.

Documentation of an employee's exceptional performance shall be kept in the employee's
personnel file.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.06.040 - Coaching and feedback.
text:
Supervisors are encouraged to provide employees regular coaching and feedback to assist
employees in successfully performing their jobs. Coaching and feedback should be provided
both with respect to positive and negative aspects of an employee's performance and/or
conduct. The act of providing coaching and feedback to employees is not considered
disciplinary action. Notes and/or other documentation relevant to any coaching and
counseling may be recorded in a manner (or method) approved by the director of human
resources (or designee), and are subject to standard retention/destruction schedules.
If employees fail to act on their supervisors' coaching and feedback, the supervisor
may take disciplinary action as set forth in chapter 6.07. This section shall not be construed to require coaching and feedback prior to disciplinary
action being taken.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.07.010 - Prohibited conduct.
text:
City employees are expected to maintain certain behavior and performance standards.
The following list of prohibited conduct is intended to provide examples of behavior
that can result in disciplinary action. This list is not exhaustive—other acts of
substance relating to misconduct or work performance of an employee may be considered
grounds for disciplinary action.

A.

Incompetency or inefficiency in performance of duties;

B.

Insubordination, unprofessionalism, and/or failure to perform assigned duties;

C.

Failure to comply with the requirements set forth in a performance improvement plan;

D.

Failure to complete assigned training and/or acquire and/or maintain any license(s),
registration(s) or certification(s) that are required of the employee's position;

E.

Failure to maintain the confidentiality of the city's non-public information;

F.

Failure to properly record employee's time—examples include but are not limited to,
recording the work time of another employee (unless an employee is assigned to be
a time-reporter) or allowing any other employee to record your work time (unless the
employee reports time to an assigned time-reporter), recording false time records,
manipulating time records, and not recording time worked or time off;

G.

Use of obscene, profane or abusive language and/or conduct, including malicious gossip;

H.

Careless, negligent or intentional misuse of city property, equipment, or funds, including
use for personal reasons or incidents that result in damage or risk of damage to property;

I.

Violation of a safety rule or safety practice;

J.

Taking audio or video recordings of another employee without the explicit permission
from all of the employees who are being recorded;

K.

Failure to follow established procedures in reporting a work related personal injury
or damage to city property or city equipment;

L.

Failure to cooperate in an internal investigation;

M.

Excessive tardiness or absenteeism, being absent without leave or failing to report
after leave of absence has expired, or abusing paid leave policies;

N.

Sleeping or malingering during work hours;

O.

Violation of the Civil Service Rules, HMC chapter 2.40, the Charter of the City of Henderson, administrative policies and procedures, and/or
other city or departmental rules and regulations;

P.

Conviction for, or entering a plea of guilty or no contest to any felony or misdemeanor
that is related to the employee's position, violates a city policy, creates a safety
concern, and/or involves actions that may diminish the public's trust, whether the
offense occurred on or off duty;

Q.

Discriminatory conduct, sexual harassment or harassment based on race, color, religion,
national origin, gender, age, sexual orientation, covered veteran status, pregnancy,
gender identity or expression, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic
information or any other basis made unlawful by any applicable law, ordinance or regulation
(disciplinary action based on this provision may not be appealed to the civil service
board);

R.

Engaging in disorderly conduct such as horseplay, scuffling and malicious mischief;

S.

Provoking or instigating a physical fight or fighting at any time while on duty or
at any city facility or worksite;

T.

Being under the influence of, use, possession, sale, distribution, dispensing or manufacturing
of intoxicating beverages, hallucinogens and/or controlled substances (not prescribed
or prescribed but abused/misused); failing to report potential hazards of working
while taking a prescribed medication; or use of illegal drugs while at work, or preceding
duty so as to be detected by behavior, physical condition or testing while on duty;

U.

Refusal to be tested when there is a reasonable suspicion that the employee was under
the influence of alcohol, controlled substances, hallucinogens, or illegal drugs while
at work; or if the employee is required to be tested as a result of having a commercial
driver's license;

V.

Verbal or physical conduct that is abusive, threatening, offensive or intimidating
while on duty or at any city facility or work site;

W.

Acceptance or solicitation of a bribe, improper gift/gratuity, or any compensation
intended to influence the employee in the performance of their assigned duties for
the city;

X.

Improper use of one's employment with the city for the employee's personal or financial
advantage or granting improper privilege to another;

Y.

Misappropriation, misuse, theft, negligent, careless or unauthorized use of city property
or funds and/or damage to city property;

Z.

Failure to follow a return-to-work/last chance agreement (terminations based on a
failure to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement are not
appealable); or

AA.

Dishonesty.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.07.020 - Suspension pending investigation.
text:
A.

In conjunction with human resources, the department head (or their designee) may suspend
an employee and/or place the employee on leave, with or without pay, pending an investigation
of an alleged conduct violation. Suspensions pending investigations are appropriate
where the presence of the employee is reasonably likely to:

1.

Be injurious to the employee, a fellow employee or the general public;

2.

Result in damage to property;

3.

Substantially impair management's ability to maintain decorum and discipline; and/or

4.

Hinder the investigatory process.

B.

If an employee has been suspended and/or placed on leave pending investigation, they
may not return to work or any city facility until they have received permission from
their department director (or designee). The employee may not perform any work for
the city.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.07.030 - Types of disciplinary actions.
text:
A.

Disciplinary actions. Employees may be subject to the following disciplinary actions
if they violate these rules or any other city or departmental policy and procedure:

1.

Documented verbal warning;

2.

Written reprimand;

3.

Suspension and/or a demotion (if appropriate and available), and/or subjected to a
performance improvement plan (discussed in subsection 6.07.030(B) or a return-to-work/last chance agreement (discussed in subsection 6.07.030(C); and/or

4.

Termination.

The foregoing enumeration of the types of discipline shall not be meant to set forth
any necessary sequence of progressive discipline. The type of discipline issued depends
upon the facts and circumstances of the incident. All suspensions, demotions, return-to-work/last
chance agreements, performance improvement plans and terminations must be approved
by the department director (or designee), and the director of human resources (or
designee). Transferring positions or accepting a voluntary demotion will not prevent
the employee from being disciplined for conduct that occurred prior to the transfer
or voluntary demotion.

B.

Performance improvement plans. A Performance Improvement Plan ("PIP") will typically
be used after the employee fails to improve their performance or after a failure to
correct their behavior after receipt of documented verbal warning or written reprimand.
A PIP is not considered to be a disciplinary action; however it may be utilized before
or after disciplinary action has been taken. A performance improvement plan is not
appropriate in all cases. A performance improvement plan may be appropriate if a supervisor
believes that an employee's performance will significantly improve such that the employee
will be able to successfully satisfy their job responsibilities at the conclusion
of a performance improvement plan. It is the employee's responsibility to fully understand
the provisions and requirements within the performance improvement plan. While it
is anticipated that the employee will be successful in changing and correcting their
substandard job performance, failure to remedy these deficiencies will lead to further
disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

A performance improvement plan shall include the following provisions:

1.

Description of unacceptable performance. The supervisor should identify the job functions
and/or behaviors that the employee is failing to satisfactorily perform and provide
specific examples of the deficiencies.

2.

Timeframe. The plan should identify the specific period of time the employee is being
given an opportunity to improve and demonstrate satisfactory performance. Performance
improvement plans should last for a minimum period of three months. For extenuating
circumstances, a supervisor may extend the timeframe of the plan.

3.

Description of acceptable level of performance. Identify the improvements that are
required of the employee and provide suggestions as to how the employee can improve
their performance.

4.

Consequences for failing to satisfy the terms and conditions. Clearly indicate that
if the employee fails to improve their performance as outlined in the performance
improvement plan, then the employee may be subject to termination.

5.

Signatures and date. Both the employee and supervisor should acknowledge the performance
improvement plan.

6.

Follow-up. The supervisor should regularly (at least once a week) follow-up with the
employee regarding their progress in carrying out the tasks identified in the performance
improvement plan. The performance improvement plan may be updated or amended based
on the follow-up meetings between the supervisor and the employee.

C.

Return-to-work/last chance agreements. If an employee comes forward to their supervisor
and/or human resources business partner and discloses that they are struggling with
addiction issues and rehabilitation is appropriate, the city, on a case-by-case basis
and in its sole discretion, may require the employee to agree to the terms of a return-to-work/last
chance agreement. The return-to-work/last chance agreement shall include a date certain
for its start and completion dates. Failure to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last
chance agreement shall result in termination without any right of appeal under the
civil service rules.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.07.040 - Pre-disciplinary procedures (suspensions without pay, demotions, and terminations).
text:
A.

Investigation. A human resources business partner, or a supervisor in conjunction
with the human resources business partner, may investigate employee misconduct if
the circumstances necessitate an investigation. At the conclusion of the investigation,
the supervisor will determine whether disciplinary action is warranted. If disciplinary
action is warranted in the form of an unpaid suspension, demotion or termination,
then notice of disciplinary action must be provided to the employee before any final
disciplinary action is issued.

B.

Notice of disciplinary action. Before an employee may be suspended (without pay),
demoted, or terminated, the employee's supervisor shall provide the employee with
notice of the disciplinary action. Human resources in conjunction with the supervisor
shall prepare a notice of the disciplinary action, which shall include the basis for
the recommended suspension (without pay), demotion, or termination.

C.

Employee response. The employee shall have two business days from the date of receipt
the notice of disciplinary action to provide a written response to the human resources
business partner (or designee). In emergency circumstances, this time period may be
extended at the sole discretion of the director of human resources (or designee).
If the employee fails to timely provide their response, the city will presume that
the employee has accepted the disciplinary action and the director of human resources
(or designee) shall approve the recommended disciplinary action, unless such recommendation
is clearly erroneous.

D.

Final approval. If an employee response is provided, the human resources business
partner (or designee) shall prepare a package for the department director and director
of human resources to review. The package shall include a copy of the notice of disciplinary
action, any relevant supporting documentation provided to the employee, and the employee's
response. The department director, in conjunction with the director of human resources,
within four business days, shall determine whether (1) disciplinary action is warranted,
and the recommended discipline should be issued by the supervisor, (2) further investigation
is required, or (3) different disciplinary action is warranted, in which case the
department director may recommend another action. If further investigation is required,
then the employee may be placed on suspension pending investigation (with or without
pay). Notice of the final disciplinary decision shall be provided to the employee
via electronic communication, certified mail or hand delivery. If further investigation
is required or additional time is needed, human resources will provide the employee
with a status update within the initial four business day timeline.

E.

Exceptions to providing notice of disciplinary action. Notice of disciplinary action
is not required for documented verbal warnings or written disciplinary actions. Notice
of disciplinary action is also not required where the employee's conduct raises a
serious safety concern to the public and/or co-workers or if the employee abandons
their job. Where there are safety concerns or where an employee abandons their job,
an employee may be immediately terminated by the director of human resources (or designee)
without an opportunity to provide a response.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.07.050 - Active discipline.
text:
A.

Disciplinary action is considered active discipline if the disciplinary action was
issued in the previous 12 months. The date the disciplinary action was presented to
the employee is the relevant date for which the 12-month period begins. For the purposes
of performance improvement plans and return-to-work agreements, the 12-month period
begins on the date that the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work agreement
becomes effective (the start date). If 12 months or more have elapsed since the disciplinary
action was issued or since the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work
agreement began, the disciplinary action/performance improvement plan/return-to-work
agreement is considered expired and may not thereafter be used as a basis for or in
support of any subsequent disciplinary action, unless the terms of the employee's
return-to-work agreement or performance improvement plan state otherwise. Active discipline
will remain active for the relevant 12-month period even if an employee is demoted
or transferred to another classified position during that time.

B.

If an employee is suspended (without pay), involuntarily demoted or terminated for
disciplinary reasons, then the employee has a right to appeal as set forth in chapter 6.08, unless the employee is suspended, involuntarily demoted or terminated for disciplinary
reasons related to discriminatory or harassing behavior, or terminated for failing
to comply with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement.

C.

Disciplinary actions are placed in the employees' personnel files. Within five business
days of receiving disciplinary action, an employee may request to include in their
personnel file a written statement of reasonable length in response to any disciplinary
action.

D.

Once a disciplinary action has expired (i.e., is no longer active discipline), an
employee may request the human resources department to visibly mark the disciplinary
action in the personnel file as "inactive." Whether or not the employee requests this,
the disciplinary action will be considered expired if 12 months have passed (unless
the terms of a performance improvement plan or return-to-work/last chance agreement
state otherwise). However, the disciplinary action shall remain in the employee's
personnel file.

E.

If the civil service board reverses a disciplinary action (suspension without pay,
demotion or termination) on appeal, then the disciplinary action will be removed and/or
revised in accordance with the civil service board's decision.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: Chapter 6.08 - APPEALS TO THE CIVIL SERVICE BOARD
6.08.010 - Appeal rights to the civil service board.
text:
A.

The civil service board has the authority to hear employee appeals on the following
issues, which shall be considered receivable appeals:

1.

Discipline that consists of suspension (without pay), involuntary demotion or termination,
with the following exceptions:

a.

The civil service board will not hear appeals if an employee is appealing the city's
decision to either suspend, involuntarily demote or terminate them as a result of
finding that the employee engaged in discriminatory or harassing behavior in violation
of the city's anti-discrimination and/or workplace harassment policies.

b.

The civil service board will not hear an appeal based on the city's decision to terminate
an employee for job abandonment.

c.

The civil service board will not hear an appeal based on the city's decision to terminate
an employee as a result of the employee's failure to comply with a return-to-work/last
chance agreement.

d.

The civil service board will not hear appeals on claims that the city engaged in discriminatory
or harassing conduct in violation of state or federal laws (including, but not limited
to N.R.S. 613.330, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disability
Act, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act and the Family Medical Leave Act). All
complaints of unlawful discrimination and harassment should be made in accordance
with the city's anti-discrimination and/or workplace harassment policies.

e.

The civil service board will not hear appeals where an employee is offered the opportunity
to return to their former classification or a similar classification (i.e., demoted),
as a result of being issued disciplinary action for failure to meet the performance
standards during a qualifying period.

2.

If an employee was laid-off as a result of a reduction-in-force, the employee may
appeal if the basis of the appeal is that the city did not follow the procedures for
implementing reduction-in-force in accordance with section 6.05.030. However, the civil service board will not hear appeals regarding the basis for the
city's decision to undertake a reduction-in-force. The appeal is limited to allegations
that the city incorrectly followed the process set forth in these rules for implementing
a reduction-in-force.

B.

The following provisions shall govern the conditions of an appeal:

1.

No employee shall bring an appeal before the civil service board until an action complained
of has become final. An action is considered to be final on the date of the effective
lay-off, suspension (for disciplinary reasons and unpaid), involuntary demotion (for
disciplinary reasons) or termination (for disciplinary reasons).

2.

An employee must file a notice of appeal with the secretary of the civil service board
(the director of human resources) within ten calendar days of the date the action
became final. The notice of appeal must contain a statement specifying the action
against which the appeal is made, the subsection or sections of the civil service
rules under which the appeal is filed and a detailed statement justifying the appeal
submission. Failure to submit a notice of appeal pursuant to this section will be
grounds to deny the appeal.

3.

Unless the employee and the City agree in writing to waive the initial hearing, the
secretary of the civil service board must schedule an initial meeting with the civil
service board members (at least three members must attend) to take place within 14
calendar days from receipt of an employee's appeal to determine whether the issue
complained of is a receivable appeal under these rules. If an employee's character,
alleged misconduct, professional competence, or physical or mental health will be
considered at the initial meeting, then the initial meeting will be conducted in a
closed meeting unless the appellant waives the closure of the meeting. The employee
must attend the initial meeting, and may bring their council at their own expense.

4.

If the issue complained of is not appealable under the civil service rules, then the
secretary of the civil service board shall notify the appellant in writing via electronic
communication or certified mail to the last known address of the appellant within
seven calendar days of the initial meeting that their request for an appeal is denied
because the rules do not allow for an appeal.

5.

If the issue complained of is a receivable appeal under these civil service rules,
then an appeal hearing shall be set within 40 calendar days of the initial meeting.
The parties may mutually agree to extend the hearing date for good cause. Notice shall
be sent by electronic communication or certified mail to the last known address of
the appellant at least 21 calendar days prior to the scheduled date of the appeal
hearing. A notice to the appellant must include the time, place, scope of the hearing,
a list of the administrative policy provisions or other rules that the appellant allegedly
violated and the possible disciplinary or other adverse administrative actions that
may be taken at the meeting. The hearing may be continued on a showing of good cause
by either the appellant or the city.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.08.020 - Hearing—Prerequisites.
text:
A.

The city shall be represented by the city attorney (or designee). The appellant may
choose to represent themselves or may be represented by counsel, at their own expense.

B.

The city, in its discretion, may choose to hire independent counsel to act as the
presiding officer at the appeal hearing or may permit a member of the civil service
board to act as the presiding officer at the appeal hearing. Any retained independent
counsel, however, will not be a voting member of the civil service board.

C.

No later than ten calendar days prior to the appeal hearing, the parties shall exchange
their list of witnesses (which shall include a brief summary of the witnesses' testimony)
and an exhibit list (which shall list and attach copies of all documents and other
tangible items that each party intends to use at the hearing).

The parties shall provide the witness list and exhibit list (with referenced documents
and tangible items attached) to the secretary of the board no later than ten calendar
days prior to the appeal hearing, who will then distribute the witness list and the
exhibit list to the members of the civil service board. The parties' witness list
and exhibit list may be sent by electronic communication or certified mail to the
secretary of the civil service board. Absent good cause, a party's failure to timely
disclose a witness or timely exchange a document or other tangible item may result
in the civil service board prohibiting the testimony of a witness or the use of the
document or tangible item at the hearing. The parties may submit objections on the
record to the civil service board as to any evidence or witnesses on the day of the
hearing, and the civil service board members may decide how much weight to give to
the objected evidence/witness when taking action.

D.

No later than eight calendar days prior to the appeal hearing, the parties shall exchange
and submit written statements to the secretary of the civil service board if they
desire to provide a written statement to the civil service board in advance of the
meeting. The secretary of the board will distribute the materials to each member of
the civil service board. The written statements should include a summary of the arguments
that the party intends to present to the civil service board. The parties' written
statement may be hand-delivered, emailed or mailed via certified mail to the secretary
of the civil service board. The written statements will become part of the hearing
record.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.08.030 - Procedures for hearing appeals.
text:
A.

An appeal hearing must be held before no fewer than three members of the civil service
board.

B.

The appellant must be present for the appeal hearing.

C.

Any hearing before the civil service board shall be conducted in accordance with NRS
241, Open Meeting Law.

D.

Appeal hearings that involve an employee's character, alleged misconduct, professional
competence, or physical or mental health, shall be held as closed meetings unless
an appellant waives the closure of the appeal hearing and requests that the meeting
be open to the public. However, no action may be taken in a closed meeting. When the
board is ready to take final action on the matter before it, the meeting must be in
open session.

E.

Appeal hearings shall be recorded on a recording instrument. The cost of transcribing
such testimony from the recording instrument shall be paid by the appellant if the
appellant requests a transcript. All recordings shall be kept for a minimum period
of two years, unless there is a litigation hold in place that requires the recordings
to be held for a longer period of time.

F.

No material amendment of, or addition to, the appellant's request for an appeal will
be considered by the civil service board.

G.

The civil service board may hear evidence specific to the issue being appealed as
described in the individual's request for an appeal. The technical rules of evidence
shall not apply, except to the extent provided herein. The proceeding shall be as
informal as is compatible with justice. The civil service board members may choose
to disregard irrelevant, immaterial and unduly repetitious evidence.

H.

The civil service board is responsible for determining the truth of the matter, and
providing adequate safeguards for the rights of the parties. The civil service board
shall be entitled to consider all relevant information, including hearsay evidence.

I.

The city shall have the initial obligation to present substantial evidence in support
of the action(s) being appealed. The appellant shall thereafter be responsible for
supporting their challenge to the adverse recommendation or action by a preponderance
of the evidence that the action lacks any substantial factual basis or that the adverse
action is arbitrary, unreasonable, and/or capricious.

J.

The parties shall have the opportunity to respond and present evidence and argument
on the matters at issue. Each party may provide an opening statement, call and examine
witnesses, introduce exhibits and cross-examine opposing witnesses, and provide a
closing statement on any matter relevant to the issues presented. The civil service
board may direct questions toward any of the parties and/or witnesses at any point
during the appeal hearing. The civil service board has the discretion to conclude
the appeal hearing when it determines that it has heard sufficient testimony from
each of the parties to make a decision on the appeal.

K.

If the parties make evidentiary objections (whether written or oral), then the presiding
officer of the civil service board may decide whether to accept or decline the objection.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.08.040 - Civil service board's final decision making authority.
text:
A.

After the civil service board has heard from both parties, the civil service board
may discuss the case further in closed session, but once they are ready to take action
the meeting cannot be in closed session. The parties to the appeal cannot be forced
to be dismissed from the closed session while the civil service board is deliberating.

B.

In making a final decision, the civil service board may, by majority vote, make a
finding:

1.

That the city's action(s) were without justification or in violation of the rules:

a.

For civil service rule violations related to a reduction-in-force, the civil service
board may require the city to comply with the rules, which may result in restoring
the appellant back to their original position, or if the position is no longer available,
to another available vacant position for which they are qualified (i.e., reverse the
decision to lay-off an employee).

b.

For disciplinary actions, the civil service board may reverse the city's disciplinary
action and take the position that no disciplinary action was warranted, which may
result in restoring the appellant back to their original position (i.e., reverse the
decision to suspend, demote or terminate an employee).

c.

The civil service board does not have the authority to determine whether an employee
is owed any form of compensation, such as but not limited to, back-pay and/or fringe
benefits.

2.

That the city's action(s) were justified and complied with the Rules and should be
confirmed; or

3.

That both parties' arguments have merit. The city was justified in issuing disciplinary
action, but the employee's conduct did not warrant the type of disciplinary action
issued.

a.

Each party shall receive an opportunity to present alternative forms of appropriate
disciplinary action that should be issued and the civil service board shall make the
final decision about the type of disciplinary action that should be issued.

b.

The civil service board does not have the authority to determine whether an employee
is owed any form of compensation, such as but not limited to, back-pay and/or fringe
benefits.

C.

The decision of the civil service board shall be final and the decision shall be binding
on the city and the appellant.

D.

Inadvertent deviations which may occur in the foregoing appeal hearing and final decision
procedures shall not invalidate the decision of the civil service board.

(Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)

heading: 6.09.010 - Glossary.
text:
Active discipline. An employee is considered to have active discipline if disciplinary action (documented
verbal warning, written reprimand, suspension, involuntary demotion, return-to-work/last
chance agreement, and/or performance improvement plan) has been issued to that employee
within the past 12 months. The date the disciplinary action was presented is the relevant
date for which the 12-month period begins. For the purposes of performance improvement
plans and return-to-work/last chance agreements, the 12-month period begins on the
date that the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work/last chance agreement
becomes effective (the start date). If 12 months or more have elapsed since the last
disciplinary action was issued or since the performance improvement plan or the return-to-work/last
chance agreement began, the disciplinary action/performance improvement plan/return-to-work/last
chance agreement is considered expired and may not thereafter be used as a basis for
or in support of any subsequent disciplinary action, unless the terms of the employee's
return-to-work/last chance agreement or performance improvement plan state otherwise.
Active discipline will remain active even if an employee is demoted or transferred
to another position.

Appeal hearing means a hearing before the civil service board in which evidence is presented by
both parties in order to allow for the civil service board to make a final decision
on the issue(s) before it pursuant to Rule 6.08.

Application materials mean the documentation the city requires an applicant to submit to apply for a position
including, but not limited to, an employment application, supplemental questionnaire,
resume, cover letter, evidence of certifications/licenses, and/or other required documentation
as stated on the job posting.

Assessment process means the process for measuring a candidate's knowledge and ability to perform the
skills required for a particular job when applying for classified positions.

Business day(s) means Monday through Thursday, excluding holidays, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

Calendar day(s) means every day of the week, including Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.

City seniority means an employee's length of continuous service in years, months and days from their
most recent full-time/regular date of hire with the city.

Civil service board means a group of five duly appointed individuals responsible for fulfilling the duties
outlined in the civil service rules.

Classification means any position which has been defined by a job description.

Classified positions means all positions now existing or hereafter created by the City of Henderson that
are not represented by a union and/or not specifically exempted by the Henderson City
Charter, which have been determined to be covered under the civil service rules.

Compensation plan means a compensation structure that sets forth the salary range for each classification.

Displaced employee means an employee who is included in a reduction-in-force. Such employee will be
provided with displacement rights as set forth in the civil service rules.

Division head means a position responsible for managing multiple sections within a department,
or is designated as a key member of a division or functional area that significantly
impacts department and/or city operations.

Eligibility list means a list of candidates who have successfully completed the application materials
review and/or the assessment process for a specific position. The list will have a
defined commencement and expiration date, and will be utilized to select the candidate(s)
who are the best fit for the available opening(s).

Initial meeting means the first meeting of the civil service board to occur after an employee has
filed a notice of appeal. The sole purpose of the initial meeting is to determine
whether the notice of appeal is a receivable appeal under the civil service Rule 6.08.01.

Probationary period (or probationary employee) means the time period a new full-time employee must serve during which time the employee
will be evaluated for the purposes of determining if the employee's performance meets
the expectations of the position. A probationary period is not less than six months
from the full-time date of hire and may be extended by an additional six months at
the city's discretion, and the probationary employee will begin a new six-month probationary
period if they accept another full-time position in the city during their initial
probationary period. A probationary employee may be terminated at the discretion of
the city, and such termination may not be appealed to the civil service board as probationary
employees are not yet members of the classified service.

Performance improvement plan. A performance improvement plan is meant to assist an employee with improving their
performance; it is a written plan that identifies specific areas that need improvement
in order to satisfactorily perform their job. An employee's failure to remedy their
deficiencies will lead to further disciplinary action, up to and including termination.

Qualifying period means the time period for which an employee who has been promoted, voluntarily or
involuntarily demoted or transferred must serve to allow the city to evaluate the
employee's performance and determine if employee meets the expectations of the position.
A qualifying period is not less than six months and may be extended by an additional
six months at the city's discretion.

Reinstatement list means a list of previously employed persons who were laid-off as a result of a reduction-in-force.

Return-to-work/last chance agreement. If an employee is struggling with addiction issues and rehabilitation is appropriate,
the city, on a case-by-case basis and in its sole discretion, may require the employee
to agree to the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement. Failure to comply
with the terms of a return-to-work/last chance agreement shall result in termination
without any right of appeal under the civil service rules.

Unclassified positions mean positions that are excluded from the civil service rules by the City Charter
or positions covered by a collective bargaining agreement between the city and a recognized
bargaining unit.

Workdays mean the days which an employee is scheduled to work, and/or expected to be available
to work.

(Ord. No. 4142, § 1, 1-6-2026; Ord. No. 4018, § 1, 4-2-2024; Ord. No. 3412, § 1, 5-16-2017; Ord. No. 3267, § 2, 5-19-2015)
