matter, and derived from Ord. No. 360, §§ 4-1—4-14, adopted December 20, 1965, and
Ord. No. 1663, § 6, adopted in 1996.

heading: 10.20.010 - Authority to install.
text:
The city traffic engineer shall place and maintain or cause to be placed or maintained,
traffic control signs, signals and devices when and as required under the traffic
ordinance of this city to make effective the provisions of said ordinances, and may
place and maintain such additional traffic control devices as he may deem necessary
to regulate traffic under the traffic ordinances of this city or under state law or
to guide or warn traffic.

(Ord. No. 3135, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.20.130 - Display of unauthorized signs, signals or markings.
text:
No person shall place, maintain or display upon or in view of any highway an unauthorized
sign, signal, marking or device which purports to be or is an imitation of or resembles
an official traffic control device or railroad sign or signal, or which attempts to
direct the movement of traffic, or which hides from view or interferes with the effectiveness
of any official traffic control device or any railroad sign or signal. This paragraph
shall not apply in cases of emergency when temporary warnings signs, flares or barricades
are necessary to avoid a hazard which constitutes an immediate and impending danger
to traffic providing that the police department is immediately notified of such hazard
and of the placing of any temporary warning signs, flares or barricades.

(Ord. No. 3135, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.20.170 - Designation and establishment of crosswalks and safety zones.
text:
The city traffic engineer is authorized:

To designate and maintain, by appropriate devices, marks, or lines upon the surface
of the roadway, crosswalks at intersections where in his opinion there is particular
danger to pedestrians crossing the roadway, and at such other places as he may deem
necessary;

To establish safety zones of such kind and character and at such places as he may
deem necessary for the protection of pedestrians.

(Ord. No. 3135, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.20.175 - Curb markings.
text:
The city may, in its discretion, mark curbs with the following colors which shall
have the following meanings:

A.

Red—No parking;

B.

Yellow—Freight loading zone;

C.

White—Passenger loading zone;

D.

Green—Parking for no more than 12 minutes.

The absence on any curb of any of the above-listed painted colors does not signify
that parking is otherwise allowed. The painting of curbs is intended to assist operators
of motor vehicles in identifying areas where parking is prohibited or restricted,
not to identify all places where parking is prohibited or restricted.

(Ord. No. 3135, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.20.180 - Traffic lanes.
text:
The city traffic engineer is authorized to mark traffic lanes upon the roadway of
any street or highway where a regular alignment of traffic is necessary.

(Ord. No. 3135, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.24.010 - Reserved.
text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3137, § 1, adopted April 1, 2014, repealed the former section 10.24.010 in its entirety,
which pertained to basic rules, and derived from Ord. No. 360, § 5-1, adopted December
12, 1965.

heading: 10.24.020 - Limits.
text:
The maximum speed limit shall be 25 miles per hour on all streets and highways unless
a different speed limit is posted pursuant to the provisions set forth in this Code.

(Ord. No. 4113, § 1, 10-21-2025)

Editor's note—
Prior to the reenactment of section 10.24.020 by Ord. No. 4113, § 1, adopted October 21, 2025, Ord. No. 3968, § 3, adopted June 6, 2023, repealed the former section 10.24.020 in its entirety,
which pertained to maximum limits, and derived from Ord. No. 360, § 5-2, adopted December
20, 1965, and Ord. No. 3137, § 1, adopted April 1, 2014.

heading: 10.24.030 - Determination of speed limits.
text:
Whenever the city traffic engineer determines, upon the basis of an engineering and
traffic investigation, that the safe and orderly movement of traffic upon any highway,
street, alley and thoroughfare whether public or private, will be facilitated by the
establishment of a different speed limit, the city traffic engineer may determine
and declare a reasonable and safe maximum speed limit. The city traffic engineer may
set conditions associated with the declared speed limit including but not limited
to day, time, type of vehicles, weather conditions and any other factors bearing on
safe speeds. The maximum speed limit shall be declared to be in effect upon the appropriate
signs being erected.

(Ord. No. 3137, § 1, 4-1-2014; Ord. 360, § 5-3, 12-20-1965)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3137, § 1, adopted April 1, 2014, changed the title of section 10.24.030 from "Establishment
of speed zones" to "Determination of speed limits." The historical notation has been
preserved for reference purposes.

heading: 10.24.040 - Reserved.
text:
Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3968, § 3, adopted June 6, 2023, repealed the former section 10.24.040 in its entirety,
which pertained to minimum speed regulations, and derived from Ord. 360, § 5-4, adopted
December 20, 1965.

heading: 10.24.050 - Drag race or drag racing.
text:
The term "drag race" or "drag racing" is defined as the operation of two or more vehicles
from a point side by side at accelerating speeds in a competitive attempt to outdistance
each other or the operation of one or more vehicles over a common selected course,
from the same point to the same point, wherein timing is made of the participating
vehicles involving competitive accelerations or speeds.

No person shall participate in a drag race within the city unless authorized in an
area approved by the chief of police and the city traffic engineer, subject to such
rules and regulations as may be required by the chief of police.

Persons rendering assistance in any manner to such competitive use of vehicles shall
be equally charged as a participant.

The operation of two or more vehicles side by side at speeds in excess of maximum
lawful speeds or the operation of one or more vehicles rapidly accelerating from a
common starting point to a speed in excess of the maximum lawful speed, shall be prima
facie evidence of drag racing.

(Ord. 360, § 5-5, 12-20-1965)

heading: 10.24.060 - Exhibition of speed.
text:
No person shall engage in any motor vehicle exhibition of power or speed on a highway,
street, alley or other thoroughfare open to the public or while exiting from an intersection,
stop sign or stop light. For purposes of this section any unnecessary or avoidable
spinning of wheels shall be deemed prima facia evidence of an exhibition of power
or speed.

(Ord. No. 3137, § 1, 4-1-2014)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3137, § 1, adopted April 1, 2014, amended section 10.24.060 in its entirety to read as
herein set out. Formerly, section 10.24.060 pertained to maximum speed limit, and
derived from Ord. No. 360, § 5-6, adopted December 20, 1965.

heading: 10.24.070 - Determination of speed.
text:
Any relevant evidence of speed is admissible including without limiting the following:

A.

Estimation by visual observation of a moving vehicle;

B.

The speedometer reading of a following vehicle at a speed not greater than the speed
of the vehicle being followed;

C.

Readings from radar equipment designed for such purposes when the equipment has been
tested with a tuning fork after being set up at the location where the reading was
taken;

D.

Computations from skid marks as follows:

1.

The speed nomograph produced herein or a facsimile thereof may be used for the purpose
of determining either skidding distance, speed, or skid resistance when two of the
factors are known, by the use of a straight line, two points of which shall be the
points of intersection on the two scales at the reading of the known factors and the
third point of which is the point of intersection with the scale for the factor to
be determined by the reading at the point of intersection,

2.

Skidding distance may be determined by total of the measurements of the skid marks
from each wheel of a vehicle divided by the number of wheels,

3.

Speed may be determined by a speedometer in the vehicle,

4.

Skid resistance may be determined by making three test stops with any vehicle traveling
at a known speed when brakes are applied and utilizing subsections (D)(2) and (3)
above with the speed nomograph. The lowest of the three results shall be considered
the skid resistance;

E.

Evidence introduced pursuant to subsections A, B or C in the first paragraph of this
section shall be prima facie evidence of the minimum speed of a vehicle.

heading: Chapter 10.28 - RECKLESS AND NEGLIGENT DRIVING
text: Sections:

heading: 10.28.010 - Full time and attention.
text:
A person shall, when operating a vehicle, give his full time and attention to the
operation of the same.

(Ord. 360, § 6-1, 12-20-1965)

heading: 10.28.020 - Reckless driving.
text:
Any person who drives any vehicle in willful or wanton disregard for the safety of
persons or property is guilty of reckless driving.

"Persons whose safety is disregarded" shall include without limiting, all occupants
of the vehicle which is driven in a willful or wanton manner including the driver
and "property" shall include, without limiting, the vehicle which is driven in a willful
or wanton manner.

Every person convicted of reckless driving shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(Ord. 1492, § 24, 1994; Ord. 360, § 6-2, 12-20-1965)

heading: Chapter 10.34 - CHARITABLE SOLICITATIONS WHILE STANDING ON MEDIAN STRIP OR SIDEWALK
10.34.010 - Purpose.
text:
This chapter is adopted pursuant to NRS 268.423 to provide for the issuance of permits
to charitable organizations to solicit charitable contributions on the median strips
of highways or on sidewalks adjacent to highways.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.020 - Definitions.
text:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise indicates, the following terms
shall have the meanings that are ascribed to them as follows:

A.

Charitable organization means an organization which:

1.

The Secretary of the Treasury has determined is an exempt organization pursuant to
the provisions of section 501(c) of the Internal Revenue Code; and

2.

Holds a current certificate of organization or is currently qualified by the secretary
of state to do business in this state.

B.

Highway means the entire width between the boundary lines of every way maintained by a public
authority when any part thereof is open to the use of the public for purposes of vehicular
traffic. The term does not include a "freeway" as that term is defined in NRS 408.060.

C.

Highway solicitation permit means a certificate of authority issued by the chief of the Henderson police department
or his/her designee to a charitable organization which allows the holder of the permit
to solicit charitable contributions for its organization while standing on the median
strip of any highway or the sidewalk adjacent to the highway within the jurisdiction
of the city.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.030 - Permit required.
text:
No charitable organization shall solicit contributions from the median strip of any
highway or the sidewalk adjacent to the highway within the jurisdiction of the city
without first obtaining and thereafter maintaining a highway solicitation permit.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.040 - Liability.
text:
Every charitable organization that applies for and receives a highway solicitation
permit shall:

A.

Defend and indemnify the city against any injury to any person or damage to any property
during the solicitation which arises from or is incident to the act of solicitation;
and

B.

Be liable for any injury to any person or damage to any property during the solicitation
which arises from negligence of the soliciting agent.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.050 - Application contents.
text:
A.

An application for a highway solicitation permit shall be made to the Henderson police
department upon forms provided by that department.

B.

An application shall be filed with the department at least three business days prior
to the date on which the solicitation is to begin and shall contain the following
information:

1.

The name, street address, and telephone number of the applicant and the charitable
organization on behalf of which the application is made;

2.

The name, street address, and telephone number of the person who will be responsible
for the conduct of the solicitation;

3.

The date and the time of day when the solicitation is to begin and end for each day
requested;

4.

The location(s) of the solicitation;

5.

The purpose of the solicitation;

6.

Proof of being a charitable organization as defined herein;

7.

A declaration that no one less than 18 years of age will be permitted to participate
in the solicitation; and

8.

The applicant's signature acknowledging that he or she has read, understood, and agreed
with the provision regarding liability set forth in HMC.

C.

A post office box address shall be unacceptable as a street address on an application
where a street address is required; provided, however, an applicant may identify and
designate on his application a post office box address as the address to which he
prefers correspondence to be mailed.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.060 - Application approval requirements.
text:
Upon receipt of:

A.

A completed application for a highway solicitation permit;

B.

Payment of a permit fee in the sum of $50.00; and

C.

Satisfactory proof that the applicant has procured a comprehensive general liability
insurance policy in the sum of $25,000.00 that names the city as an additional insured;

The chief of the Henderson police department or his designee may grant the highway
solicitation permit if all of the requirements set forth in this section and in HMC
section 10.34.050 are met in all respects.

(Ord. No. 3151, § 1, 4-15-2014; Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.070 - Permit—Time limit.
text:
Upon approval of an application, the chief of the Henderson police department or his/her
designee shall issue a highway solicitation permit for the period requested which
may not exceed three days in a calendar year.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.080 - Permit—Hours of use.
text:
Highway solicitation permits shall be issued for solicitation between the hours of
30 minutes after sunrise and 30 minutes before sunset.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.090 - Permit—Age requirement.
text:
No person whose age is less than 18 years may be permitted to participate in any highway
solicitation.

(Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.100 - Solicitation—Unlawful when.
text:
It is unlawful for any person engaged in highway solicitation to:

A.

Solicit on a median strip that is less than four feet wide; provided, however, that
if a median strip of adequate width is not available, solicitors may start and end
their solicitation on a sidewalk.

B.

Except as provided in subsection 3 below, solicit while:

1.

Standing within that portion of a highway specifically designated for travel and use
by vehicles.

2.

Walking from vehicle to vehicle within that portion of a highway specifically designated
for travel and use by vehicles.

3.

Subsections 1 and 2 do not apply to intersections controlled by traffic signals, provided
that the vehicles the occupants of which are being solicited are at a complete stop
for a red traffic signal, and the solicitor returns to the median or sidewalk before
the traffic signal controlling the lanes or portion of the highway in which the solicitor
is present turns green. In the interests of safety, it is also a requirement for all
solicitors to wear orange vests while soliciting.

C.

Solicit at any location that is under construction or repair.

D.

Solicit at any location at which is taking place a permitted special event, public
assembly or parade pursuant to HMC [chapter] 8.10 or 8.11.

(Ord. No. 3151, § 1, 4-15-2014; Ord. 2827, § 1, 7-21-2009)

heading: 10.34.110 - Right of appeal and judicial review.
text:

heading: 10.40.020 - Authority to place and obedience to turning markers.
text:
The city traffic engineer is authorized to place markers, buttons, or signs within
or adjacent to intersections indicating the course to be traveled by vehicles turning
at such intersections, and such course to be traveled as so indicated may conform
to or be other than as prescribed by law or ordinance.

When authorized markers, buttons, or other indications are placed within an intersection
indicating the course to be traveled by vehicles turning thereat, no driver of a vehicle
shall disobey the directions of such indications.

(Ord. No. 3139, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.40.030 - Authority to place restricted turn signals.
text:
The city traffic engineer is hereby authorized to determine those intersections at
which drivers of vehicles shall not make a right turn, left turn or U-turn, and shall
place proper signs at such intersections. The making of such turns may be prohibited
between certain hours of any day and permitted at other hours, in which event the
same shall be plainly indicated on the signs or they may be removed when such turns
are permitted.

(Ord. No. 3139, § 1, 4-1-2014)

heading: 10.44.140 - Unlawful riding.
text:
No person shall ride on any vehicle upon any portion thereof not designed or intended
for the use of passengers. This provision shall not apply to an employee engaged in
the necessary discharge of a duty.

(Ord. No. 3171, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.44.180 - Exhaust system.
text:
The exhaust system of every motor vehicle subject to the provisions of this code shall
extend beyond the rear or side of the body, but shall in no case terminate in the
vicinity of an exit. Exhaust pipes, mufflers, and tailpipes shall be entirely outside
the body of the motor vehicle. No flexible pipe or tubing shall be used except where
necessary to prevent breakage, and shall be only of the hermetically sealed exhaust
type.

(Ord. No. 3171, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.44.190 - Exhaust pipes.
text:
The exhaust gases from a motor vehicle shall not be directed to the side of the vehicle
between two feet and 11 feet above the ground.

(Ord. No. 3171, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.44.210 - Gases and fumes.
text:
The cab of any motor vehicle shall be reasonably tight against the penetration of
the gases and fumes from the engine and exhaust system. The exhaust system, including
the manifold, muffler, and exhaust pipes shall be so constructed as to be capable
of being maintained and shall be maintained in a reasonably gas-tight condition.

(Ord. No. 3171, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: Chapter 10.58 - OFF-ROAD USE OF MOTOR VEHICLES
text: Sections:

heading: 10.58.010 - Prohibited.
text:
No person shall drive or operate any motor vehicle upon lands belonging to or occupied
by another, except as provided in this chapter, without having in his immediate possession
written permission therefor from the legal owner, his agent, or lawful occupant of
said real property; and said written permission must be exhibited to a police officer
upon request or it will be presumed that said authorization does not exist and that
said person is in violation of this chapter.

(Ord. 569, § 1 (part), 1977)

heading: 10.58.020 - Exemptions.
text:
This chapter shall not apply to any person who drives or operates any motor vehicle
as follows:

A.

Upon a dedicated highway, street or roadway;

B.

Upon real property where such person has or is doing lawful business with or for the
legal owner, his agent, or lawful occupant thereof;

C.

For any legitimate emergency or governmental purpose;

D.

Upon public or private real property which is specifically designed for the said use
thereof through proper compliance with zoning and licensing procedures according to
law;

E.

If such person drives or operates such motor vehicle at a distance greater than 1,000
feet from any residential or commercial building.

This chapter shall not be deemed to interfere with the right of the federal or state
government or any of its agencies to regulate, prohibit or permit the use of motor
vehicles on real property owned by it or under its control or jurisdiction, nor shall
this chapter be deemed to permit or authorize any trespass or nuisance.

(Ord. 569, § 1 (part), 1977)

heading: Chapter 10.59 - EXCESSIVE VEHICLE NOISES
text: Sections:

heading: 10.59.010 - Prohibited acts.
text:
A.

It is unlawful for any person to operate a motorcycle, motor-powered bicycle, or other
motor vehicle in, upon, or along any street, highway, or near any private residence,
apartment house, or other dwelling house in the City of Henderson, Nevada, unless
such motor vehicle is at all times equipped with a muffler upon the exhaust thereof,
in good working order, and in constant operation to prevent excessive or unusual noise;
and it is unlawful for any person operating any motor vehicle to use a cutout, bypass
or similar muffler elimination, appliance or device.

B.

It is unlawful to make, cause, or suffer or permit to be made or caused upon any premises
near any private residence, apartment house, dwelling house, or public place in the
City of Henderson, Nevada, any unnecessary noises or sounds which are physically annoying
to persons of ordinary sensitivity or which are so harsh or so prolonged or unnatural
or unusual in their use, time or place, as to occasion physical discomfort.

(Ord. 568, §§ 1, 2, 1977)

heading: 10.59.020 - Exception.
text:
Nothing under the provisions of this chapter shall apply to the use of sirens or other
warning devices on police, fire or other emergency vehicles.

(Ord. 568, § 3, 1977)

heading: 10.60.020 - Traction engines.
text:
A.

The provisions of section 10.60.040 shall apply to traction engines or tractors, the propulsive power of which is exerted
not through wheels resting upon the ground but by means of a flexible band or chain
known as a movable track, when the portions of the movable tracks in contact with
the surface of the street, highway or alley present plain surfaces.

B.

No traction engine or tractor having lugs, grousers or other mechanical contrivances
on its wheels or tracks designed to give tractive effect shall be operated on any
public street, highway or alley within the City of Henderson unless a circular metal
band of a width of not less than three inches is placed entirely around the periphery
of such wheels or tracks, such band to serve as a protection against the tearing up
or marring of the surface of the street, highway or alley.

(Ord. No. 3172, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.60.030 - Maximum width and length of vehicles—Exception.
text:
This chapter does not apply to any street or highway which is a part of the National
System of Interstate and Defense Highways, as described in subsection (D) of section
103 of title 23, U.S.C.

A.

No person shall operate any bus, motor truck or combination of vehicles, including
any attachments thereto coupled together in excess of 70 feet, upon the streets of
the City of Henderson, except on those routes described in section 10.60.100, copies of which shall be maintained for public inspection in the office of the city
clerk and the city traffic engineer and may be amended from time to time by resolution
of the city council.

B.

The provisions of this chapter shall not apply to any specially designed equipment
operated by any duly franchised public utility for the purposes of the installation,
maintenance or repair of public facilities; provided, however, that the public utility
desiring to operate any such specially designed equipment in excess of the maximum
widths and lengths set forth in this section shall first register the same with the
department of public works.

(Ord. No. 3172, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.60.040 - Issuance of special permits for movement of buildings and other structures—Conditions—Applications therefor.
text:
A.

The traffic engineer may, at his discretion, upon application in writing filed with
their respective departments at least 48 hours in advance of the requested movement,
issue a special permit in writing authorizing the applicant to operate or move a vehicle,
combination of vehicles or special mobile equipment for the purpose of transporting
a building or other structure of a size or weight in excess of the legal maximums
set forth in this chapter, within, into or through the City of Henderson.

B.

Such permits shall be issued on a single trip basis only.

C.

In issuing such special permits, the traffic engineer may impose such conditions thereon,
such as routes to be followed, place of operation or movement, time of operation or
movement or other matters he shall deem necessary or proper to protect the streets,
highways and alleys from excessive damage or to minimize the dangers, inconveniences
or delays to the general public.

D.

The application for a special permit provided for in this section shall:

1.

Specifically describe the vehicle, combination of vehicles or special mobile equipment,
and load thereon, including the width, length, total gross weight with load imposed
and number of axles of the vehicle or equipment and the width, length and height of
the building or other structure to be moved thereby;

2.

Indicate the particular streets, highways or alleys over which the special permit
to operate or move is requested;

3.

State the date and time for which such special permit is requested.

E.

The department of public works shall notify the police and fire departments of the
issuance of such special permits at least 24 hours in advance of the requested movement,
describing the conditions of the permit and the appointed route and time of the movement.

(Ord. No. 3172, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.60.060 - Parking of vehicles laden with hazardous materials.
text:
It is unlawful for any operator or owner to park any vehicle laden with hazardous,
flammable or explosive materials in any residential or commercial area within the
city limits of the City of Henderson, unless such area has been designated a proper
parking place for these vehicles by the fire chief of the City of Henderson, or his
designee.

(Ord. No. 3172, § 1, 6-3-2014)

heading: 10.60.070 - Truck routes.
text:
A.

As used in this section, "unladen weight" means the weight of any vehicle without
load, but fully equipped with such accessories and appliances belonging to and used
by such vehicle in the transportation of persons or property.

B.

Notwithstanding any of the other provisions of this section, no vehicle in excess
of 8,000 pounds unladen weight shall be operated or moved upon any public street,
highway or alley within the city, except upon truck routes, as set forth in section
10.60.100, copies of which shall be maintained for public inspection in the office of the city
clerk and the city traffic engineer and may be amended from time to time by resolution
of the city council, or upon temporary truck routes hereafter designated by the department
of public works pursuant to subsection C of this section unless merchandise, freight
or other supplies are to be picked up by or delivered from such vehicle or unless
such vehicle is required in the performance of service, repair, construction or similar
essential use; provided, however, that in such event, such vehicle shall use the shortest
possible route from a designated truck route to the point of pickup, delivery or essential
use and shall return therefrom to the nearest designated truck route; provided, further,
that the following additional restrictions shall apply:

1.

No vehicle in excess of 8,000 pounds unladen weight shall be operated or moved upon
any street unless the use of such route is required in the pickup or delivery of merchandise,
freight or other supplies or in some essential use at some point not served by a truck
route but served by such direct route street.

2.

Streets, other than truck routes, shall not be used as through routes from one truck
route to another unless pickup, delivery or essential use is required en route.

C.

The department of public works shall have authority to designate additional, temporary
truck routes for the purpose of directing and controlling traffic along necessary
detours or between designated truck routes and construction projects or other areas
where commercial vehicles are required to be employed over extended periods of time.
Such temporary routes, when so designated, shall be posted with appropriate signs
as truck routes, and the use of such routes shall be subject to the same conditions
as set forth in this section for permanent truck routes.

D.

The provisions of this section shall not apply to any specially designed equipment
operated by any duly franchised public utility or governmental agency when such equipment
is required in providing an essential public service.

E.

The truck routes provided for in this section shall be posted with adequate signs
indicating that such routes are truck routes.

(Ord. No. 3172, § 1, 6-3-2014)

Chapter 10.62 - OPERATION OF GOLF CARTS ON STREETS
text: Sections:

heading: 10.62.010 - Where permitted.
text:
A.

Those streets, parts of streets, or areas described in the schedule attached to the
ordinance codified in this chapter, a copy of which is to be maintained for public
inspection in the office of the city clerk and the city traffic engineer, and such
other streets, parts of streets, or areas as may be added to said schedule by resolution
of the city council, are declared to be public street segments where the operation
of golf carts is permitted in accordance with the provisions of the Nevada Revised
Statutes.

B.

Except in locations designated by the schedule, and except where crossing a public
street at a marked and signed crossing authorized by the city traffic engineer, it
is unlawful to operate a golf cart on any city street or right-of-way.

(Ord. 1539, §§ 2, 3, 1994)

heading: 10.64.010 - Defacing of traffic citations, warrants and complaints.
text:
Unlawful to deface citation. It shall be unlawful and official misconduct for any
member of the police department or any other officer or public employee to dispose
of, alter, or deface a traffic citation or any copy thereof, or the record of the
issuance or disposition of any traffic citation, complaint, or warrant, in a manner
other than as required in this section.

(Ord. No. 3176, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 10.64.020 - Record of traffic cases — Report of convictions to state.
text:
Every magistrate or judge of a court shall keep or cause to be kept a record of every
traffic complaint, traffic citation, or other legal form of traffic charge deposited
with or presented to the court or its traffic violations bureau, and shall keep a
record of every official action by the court of its traffic violations bureau in reference
thereto, including but not limited to a record of every conviction, forfeiture of
bail, judgment of acquittal, and the amount of fine or forfeiture resulting from every
traffic complaint or citation deposited with or presented to the court or traffic
violations bureau.

A record of convictions or forfeitures of bail shall be forwarded to the state department
of motor vehicles as required by the NRS.

(Ord. No. 3176, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: 10.64.030 - Disposition of traffic fines and forfeitures.
text:
All fines or forfeitures collected upon conviction or upon the forfeiture of bail
of any person charged with a violation of any of the provisions of this title shall
be paid into the city treasury.

(Ord. No. 3176, § 1, 6-17-2014)

heading: Chapter 11.01 - STANDARD SPECIFICATIONS FOR PUBLIC IMPROVEMENTS
11.01.010 - Integration and title of standard specifications.
text:
A.

At the direction of the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee,
all subdivision improvements construction and any work within the public right-of-way
must conform to the standard and specifications, the standard drawings, the City of
Henderson Development Code, and, as applicable, the additional specifications described
in subsection 11.01.010(D), as amended.

B.

All references to "standard specifications" are to the most recent edition of the
Uniform Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction Off-Site Improvements,
Clark County Area, Nevada.

C.

All references to "standard drawings" are to the most recent edition of the Uniform
Standard Drawings for Public Works Construction Off-Site Improvements, Clark County
Area, Nevada.

D.

At the direction of the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee,
additional specifications or standards may govern subdivision improvements and right-of-way
construction. Such additional specifications or standards shall include, but are not
limited to, the following:

1.

Clark County Area Uniform Standard Specifications and Drawings;

2.

Clark County Regional Flood Control District Hydraulic Criteria and Drainage Design
Manual;

3.

Design and Construction Standards for Waste Water Collection Systems;

4.

Uniform Design and Construction Standards for Potable Water Systems;

5.

City of Henderson Utility Guidelines;

6.

City of Henderson Utility Services Approved Material List;

7.

Current International Fire Code with City of Henderson Amendments;

8.

Nevada Department of Transportation Standard Plans for Road and Bridge Construction;

9.

Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices;

10.

American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials a Policy on Geometric
Design of Highways and Streets;

11.

Transportation Research Board Highway Capacity Manual; and

12.

ADA Guidelines.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: Chapter 11.02 - CONSTRUCTION AND EXCAVATION WITHIN RIGHT-OF-WAY
11.02.010 - Permit required.
text:
No person, firm or corporation shall excavate or perform any construction on any street,
sidewalk, alley, easement or right-of-way within the corporate limits of the city
without first obtaining an excavation permit from the department of public works,
parks and recreation of the city.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.020 - Permit issuance.
text:
A permit shall be issued to an applicant if:

A.

The applicant has filled out an application for a permit stating the time and location
of the excavation;

B.

The plans for the proposed excavation have been approved by the director of the department
of public works, parks and recreation, or designee;

C.

A bond or deposit in lieu of bond has been made according to the provisions of chapter
11.11 of this title;

D.

The excavation will not unreasonably interfere with vehicular and pedestrian traffic,
the demand and necessity for parking spaces, and the ingress and egress from the affected
or adjacent properties; and

E.

The health, safety and welfare of the public will not be impaired; and

F.

The applicant has submitted a traffic barricade plan and, pursuant to this chapter,
has obtained approval of the plan and barricade permit from the director of public
works, parks and recreation or designee.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.030 - Standards and specifications.
text:
A.

All work shall be made and completed in accordance with the standard specifications,
standard drawings, and additional specifications or standards adopted pursuant to
section 11.01.010.

B.

All pavement cuts that result in a patch shall be made by power saw, leaving vertical
edges. Mass pavement removal in areas of full replacement may be wheel cut or removed
with excavation equipment so long as the final edge to pave is clean and vertical.

C.

All trenches shall be made safe to pedestrian and vehicle traffic from start to completion
of work.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.040 - Denial of excavation permit.
text:
The director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, may deny an excavation
permit to any applicant who:

A.

Has a documented history of unsatisfactory safety conditions;

B.

Has failed or refused to honor warranty requirements;

C.

Has failed to correct noncompliance with permit requirements; or

D.

Otherwise has failed to comply with the requirements of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.050 - Drains connected with public sewer.
text:
Whenever any excavation as mentioned in the preceding sections and any excavation
involving a private roadway is made for the purposes of connecting a drain with a
public sewer or repairing a drain connected with a public sewer, before beginning
such excavation, such person, firm, association or corporation must receive approval,
in writing, from the department of public works, parks and recreation and the department
of utility services. Such written approval shall include the place where, and the
time when such excavation is to be made. Such excavation and filling shall be made
under the direction of the director of public works, parks and recreation. In such
cases, unless waived by the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee,
the provisions of this title shall apply in all respects.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.060 - Inspection.
text:
The director of public works, parks and recreation shall furnish an inspector during
normal business hours for each permit for improvements or installation of underground
utilities in the streets, alleys, or easements within the city, whose duties shall
be to check for application and conformance to the standard specifications adopted
pursuant to section 11.01.010. The director of public works, parks and recreation shall be notified at least one
business day in advance of the time when the work is proposed to be started unless
an emergency occurs during the period in which the office is not open, in which instance
the applicant for a permit shall contact the department of public works, parks and
recreation within the first hour after the office reopens.

The city is authorized to charge fees related to the patching and resurfacing of pavement
that is cut or disturbed in connection with utility installations and other development-related
work. The fees may include the costs of slurry seal installation, asphalt resurfacing
or reinstallation, or may be based upon reimbursement for lost value. The fees shall
be in accordance with the fee schedule established pursuant to chapter 11.08 of this title.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.02.070 - Time restrictions on work in streets.
text:
A.

For purposes of this chapter, the term "emergency work" means work performed by the
owner or operator of a utility, by any governmental entity, or by persons authorized
to perform work within the city rights-of-way that must be performed or that will
compromise the health, safety and welfare of the public if not performed and completed
as soon as possible, even if such completion requires continuous repairs at times
other than normal working hours.

B.

The director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, shall establish and
maintain a schedule of time restrictions applicable to work to be performed on city
streets. Except for emergency work, no work may be performed in the travel lanes of
any street except in accordance with the schedule.

C.

The schedule described in subsection B may be amended from time to time as necessary
by the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee. No amendment to
the schedule shall become effective without at least ten days' notice to a general
contractor performing the construction work.

D.

The director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, may waive the time
restrictions set forth in this section if the health, safety or welfare of the public
is not adversely affected and if the work to be performed:

1.

Is not within 250 feet of a residential dwelling;

2.

Will not unnecessarily disrupt traffic flow;

3.

Requires materials that are not readily available during the restricted time periods;

4.

Would not significantly disrupt traffic flow during the restricted time periods any
more than during the unrestricted time periods;

5.

Necessitates that such work be accomplished at different time periods than those specified
herein; or

6.

Can be completed in whole or in part with more intense construction activity that
shortens the overall length of the traffic disruption.

7.

If the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, denies a waiver
of the time restrictions, the applicant may appeal the decision to the city council
within ten days after the decision is made. The appeal shall be in writing, shall
be filed with the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, and
shall state the factual basis for the appeal. The director of public works, parks
and recreation, or designee shall, within 30 days thereafter, place the matter before
the city council, whose decision shall be final.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.03.010 - Obstructions or encroachments within city rights-of-way.
text:
A.

Except as otherwise provided in this section or another provision of this Code, it
is unlawful for any person to erect, place or maintain any obstruction, or to cause
or permit any obstruction to encroach within, upon, or over any public right-of-way,
including any public street, public sidewalk, or public alley. Each day any unauthorized
obstruction is allowed to remain after 24 hours notice to remove the obstruction shall
constitute a separate offense. Such notice may be provided by:

1.

Any officer of the Henderson Police Department;

2.

Any officer or employee of the department of public works or department of community
development and services office of public response (code enforcement); or

3.

Any other officer or employee of the city who has been specifically authorized to
enforce this section.

B.

An obstruction otherwise prohibited by subsection A may be permitted by means of an
encroachment agreement approved by the city in accordance with this section. The agreement
must be in a form prepared by, or otherwise acceptable, to the city. Approval by the
city of an encroachment agreement:

1.

Is entirely within the city's discretion;

2.

Is contingent upon a determination by the director of public works or designee, that
the obstruction or encroachment can be accomplished without negatively impacting traffic,
public safety, pedestrian safety, or the use of and access to utility facilities;
and

3.

May be denied based on plans for future improvements to the affected right-of-way,
street, sidewalk or alley.

C.

An encroachment agreement under this section:

1.

May include conditions reasonably calculated to mitigate any impact, including without
limitation a time limit, provisions regarding ongoing maintenance, and appropriate
remedial measures; and

2.

May be required to be recorded against property that is benefitted by the agreement.

3.

May be recorded against the property of the party seeking the encroachment agreement.

D.

Except as otherwise provided in subsections E and F, the approval authority for an
encroachment agreement under this section shall be the director of public works or
designee. Typical items qualifying under this subsection D include:

1.

Encroachments related to subdivision improvements;

2.

Encroachments for monitoring wells;

3.

Encroachments necessary for compliance with a building-related code; and

4.

Other minor encroachments related to signage, outdoor dining, landscaping, fencing,
and similar minor intrusions into public right-of-way.

E.

The approval authority for the following items shall be the city council:

1.

Encroachments which, in the judgment of the director of public works or designee,
are of a significant nature, character or size so as to warrant consideration by the
city council; and

2.

Encroachments concerning which a member of the city council, prior to administrative
approval of an agreement pursuant to subsection D, has requested that the encroachment
be considered by the city council.

F.

In the case of encroachment agreements to be forwarded to the city council for consideration
pursuant to subsection E, the director of public works or designee, shall schedule
the encroachment agreement for council consideration at the next regular meeting of
the city council that is reasonably available.

G.

If the director of public works or designee, denies administrative approval of an
encroachment agreement pursuant to subsection D, the person seeking encroachment approval
may appeal the decision to the city council within ten days after the denial decision
is made. The appeal shall be in writing, shall be filed with the director or designee,
and shall state the factual basis for the appeal. The director or designee shall schedule
the matter for consideration by the city council within 30 days following receipt
of the appeal. The decision by the city council shall be final.

H.

Unless approved by city council, encroachment agreements approved administratively
pursuant to subsection D shall be signed by the director of public works or designee.

I.

Nothing in this section shall apply to obstructions or improvements installed:

1.

By or on behalf of the city; or

2.

By another governmental agency acting in accordance with an interlocal or cooperative
agreement with the city that has been approved by city council.

J.

For purposes of this chapter:

1.

"Encroachment agreement" includes any agreement, however named, that by its terms
authorizes an encroachment or obstruction.

2.

"Obstruction" means a structure, installation, amenity or improvement of any kind
within the right-of-way, street, sidewalk or alley. This term includes any tree, plant,
or shrub that overhangs a sidewalk less than ten feet above the sidewalk or less than
16 feet and four inches above any street, or any overhanging foliage that presents
a danger to the public.

(Ord. No. 4042, § 1, 11-6-2024; Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.03.020 - Removal—Dangerous or unsafe obstruction.
text:
The director of public works, parks and recreation shall cause all obstructions above,
across or under the streets of the city, which upon investigation may be considered
dangerous or unsafe to the public using such streets, to be removed. Any person failing
or refusing to obey the order directing the removal of such obstruction shall forfeit
and pay a penalty of $500.00 for each day such obstruction shall be allowed to remain
after the notice of removal shall have expired.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.03.030 - Sidewalks and streets to be free of landscaping, building, and other materials—Abutting owner's duties—Civil liability—Indemnity.
text:
A.

Owner and/or occupant of property shall not allow off-premises delivery of materials.
The owner or occupant of property shall not direct or permit the delivery of landscaping,
building, or other material on the public sidewalk, public street, or otherwise off,
of the owner or occupant's property.

B.

Off-premises delivery of materials prohibited. No person shall deliver landscaping,
building, or other material on the public sidewalk, public street or otherwise off,
of the premises of the deliveree.

C.

Maintenance of sidewalks. Owners and/or occupiers of private property shall maintain
in good and safe condition all public sidewalks abutting their land by not placing
or allowing to be placed or to remain any object which may reasonably constitute a
hazard to a pedestrian. No person may place any object on a public sidewalk which
may reasonably constitute a hazard to a pedestrian.

D.

Ice removal. No person owning or controlling any premises abutting upon any public
sidewalk within the city shall permit any such sidewalk to be covered with ice formed
by water which came from the private premises. It shall be the duty of any such person
to remove any ice accumulating on such sidewalk.

E.

Liability. Any person who violates this Section shall be liable for any injuries proximately
resulting therefrom.

F.

Indemnity. Whenever any injury proximately results from a violation of any of subsections
A through D of this section, the violator shall be liable to the City of Henderson
for all damages and costs which the City of Henderson may be required to pay by reason
of a judgment or settlement to the person damaged.

G.

Penalties. Any person violating any of the provisions of this section shall be deemed
guilty of a misdemeanor. Each day such a violation is committed or permitted to continue
shall constitute a separate offense and shall be punishable as such hereunder.

H.

Applicability. The provisions of this section shall only apply to public sidewalks
and streets. As used in this section, no sidewalk or street shall be considered public
unless all of the following have occurred:

1.

The sidewalk or street has been dedicated to the City of Henderson;

2.

The City of Henderson has accepted maintenance of such sidewalk or street; and

3.

The City of Henderson has released any bond for public improvements posted with the
City of Henderson by the developer constructing the sidewalk or street.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.04.010 - Permit required.
text:
A.

Except as previously authorized by the director of public works, parks and recreation,
no person, firm, corporation or other entity shall temporarily, whether partially
or fully, close or obstruct any city street, highway, freeway, or alley, or any portion
thereof, without first obtaining a barricade permit from the director of public works,
parks and recreation or an authorized agent thereof, except:

1.

Under emergency conditions;

2.

Pursuant to a special events permit; or

3.

Pursuant to activities authorized by the director of public works, parks and recreation.

B.

Unless otherwise instructed by the director of public works, parks and recreation,
any person, firm, corporation, or other entity that closes or obstructs a street,
highway, freeway, or alley shall place the proper barricades on such roadway in accordance
with the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices on file with the city clerk.

C.

Reserved.

D.

Only persons, contractors, owners or other individuals who are properly licensed and
bonded for performance of work within public rights-of-way shall be issued a permit
for any work, cause the deposit of materials, or use the rights-of-way for other than
normal operation of motor vehicles and pedestrians.

E.

Where barricades or other traffic-control devices are left within the travel lanes
or sidewalk areas of a right-of-way for longer than the period authorized by a permit,
or at time unauthorized by the permit, the city is authorized to charge a correction
fee, including fees charged on a per-unit of equipment basis, in accordance with the
fee schedule established pursuant to chapter 11.07.

F.

As used in this chapter, emergency conditions shall mean any condition or occurrence
which poses an imminent or existing threat to the safety or security of persons or
property. As soon as reasonably possible, emergency conditions shall be reported to
the city and a barricade permit shall be obtained.

G.

As used in this chapter, the word obstruct does not include sporadic or intermittent
access to the right-of way by a person who:

1.

Is authorized by the director of public works, parks and recreation to enter the right-of-way;
and

2.

Has no discernable impact on the flow of traffic or pedestrians.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.05.010 - Removal of unauthorized sidewalks.
text:
Any person, firm or corporation failing to construct sidewalks in compliance with
this chapter and applicable standards, or any person, firm or corporation not having
on record with the city clerk a receipt for permit and inspection fees, may be ordered
in writing, by the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, to
remove constructed sidewalks within five days.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.05.020 - Force removal of unauthorized sidewalks.
text:
In the event of the failure of any person, firm or corporation to remove constructed
sidewalks as provided in section 11.05.010, the director of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, may order the city
maintenance superintendent to remove and replace constructed sidewalks, or such defective
or unacceptable sidewalks, as he deems in the best interest of the City of Henderson,
and bill the person, firm or corporation for actual man-hours, materials and equipment
used in removal and replacement thereof.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.05.030 - Sweeping onto sidewalk, street or gutter.
text:
A.

It shall be unlawful for any person to sweep dust, dirt, accumulations, refuse or
deposits from any building onto any public sidewalk in the city. Such dust, dirt,
accumulations, refuse or deposits shall be gathered up and deposited into some suitable
receptacle.

B.

It shall be unlawful for any person to sweep the dust, dirt, accumulations, refuse
or deposits on any public sidewalks into any street or gutter within the city.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.05.040 - Running water—Broken pipes.
text:
A.

It shall be unlawful for any person owning or controlling any hose, water pipe, ditch,
canal, flume, lawn sprinkling system or waterway to allow or permit water from the
same or any part thereof, or through or from either or through or from any other source,
to flow over or into any sidewalk, street, alley or public place; provided, however,
that nothing herein shall be construed as preventing the wetting of any sidewalk,
alley, street or public place for the purpose of cleaning the same or allaying the
dust thereon, or to the accidental breaking of any such hose, water pipe, ditch, canal
or flume, landscape sprinkling system or waterway; provided, however, that such break
shall be repaired or the flow of water through the same shall be abated within two
hours after notice of such break is given to any person who owns or occupies, or to
the manager, superintendent, agent or officer of any company, corporation, association
or organization that owns, controls or maintains such water pipe, ditch, canal or
flume, lawn sprinkling system or waterway or has any pecuniary interest therein. If
such break is not repaired or the water turned off within such time, it shall be the
duty of the director of public works, parks or recreation; or designee, the director
of utilities, or designee; or any police officer, to cause the water flowing through
such hose, water pipe, ditch, canal, flume, lawn sprinkling system or waterway to
be shut off, and it shall be unlawful for any person to again turn water through the
same until proper repairs have been made.

B.

Any person who violates any portion of subsection A is guilty of a misdemeanor and
upon the conviction thereof shall be fined:

1.

If the property from which the water is flowing is zoned R-1, in an amount that is
determined by the municipal court to be appropriate under the attendant circumstances;
or

2.

If the property from which the water is flowing is subject to a zoning classification
that is less restrictive than R-1:

a.

Upon the first conviction, a minimum of $10.00;

b.

Upon the second conviction within a period of three years, a minimum of $250.00; and

c.

Upon the third conviction within a period of three years and upon each subsequent
conviction within such period, a minimum of $500.00.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.05.050 - Display, parking and sale of motor vehicles or merchandise on or within any unimproved public right-of-way.
text:
A.

It is unlawful for any person to sell or to display for the purpose of sale any motor
vehicle or merchandise on or within any unimproved portion of a public right-of-way.
For purposes of this section, "merchandise" means goods or wares, including, but not
limited to, produce, nursery stock, ceramics and other similar items. A violation
of this subsection A may be enforced either by means of a criminal proceeding or as
a civil violation under this title.

B.

Members of the Henderson Police Department are authorized to remove or cause to be
removed, to a designated garage or storage area, any motor vehicle which is being
displayed in violation of this section if the vehicle has not been removed within
72 hours after a written notice to remove is attached to the vehicle. The costs of
removal and storage shall be borne by the owner or operator of the vehicle.

C.

Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorize any sale or display on any improved
portion of a public right-of-way except that which is otherwise expressly permitted
by this Code.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: Chapter 11.06 - CONSTRUCTION, MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR OF SIDEWALKS, TRANSITION STRIPS, AND MEDIANS
11.06.010 - Purpose.
text:
It is the purpose of this chapter to:

A.

Require the property owners abutting the public right-of-way to maintain the unimproved
portion of the right-of-way referred to as a transition strip whenever necessary to
the public health, safety, welfare and benefit;

B.

Require the property owner abutting the public right-of-way to construct new sidewalk,
or maintain or repair existing sidewalk whenever necessary to the public health, safety,
welfare and benefit;

C.

Require private persons or entities that are responsible for maintaining the medians
within public rights-of-way to provide proper maintenance and upkeep;

D.

Assure the uniform and safe development of the public right-of-way within the city
by requiring that sidewalks be constructed, maintained and repaired in accordance
with those standards adopted by the city.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.020 - Definitions.
text:
For purposes of this chapter, the following definitions shall be applicable:

Maintenance means the upkeep, cleaning or preservation of the transition strip or existing sidewalk,
including the trimming or removal of vegetation, which is necessary to insure the
public health, safety, welfare and benefit.

Median or median strip means the strip of land between lanes of opposing traffic on a divided roadway.

Repair means the cutting, removing or replacing of existing sidewalk.

Sidewalk means that portion of the public right-of-way which has been improved for pedestrian
traffic.

Transition strip means the unimproved portion of the public right-of-way, including any vegetation
growing thereon, lying between the back of the curb, or in the event there is no curb
then that portion between the end of the paved street, and the property line of the
property abutting the public right-of-way.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.030 - Installation of new sidewalk.
text:
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to install new sidewalk along
the transition strip whenever necessary to the health, safety, welfare and benefit
of the public or as determined by the director of public works, parks and recreation.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.040 - Maintenance and repair of existing sidewalks.
text:
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to maintain and repair existing
sidewalk whenever necessary to the health, safety, welfare and benefit of the public.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.050 - Maintenance of transition strip.
text:
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner to maintain the transition strip
abutting his property whenever necessary to the health, safety, welfare benefit, and
beautification of the public.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.060 - Maintenance of the median.
text:
If a median strip is not owned by the city, or if the median strip is maintained by
a third party through an agreement with the city, it shall be the responsibility of
the median strip property owner or contractee to maintain the median strip whenever
necessary to the health, safety, welfare, benefit and beautification of the public.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.070 - Noncompliance—Notice or approval.
text:
Whenever the owner has failed to install a new sidewalk, maintain or repair an existing
sidewalk, or maintain the transition strip as required by this chapter, the director
of public works, parks and recreation, or designee, may notify the abutting property
owner in writing that he has 30 days in which to remedy the situation or to file an
appeal with the city council. The notice shall also state that in the event the property
owner fails to take appropriate action or file an appeal to the city council that
a lien may be imposed by the city against the property for the cost of remedying the
situation.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.080 - Appeal procedure.
text:
In the event that the property owner elects to appeal, then the property owner shall
notify the city clerk in writing who shall set a hearing date before the city council.
Written notification of the hearing date shall be sent to the property owner at least
seven days before the scheduled hearing.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.090 - Necessity for remedial action.
text:
If after the expiration of 30 days from the date of receipt of the written notice
required by section 11.06.070, the property owner has refused or failed to install new sidewalk as required by
section 11.06.030, maintain or repair existing sidewalk as required by section 11.06.040 or to maintain the transition strip or median strip as required by section 11.06.050 or section 11.06.060 respectively, and the property owner has not appealed the written notice from the
director of public works, parks and recreation as provided under section 11.06.080, then such refusal or failure and lack of appeal shall be reported to the city council.
The city council shall determine if the remedial action, as recommended by the director
of public works, parks and recreation is necessary and if so, the city council may
instruct and authorize the director of public works, parks and recreation to proceed
with remedial action.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.100 - Appeal hearing—Determination by council.
text:
In the event of hearing as provided by section 11.07.080, the property owner may present
evidence for consideration by the city council. After considering the presentations
and evidence of both the property owner and the department of public works, parks
and recreation, the city council shall determine if remedial action on the part of
the property owner is necessary to the health, safety, welfare or benefit of the public.
If such action is found to be necessary to the public health, safety, welfare or benefit,
then the property owner shall be notified of the decision of the city council that
remedial action shall be commenced and completed within ten days from the date of
notification of the city council's decision and that failure to complete such action
shall result in the department of public works, parks and recreation proceeding with
such remedial action and a lien being placed against the property of the abutting
property owner for the costs incurred by the city.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.110 - Remedial action—Cost—Time limit.
text:
Subsequent to the completion of the work, the director of public works, parks and
recreation shall forward to the property owner a statement as to cost incurred by
the city in connection with the remedial action and informing the property owner that
failure to pay the amount stated therein within 30 days from the date of the statement
shall result in a lien being assessed against the property of the property owner.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.120 - Remedial action—Nonpayment—Statement.
text:
If after the expiration of the 30-day period provided under section 11.06.110 the property owner has failed to reimburse the city for the costs of the remedial
action, the city clerk shall forward to the county recorder's office a sworn statement
stating the location of the work performed by the city, the date the remedial action
was completed, the amount to be assessed as a lien which amount is to equal the cost
of the remedial action plus ten percent and identifying the property subject to the
assessment.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.130 - Standards and inspection.
text:
The construction of new sidewalk, or the maintenance or repair of existing sidewalk,
shall be in accordance with the standards and specifications described in section
11.01.010 of this title. Upon completion of the construction, maintenance or repair, the sidewalk
shall be inspected and approved by the department of public works, parks and recreation.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.06.150 - Compliance.
text:
It is unlawful for any person including the owner of property abutting the public
right-of-way, or the agent, servant, contractor or employee of the owner, to construct
new sidewalk or to repair existing sidewalk located within the public right-of-way
within the city if the construction or repair does not comply with the standards and
specifications provided for in section 11.01.010 of this title. Any approval of the survey lines or grades submitted by the property
owner or his agent, servant, contractor or employee does not relieve the property
owner for the accuracy of said survey lines and grades.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.07.010 - Fees—Authorization and payment.
text:
A.

The director of public works, parks and recreation is authorized to charge fees in
connection with the issuance of any permit required by this chapter. Such fees may
include fees associated with plan checking and inspection, fees for services performed
by or on behalf of the city in implementing this chapter, fees relating to noncompliance
with the provisions of this chapter, fees for closure of the right-of-way, and fees
associated with corrective action required under this chapter.

In connection with the issuance of a permit, the city is authorized to establish and
collect an additional fee to cover work that was previously performed by or on behalf
of the applicant without the benefit of a valid permit. In addition, the city is authorized
to charge fees for noncompliance with permit requirements set forth in this title.

B.

Permit fees established pursuant to this chapter shall be paid before the issuance
of a permit. Inspection and service fees shall be paid before any work is done. In
connection with fees that are required in order to recover the city's costs in performing
corrective action, the city is authorized to charge the permittee the cost of the
work, and may calculate the cost in the same way that the cost of extra and force
account work is determined and charged under the standard specifications. The city
may collect the amount so charged by any available means. In cases where the corrective
work is the responsibility of the abutting property owner, collection efforts may
include making the amount a charge against the abutting property and recording an
appropriate lien against the property.

C.

Except as otherwise provided in this chapter, the fees chargeable by the city pursuant
to this section shall be those that are set forth in a fee schedule that shall be
approved and amended from time to time by resolution of the director of public works,
parks and recreation, or designee.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: Chapter 11.08 - FEES FOR CLOSURE OF RIGHT-OF-WAY
11.08.010 - Right-of-way fees and occupancy charges.
text:
A.

Schedule of right-of-way fees.

1.

Barricade permit fee.

a.

The barricade permit fee shall be $200.00.

b.

The barricade permit fee shall be paid with the barricade permit application, or,
pursuant to an emergency condition described in subsection 11.02.070 A., as soon as reasonably possible.

2.

Right-of-way occupancy charge.

a.

Calculation of the fees for a right-of-way occupancy charge shall commence on the
fourth day following the effective date of the barricade permit fee for the lane closure.

b.

The fee shall be $50.00 per day for each lane that is closed at any time of the day.

c.

The right-of-way occupancy charge will be billed once the right-of-way work is complete
and the lane re-opened; amounts billed shall be due within 30 days after a bill is
issued; fines or penalties will begin to accrue on the 31st day after the bill is
issued.

d.

A right-of-way occupancy charge shall not be assessed for work performed during a
continuing emergency condition described in subsection 11.02.070 A. or for work performed within rights-of-way managed by the State of Nevada or the
United States Government.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.08.012 - Definitions.
text:
For purposes of this chapter, the following definition shall be applicable:

Lane means the portion of the public roadway utilized for the movement of a single line
of vehicles, both motor vehicle and bicycle.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: Chapter 11.09 - PENALTY FOR VIOLATION OF TITLE
11.09.010 - Misdemeanors.
text:
Any person violating any of the provisions of this title shall be guilty of a misdemeanor;
and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished as the law allows for a misdemeanor
crime. Whenever in this chapter any act is prohibited, or is made or declared to be
unlawful, or an offense or a misdemeanor, or whenever in such chapter the doing of
any act is required, or the failure to do any act is made or declared to be unlawful,
or an offense or misdemeanor, the doing of any such prohibited act, or the failure
to do any such required act, shall constitute a violation of this chapter. Every day
of violation of this chapter constitutes a separate offense. Any person being adjudged
guilty of a violation of this chapter or any of the provisions or prohibitions thereof
may, in the discretion of the council, be denied a license thereafter.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.020 - Alternative to criminal prosecution.
text:
As an alternative to criminal prosecution for a violation of any provision of title 11, the city may impose a civil penalty in accordance with the provision of this chapter.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.030 - Notice of violation—Required information.
text:
A.

A civil penalty under this chapter shall be imposed by the issuance of a notice of
violation by the city. The notice of violation must contain, at a minimum, the following
information:

1.

The name and address (if known) of the person or entity responsible for the violation;

2.

A brief description of the violation and a reference to the applicable ordinance or
code citation(s);

3.

The location, date and time of the violation;

4.

The name of the person issuing the notice of violation;

5.

The amount of the civil penalty; and

6.

Information advising of the manner and time for responding to the notice of violation.

B.

No error concerning, or omission of, any of the above-described information is grounds
for the dismissal of a proceeding relating to a notice of violation unless the person
requesting the dismissal demonstrates substantial prejudice from the error and/or
omission.

C.

Where the notice of violation data is entered into and stored in a computer or similar
device, any printout or other output readable by sight that accurately reflects such
data is an original notice of violation for purposes of a proceeding under this chapter.
Any such data entry that is moved or copied into another computer or similar device
is intended to constitute an additional or replacement of the record of the data by
the issuing officer or employee and is also an original notice of violation for purposes
of a proceeding under this chapter.

D.

Any notice of violation issued pursuant to this chapter shall constitute a declaration
which is subject to the penalty of perjury.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.040 - Notice of violation—Issuance.
text:
The notice of violation may be issued by any peace officer or by any authorized officer
or employee of the department of public works, parks and recreation.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.050 - Notice of violation—Filing.
text:
An original notice of violation, or a facsimile thereof, must be filed with and retained
by the department of public works, parks and recreation. A notice of violation is
prima facie evidence of the facts which are alleged therein. The notice of violation
must be served on the person responsible for the violation or, in the case of an entity,
an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. A
notice of violation may be served on the person responsible for the violation either
personally or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, at the address
on file with the department of public works, parks and recreation.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.060 - Notice of violation—Response—Hearings.
text:
A.

The person cited must respond to a notice of violation within the time prescribed
by section 11.10.070 of this chapter in one of the following ways:

1.

Admit responsibility for the commission of the violation and liability by paying the
amount of the civil penalty; or

2.

Dispute the notice of violation by requesting a hearing before a hearing officer.
A hearing may be requested by sending a written request to the director of public
works, parks and recreation with the following information:

a.

The name of the individual on the notice of violation;

b.

The current address of the individual; and

c.

The notice(s) of violation(s) which the person wishes to dispute at the hearing.

B.

After receipt of a person's written request for a hearing, the director of public
works, parks and recreation shall set a hearing date and provide notice of the hearing
to the person requesting it at least 14 days before the date of the hearing.

C.

Any hearing conducted pursuant to this chapter shall be presided over by a hearing
officer appointed pursuant to section 4.06.100. With respect to any such hearing, a properly filed notice of violation shall constitute
a claim of liability and a claim for relief and no other such claim shall be required.
Prima facie proof of the violation alleged shall be established by the city providing
the hearing officer with either a certified copy of the notice of violation or the
data stored in a computer or other device as described in subsection 11.09.030(C). No formal appearance by the city attorney's office is required at the hearing.
The hearings and dispositions of all such actions shall be informal, with the hearing
officer receiving witness statements or testimony and other evidence for the sole
purpose of dispensing a fair and speedy resolution between the parties.

D.

Any person initiating a hearing pursuant to this chapter shall be referred to as "defendant".
If a defendant requesting a hearing before the hearing officer fails to appear at
the hearing without having first sought and obtained a continuance of the hearing,
the hearing officer may enter a decision against the defendant for the full amount
of the civil penalty scheduled to be reviewed. The burden of proving any defense shall
be upon the person raising such defense.

E.

If the hearing officer finds that a violation did not occur or that the defendant
should not be held liable, the hearing officer shall enter a decision for the defendant.

F.

The defendant shall pay the total civil penalty forthwith or at such times and on
such conditions as the hearing officer shall prescribe if it is found that the person
has either failed to appear or otherwise defend against the issuance of the notice
of violation as agreed or that the violation was committed and no applicable defense
exists. Any decision by the hearing officer pursuant to this chapter shall be a final
determination.

G.

Upon reaching a decision, the hearing officer shall, as soon as practicable thereafter,
file a written decision with the director of public works, parks and recreation substantially
conforming to the following form:

City of Henderson, Clark County, Nevada

City of Henderson, Plaintiff v. ____________, Defendant. Before, ____________, Hearing
Officer for the City of Henderson, Nevada, decision is entered in favor of ____________,
(plaintiff or defendant) for $____________/____________/____________ (enter $0.00
if judgment is for the defendant), on the ____________ day of ____________/____________/____________,
20____________. Any payments are due in full within ___ days of the date hereof to
the City of Henderson Finance Department.

I certify that the foregoing is a correct reflection of the decision entered in the
proceeding properly brought for my consideration pursuant to HMC ________________
et seq.

_________________________

Hearing Officer

H.

The city attorney may petition the Henderson municipal court for the entry of a civil
judgment against the defendant in an amount equal to that stated in the written decision
of the hearing officer if the city attorney determines this action to be necessary
to enforce the decision. Service of such petition on the defendant must be made by
certified mail, return receipt requested, restricted delivery, addressed to the defendant
at the defendant's last known address, or in any other manner which is authorized
by law. An affidavit or declaration of mailing, a signed, returned receipt, or other
evidence of service of the civil judgment shall be filed upon such service of the
petition.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)

heading: 11.09.065 - Notice of violation—Response period.
text:
A.

A response to a notice of violation, as provided in section 11.09.060, must be made within 30 calendar days after the date on which the notice of violation
is served. If no response is received during such 30-day period, an additional civil
penalty which is equal to the amount of the original civil fine may be assessed.

B.

If a person does not respond to a notice of violation within the 30-day response period,
the director of public works, parks and recreation, or an authorized designee, shall
send a notice of delinquency by mail to the person responsible for the violation or,
in the case of an entity, an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered
agent of that entity at the address on file with the department of public works, parks
and recreation.

C.

The notice of delinquency shall contain the original date of the violation, the amount
of the civil fine and the amount of any late penalty which is associated therewith.
The person responsible for the violation or, in the case of an entity, an officer,
key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity has 15 calendar
days after the date of the notice of delinquency in which to respond to the department
of public works, parks and recreation. If no response is made to the notice of delinquency
within such additional 15-day period, an additional civil penalty may be assessed
equal to the original civil penalty imposed and the matter may be referred to the
city attorney's office to initiate proceedings to suspend and/or revoke the business
license or permit.

D.

If a person fails to respond to a notice of violation or a notice of delinquency in
accordance with this chapter, the city is entitled to collect the amount of any fines
and penalties by means of any remedy available under applicable law, including without
limitation referring the matter to a collection agency and initiating proceedings
to suspend and/or revoke the person's business license or permit.

(Ord. No. 3380, § 2, 1-3-2017)
