(Ord. No. 3905, § 16, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3413, § 2, 6-6-2017; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009)

heading: 14.14.070 - Restrictions on surface, building, equipment, and vehicle washing; splash pads.
text:
A.

Surface, building, and equipment washing.

1.

Surface, building, and equipment washing (excluding motor vehicles) at a non-residential
property in the city's corporate boundaries and on real property to which the city
provides water service is prohibited unless (a) the water is contained on site (i.e.
does not flow off that property) or is discharged to a municipal sewer system that
has the ability to treat and discharge that treated water to Lake Mead (the "MSS")
through approved methods as determined by the city and (b) there is no violation of
any other applicable code requirement, such as a requirement in title 13 of the Code.

A responsible person shall not perform surface or building washing more often than
once each calendar month other than to remediate a condition on the property for the
protection of public health, safety, or welfare. If the responsible person is remediating
a condition, then that responsible person must provide the city documentation of that
condition, at the department's request.

2.

If a person performs surface, building, or equipment washing (including motor vehicles)
at a residential property in the city's corporate boundaries or on residential property
to which the city provides water service, that person must use a positive shut-off
nozzle and comply with any other applicable code requirements, such as those in title 13 of the code.

B.

Vehicle washing.

1.

Washing a non-commercial vehicle at a residential property in the city's corporate
boundaries or on real property to which the city provides water service is limited
to one day per week with the use of a positive shut-off nozzle.

2.

A commercial vehicle may only be washed at a commercial facility (including a commercial
car wash business) where water is contained on site or discharged to the MSS through
approved methods, as determined by the city, and a high-pressure, low volume sprayer
(or spray system) is used.

3.

A commercial car wash business (including mobile and stationary operations) with a
valid City of Henderson business license may wash commercial and non-commercial vehicles
and must use a high-pressure, low volume sprayer (or spray system) that uses less
than ten gallons of water per vehicle.

4.

Charitable car washes performed by a nonprofit group, charity fund raiser, or school
group are permissible only when:

a.

High-pressure, low volume sprayers (or spray systems) are used; and

b.

Less than ten gallons of water per vehicle is used; and

c.

Any other applicable code requirements, such as those in title 13, are complied with.

C.

Splash pads.

1.

A splash pad installed or modified after January 1, 2023, may only be operated if
it meets the following requirements:

a.

The splash pad is designed and operated in a manner that prevents surface water run-on
from the area adjacent to and surrounding the splash pad from entering the MSS; and

b.

The majority of the water dispersed in connection with operation of the splash pad
is discharged into the MSS through an approved method (as determined by the city);
and

c.

In compliance with any applicable requirement in title 13 and any other applicable code requirement, any other water, including surface water
run-on from the area adjacent to and surrounding the splash pad, is diverted to the
storm drain system; and

d.

The splash pad automatically shuts off after five minutes; and

e.

When the splash pad is not in use, the splash pad drainage area is covered to prevent
stormwater and other substances from entering the MSS; and

f.

The splash pad is located in any of the following: a public park, a recreational water
park, a homeowner association-owned or -managed property, a residential property (provided
the splash pad is not located in the front yard), a school, a daycare, a recreation
center, a senior center, a mixed-use development, a government facility, or a religious
institution; and

g.

The method used to discharge splash pad water to the MSS is regularly maintained and
replaced as necessary to maintain operational efficiency and pollutants (defined in
section 14.09.010) are not discharged to the MSS through that connection.

2.

As used in chapter 14.14, "splash pad" means an outdoor water play area intended for human contact that has
potable water typically dispersed by sprinklers, fountains, nozzles, or other devices
that spray, mist, or dump that water and that diverts the dispersed water through
an approved method (as determined by the city) into the MSS so that the play area
is continuously drained and, as a result, has little or no standing water.

(Ord. No. 4062, § 1, 3-4-2025; Ord. No. 3905, § 17, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3413, § 3, 6-6-2017; Ord. 2798, § 5, 1-20-2009)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3905, § 17, adopted September 13, 2022, changed the title of section 14.14.070 from "Other
outdoor water use standards" to "Restrictions on surface, building, equipment, and
vehicle washing; splash pads." The historical notation has been preserved for reference
purposes.

heading: 14.14.080 - Water features.
text:
A.

A water feature is prohibited on real property in the city's corporate boundaries
and on real property to which the city provides water service, unless an exemption
in subsection 14.14.080.B applies.

B.

The following water features are exempted from the prohibition in subsection 14.14.080.A:

1.

Swimming pools, spas, and hot tubs, provided, as to any residential property with
an attached or a detached single-family residential dwelling unit:

a.

The swimming pool, spa, and/or hot tub is not located in the front yard; and

b.

For any swimming pool, spa, and hot tub issued a permit for construction by the city
on or after September 19, 2022, the combined water surface area of the swimming pool,
spa, and hot tub does not exceed 600 square feet of surface area of water; and

c.

For any swimming pool, spa, and hot tub issued a permit for construction by the city
before September 19, 2022, the combined water surface area of the swimming pool, spa
and hot tub cannot be increased beyond the surface area of water in the permit originally
approved or beyond 600 square feet, whichever is greater; and

d.

There is at most one swimming pool and one spa or hot tub on that property.

2.

A water feature that is necessary and/or a functional component serving at least one
of the following uses:

a.

An irrigation reservoir for a golf course; or

b.

An engineered component of a heat exchanger for a cooling system.

3.

A water feature within a climate-controlled, enclosed structure.

4.

Not including a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub, a single water feature of not more
than 25 square feet of surface area of water upon a residential property with an attached
or a detached single-family residential dwelling unit. Regardless of depth, a lazy
river may be a separate water feature or be part of the swimming pool, spa, or hot
tub. As used in chapter 14.14, "lazy river" means a channeled flow of water of near-constant depth in which the
water is moved by pumps or other means of propulsion to provide a riverlike flow and
is usually found in water parks, hotels, resorts, and recreation centers.

5.

Not including a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub, a single water feature of not more
than 25 square feet of surface area of water within a common area of a residential
property with a multi-family residential unit, provided that the feature is not located
at an entryway to the property.

6.

A water feature that was installed and operating prior to June 9, 2017 or approved
or otherwise authorized by the city in a contract with the city in accordance with
title 19 of the Code prior to June 9, 2017.

7.

A lazy river in a recreational water park.

8.

Interactive water play features in a city-operated pool or in a privately owned and
maintained pool that is open for general community use.

9.

A splash pad.

C.

For purposes of calculating the square feet of surface area of water, the square feet
of the surface over which water continuously flows or falls, or is designed to continuously
flow or fall, shall be included in the calculation of the surface area.

D.

As used in chapter 14.14, "water feature" means any artificially constructed or installed stream, lazy river,
fountain, waterfall, reflective pool, pond, lake, body of water, waterfall, swimming
pool, spa, hot tub, or other artificially constructed or installed feature using water
that is located outdoors that:

1.

Contains water that flows, is recirculated, or is sprayed into the air; and

2.

Was constructed or is used, in whole or in part, for recreational, cooling-off, decorative,
scenic, aesthetic, or landscape purposes.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 18, 9-13-2022)

Editor's note—
Ord. No. 3905, § 18, adopted September 13, 2022, amended section 14.14.080—14.14.110 in their entirety
to read as herein set out. Formerly, sections 14.14.080—14.14.110 pertained to conservation
rates, fees, and penalties, manmade decorative water features, pool and hot tub draining,
and violations, respectively, and derived from Ord. No. 2798, § 5, adopted January
20, 2009; Ord. No. 2909, § 1, adopted March 15, 2011; Ord. No. 3020, § 1, adopted June 11, 2013, and Ord. No. 3413, §§ 4—6, adopted June 6, 2017.

heading: 14.14.090 - Swimming pool, spa, and hot tub draining.
text:
A.

When submitting an application for a swimming pool or spa permit, the applicant must
show an onsite sewer lateral cleanout on the plans and that cleanout must be constructed.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection B of this section 14.14.090, swimming pool, spa, or hot tub water shall only be discharged into the MSS through
a private connection such as a sewer lateral cleanout, sink, toilet, or bathtub.

B.

Exemptions.

1.

Real property that is on a septic system may drain water from a swimming pool, spa,
or hot tub into the storm drain system, provided the water is dechlorinated, prior
notification has been given to the department's customer care center, and such discharge
is permitted by and performed in compliance with title 13 of the Code.

2.

Where there is limited hydraulic capacity in the MSS, real property that is provided
wastewater service by the city may drain water from a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub
into the storm drain system, provided the water is dechlorinated, such discharge is
allowed by and performed in compliance with title 13 of the Code, and such discharge is authorized by the department.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 19, 9-13-2022)

Note—
See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

heading: 14.14.100 - Recreational water park.
text:
A.

Any recreational water park that is on real property to which the city provides water
service or on real property in the city's corporate boundaries and that, after September
19, 2022, changes a use at the recreational water park in relation to water used that
requires a city-issued permit, license, or other city authorization must comply with
the following:

1.

The recreational water park must submit to the department a water efficiency plan
for review within three months of receiving City's approval of that use change, and,
at least once annually thereafter, review its water efficiency plan and, as soon as
practicable after its review is completed but not later than December 31 of each year,
submit the results of its review and any additions or modifications to its water efficiency
plan to the department, and incorporate any changes identified by the department into
the water efficiency plan. The department must approve the original plan and any additions
or modifications. The recreational water park must implement the approved water efficiency
plan.

2.

The recreational water park must mitigate water use and, subject to the department's
approval, identify methods to mitigate water use in their water efficiency plan. Methods
to mitigate water use may include one or more of the following:

a.

Installing and maintaining drought-tolerant landscaping, instead of lawn grass, in
the landscaped areas of the recreational water park; and

b.

Instituting measures to prevent water loss at water play areas at the recreational
water park.

B.

As used in chapter 14.14:

1.

"Recreational water park" means a commercial amusement park with any combination of
water play areas intended for human contact such as pools, water slides, splash pads,
lazy rivers, artificial surfing, artificial bodyboarding, and/or water playgrounds,
as well as areas for floating, wading, or swimming.

2.

"Water efficiency plan" means a comprehensive plan conforming to department guidelines
that contains information related to a development's consumptive and non-consumptive
water demand projections. The plan may include a summary of indoor and outdoor water
uses, a description of water fixtures and appliances, cooling systems, misting systems
and other water dependent applications, a summary of efficiency measures proposed
on site, and methods to mitigate water use.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 20, 9-13-2022)

Note—
See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

heading: 14.14.110 - Artificial lakes.
text:
A.

As of September 19, 2022, an artificial lake is prohibited on real property in the
city's corporate boundaries and on real property to which the city provides water
service, unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.110.B applies.

B.

The following are exempted from the prohibition in subsection 14.14.110.A:

1.

An artificial lake that was installed and operating prior to June 9, 2017.

2.

An artificial lake that was approved or otherwise authorized by the city in a contract
with city in accordance with title 19 of the Code prior to June 9, 2017.

3.

An artificial lake located on a golf course that is used for the purpose of storing
irrigation water for the irrigated acreage at the golf course in conformance with
section 14.14.040.

C.

As used in chapter 14.14, "artificial lake" means an outdoor body of water that is artificially constructed
or installed, is privately owned, is used in whole or in part for a recreational,
scenic, aesthetic, or landscape purpose, and is filled, or refilled, with potable
water or non-potable water from any source, including lakes, ponds, lagoons, and reservoirs
but excluding tank-type reservoirs that are fully enclosed and contained. The term
"artificial lake" does not include a water feature or a recreational water park.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 21, 9-13-2022)

Note—
See editor's note at section 14.14.080.

heading: 14.14.120 - Drought emergency.
text:
A.

The department is authorized to draft, modify, implement, and enforce a drought response
plan. The department shall make that drought response plan publicly available on the
city's website.

B.

All responsible persons shall comply with the requirements in that drought response
plan.

C.

As used in chapter 14.14, "drought response plan" means a plan to mitigate the impacts of drought or low Lake
Mead water level conditions by requiring customers to reduce, limit, or curtail their
demand for and use of city-supplied water generally or through specific types of action
(such as not filling a water feature), by prioritizing uses by different customers,
and by prohibiting water use.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 22, 9-13-2022)

heading: 14.14.130 - Water use restriction in deed or other written instrument recorded against real property.
text:
An owner, and any lessee, renter, or occupant, of real property shall comply with
all restrictions in a deed or other written instrument that limits, restricts, prohibits,
or prescribes particular water use or landscaping materials at that real property,
provided that the deed or other written instrument containing the restriction(s) is
recorded against that real property in the office of the county recorder of Clark
County, Nevada.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 23, 9-13-2022)

heading: 14.14.140 - Violations.
text:
Any person who commits an act or refuses to correct a condition that is not in compliance
with a requirement in this chapter as set forth in any section above, and any responsible
person who violates this chapter as set forth below, is subject to discontinuance
of service, subject to any penalties and charges assessed in accordance with this
title and/or department service rules, and subject to all compliance procedures as
prescribed within this title. It is a violation of this chapter for a responsible
person to commit water waste and/or allow water waste to occur on real property that
the responsible person controls, has a property interest in or maintains by:

A.

Allowing the loss, escape, or excess use of water through a break, leak or other malfunction
in the water distribution facilities on the real property for any period of time after
such escape of water should have been reasonably discovered as determined by the department.

B.

Failing to repair a break, leak, or other malfunction in the water distribution facilities
on the real property within 120 hours of knowing, or being notified, of the malfunction
or by the deadline set by the city, whichever date is later.

C.

Allowing water from a water distribution facility, tank, or water feature on the real
property water to flow onto, spray onto, pool on, or run off onto (1) non-irrigated
or non-landscaped areas on the real property, (2) adjacent real property, or (3) private
or public walkways, roadways, pavement, gutters, alleys, parking lots, or structures.

D.

Allowing water from a tank or water feature on the real property to pool on an irrigated
or landscaped area on the real property.

E.

Watering lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation at a time prohibited
unless an exemption in section 14.14.030 or section 14.14.040 applies.

F.

Watering lawn grass, a garden, a tree, shrubbery, or other vegetation on a day that
is not a day in the watering group assignment for the real property or service location
unless an exemption in section 14.14.030 or section 14.14.040 applies.

G.

Using spray irrigation for any purpose other than to irrigate lawn grass.

H.

Failing to comply with a requirement in a water budget.

I.

Using landscaping materials other than as allowed in section 14.14.050 and/or imposing landscaping requirements that do not comply with the requirements
in section 14.14.050.

J.

Using a mist cooling system at a time or on a day other than as allowed in section
14.14.060.

K.

Using water to perform surface, building, equipment, or vehicle washing other than
as allowed in section 14.14.070.

L.

Failing to operate a splash pad installed or modified after January 1, 2023 in compliance
with section 14.14.070.

M.

Having a water feature unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.080.B applies.

N.

Draining or emptying any water from a swimming pool, spa, or hot tub water into any
component of the storm drain system other than as allowed in section 14.14.090.

O.

Failing, as a recreational water park, to comply with the requirements in section
14.14.100.

P.

Having an artificial lake unless an exemption in subsection 14.14.110.B applies.

Q.

Failing to comply with a requirement in the drought response plan.

R.

Failing to comply with a restriction in a deed or other written instrument that limits,
restricts, prohibits, or prescribes particular water use or landscaping materials
on real property, provided that the deed or other written instrument containing the
restriction(s) is recorded against that real property in the Office of the County
Recorder of Clark County, Nevada.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 24, 9-13-2022)

heading: 14.16.010 - General provisions.
text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to provide a mechanism
for the orderly development of the utility system through refunding of costs associated
with the design and construction of utility infrastructure.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all residents of the city, a responsible
party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating, removing, and/or disconnecting
the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, and/or users of city-provided
utilities.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and
enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any powers granted or duties imposed upon
the director may be delegated by the director to persons acting in the beneficial
interest of the city.

D.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in
this title and the department service rules.

(Ord. 2676, § 11 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 84, 2006)

heading: 14.16.020 - Cost for infrastructure.
text:
The cost to design and construct any water, sewer, and/or reclaimed infrastructure
required in connection with the extension of the public utility system to serve the
customer shall be advanced by the customer requesting such service.

(Ord. 2536, § 85, 2006)

heading: 14.16.030 - Construction specifications.
text:
All utility extensions, facilities and/or infrastructure to be constructed by the
customer shall conform to adopted standards.

(Ord. 2536, § 86, 2006)

heading: 14.16.040 - Standard refunding.
text:
A.

Standard refunding agreements.

1.

The city may enter into an agreement which provides for repayment of a portion of
the cost of the main extension lying between the original point of supply and the
customer's property from main frontage fees collected from other properties frontage
to the main extension covered by such agreement during the term provided in the agreement
or until the amount advanced by the customer has been satisfied, as determined in
accordance with the provisions of this title and/or the department's service rules.

2.

The following items may be eligible for standard refunding:

a.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water main extensions to a project;

b.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water main extensions adjacent to a project; and/or

c.

Water, sewer, and reclaimed water mains replacing existing mains.

3.

The period during which refunds are due shall be 20 years, commencing on the date
when the infrastructure covered by the agreement is completed, tested, and accepted
by the city.

4.

Construction shall be deemed to be complete when the utility infrastructure is constructed
according to the approved plans and satisfies all applicable testing and acceptance
criteria.

5.

The city council shall grant the director the authority to enter into and execute
any standard refunding agreement in which the city is not a participant. Should the
city be a participant in a standard refunding agreement, such agreement must be approved
according to city standard operating procedures and policies.

B.

Standard refunding conditions.

1.

Application for standard refunding agreement shall be submitted to the department
in writing accompanied by documentation as required by the city from customer(s) constructing
such infrastructure covered by the agreement. This application shall be submitted
within 90 days of date of acceptance by the city of the infrastructure to be covered
by such agreement.

2.

All customers entering into any refunding agreement with the city shall pay all fees
as outlined in this title and/or the department service rules. These fees are due
and payable at the time of the execution of the agreement.

3.

Customers may be eligible for a refund of main frontage fees collected by the city
from other properties in accordance with this title.

4.

All standard refunding calculations shall be rounded to the nearest foot and shall
be assessed based on the frontage of the applicant's property, as indicated by the
most current data in the Clark County assessor office records, adjacent to the right-of-way
or easement where the existing water, sewer, or reclaimed water main is located in
accordance with this title and/or the department's service rules.

5.

After execution of a valid standard refunding agreement, all main frontage fees collected
in accordance with this title and/or department service rules shall be paid within
60 days from the date of collection.

6.

In the event any expense is incurred by the city within a period of one year after
acceptance of the infrastructure installed by the customer covered by a standard refunding
agreement due to defective materials or workmanship the amount of such expense shall
be deducted from any refund(s) that may become due to the customer thereafter.

(Ord. 2536, § 87, 2006)

heading: 14.16.050 - Special refunding.
text:
A.

Special refunding agreements.

1.

The city may enter into a special refunding agreement which provides for repayment
of a portion of the cost of that backbone infrastructure lying between the original
point of supply and the customer's property from special refunding fees to be collected
by the city from other customers obtaining direct or indirect service from the backbone
infrastructure during the term provided in the special refunding agreement, pursuant
to this title, or until the proportional cost of design and construction advanced
by the customer has been repaid, whichever is earlier.

2.

Any special refunding agreement entered into by the city must be based upon a refunding
report completed in accordance with the department service rules and adopted by the
city council.

3.

The term of any special refunding agreement shall be 20 years, which will commence
on the date the infrastructure covered by the special refunding agreement is completed,
tested and accepted by the city.

4.

Application for special refunding agreement shall be submitted to the director in
writing accompanied by documentation as required by the city within 90 days of the
date of acceptance of the pre-design report by the city for the infrastructure to
be covered by such agreement. All final costs are subject to verification by the city.

5.

The amount subject to repayment under a special refunding agreement shall be the amount
of the actual cost of the work as verified by the city. The final cost of the work
shall be the basis for the determination and calculation of refunds under the special
refunding agreement. Final costs that are eligible for inclusion in the special refunding
agreement are:

a.

Actual construction costs (including administration and safety and traffic control
measures);

b.

Design engineering costs and inspection costs not to exceed an aggregate 15 percent
of item 5 of this section;

c.

Permits and fees;

d.

Performance and related bond costs to the extent not included in item 5 of this section;

e.

Actual financing costs related to subsections (A)(5)(a) through (A)(5)(d) of this
section. Said financing costs shall be computed through the date of final acceptance
of the backbone infrastructure by the city; and

f.

All fees and expenses reasonably incurred concerning the preparation of the special
refunding agreement shall be added to the refunding amount.

6.

Construction shall be deemed to be complete when the utility infrastructure is constructed
according to the approved plans and satisfies all applicable testing and approval
criteria.

B.

Special refunding conditions.

1.

Customers entering into any special refunding agreement with the city shall pay all
fees as outlined in this title and/or the department service rules. These fees are
due and payable upon execution of the agreement.

2.

After execution of a valid special refunding agreement, special refunding fees collected
in accordance with this title and/or department service rules shall be paid to the
customer within 30 days from the last business day of the quarter in which such fees
were collected and will be issued in accordance to the procedures outlined in the
department service rules.

3.

Special refunding fees collected by the city shall be computed as follows:

a.

As to the portion of cost attributable to the holder of the special refunding agreement,
advances shall be accrued quarterly with interest equal to one-fourth the prime rate
plus two percentage points with a maximum of ten percent per year. The prime rate
that is published in the Wall Street Journal or a similar publication approved by
the city's finance director for utilization in the refunding report and being the
prime rate published at the last business day of each calendar quarter for the subsequent
quarter.

b.

As to the portion of cost attributable to city, advances shall be accrued quarterly
with interest equal to one-fourth the Merrill Lynch Bond Index for tax-exempt 30-year
A-rated revenue bonds as printed in the Wall Street Journal or a similar publication
approved by the city's finance director for utilization in the refunding report with
a maximum of ten percent per year. The rate shall be based upon the index rate published
the last business day of each calendar quarter for the subsequent quarter.

c.

The amount that makes up the actual final cost of work shall be depreciated annually
over 40 years using the straight-line method of depreciation or such time line as
recommended and approved in the refunding report. The net book value of the infrastructure
shall become the base for purposes of calculating amounts to be refunded and of computing
the addition of accrued interest.

4.

Special refunding fees, as allocated in the refunding report to a customer, will only
be made for utility infrastructure that service areas not only of the customers but
areas designated in the approved refunding report.

5.

Special refunding fees will be made from fees collected from other customers or the
city whose properties are served by the backbone infrastructure and paid prior to
final issuance of a certificate of occupancy.

6.

In the event two or more customers have designed the same backbone infrastructure,
those eligible costs, or an applicable portion thereof, paid by the customer who has
submitted a performance bond to the city for construction of the relevant system or
facility and has completed said construction shall be refunded.

7.

In the event any expense is incurred by the city within a period of one year after
acceptance of the infrastructure installed by the customer covered by a special refunding
agreement due to defective materials or workmanship on, the amount of such expense
shall be deducted from any refund(s) that may become due to the customer thereafter.

(Ord. 2676, § 11 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 88, 2006)

heading: 14.16.060 - Violations.
text:
Any person who fails or refuses to comply with any provision of this chapter or department's
service rules or who provides false information to the city shall be deemed to be
in violation of this title and shall be subject to discontinuance of service; subject
to any penalties and charges assessed in accordance with this title and/or department's
service rules; and subject to all compliance procedures as prescribed within this
title.

(Ord. 2536, § 89, 2006)

heading: 14.17.010 - General provisions.
text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to ensure compliance
with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health,
safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to all residents of the city, a responsible
party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating, removing, and/or disconnecting
the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, and/or users of city-provided
utilities.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and
enforce the provisions of this chapter. Any powers granted or duties imposed upon
the director may be delegated by the director to persons acting in the beneficial
interest of the city.

D.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in
this title and the department service rules.

(Ord. 2676, § 12, 2008; Ord. 2536, § 91, 2006)

heading: 14.17.020 - Establishment of service.
text:
A.

Applications for service.

1.

The property owner or owner's representative shall make application to the department
and obtain approval from the city prior to connection to or use of a permanent and/or
temporary service. The applicant shall agree to pay for all services used and to abide
by all rules and regulations of the city, this title, and the department service rules.
Applications for temporary service shall be renewed on an annual basis.

2.

The city reserves the right to refuse any request for utility service from any applicant
for any of the following reasons:

a.

An account in their name at the same or any other location is delinquent;

b.

The applicant fails to provide any and all requested information;

c.

When the department determines that the purpose of the request is to circumvent discontinuance
of service in another name because of non-payment of bill(s), fees, fines, reimbursements
or other charges owed to the utility or other violations of the regulations; and/or

d.

When the department determines that the applicant has failed to comply with any provisions
of this title.

3.

A single customer shall be responsible for payment of utility bills for each service
connection. When more than one building or parcel of land is served by a single service
connection, a single customer must be responsible for payment of the utility bill.

4.

The city is not responsible for damage to customer's property and/or piping due to
activation of service. Customer shall ensure piping is in good repair and that all
interior and exterior fixtures are in the "off" position prior to requesting activation
of water service.

(Ord. No. 3023, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. 2536, § 92, 2006)

heading: 14.17.030 - Discontinuance of service.
text:
A.

A customer desiring to discontinue service shall provide advance notice to the department
and provide a mailing address to which the closing bill shall be mailed. Service and
charges will cease as of the discontinuance date provided.

B.

Failure to notify the department of discontinuance of service shall not relieve the
customer of responsibility for payment of any existing billings, or any charges due
prior to notifying the department.

C.

The city reserves the right to discontinue service if there is running and/or leaking
water on the customer's property during service activation.

(Ord. No. 3023, § 1, 6-11-2013; Ord. 2536, § 93, 2006)

heading: 14.17.040 - Meter readings and registration.
text:
A.

Meters shall be read monthly or as reasonably possible.

B.

Customers are responsible for payment of all water that passes through the meter,
regardless of whether such water was put to beneficial use.

C.

Should a meter be inaccessible at the time of regular reading time, or should it be
found to be stuck or damaged so that a reading cannot be obtained, or in cases of
emergency as the city deems necessary, the city reserves the right to estimate the
water consumption for the billing period and to compute the charges on the basis of
the estimated consumption. Should the city determine that a succeeding reading indicates
a material error in the estimated reading, an appropriate adjustment shall be made.

D.

Meter accuracy shall be maintained to the fullest extent practicable for any meter
installed within the city's service area. If there is a dispute, the city may test
the meter using the procedures identified in department service rules.

E.

At the customer's request, a meter testing fee as outlined in the department service
rules will be charged to the customer and the meter will be tested. If the meter is
found to register more or less than the actual water flow, the city will, as reasonably
practical, make the appropriate billing adjustment. Additionally, if the meter is
found to register more than the actual water flow, the meter testing fee will be returned
to the customer.

(Ord. 2536, § 94, 2006)

heading: 14.17.050 - Billing periods.
text:
A.

The city shall establish regular billing periods subject to adjustment at the city's
discretion.

B.

Failure to receive or accept a bill does not relieve a customer of liability for payment
of such bill.

C.

If any opening or closing bill is for a period other than the regular billing period,
the basic monthly service charge shall be prorated based on the actual number of days
in the billing period.

(Ord. 2536, § 95, 2006)

heading: 14.17.060 - Delinquent bills.
text:
A.

Bills shall be due and payable upon the applicable due date. When any bill becomes
delinquent, the city may discontinue utility service pursuant to notification and
termination procedures. Utility service may not be re-established until the delinquent
bill and/or all succeeding bills which may have become due, and any applicable charges
have been paid.

B.

Should any customer fail or refuse to pay for service furnished and charged for in
accordance with this title, the city may not provide service to the customer at the
same or any other location until all delinquent utility bills, applicable fees and
charges have been paid.

C.

Until paid, all fees, rates, and charges imposed by title 14 for water service, wastewater service, reclaimed water service, raw water service,
or any combination of those services, shall constitute a debt owing to the city by
the customer of record and by the owner of such property as shown on the records of
the county assessor, if such record owner is someone other than the customer of record.
Under subsection 2.280.1(c) of the Charter, such delinquent fees, rates, and charges
shall be a lien upon the property to which the service is rendered.

1.

The city may collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges (a) in accordance with
NRS 268.043 by having them collected at the same time as, together with and not separately
from, Clark County's general taxes by having the city through a designee in its department
comply with the requirements in NRS 268.043.1; (b) by perfecting the city's lien upon
the property to which service is rendered by filing/recording in the office of the
county recorder a notice of lien signed by the city clerk, or the city clerk's designee,
that identifies the amount due and unpaid, the name of the record owner(s) of the
property, and a description of the real property subject to the lien; (c) through
a collection agency, as defined in NRS Chapter 649; (d) directly; (e) through a civil
action in any court of competent jurisdiction; and/or (f) through any other means
available to the city under applicable law.

2.

If the city chooses to collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges under subsection
1(a) of this section, the city shall have the right to collect all penalties allowable
under NRS 268.043 and NRS 361.483.7 from the owner(s) of the real property with respect
to which the fees, rates, and charges are delinquent at the time such delinquencies
became a lien against that property.

3.

If the city chooses to collect such delinquent fees, rates, and charges under subsection
1(b) of this section, no notice of lien shall be recorded against the property by
the city unless written notice of the delinquency has been mailed or personally delivered
to the record owner of the property at the last mailing address shown by the records
of the county assessor and the record owner of the property has been given 15 days
to pay the delinquent amount in full. If there is more than one record owner, failure
to send a copy of that notice to a particular owner does not invalidate a notice if
properly sent to another record owner. An error or mistake in the name of the record
owner contained in any notice of lien does not defeat the lien, unless a correction
of the notice of lien in a particular instance would prejudice the rights of an innocent
bona fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value, but then only with respect to the bona
fide purchaser or encumbrancer for value who was prejudiced. The owner(s) of record
and/or customer(s) of record must pay the city a service charge, in an amount approved
by city council and identified in the department service rules, for a release of the
lien filed with the office of the county recorder and any and all recording costs
incurred by the city in recording the release of lien. After the delinquency is fully
satisfied or discharged, at the written request of the owner(s) of record or customer(s)
of record, and after that owner or customer pays the required fees, the city will
cause to be recorded a notice of discharge or release of the notice of lien. After
recording the required notice of lien and unless the delinquency is fully satisfied
or discharged, the city may foreclose said lien against such property by following
the process identified in NRS 108.239, as amended, for the foreclosure of mechanic's
liens. Pursuant to section 2.280.1 of the Charter, the lien is coequal with the latest
lien thereon to secure the payment of general taxes, the lien is not subject to extinguishment
by the sale of any property on account of the nonpayment of general taxes, and the
lien is prior and superior to all liens, claims, encumbrances and titles other than
the liens of assessments and general taxes. The lien is not extinguished if the city
does not commence a foreclosure action.

D.

When a customer receiving service at multiple locations allows a bill for one or more
locations to become delinquent, and the service for which the bill is delinquent is
shut off, then all of the other service locations may be shut off and subject to all
applicable fees and charges in accordance with this title and department service rules.

E.

When a customer's utility bill is not paid in full on or before the due date, it will
be considered delinquent in accordance with the provisions of this title and any and
all charges shall be subject to the assessment of late charges as established in the
department service rules.

(Ord. No. 3442, § 1, 9-19-2017; Ord. No. 2909, § 2, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2536, § 96, 2006)

heading: 14.17.070 - Billing adjustments.
text:
Upon notification of a potential billing error, the city will investigate to verify
billing accuracy. In no case shall the city make corrections retroactively for a period
of more than 12 months. Any adjustments to the customer's account shall be at the
discretion of the director.

(Ord. 2536, § 97, 2006)

heading: 14.17.080 - Violations.
text:
Any person who fails or refuses to comply with any of the provisions in this chapter
shall be deemed to be in violation of this title and shall be subject to discontinuance
of service, subject to any penalties and charges assessed in accordance with this
title and/or department service rules, and subject to all compliance procedures as
prescribed within this title.

(Ord. 2536, § 98, 2006)

heading: 14.18.010 - General provisions.
text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter sets forth responsibility, authority, and provisions to ensure compliance
with all federal, state, and local requirements for the protection of public health,
safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter shall apply to (1) all residents of the city, (2)
a person that operates, maintains, repairs, relocates, removes, and/or disconnects
to or from the city's water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, (3) a person
who wishes to connect to the city's water system and/or publicly owned treatment works,
(4) a user, and (5) a customer.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and
enforce the provisions of this chapter. The director may delegate any powers granted
to or duties imposed upon the director, the city, or the department to a person acting
in the beneficial interest of the city.

D.

Compliance. All provisions of this chapter are subject to compliance procedures as outlined in
this title and the department service rules.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 25, 9-13-2022; Ord. 2676, § 13 (part), 2008; Ord. 2536, § 100, 2006)

heading: 14.18.020 - Fees, rates and charges.
text:
A.

Per article II, section 2.280(c) of the Henderson City Charter, the Henderson city council shall fix charges and
rates for water and wastewater services.

B.

Fees, rates and charges shall be billed in accordance with this title and shall be
applied as outlined in this title and the department service rules.

C.

Final determination of a customer's use or billing category shall be made by the director.
All applicable fees and charges shall be assessed accordingly.

D.

The assessment and collection of all fees and charges shall be made in accordance
with the established procedures of the city, relative to the assessment and collection
of those fees and charges. Notwithstanding this requirement, the director reserves
the right to determine the manner through which all fees and charges are collected.

E.

All fees and charges shall be paid to the city prior to issuance of the certificate
of occupancy.

F.

Basic service and usage charges.

1.

Service connections shall be considered in use and appropriate charges shall be assessed
commencing with the date of installation unless the customer has provided advance
notice that the connection shall not be used until such time as it is needed. If the
customer has provided such advance notice, charges shall commence on the date the
service is first turned on by the city.

2.

Any service turned on without advance authorization from the city shall be assessed
charges based on the date of installation in addition to any other charges or fees.

3.

Charges for usage shall be based upon the volume of flow based upon either readings
from city approved water meters, approved wastewater flow monitoring equipment or
other methods that may be approved by the city.

4.

All users shall be charged a monthly basic service charge in addition to any monthly
usage charges accrued.

5.

Exemptions from basic monthly water and sewer service charge.

a.

Upon application to the department, a low-income or permanently disabled person may
have their own private residential account exempted from all or a portion of the basic
monthly water and sewer service charge, as determined by the department, by qualifying
in accordance with the Nevada Energy Assistance Program, or similar program criteria
as established by the department.

b.

All customers who received an exemption based on income must re-qualify annually to
continue receiving that exemption and provide information required by the department
to support that exemption.

c.

Residents who are senior citizens, received the senior exemption on or before November
1, 1996, and have not changed their place of residence from the residence they were
in as of the date they began receiving the senior exemption continue to be eligible
to receive an exemption from the basic monthly water and sewer service charge until
such time as the customer changes their place of residence.

d.

The applicant shall furnish such information as the city may require, supporting their
application for an exemption.

G.

The city reserves the right to inspect any facility to determine the actual equivalent
residential units (ERUs) being contributed to the collection system. Additional sewer
system development charges and regional fees may be assessed as a result of the findings.
Fees will be based on the current rate in place at the time of verification. Regional
fees will be charged if applicable at the time of permit issuance.

(Ord. No. 3831, § 1, 1-4-2022; Ord. No. 2951, § 4, 12-20-2011; Ord. 2798, § 6, 1-20-2009; Ord. 2536, § 101, 2006)

heading: 14.18.030 - Deposits.
text:
A.

The city may require a deposit from any applicant or existing customer in any situation
where the city has cause to believe that a deposit is required.

B.

The deposit paid to the city shall be held until all equipment has been returned and
verified by the city to be in satisfactory working and operational condition with
no damages and/or all charges for the service and any damages have been paid.

C.

Upon service discontinuance, any applicable deposit shall be credited to the closing
bill and any amount remaining shall be refunded to the customer in accordance with
this title and department service rules.

D.

The customer's deposit may be applied as a credit on the customer's account when 12
months of service have passed and none of the bills become delinquent or applied to
the closing bill upon discontinuance of service.

(Ord. 2536, § 102, 2006)

heading: 14.18.040 - System development charges.
text:
All permits, will be charged water system and sewer system development charges based
on the fee and charge scheduled in the department service rules.

For large commercial and/or industrial customers with estimated peak wastewater flows
over 100,000 gallons per day (GPD), after one year of full operation, a one-time adjustment
may be made based on actual maximum month (30 days) wastewater flows multiplied by
12 months. The annual peak wastewater flows shall be divided by 90,000 gallons to
determine the actual ERUs. The actual ERUs shall be multiplied by the single-family
resident ERU rate to derive the customer's adjusted SDC. The initial SDC shall be
compared to the actual.

(Ord. No. 2909, § 3, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2798, § 6, 1-20-2009; Ord. 2536, § 103, 2006)

heading: 14.18.045 - West Henderson 2630/2760 PZ water backbone infrastructure rates.
text:
A.

Planning and design of water backbone infrastructure for the West Henderson 2630 Pressure
Zone and the West Henderson 2760 Pressure Zone, construction of that infrastructure,
and financing of that construction are required to support water service to existing
and future developments in the West Henderson area. The director has the right to
determine the size and capacity of the water backbone infrastructure, timing of construction
of the water backbone infrastructure, and method of financing the construction, taking
into account projected service needs of the West Henderson area served and the need
for the orderly and efficient development of the city's public infrastructure system.
The West Henderson 2630 Pressure Zone ("2630 PZ") and the West Henderson 2760 Pressure
Zone ("2760 PZ") are located in West Henderson. A depiction of the 2630 PZ and the
2760 PZ is available on the city's website.

B.

Through December 31, 2022, the rate charged to projects that the city determines will
receive a benefit from the water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed,
and/or financed for (1) a portion of the 2630 PZ is referred to as the "phase 1A 2630
PZ water infrastructure rate" and (2) a portion of the 2760 PZ is referred to as the
"phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate." These rates are addressed in this section
14.18.045. The amount charged for the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and phase
1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate (collectively, "phase 1A 2630/2760 PZ rates")
shall be in addition to system development, regional connection, and other applicable
charges for water service.

C.

Effective January 1, 2023, the rate charged to projects that the city determines will
receive a benefit from the water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed,
and/or financed for (1) a portion of the 2630 PZ is referred to as the "WH 2630 PZ
water infrastructure rate" and (2) a portion of the 2760 PZ is referred to as the
"WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate." These rates are addressed in this section
14.18.045. The amount charged for the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and WH 2760 PZ water
infrastructure rate (collectively, "WH 2630/2760 PZ rates") shall be in addition to
system development, regional connection, and other applicable charges for water service.

D.

Effective January 1, 2023, all new projects that the city determines will receive
a benefit from existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed,
constructed, and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ shall be charged and
pay the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure
rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s) charged shall be based
upon the total EDUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement
plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s)
in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or, if
a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the rate in
effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the project.

E.

Any project that was initiated at the city before January 1, 2023, and either was
required to pay the rate(s) established (or other amount charged by the city) for
existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or
financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ or whose approval was conditioned on the
city being paid such rate(s) shall be charged and pay, as the city determines is appropriate,
(1) if the building permit is issued prior to January 1, 2023, the phase 1A 2630 PZ
water infrastructure rate and/or the phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate or
(2) if the building permit is issued on or after January 1, 2023, the WH 2630 PZ water
infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate. The amount(s)
charged shall be based upon the total EDUs proposed for the project, as reflected
in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s)
used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit
for the project or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from
the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement
plans for the project.

F.

All projects that proceed with additional improvements to a property that result in
an increase in water usage above the usage previously proposed - as reflected in the
civil improvement plans approved by the city, in the building permit issued by the
city, or by other means of receiving official city approval for such additional improvements
(each, a "city approval") - and that the department determines will receive a benefit
from existing or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed,
and/or financed for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ shall be charged and pay, as the
department determines is appropriate, (1) if the city approval is issued prior to
January 1, 2023, the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, and/or phase 1A 2760
PZ water infrastructure rate and (2) if the city approval is issued on or after January
1, 2023, the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure
rate. Whether there is an increase in water usage shall be determined by the director
in their sole discretion. The rate(s) charged shall be based upon the increase in
total additional EDUs associated with the property improvements and at the rate in
effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the proposed improvements
or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the
rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the proposed
improvements or provides its approval of the additional improvements by other means.

G.

As provided for in this title, equivalent dwelling unit (EDU) is defined as "a measure
of water demand equivalent to the amount of water used annually by an average single-family
residential dwelling unit. One EDU is equivalent to 0.55 acre-feet of water per year."
For the purpose of calculating the total EDUs attributable to each project being assessed
a rate under this section 14.18.045, the EDU calculation table in subsection 14.18.045.L shall apply. However, where
it is determined by the director that the "EDU Calculation Factor" or "EDU %" reflected
in that table does not adequately reflect the water demands placed upon the city's
water system by a proposed project, then the city shall not use that table and instead
shall use an alternate method in order to determine the appropriate amount to charge
that project for its equitable share of the water backbone infrastructure planned,
designed, constructed, and/or financed for 2630/2760 PZ. Final determination of such
alternate method shall be made by the director.

H.

The phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $3,067.00 per EDU, and the
phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $5,145.00 per EDU. The initial
WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $3,527.00 per EDU, and the initial WH
2760 PZ water infrastructure rate shall be $5,660.00 per EDU. These rates are based
upon actual and estimated costs for the city to fund the planning, design, construction,
and/or financing of the water infrastructure for the 2630 PZ and the 2760 PZ. The
city manager may adjust the WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate and/or the WH 2760
PZ water infrastructure rate once each calendar year by an amount that (1) for the
WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, is no more than 15 percent of the WH 2630 PZ
water infrastructure rate in effect in the immediately preceding period; and (2) for
the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate, is no more than ten percent of the WH 2760
PZ water infrastructure rate in effect in the immediately preceding period. The city
will identify the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, the phase 1A 2760 PZ
water infrastructure rate, the then-current WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate,
and the then-current WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate in the department service
rules. Unless otherwise approved in writing by the director in their sole discretion,
the rate(s) assessed shall be paid to the city when the city issues a building permit,
prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy, or prior to commencement of temporary
or permanent water service, whichever date is earliest.

I.

For five years after a certificate of occupancy is issued for a project or an improvement
is made to a project, the city has the right to audit that project to confirm that
the project's average annual water usage is substantially the same as the total EDUs
proposed for the project or project improvement. If the city determines the project
is using more EDUs than proposed, the city may require the original developer of the
project or project improvement, as applicable, to pay the difference between the total
EDUs charged the project and total EDUs actually used at the property at the phase
1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate,
WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, and/or WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure rate,
as appropriate, in effect on the date the city prepares a bill for the additional
payment.

J.

If the phase 1A 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, phase 1A 2760 PZ water infrastructure
rate, WH 2630 PZ water infrastructure rate, or the WH 2760 PZ water infrastructure
rate is adjusted after the city receives a payment, the city is not obligated to true-up
the payment received or to refund/collect any difference.

K.

If a customer requests to design, construct, and pay for all or a portion of the WH
water backbone water infrastructure for the 2630 PZ and/or for the 2760 PZ, the city
may enter into a special refunding agreement acceptable to the city and in accordance
with applicable provisions in section 14.16.050 that provides for repayment of a portion of those costs from WH rates collected,
or to be collected, by the city from customers that will receive a benefit from existing
or future water backbone infrastructure planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed
for the 2630 PZ or for the 2760 PZ.

heading: 14.18.047 - West Henderson-Bermuda wastewater backbone infrastructure rates.
text:
A.

Planning and design of wastewater backbone infrastructure for West Henderson, construction
of that infrastructure, financing of that construction, and phasing of that construction
are required to support wastewater service to existing and future developments in
the West Henderson area. The director has the right to determine the size and capacity
of that wastewater backbone infrastructure, phasing of construction of that wastewater
backbone infrastructure, and method of financing the construction, taking into account
projected service needs of the West Henderson area served and the need for the orderly
and efficient development of the publicly-owned treatment works.

B.

The rates charged to projects that the city determines will receive a benefit from
segment 1, segment 2, segment 3 or segment 9 of the wastewater backbone infrastructure
planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for the Bermuda Sewer Basin within
West Henderson are referred to as the "segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate,"
"segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate," "segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate"
and "segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate," respectively, and, collectively, as
the "WH-Bermuda backbone wastewater infrastructure rates." The WH-Bermuda wastewater
backbone infrastructure rates shall be in addition to system development and other
applicable charges for wastewater service.

C.

Effective November 25, 2019, all new projects that the city determines will receive
a benefit from existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed,
constructed, and/or financed for the Bermuda Sewer Basin within West Henderson shall
be charged and pay the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater
infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment
9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s)
charged shall be based upon the total ERUs proposed for the project, as reflected
in the civil improvement plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s)
used will be the one(s) in effect on the date the city processes the building permit
for the project or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from
the city, at the rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement
plans for the project.

D.

Any project that was initiated at the city before November 25, 2019 and whose approval
was conditioned on the city being paid the rate(s) established or other amount charged
by the city for existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure planned, designed,
constructed, and/or financed for West Henderson shall be charged and pay the segment
1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the
segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure
rate, as the city determines is appropriate. The amount(s) charged shall be based
upon the total ERUs proposed for the project, as reflected in the civil improvement
plans for the project approved by the city, and the rate(s) used will be the one(s)
in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the project or November
25, 2019, whichever is later.

E.

Effective November 25, 2019, all projects that proceed with additional improvements
to a property that result or might result in an increase in the amount of wastewater
discharged to the publicly owned treatment works above that previously proposed -
as reflected in the civil improvement plans, in the building permit or by other means
of receiving city approval for such additional improvements - and that the city determines
will receive a benefit from existing or future wastewater backbone infrastructure
planned, designed, constructed, and/or financed for West Henderson shall be charged
and pay the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure
rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater
infrastructure rate, as the city determines is appropriate. Whether the improvements
result or might result in an increase in the amount wastewater discharged to the publicly-owned
treatment works above that previously proposed shall be determined by the director
in his or her sole discretion. The rate(s) charged shall be based upon the increase
in total additional ERUs associated with the property improvements and at the rate
in effect on the date the city processes the building permit for the proposed improvements
or, if a project is not required to obtain a building permit from the city, at the
rate in effect on the date the city approves the civil improvement plans for the proposed
improvements or provides its approval of the additional improvements by other means.

F.

The initial segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $31.52 per ERU. The
initial segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $79.45 per ERU. The initial
segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $131.39 per ERU. The initial segment
9 wastewater infrastructure rate shall be $270.83 per ERU. Initially, these rates
have been based upon actual and estimated costs for the city to fund the planning,
design, construction, and/or financing of the West Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure.
After construction of the particular segment is completed, the city manager may adjust
the rate for that segment to reflect the actual costs to plan, design, construct,
and finance the West Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure in that segment.
The city will identify the then-current segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate,
the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure
rate and/or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure rate in the department service
rules. Unless otherwise approved in writing by the director at his or her sole discretion,
the rate(s) assessed shall be paid to the city when the city issues a building permit,
prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy or prior to commencement of permanent
wastewater service, whichever is earliest.

G.

For five years after a certificate of occupancy is issued for a project or an improvement
is made to a project, the city has the right to audit that project to confirm that
the project's average annual wastewater discharge to the publicly owned treatment
works is substantially the same as the total ERUs proposed for the project or project
improvement. If the city determines the project is using more capacity of the West
Henderson wastewater backbone infrastructure than proposed, the city may require the
original developer of the project or project improvement, as applicable, to pay the
difference between the total ERUs charged the project and total ERUs actually used
at the property at the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater
infrastructure rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate and/or the segment
9 wastewater infrastructure rate, as appropriate, in effect on the date the city prepares
a bill for the additional payment.

H.

If the segment 1 wastewater infrastructure rate, the segment 2 wastewater infrastructure
rate, the segment 3 wastewater infrastructure rate or the segment 9 wastewater infrastructure
rate is adjusted after the city receives a payment, the city is not obligated to true-up
the payment received or to refund/collect any difference.

(Ord. No. 3638, § 2, 11-19-2019)

heading: 14.18.050 - Southern Nevada Water Authority regional connection charge.
text:
A.

Effective March 1, 1996, a regional water connection fee shall be assessed to all
projects as per the Southern Nevada Water System Facilities and Operations Agreement
among the Southern Nevada Water Authority (SNWA), City of Boulder City, City of Henderson,
City of North Las Vegas, and the Las Vegas Valley Water District. The rate charged
shall be based on the rate in effect at the time the application for new utility service
or improvement plans (as required by the city) are approved and the actual connection
fees are paid. For combination fire and domestic meters, the charge shall be based
on the smaller meter.

B.

Effective November 1, 2005, regional connection charges assessed, in amounts to be
increased on the first of the month in May and November each year thereafter through
the year 2008, to all projects served by the city.

C.

The city reserves the right to audit any project within the initial three years of
operation to confirm the basis or estimate used to determine the regional connection
charge and may adjust the amount of the regional connection charge based upon the
results of such audit. Subsequent audits may be conducted by the city to determine
any increase in the basis of the regional connection charge and may adjust the regional
connection charge at the rate in place at the time of the audit.

(Ord. No. 2909, § 3, 3-15-2011; Ord. 2536, § 104, 2006)

heading: 14.18.060 - Clean Water Coalition regional sewer connection charge and regional sewer user charge.
text:
The Clean Water Coalition (CWC) consists of four member agencies, the City of Henderson,
the City of Las Vegas, Clark County Water Reclamation District, and the City of North
Las Vegas. The CWC is tasked to implement the systems conveyance and operations program
(SCOP) to improve our community's water quality through construction of a 17-mile
pipeline that will carry high quality treated wastewater deep into Lake Mead. The
SCOP project is funded through a combination of sewer connection and user charges.
All member agencies of CWC have implemented these charges.

The regional sewer connection charges for wastewater became effective October 1, 2006.
The regional sewer user charges for wastewater became effective July 1, 2007. At its
meeting of February 23, 2010, the CWC voted to stop levying assessments to its member
agencies based on regional connection and sewer user charges, effective March 1, 2010.
With formal termination of the Clean Water Coalition imminent, the city ceased assessment
of regional connection fees effective March 1, 2010, and regional sewer user charges
effective May 1, 2011.

(Ord. No. 2915, § 1, 5-3-2011; Ord. No. 2857, § 1, 6-1-2010; Ord. 2592, § 1, 2007; Ord. 2536, §
105, 2006; Ord. No. 2951, § 4, 12-20-2011)

heading: 14.18.070 - Southern Nevada Water Authority regional commodity charge.
text:
Effective on all bills mailed after November 5, 1996, a charge per 1,000 gallons shall
be assessed to all metered potable water consumption as per the Southern Nevada Water
System Facilities and Operations Agreement among the Southern Nevada Water Authority,
City of Boulder City, City of Henderson, City of North Las Vegas and the Las Vegas
Valley Water District.

(Ord. 2536, § 106, 2006)

heading: 14.18.110 - Charge for taking water without authorization.
text:
A.

If a person takes water from the city's water system in violation of a provision of
chapter 14.03, chapter 14.05, or chapter 14.06 of the Code, that person and/or the owner(s) of the equipment used to transport the
water taken shall be charged and shall pay the estimated water usage at 12x the highest
rate per 1,000 gallons in the highest rate block for the potable water volume charge
or other rate authorized by council and set forth in the department service rules,
whichever rate is higher, and the cost of any damage to city facilities. The department
may estimate the amount of water taken, including, but not limited to, based on the
use to which that water was apparently put, the equipment used to take or apply that
water, the estimated length of time the person was taking the water, and the container
or tank used to transport or store that water. The applicable rate shall be based
on the rates, fees and charges in this title and/or the department service rules that
the department determines is appropriate. Using a container or tank to store that
water shall constitute a rebuttable presumption that the container or tank was empty
before the person took water from the city's water system and that the container or
tank was completely filled after that person took the water.

B.

In addition to being responsible for the charges described in subsection 14.18.110.A,
the person who took water from the city's water system in violation of a provision
of chapter 14.03, chapter 14.05, or chapter 14.06 of the Code and/or the owner(s) of the equipment used to transport that water is
subject to all compliance procedures as prescribed within this title and is subject
to all penalties imposed by applicable law.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 27, 9-13-2022)
