heading: 14.21.010 - General provisions.
text:
A.

Purpose and policy. This chapter 14.21 sets forth provisions and authority to ensure compliance with title 14 of the Code and all federal, state, and local requirements enforceable by the city
for the protection of public health, safety and welfare.

B.

Scope. The provisions of this chapter 14.21 shall apply to (1) all residents of the city, (2) a person that operates, maintains,
repairs, relocates, removes, and/or disconnects to or from the city's water system
and/or publicly owned treatment works, (3) a person that violates a provision of title 14 of the Code, (4) a person with a property interest in or control over real property
in the city's corporate boundaries or with a property interest in or control over
real property to which the city provides any type of water or wastewater service (such
as a homeowners association), (5) a user, and (6) a customer. The operation or administration
of this chapter 14.21 shall in no way change or diminish the effect of other provisions in this Code dealing
with like or similar matters.

C.

Administration. Except as otherwise provided herein, the director shall administer, implement, and
enforce the provisions of title 14 of the Code. The director may delegate any powers granted to or duties imposed upon
the director, the city, or the department to a person acting in the beneficial interest
of the city.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 28, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.020 - Criminal prosecution.
text:
A person who willfully, knowingly, or negligently violates a provision of chapter 14.03, chapter 14.04, chapter 14.05, chapter 14.06, chapter 14.08, and/or chapter 14.14 of the Code is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punishable
by imprisonment in the Henderson Detention Center for not more than six months and/or
by a fine of not more than $1,000.00 per day for each violation. In lieu of all or
part of the foregoing punishment which may be imposed, the convicted person may be
sentenced to perform a fixed period of community service pursuant to the conditions
prescribed in NRS 176.087 and, as applicable, to pay restitution in accordance with
NRS 176.033. If a corporation is convicted of a violation, the corporation is punishable
by a fine not exceeding $1,000.00 and, as applicable, shall pay restitution in accordance
with NRS 176.033, unless otherwise provided by law or the code. With respect to violations
that are continuous with respect to time, each day that the violation continues is
a separate offense. With respect to violations that are not continuous with respect
to time, each prohibited act and/or each failure to perform a required act is a separate
offense.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.030 - Injunctive relief.
text:
The city may petition a court of competent jurisdiction for the issuance of a temporary
or permanent injunction, as appropriate, to restrain the continuance of a violation
or compel the specific performance of a requirement imposed under title 14 of the Code. The city may also seek such other action as is appropriate for legal
and/or equitable relief. A petition for injunctive relief shall not be a bar against,
or a prerequisite for, the city to take any other action.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.040 - Administrative enforcement.
text:
A.

General.

1.

An enforcement official has the authority to determine whether a violation of title 14 of the Code exists and to take appropriate action to gain compliance with the provisions
of title 14 of the Code. These powers include the power to impose administrative fines, to issue
notices of violation, to have the city take corrective action, to issue notices and
orders, to order and conduct a show cause hearing, to inspect public and private property,
to order abatement of a violation, and to use any remedy that is available in title 14 of the Code, in another provision of the Code, and in Nevada law. "Enforcement official"
shall mean the director and any director designee.

2.

The enforcement official is authorized to grant minor variations from the strict application
of specific provisions of title 14 of the Code where, in the opinion of the director, the corrective work or compliance
measures are in substantial compliance with the intent of the applicable provision.

B.

Administrative fine.

1.

The enforcement official may impose, as an alternative to criminal prosecution, administrative
fines identified in section 14.21.050 for a violation of a provision of chapter 14.02, chapter 14.03, chapter 14.04, chapter 14.05, chapter 14.06, chapter 14.08, and/or chapter 14.14 of the Code by issuing a notice of violation and shall impose a fine(s) as outlined
in this chapter 14.21 and any department enforcement response plan. Payment of an administrative fine shall
not relieve the person(s) responsible from their obligation to correct, abate, or
stop the violation nor shall it bar further enforcement action by the city or an enforcement
official.

2.

Before issuing a notice of violation and imposing a fine for violation of chapter 14.14 of the Code, the enforcement official may (but is not required to) send one or more
warning letters to the person(s) alleged or deemed to have violated that chapter or
otherwise potentially responsible for the violation. If the enforcement official sends
a warning letter, that letter must notify them of the violation and, if applicable,
provide a deadline to correct the violation. The enforcement official may have that
letter delivered by email, mail, courier service, personal delivery, or any other
method of delivery the enforcement official determines is appropriate.

3.

If an administrative fine amount is due and owed to the city by a person cited, the
person cited is a customer and the violation relates to utility service to the customer,
the city may add that fine amount to the person cited's utility bill as a charge for
utility service if:

a.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer and
did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The person cited timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, the DUS
hearing officer identified a deadline that fine amount was due, the person cited did
not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the DUS hearing officer in the Hearing
Officer Decision and (1) the person cited did not file a timely request for reconsideration
of the Hearing Officer Decision or (2) the person cited filed a timely request for
reconsideration of the Hearing Officer Decision, the director identified a deadline
the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline
identified by the director and the person cited did not file a timely written appeal
of the director's decision to the city manager or (3) the person cited filed a timely
request for reconsideration of the Hearing Officer Decision, the director affirmed
or modified the fine amount, the person cited filed a timely written appeal to the
city manager, the city manager identified a deadline that amount was due and the person
cited did not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the city manager; or

c.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer,
the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director identified
a deadline the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the
deadline identified by the director and the person cited did not file a timely written
appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

d.

The person cited did not timely request a hearing before the DUS hearing officer,
the person cited filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director identified
a deadline the fine amount was due, the person cited did not pay that amount by the
deadline identified by the director, the person cited filed a timely written appeal
of the director's decision to the city manager, the city manager identified a deadline
the fine amount was due and the person cited did not pay that amount by the deadline
identified by the city manager.

However, if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and accordingly
the city delivered the notice of violation to the property owner in accordance with
subsection 14.21.040.F.4, the city may only add an administrative fine amount due
and owed to the city to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service
if, as to that fine amount, (w) the property owner did not timely request a hearing
before the DUS hearing officer and did not file a timely request for reconsideration,
or (x) the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer,
received a Hearing Officer Decision and did not file a timely request for reconsideration
of that order, or (y) the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS
hearing officer, received a Hearing Officer Decision, filed a timely request for reconsideration
of that Hearing Officer Decision, received a decision from the director and did not
file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager, or (z)
the property owner timely requested a hearing before the DUS hearing officer, received
a Hearing Officer Decision, filed a timely request for reconsideration of that Hearing
Officer Decision, received a decision from the director, filed a timely written appeal
of the director's decision to the city manager and received a decision from the city
manager.

4.

If an administrative fine amount is due and owed to the city and the person who owes
the city that amount holds a city-issued license or city-issued permit, has applied
for a city-issued license or city-issued permit, has requested a city inspection,
is seeking renewal or transfer of a city-issued license or city-issued permit, or
is seeking a city approval, the city may take one or more of the following actions
until that person pays the city the amount owed:

a.

Revoke the city-issued license and/or city-issued permit;

b.

Deny, or condition the city's approval of, that person's application for the city-issued
license and/or city-issued permit;

c.

Refuse to schedule or perform the city inspection;

d.

Deny, or condition the city's approval of, a renewal or transfer of the city-issued
license or city-issued permit; or

e.

Refuse to provide, or impose conditions on, the city approval being sought.

C.

Corrective actions.

1.

When a person, with or without prior authorization from the department, operates,
maintains, repairs, relocates, cuts, changes, removes, disconnects, interferes with
or damages in any manner the city's public water system, reclaimed water system, raw
water system and/or publicly owned treatment works, the department may choose but
is not obligated to repair the damages to the city facilities, replace the city facilities,
repair some or all damages to any real property or personal property, perform any
other remediation work the city determines is necessary and invoice that person for
the actual costs of the work. The person invoiced may file a request for reconsideration
in accordance with section 14.21.120. The city may add the invoiced amount, as modified by the director or the city manager
in accordance with section 14.21.120, to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service if the person invoiced
is a customer and:

a.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice and
did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the
customer filed a timely request for reconsideration and the director affirmed or modified
the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, the customer did
not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director, and the customer did
not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

c.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the
customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified
the invoiced amount, the customer files a timely written appeal of the director's
decision to the city manager, the city manager affirmed or modified the invoiced amount
and identified a deadline that amount was due, and the customer did not pay that amount
by the deadline identified by the city manager.

2.

If, under another provision in title 14 of the Code, the city takes corrective action and issues an invoice for the services
or work performed, the person invoiced may file a request for reconsideration in accordance
with section 14.21.120. The city may add the invoiced amount, as modified by the director or the city manager
in accordance with section 14.21.120, to the customer's utility bill as a charge for utility service if the person invoiced
is a customer and:

a.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice and
did not file a timely request for reconsideration; or

b.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the
customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified
the invoiced amount and identified a deadline that amount was due, the customer did
not pay that amount by the deadline identified by the director, and the customer did
not file a timely written appeal of the director's decision to the city manager; or

c.

The customer did not pay the invoice by the deadline identified on the invoice, the
customer filed a timely request for reconsideration, the director affirmed or modified
the invoiced amount, the customer filed a timely written appeal of the director's
decision to the city manager, the city manager affirmed or modified the invoiced amount
and identified a deadline that amount was due, and the customer did not pay that amount
by the deadline identified by the city manager.

D.

Termination of service. With or without prior notice and in accordance with any applicable requirements in
this title, in the department service rules, and in the department's written procedures,
the city may shut off, stop, prevent turn-on of utility service and any associated
equipment, and otherwise terminate water, wastewater, reclaimed and/or raw water service
without the customer's permission. The city is not obligated to resume or re-establish
service until after all violations are corrected to the director's satisfaction, all
delinquent fees, rates and charges are paid to the city, and all administrative fine
amounts due and owed to the city are paid.

E.

Denial and revocation of permits, licenses and inspections. The city may deny, revoke or withhold city-issued permits, city-issued licenses,
and/or inspections for any facility or person associated with the premises.

F.

Notice of violation(s). The city may issue a notice of violation(s).

1.

The notice of violation must contain, at a minimum, the following information:

a.

The name and address (if known) of the person or customer responsible for the violation
(referred to as the "person cited");

b.

A brief description of the violation(s) and a reference to the applicable ordinance
or code citation(s);

c.

The location, date and (when known) time of the violation;

d.

Where appropriate, the action required to correct the violation(s) and the deadline
by when the violation(s) must be corrected;

e.

The name of the person issuing the notice of violation;

f.

The amount of the administrative fine(s) imposed for the violation(s); and

g.

Information advising of the manner and time for responding to the notice of violation.

2.

No error concerning, or omission of, any of the above-described information is grounds
for the dismissal of a proceeding relating to a notice of violation unless the person
requesting the dismissal demonstrates substantial prejudice from the error and/or
omission.

3.

The notice of violation may be issued by any peace officer employed by the city or
by an enforcement official. Any notice of violation issued pursuant to this subsection
14.21.040.F shall constitute a declaration that is subject to the penalty of perjury.

4.

An original notice of violation, or a copy thereof, must be filed with and retained
by the department. A notice of violation is prima facie evidence of the facts that
are alleged therein. The department must deliver the notice of violation personally,
by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to
the person cited, the property owner (if the person cited is a user and not the owner
of the property and the violation relates to utility services at the property) and,
if the person cited is an entity, to an officer, key employee, manager in charge,
or registered agent of that entity. That notice of violation will be deemed to have
been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered
personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt
if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or
otherwise unsuccessful.

5.

Where the notice of violation data is entered into and stored in a computer or similar
device, any printout or other output readable by sight that accurately reflects such
data is an original notice of violation for purposes of a proceeding under this chapter 14.21. Any such data entry that is moved or copied into another computer or similar device
is intended to constitute an additional or replacement of the record of the data by
the issuing officer or employee and is also an original notice of violation for purposes
of a proceeding under this chapter 14.21.

6.

The person cited must respond to a notice of violation within the time prescribed
in that notice in one of the following ways:

a.

Admit responsibility for the commission of the violation and liability by paying the
amount of any administrative fines; or

b.

Dispute the notice of violation by requesting a hearing before the DUS hearing officer
or filing a request for reconsideration. A hearing may be requested by sending a written
request to the department with the following information:

(1)

The name of the individual on the notice of violation;

(2)

The current address of the individual; and

(3)

The violation(s) and any administrative fines identified in the notice of violation
the person wishes to dispute at the hearing.

7.

If the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation
relates to utility services at the property and accordingly the department delivered
the notice of violation to the property owner in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.4,
that property owner may (a) admit responsibility in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.a
and correct the violations in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.8, or (b) dispute
the notice of violation by requesting a hearing in accordance subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b.

8.

If the person cited (and any property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7)
admits responsibility, that person must correct the violation(s) identified in the
notice of violation by the deadline in that notice or, if approved in writing by the
director, by a different deadline(s).

9.

If the person cited (and any property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7)
fails to admit responsibility or dispute the notice of violation within the time prescribed
in that notice and in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6, such failure shall
constitute an admission of all matters and facts contained in the notice of violation,
each such person is deemed to admit responsibility for the commission of the violation(s)
and any administrative fine amounts imposed, any administrative fine amounts imposed
are immediately due and owed to the city by each such person and each such person
must correct the violation(s) identified in the notice of violation by the deadline(s)
in that notice. If the violation(s) are not corrected by such deadline(s), the department
(after providing written notice to that person and the property owner - if the person
cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility
services at the property - and at that customer's and that property owner's expense)
may choose but is not obligated to perform the abatement or take other action(s) to
correct or address the violation(s).

The city shall invoice the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited
is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services
at the property) for the actual costs of that work.

10.

If the person cited requests a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b
(or the property owner requests a hearing pursuant to subsection 14.21.040.F.7 and
in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b), the department shall schedule a hearing
at which each such person that requested the hearing shall be required to appear to
dispute the notice of violation(s). The scheduling of the hearing, its conduct and
other procedures of the administrative hearing shall be governed by section 14.21.110.

G.

Show cause hearing. The enforcement official may order a person who has violated a provision of title 14 of the Code to appear before the enforcement official and show cause why a proposed
enforcement action or additional enforcement action should not be taken.

1.

The notice of the show cause hearing must specify the time and place for the hearing,
the proposed enforcement action(s) or additional enforcement action(s), the reasons
for such action(s), and a request that the person who has violated a provision of
title 14 of the Code show cause why the proposed or additional enforcement action(s) should
not be taken.

2.

An original notice of the show cause hearing, or a copy thereof, must be filed with
and retained by the department. A notice of the show cause hearing is prima facie
evidence of the facts that are alleged therein. The notice must be delivered personally,
by courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested to
the person responsible for the violation, the property owner (if the person ordered
to appear for the show cause hearing is a user and not the owner of the property and
the violation relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person responsible
is an entity, on an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent
of that entity. A show cause hearing shall not be a bar against, or prerequisite for,
taking any other enforcement action. That notice of show cause hearing will be deemed
to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date of delivery
if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery
attempt if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused
or otherwise unsuccessful.

3.

After the director's designee has reviewed the evidence, the enforcement official
may issue one or more orders and notices of violation as are necessary and appropriate
to correct and address the violation and bring the person who has violated a provision
of title 14 of the Code into compliance with title 14 of the Code.

H.

Administrative orders and consent orders.

1.

When an enforcement official finds that a person has violated, or continues to violate,
any provision of title 14 of the Code or an order or decision issued under this chapter, the enforcement official
may issue an administrative order to that person that directs that person to come
into compliance within a specific time and contains other requirements to address
the noncompliance and bring that person into compliance with title 14 of the Code. Issuance of an administrative order shall not be a bar against, or a
prerequisite for, taking any other action against that person.

2.

After a notice of violation has been issued, the city may enter into a consent order,
assurances of voluntary compliance, or other similar documents establishing an agreement
with any person who has violated, or is responsible for noncompliance with, a provision
of title 14 of the Code. Such documents shall include specific actions to be taken by the person
to correct the noncompliance within a time period specified by the document. A consent
order may address administrative fines, corrective action to be taken, and/or other
conditions and requirements as agreed to by the city and that person.

I.

Continuous violations. With respect to violations that are continuous with respect to time, each day that
the violation continues is a separate violation. With respect to violations that are
not continuous with respect to time, each prohibited act and/or each failure to perform
a required act is a separate violation.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 29, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.060 - Fine pass through.
text:
Whenever a resident, person, responsible party, or customer violates any of the provisions
of title 14 of the Code, such violation causes the city to violate state or federal law or any
condition of a permit issued to the city, and the city is fined for such violation,
then such resident, person, responsible party, or customer shall be fully liable to
city for the total amount of the fine assessed against the city.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.070 - Civil litigation.
text:
The city attorney may file an action in a court of competent jurisdiction to seek
correction of a violation(s) of a provision of title 14 of the Code, payment of administrative fines, restitution for corrective action(s)
taken by the city, pass through of a fine(s) and any other appropriate relief.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.080 - Referral for state and/or federal enforcement.
text:
The city may refer a violation of a provision of title 14 of the Code to the U.S. Attorney General's Office, State Attorney General, EPA Criminal
Investigation Division or other appropriate agency for enforcement, and this referral
shall not preclude the city from taking parallel enforcement or other action.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.090 - No waiver.
text:
Failure of the city to discover violations and/or to take action to enforce any requirement,
including but not limited to the assessment and collection of applicable charges,
fees, administrative fines, and penalties, shall not constitute a forfeiture or waiver
of the city's right to take appropriate action at any time thereafter. This entitlement
shall be retained by the city as a condition of service.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.100 - Remedies cumulative.
text:
The remedies provided for in this chapter 14.21 are not exclusive of any other remedies that the city may have under the Code, state
law, or federal law, and the administrative fines and penalties in this chapter 14.21 may be imposed in addition to any other fine, penalty, fee, charge, notice of violation,
or any other remedy provided for in this Code, the laws of the state of Nevada, or
the laws of the United States of America. The city is entitled to collect the amount
of any administrative fines that are due and owed to the city and its actual costs
for any work performed by or on its behalf to correct or abate a violation of title 14 by means of any remedy available under applicable law, including without limitation
referring the matter to a collection agency. The person that owes such an amount shall
be liable to the city for an additional collection fee where the city refers the administrative
fine(s) and/or the city's actual costs to a collection agency, as defined in NRS Chapter
649. The amount of such fee shall be 25 percent of the outstanding indebtedness or
$250.00, whichever is less. The amount of any such collection fee shall accrue and
become due and payable at the time the indebtedness is referred for collection to
the collection agency, and that amount may be added by the collection agency to the
amount sought to be collected.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.110 - Administrative hearings.
text:
A.

This section 14.21.110 establishes the procedures governing administrative hearings requested in accordance
with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b. Any hearing conducted pursuant to this section 14.21.110 shall be presided over by the director's designee and such person is referred to
as the "DUS hearing officer."

B.

The DUS hearing officer shall issue a notice of hearing that specifies the date, time,
and place for the administrative hearing. An original notice of the hearing, or a
copy thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. The department must
deliver the notice personally by courier service, or by registered or certified mail,
return receipt requested to the person cited, the property owner (if the person cited
is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services
at the property) and, if the person cited is an entity, on an officer, key employee,
manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity. That notice of hearing will
be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the date
of delivery if delivered personally by courier service, or by mail or the date of
the last delivery attempt if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail
and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful. The DUS hearing officer may continue
the hearing to a different date and/or time at the written request of a party if the
DUS hearing officer determines good cause for the continuance exists and the requestor
makes such a request before the date and time then scheduled for the hearing.

C.

The person cited, and/or a property owner as allowed under subsection 14.21.040.F.7,
that timely requested a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b is referred
to as the "defendant." The city and each defendant are each referred to as a "party."

D.

A party may not serve any interrogatories or other written discovery, take any depositions
or conduct other discovery. Affidavits or declarations made under penalty of perjury
may be received in evidence at the hearing. The party wishing to use such affidavit
or declaration shall, not less than 11 days prior to the date set for the hearing,
deliver to the opposing party, either personally or by mail, a copy of the affidavit
or declaration which that party proposes to introduce in evidence.

E.

A properly filed notice of violation shall constitute a claim of liability and a claim
for relief and no other such claim shall be required. Prima facie evidence of the
violation alleged shall be established by the city providing the DUS hearing officer
with either a copy of the notice of violation or the data stored in a computer or
other device as described in subsection 14.21.040.F.5. No formal appearance by the
city attorney's office is required at the hearing.

F.

The DUS hearing officer shall call the hearing to order and otherwise conduct the
hearing proceedings. At the request of the hearing officer, city or defendant, a city
police officer or marshal shall be present at the hearing to provide security and
help maintain order.

G.

At the hearing, each party shall have the opportunity to present witnesses, cross-examine
witnesses and present other evidence in support of the party's case. Every witness
shall declare, by oath or affirmation, that he or she will testify truthfully. The
hearings and dispositions of all such hearings shall be informal, with the DUS hearing
officer receiving photographs, testimony and other evidence for the sole purpose of
dispensing a fair and speedy resolution between the parties. The DUS hearing officer
may exclude irrelevant, immaterial or unduly repetitious evidence. The DUS hearing
officer is not bound by the technical rules of evidence, and no informality in any
proceeding or in the manner of taking testimony or receiving evidence will invalidate
any Hearing Officer Decision.

H.

The DUS hearing officer may question a witness at any time during the hearing. If
a witness is questioned by the DUS hearing officer, the party who called the witness
may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area addressed by
the DUS hearing officer. When the party who called the witness has asked those questions,
the other party may request permission to ask further questions, limited to the area
addressed by the DUS hearing officer. The DUS hearing officer may use the experience,
technical competence and specialized knowledge of the city's departments, divisions
and personnel to evaluate the evidence.

I.

The city has the burden of proof in any such hearing to establish the existence of
a violation of title 14 of the Code. The standard of proof to be used by the DUS hearing officer in deciding
the issues at such a hearing is by a preponderance of the evidence. The burden of
proving any defense shall be upon the party raising that defense.

J.

At the hearing, the DUS hearing officer shall only consider evidence that is relevant
to the following issues:

1.

Whether the conditions listed in the issued notice violate title 14 of the Code;

2.

Whether the city afforded the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited
is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services
at the property) due process by adhering to the notification procedures specified
in subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b and subsection 14.21.110.B;

3.

Whether administrative fine(s) in the issued notice is(are) appropriate;

4.

Whether the action(s) required to correct or abate the violation(s), deadline(s) by
when the violation(s) must be corrected or abated, and the consequences of failing
to comply are reasonable; and

5.

If a defendant asserts that the violation(s) have been corrected or abated, whether
the violation(s) have been adequately corrected or abated.

K.

The hearing may be reported stenographically and/or recorded by audio record, as determined
appropriate by the DUS hearing officer. If any party desires the hearing reported
stenographically and transcribed by a certified court reporter, that party must make
the necessary arrangements and bear the costs thereof and any other party is entitled
to purchase a copy of that transcription.

L.

After the DUS hearing officer has reviewed the information presented at the hearing
and within 45 days of the hearing (unless the DUS hearing officer extends that 45-day
period for good cause), the DUS hearing officer shall issue a written decision, deciding
for the defendant(s) and/or the city, entitled "Hearing Officer Decision":

1.

Deciding for the defendant if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation did not
occur or that the defendant should not be held liable; or

2.

Deciding for the city if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation occurred and
that either the person cited or the property owner (if the person cited is a user
and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at
the property) should be held liable and, as part of that Hearing Officer Decision:

a.

Affirm or modify the action(s) required to correct or otherwise abate the violation(s);

b.

Modify the deadline by when the violation(s) must be corrected or abated;

c.

Affirm, increase or reduce the administrative fine(s);

d.

Establish specific deadlines by when the administrative fine(s) must be paid; and/or

e.

If the defendant fails to comply with the Hearing Officer Decision, confirm that the
city may perform the abatement or take other action(s) to correct or address the violation(s)
and require the person cited and any property owner (if the person cited is a user
and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services at
the property) to pay the city's actual costs of that work within 30 days of receiving
an invoice from the city; or

3.

Deciding for the city if the DUS hearing officer finds that a violation occurred,
that the defendant did not attend the hearing, that the defendant was given sufficient
legal notice of the hearing and that the defendant should be held liable and, as part
of that Hearing Officer Decision:

a.

Affirm or modify the action(s) required to correct or otherwise abate the violation(s);

b.

Confirm that the city may perform the abatement or take other action(s) to correct
or address the violation(s) and require the person cited and any property owner (if
the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates
to utility services at the property) to pay the city's actual costs of that work within
30 days of receiving an invoice from the city;

c.

Affirm, increase or reduce the administrative fine(s); and/or

d.

Provide that those administrative fine amounts are deemed to be immediately due and
owed to the city.

M.

The DUS hearing officer shall include a certification in the Hearing Officer Decision
substantially conforming to the following form: "I certify that the foregoing is a
correct reflection of the decision entered in the proceeding properly brought for
my consideration pursuant to section 14.21.110 of the Henderson Municipal Code." The original Hearing Officer Decision, or a copy
thereof, must be filed with and retained by the department. The department must deliver
a copy of the Hearing Officer Decision personally, by courier service, or by registered
or certified mail, return receipt requested to the person cited, the property owner
(if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation
relates to utility services at the property) and, if the person cited is an entity,
on an officer, key employee, manager in charge, or registered agent of that entity.
That Hearing Officer Decision will be deemed to have been received by the person to
whom it was addressed on the date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier
service, or by mail or the date of the last delivery attempt if delivered, personally,
by courier service, or by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise unsuccessful.

N.

If the administrative fine amounts are not paid by the deadline(s) established in
a Hearing Officer Decision, the unpaid amounts are deemed to be immediately due and
owed to the city by the person cited and the property owner (if the person cited is
a user and not the owner of the property and the violation relates to utility services
at the property).

O.

The city attorney may petition the Henderson municipal court or such other court of
competent jurisdiction for the entry of a civil judgment against each defendant in
an amount equal to that stated in the Hearing Officer Decision if the city attorney
determines this action to be necessary to enforce the Hearing Officer Decision. Service
of such petition on each defendant must be made by certified mail, return receipt
requested, restricted delivery, addressed to the defendant at the defendant's last
known address, or in any other manner that is authorized by law. An affidavit or declaration
of mailing, a signed, returned receipt, or other evidence of service of the civil
judgment shall be filed upon such service of the petition.

P.

If the person that timely requested a hearing in accordance with subsection 14.21.040.F.6.b
does not attend the hearing, that person is deemed to admit responsibility for the
commission of the violation(s), be responsible for correction or abatement of the
violation(s), be responsible for any administrative fine(s), be responsible for the
city's actual costs to correct or abate the violation(s), and unpaid amounts are deemed
to be immediately due and owed to the city by the person cited and the property owner
(if the person cited is a user and not the owner of the property and the violation
relates to utility services at the property).

Q.

The Hearing Officer Decision shall be the final administrative action unless a timely
request for reconsideration of that decision is filed under subsection 14.21.120.A.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 31, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.120 - Request for reconsideration; appeals.
text:
A.

Any resident of the city, a responsible party operating, maintaining, repairing, relocating,
removing, or disconnecting the public water system and/or publicly owned treatment
works, a person that violates a provision of title 14 of the Code, or a customer directly aggrieved by an enforcement action taken by the
city under section 14.21.040 may file a request for reconsideration. Any defendant aggrieved by a Hearing Officer
Decision under section 14.21.110, may also file a request for reconsideration. All requests for reconsideration (1)
shall be made by that aggrieved person submitting a written request for reconsideration
to the director that identifies the action taken or decision made by the department,
enforcement official, or city that the aggrieved person would like reconsidered, sets
forth in detail the facts supporting the request for reconsideration, and identifies
any relief requested; (2) shall be delivered personally, by courier service, or by
registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the director; and (3) must
be received by the director, if delivered personally, by courier service, or must
be postmarked, if delivered by registered or certified mail, on or before the 11th
day after the city takes the action or makes the decision that the aggrieved person
would like reconsidered.

B.

After the director receives a request for reconsideration that complies with the requirements
in subsection 14.21.120.A, the director may modify or affirm the action taken or decision
made and, as part of that decision-making process, may review any information the
director determines is relevant and request that the department or the aggrieved person
provide additional information. If a request for reconsideration is not timely or
fails to provide the information required in subsection 14.21.120.A(1), then the director
shall dismiss the request for reconsideration on the grounds that it was untimely
and/or insufficient. The director's decision must be in writing, be made within 30
days of the director's receipt of that request for reconsideration and delivered to
the aggrieved person that made the request personally, by courier service, or by registered
or certified mail, return receipt requested. In the director's discretion, the director
may extend the time for the director to issue that decision. The director's decision
will be deemed to have been received by the person to whom it was addressed on the
date of delivery if delivered personally, by courier service, or by mail or the date
of the last delivery attempt if delivered by mail and delivery was refused or otherwise
unsuccessful. The director's decision to modify or affirm the action taken or decision
made, or to dismiss the request for reconsideration, shall be deemed to be the city's
final administrative action and decision unless timely and sufficiently appealed to
the city manager in accordance with subsection 14.21.120.C. Unless otherwise ordered
by a court of competent jurisdiction, the director's decision shall remain in effect
during the pendency of any judicial appeal or other judicial review of that decision
sought pursuant to and in accordance with applicable law.

C.

If a decision made by the director in accordance with subsection 14.21.120.B is unsatisfactory
to the aggrieved person requesting reconsideration, the aggrieved person may, within
11 days after receiving the director's decision, appeal that decision to the city
manager. All appeals (1) shall be made by that aggrieved person submitting a written
request to the city manager that identifies the director's decision that the aggrieved
person wishes to reverse or modify, sets forth in detail the facts supporting the
appeal, and identifies any relief requested; (2) shall be delivered personally, by
courier service, or by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to
the city manager and to the director; and (3) must be received by the city manager
and the director, if delivered personally or by courier service, or must be postmarked,
if delivered by registered or certified mail, on or before the 11th day after the
aggrieved person receives the director's decision. An appeal that complies with the
foregoing requirements shall be decided by the city manager within 30 days from the
date it is received by the city manager unless the city manager, in the city manager's
discretion, extends the time for the city manager to issue that decision. As part
of that decision-making process, the city manager may review any information city
manager determines is relevant and request that the department or the aggrieved person
provide additional information. If an appeal is not timely or does not provide the
information required in item (1) in this subsection, the city manager shall dismiss
the appeal. The city manager's decision to modify or affirm the action taken or decision
made, or to dismiss the appeal, shall be deemed to be the city's final administrative
action and decision. The director's decision shall remain in effect during the pendency
of any appeal to the city manager. Unless otherwise ordered by a court of competent
jurisdiction, the city manager's decision shall remain in effect during the pendency
of any judicial appeal or other judicial review of that decision sought pursuant to
and in accordance with applicable law.

(Ord. No. 3905, § 32, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.130 - Public nuisance.
text:
Any condition caused or permitted to exist in violation of any of the provisions of
chapter 14.02, chapter 14.03, chapter 14.04, chapter 14.05, chapter 14.06, chapter 14.08, or chapter 14.14 of the Code is a threat to public health, safety, and welfare and is declared and
deemed a nuisance by the city council. The city may summarily, at the violator's expense,
abate the condition after following the procedures in subsection 14.21.040.F or correct
the condition pursuant to subsection 14.21.040.C or another provision in title 14 of the Code, and the city attorney may file an action in a court of competent jurisdiction
to abate, enjoin, or otherwise compel the cessation of such public nuisance.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: 14.21.140 - Inapplicability to chapter 14.09—Pretreatment regulations.
text:
Sections 14.21.010 through 14.21.130, inclusive, do not apply to a violation of a provision of chapter 14.09 of the Code. Compliance and enforcement of a violation of chapter 14.09 are addressed in that chapter 14.09.

(Ord. No. 3497, § 1, 7-10-2018)

heading: Chapter 15.01 - BUILDING AND FIRE SAFETY ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF HENDERSON, NEVADA
15.01.005 - Title.
text:
Chapter 15.01 shall be known as the "Building and Fire Safety Administrative Code of Henderson,
Nevada." It may be cited as such or by the short title "administrative code." It is
referenced herein as "this chapter."

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.010 - Purpose.[1]
text:
The purpose of this chapter is to provide the administrative rules and regulations
for the administration and enforcement of the technical codes adopted by the City
of Henderson. These technical codes are set out generally in chapters 15.08, 15.09, 15.10, 15.11, 15.16, 15.20, 15.24, 15.30, 15.40, 15.44, 15.45 and 15.56 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

The purpose of this chapter and the technical codes is to provide appropriate design
and construction regulations to safeguard the public health, safety and general welfare
by regulating and controlling the permitting, design, construction, quality of materials,
use and occupancy, location and maintenance of buildings, service equipment and structures
in the jurisdiction of the City of Henderson specifically regulated herein.

(Ord. No. 3906, § 1, 9-13-2022; Ord. No. 3503, § 1, 8-7-2018; Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

Effective February 4, 2019.

heading: 15.01.015 - Scope.
text:
The provisions of this chapter shall serve as the administrative, organizational and
enforcement rules and regulations for the technical codes, that regulate the site
preparation, construction, alteration, moving, enlargement, replacement, demolition,
repair, maintenance, use and occupancy of buildings and structures and appurtenances
connected or attached to such buildings and structures, signs, amusement and transportation
systems and building service equipment.

For the purpose of this chapter, the term "equipment" or "systems" shall apply to
any equipment or system regulated by the technical codes. Where, in any specific case,
different sections of the technical codes specify different materials, methods of
construction or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern. Whenever the
technical codes make a reference to an appendix chapter, the appendix chapter shall
not apply unless specifically adopted by the City of Henderson. Where differences
occur between provisions of this chapter and the technical codes, the most restrictive
shall govern.

Exception. This chapter does not apply to the following:

A.

Facilities or installations within the City of Henderson which are owned and operated
by an entity which invokes preemptive power such as the State of Nevada or the federal
government.

B.

Buildings, structures or service equipment and installations directly used in utility
generation or distribution which are installed on properly recorded easements belonging
to water, gas, power, telephone, or other utility companies that are preemptively
regulated and governed by the Nevada Public Service Commission, a State of Nevada
Charter, or other public franchise. This exception does not apply to non-exempted
buildings and structures containing occupiable space such as offices, meeting rooms,
service counters, public restrooms, site preparation, block walls and fences.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.020 - Substantial compliance standard.
text:
In the enforcement of specific provisions of this chapter and the technical codes,
the building official and the fire chief are authorized to grant minor variations
from the strict application of specific code provisions where, in the opinion of the
building official and the fire chief, the work is in substantial compliance with the
intent of the adopted codes and standards, and these minor variations are warranted.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.025 - Guarantee or warranty.
text:
The building official reviews and approves construction drawings and conducts periodic
inspections of work in progress to verify that the approved plans and work inspected
at specific points in time are in substantial compliance with the technical codes.
The building official does not conduct continuous inspections of work in progress.
Accordingly, reviews, approvals and inspections performed by the building official
pursuant to this chapter do not create any guarantee or warranty that buildings, structures
or service equipment have been constructed in accordance with all of the applicable
provisions of the technical codes.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.030 - Emergency provisions.
text:
In the event of a national, state or local emergency declaration, the building official
may waive or augment the provisions of this chapter and the technical codes as needed
during the periods of emergency to protect public safety.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.035 - Existing buildings, structures, and building service equipment.[2]
text:
Existing buildings, structures and building service equipment shall comply with the
provisions of this section.

A.

Additions, alterations or repairs. Buildings, structures and building service equipment to which additions, alterations
and repairs are made shall comply with all the requirements of the technical codes
for new facilities, except as specifically provided in this chapter.

Additions, alterations and repairs may be made to any building, structure and building
service equipment without requiring the existing building, structure or building service
equipment to comply with all the requirements of the technical codes provided the
addition, alteration or repair conforms to that required for a new building, structure
or building service equipment.

Additions, alterations or repairs shall not be made to an existing building, structure
or building service equipment that will cause the existing building or building structure
service equipment to be in violation of any of the provisions of the technical codes,
nor shall such additions, alterations or repairs cause the existing building, structure
or building service equipment to become unsafe. An unsafe condition shall be deemed
to have been created if an addition, alteration or repair:

1.

Causes the existing building to become structurally unsafe;

2.

Does not provide adequate means of egress in compliance with the provisions of the
building code;

3.

Creates a fire hazard as determined by the Henderson fire marshal;

4.

Reduces required fire resistance;

5.

Causes building service equipment to become overloaded or exceed its rated capacity;

6.

Creates a health hazard as determined by the Health District of Southern Nevada or
otherwise creates conditions dangerous to human life and safety.

Any addition, alteration or repair of a building which involves a change in use or
occupancy shall not exceed the height, number of stories or area permitted by the
building code for new buildings. Any building plus new additions shall not exceed
the height, number of stories or area permitted by the building code for new buildings.
All fire systems required by chapter 9 of the Building and Fire Safety Administrative
Code because of the area of the addition or the area of the addition plus the existing
building area shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated
per the fire code.

New additions and alterations shall comply with the code in effect at the time of
construction of the addition or alteration. Additions and alterations may not be made
to an existing building or structure where such building or structure is not in full
compliance with the provisions of the applicable building code in effect at the time
of construction of the building unless the proposed addition or alteration includes
work to bring the existing building into compliance with the applicable code.

Alterations and repairs to an existing building or structure which are nonstructural
and do not adversely affect a structural member or system, or a part of the building
having required fire resistance, may be made with the same materials as the building
or structure, subject to the approval of the building official. The installation or
replacement of glass shall be as required for new installations.

Additions or alterations shall not be made to an existing building or structure which
is in violation of other provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code unless such additions
or alterations include work to bring the building into compliance with the applicable
provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code. This limitation does not apply to lawful
non-conforming buildings or uses as determined by the Henderson community development
department.

B.

Existing building service equipment installations. Building service equipment lawfully in existence at the time of adoption of the technical
codes may have its use, maintenance or repair continued if such building service equipment
is in accordance with its original design and does not pose a hazard to life, health
or property. Minor additions, alterations and repairs to existing building service
equipment may be made in accordance with the technical codes in effect at the time
of original installation, subject to approval of the building official, and provided
such additions, alterations and repairs will not cause the existing building service
equipment to become unsafe, unsanitary or overloaded.

C.

Existing occupancy. Buildings in existence at the time of the adoption of the building code may have
their use or occupancy continued if such use or occupancy was legal at the time of
the adoption of the building code and provided such continued use is not dangerous
to life, health or safety. Any change in the use or occupancy of an existing building
shall require that the building be made to conform to all current technical code requirements
based upon the new use or occupancy, including upgrade of the building's structural
system. In addition, any fire safety system required by the codes because of the occupancy
change shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated per the
fire code.

D.

Maintenance. All existing and new buildings, structures, signs, and building service equipment
and all parts thereof shall be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance
with the provisions of the adopted technical codes and City of Henderson Property
Maintenance Code as adopted in chapter 15.12 of the Henderson Municipal Code. All devices and safeguards which are required by
the technical codes shall be maintained in conformance with the technical code in
effect at the time of installation. The owner or his designated agent shall be responsible
for the maintenance of buildings, structures, building service equipment and assuring
that all required fire and life safety systems are maintained in an operable condition
at all times. To determine compliance with the requirement of this section, the building
official may cause any building, structure or building service equipment to be re-inspected.

(Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

or building service equipment.

Additions, alterations or repairs shall not be made to an existing building, structure
or building service equipment that will cause the existing building or building structure
service equipment to be in violation of any of the provisions of the technical codes,
nor shall such additions, alterations or repairs cause the existing building, structure
or building service equipment to become unsafe. An unsafe condition shall be deemed
to have been created if an addition, alteration or repair:

1.

Causes the existing building to become structurally unsafe;

2.

Does not provide adequate means of egress in compliance with the provisions of the
building code;

3.

Creates a fire hazard as determined by the Henderson fire code official;

4.

Reduces required fire resistance;

5.

Causes building service equipment to become overloaded or exceed its rated capacity;

6.

Creates a health hazard as determined by the Health District of Southern Nevada or
otherwise creates conditions dangerous to human life and safety.

Any addition, alteration or repair of a building which involves a change in use or
occupancy shall not exceed the height, number of stories or area permitted by the
building code for new buildings. Any building plus new additions shall not exceed
the height, number of stories or area permitted by the building code for new buildings.
All fire systems required by chapter 9 of the Building and Fire Safety Administrative
Code because of the area of the addition or the area of the addition plus the existing
building area shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated
per the fire code.

New additions and alterations shall comply with the code in effect at the time of
construction of the addition or alteration. Additions and alterations may not be made
to an existing building or structure where such building or structure is not in full
compliance with the provisions of the applicable building code in effect at the time
of construction of the building unless the proposed addition or alteration includes
work to bring the existing building into compliance with the applicable code.

Alterations and repairs to an existing building or structure which are nonstructural
and do not adversely affect a structural member or system, or a part of the building
having required fire resistance, may be made with the same materials as the building
or structure, subject to the approval of the building official. The installation or
replacement of glass shall be as required for new installations.

Additions or alterations shall not be made to an existing building or structure which
is in violation of other provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code unless such additions
or alterations include work to bring the building into compliance with the applicable
provisions of the Henderson Municipal Code. This limitation does not apply to lawful
non-conforming buildings or uses as determined by the Henderson community development
department.

B.

Existing building service equipment installations. Building service equipment lawfully in existence at the time of adoption of the technical
codes may have its use, maintenance or repair continued if such building service equipment
is in accordance with its original design and does not pose a hazard to life, health
or property. Minor additions, alterations and repairs to existing building service
equipment may be made in accordance with the technical codes in effect at the time
of original installation, subject to approval of the building official, and provided
such additions, alterations and repairs will not cause the existing building service
equipment to become unsafe, unsanitary or overloaded.

C.

Existing occupancy. Buildings in existence at the time of the adoption of the building code may have
their use or occupancy continued if such use or occupancy was legal at the time of
the adoption of the building code and provided such continued use is not dangerous
to life, health or safety. Any change in the use or occupancy of an existing building
shall require that the building be made to conform to all current technical code requirements
based upon the new use or occupancy, including upgrade of the building's structural
system. In addition, any fire safety system required by the codes because of the occupancy
change shall be extended throughout the building or structure or separated per the
fire code.

D.

Maintenance. All existing and new buildings, structures, signs, and building service equipment
and all parts thereof shall be maintained in a safe working condition and in accordance
with the provisions of the adopted technical codes and City of Henderson Property
Maintenance Code as adopted in chapter 15.12 of the Henderson Municipal Code. All devices and safeguards which are required by
the technical codes shall be maintained in conformance with the technical code in
effect at the time of installation. The owner or his designated agent shall be responsible
for the maintenance of buildings, structures, building service equipment and assuring
that all required fire and life safety systems are maintained in an operable condition
at all times. To determine compliance with the requirement of this section, the building
official may cause any building, structure or building service equipment to be re-inspected.

(Ord. No. 3503, § 1, 8-7-2018; Ord. 2736, § 1 (part), 2008)

heading: 15.01.040 - Definitions.
text:
For the purposes of this chapter, certain terms, phrases, words and their derivatives
shall be defined as specified in this section or other adopted technical codes. Where
words and terms are not defined, they shall have their ordinary accepted meanings
within the context with which they are used. The latest edition of Webster's Third
New International Dictionary of the English Language, Unabridged, shall be considered
as providing ordinary accepted meanings. Words used in the singular include the plural,
and the plural the singular. Words used in the masculine gender include the feminine,
and the feminine the masculine.

Alter or alteration means any construction or renovation to an existing building, structure or building
service equipment other than repair or addition.

Amusement and transportation system (ATS) is any ride, device, building or structure that is used primarily for human entertainment
and enjoyment, either moving or stationary. The final determination whether a ride,
device or structure shall be classified under this definition shall be made by the
building official. For the purposes of this chapter, slot machines, electronic gaming
devices, pinball games, electronic arcade games, and non-motorized playground equipment
are not amusement and transportation systems.

Amusement system or transportation system permit means permits issued by the building official authorizing construction and installation
of an ATS. At the option of the building official, an amusement and transportation
system permit may include in its scope any subsidiary permits for supporting or enclosing
structures and buildings, associated and accessory structures, utility permits, and
other building service equipment.

Approved, as to materials, types of construction, equipment and systems refers to approval
by the building official as the result of investigation and tests, or by reason of
accepted principles or tests by recognized authorities, technical or scientific organizations.

Approved agency is a quality assurance agency that has been approved and listed by the building official
pursuant to this chapter.

Approved construction documents are construction documents that have been reviewed and approved for permit by the
building official pursuant to this chapter.

Approved fabricator means a company that constructs or assembles standardized building components into
assemblies in an approved manner based on submittal of specified documentation and
successful periodic evaluation for conformance to standard operating procedures and
tests such that the company is listed on the published approved fabricators list.

Approved products are products that are included on product listings from testing and listing agencies
approved by the building official.

Approved special inspector is a special inspector who has been approved and listed by the building official
pursuant to this chapter.

Area acceptance report is a report to the building official that states all required activities for special
inspection item(s) are complete and acceptable for a portion of the work authorized
by a permit.

ATS means "amusement and transportation system" as defined in this chapter.

Building means any structure used or intended for supporting or sheltering any use or occupancy.

Building code means that edition of the International Building Code and amendments thereto adopted
by the City of Henderson and referenced in chapter 15.08 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Building, existing. "Existing building" means a building erected prior to the adoption of the currently
adopted technical codes or one for which a legal, unexpired building permit has been
issued by the building official.

Building official means the City of Henderson building official and the building official's designee(s).

Building service equipment means the plumbing, mechanical, electrical and elevator equipment including piping,
wiring, fixtures and other accessories that provide potable water, sanitation, lighting,
heating, ventilation, cooling, refrigeration, fire-fighting and transportation facilities
essential for the habitable occupancy of a building or structure for the designated
use and occupancy.

Building service equipment, existing. "Existing building service equipment" means building service equipment lawfully installed
prior to the adoption of the currently adopted technical codes or for which a legal,
unexpired permit has been issued by the building official.

Certificate of operation means a document issued by the building official on an annual basis certifying that
an amusement and transportation system (ATS) has been inspected and found to be in
compliance with the manufacturer's requirements for operation and maintenance, the
approved operations and maintenance manual(s), and approved plans and any other requirements
of this chapter. A current certificate of operation is required in order to lawfully
operate an ATS.

Commercial coach means a structure without motive power which is designed and equipped for human occupancy
for industrial, professional or commercial purposes. A commercial coach is intended
to be shipped to a location and remain at that site for a temporary period of time.
A commercial coach does not include a recreational park trailer.

Construction documents are plans, specifications, supporting calculations and other data prepared to describe
the design, materials, physical characteristics, location, orientation, and scope
of a proposed project necessary to obtain a permit.

Construction offices are those trailers which are intended to serve as temporary, on-site office and meeting
space for the owner, architects, engineers and other project representatives during,
and related to, the actual construction of a project. Construction offices do not
include office space of the contractor's construction personnel.

Construction trailers are those trailers which are intended to serve as temporary, on-site office and meeting
space for contractors, subcontractors and other project representatives during, and
related to, the actual construction of a project. Construction trailers do not include
sales offices or satellite offices of the contractors, architect, engineer, etc.,
if the staff is working permanently therein.

Dangerous building code means that edition of the Uniform Code for the Abatement of Dangerous Buildings and
amendments thereto adopted by the City of Henderson and referenced in chapter 15.10 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Demolition means the wrecking, razing, rendering, movement or removal of a structure or mass
material by means of tools, equipment, or the placement and discharge of explosives.

Department means the City of Henderson building and fire safety department.

Design professional is an individual who is registered or licensed by the State of Nevada pursuant to
Nevada Revised Statutes chapters 623, 623A, or 625.

Device is a component or system that may contain electrical, mechanical and/or pyrotechnic
effects that require specific safety features to protect the general public.

Electrical code means that edition of the National Electrical Code and amendments thereto adopted
by the City of Henderson in chapter 15.16 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Fire code means that edition of the International Fire Code and amendments thereto adopted
by the City of Henderson in chapter 15.32 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Jurisdiction as used in this chapter is the area within the incorporated boundaries of Henderson,
Nevada.

Life-safety system means, without limitation, electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilating, air conditioning,
emergency lighting, fire alarm systems, fire sprinklers, smoke detectors, fire walls,
fire barriers and exits required by the technical codes for the protection of human
life and safety.

Listed equipment, materials or services included in a list published by an organization acceptable to the building official
and concerned with evaluation of products or services that maintains periodic inspection
of production of listed equipment or materials or periodic evaluation of services
and whose listing states either that the equipment, material or service meets identified
standards or has been tested and found suitable for a specified purpose by an approved
testing agency that is qualified and equipped for experimental testing and maintaining
an adequate, periodic inspection of current productions, and whose listing states
the equipment complies with recognized safety standards.

Listing and listing report is a published statement or document that details the products and services evaluated
by a nationally recognized body and any conditions or limitations placed on the use
of the product or service by that body. Listings and reports are subject to acceptance
by the building official.

Major modification of any amusement and transportation system (ATS) is any change in either the structural
or operational characteristics of the ATS that will alter its performance from that
specified in the manufacturer's design criteria, including ride control software.

Manufactured home means a structure which is built on a permanent chassis, designed to be used with
or without a permanent foundation as a dwelling when connected to utilities; a manufactured
home does not include a recreational park trailer, travel trailer, modular building,
commercial coach or mobile home.

Mechanical bull is an operator-controlled device, operated in such a manner that the intention is
to cause the ejection of the rider.

Mechanical code means that edition of the Uniform Mechanical Code and amendments thereto adopted
by the City of Henderson in chapter 15.24 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Mobile home means a vehicular structure which is built on a chassis or frame, is designed to
be used with or without a permanent foundation, is capable of being drawn by a motor
vehicle and is used as a dwelling when connected to utilities. Mobile home does not
include a recreational park trailer, travel trailer, modular building, commercial
coach or manufactured home.

Modular building means an office, apartment, school, motel or other building, whether it is a total
building or room, which is either wholly manufactured or is in substantial part manufactured
at an off-site location to be wholly or partially assembled on-site in accordance
with regulations adopted by the State of Nevada. A modular building is intended to
be shipped to a location and remain at that site for its intended life as an improvement
to the real estate. A modular building does not include a mobile home or recreational
park trailer.

Nationally recognized body is an organization that evaluates testing laboratories, inspection agencies as well
as fabrication and manufacturing facilities that produce products and services in
accordance with the technical codes. A listing or report is published that details
the products and services evaluated and any conditions or limitations placed on their
use. The listing or report is subject to acceptance by the building official.

Occupancy means the purpose of which a building or structure or part thereof is used or intended
to be used. The term "occupancy" as used in this chapter shall include the building
or structure or part thereof housing the intended use.

Occupant means the person who resides in and/or has primary use of a building or structure
or a portion of a building or structure.

Owner means any person, agent, firm or corporation having a legal or equitable interest
in the property.

Patron is a person who participates in an amusement and transportation system (ATS) whether
paying or non-paying, including employees.

Permit means an official document or certificate issued by the building official authorizing
performance of a specified activity.

Permit applicant means the person that has filed an application with the building official for a permit.

Permitee means the person to whom a permit is issued.

Permitted work means the work for which a permit is issued.

Person means an individual, heirs, executors, administrators or assigns, and also includes
a firm, partnership or corporation, its or their successors or assigns, or the agent
of any of the aforesaid.

Plumbing code means that edition of the Uniform Plumbing Code and amendments thereto adopted by
the City of Henderson in chapter 15.20 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Pool code means the Southern Nevada Pool Code adopted in chapter 15.44 of the Henderson Municipal
Code.

Prime agency means an approved agency designated by the owner or design professional acting on
behalf of the owner to provide special inspection services and required special inspection
documents to the building official.

Principal design professional is an architect registered pursuant to Nevada Revised Statutes chapter 623 or a professional
engineer licensed pursuant to Nevada Revised Statutes [chapter] 625 who is responsible
for the coordination of each aspect of the construction documents that are submitted
to the building official for approval.

Prohibited use notice means a written document issued by the building official indicating non-compliance
with the requirements of certification, installation, inspection, operation or any
provisions of the amusement and transportation system (ATS) code and further indicating
that the ATS may not be operated for other than repairs, inspection or testing.

Public facility model means a comprehensive model or map of the physical location of all or a substantial
portion of the facilities of a public utility, public water system or video service
provider. A public facility model does not include public utilities or public water
systems that are owned or operated by the city.

Public utility has the meaning ascribed to it in NRS 704.020.

Public water system has the meaning ascribed to it in NRS 445A.235.

Quality assurance agency (QAA) means an approved organization that is in the business of providing inspection, testing
and reporting services for the types of construction and construction work that are
regulated in the technical codes.

Quality assurance agency special inspection agreement means an agreement between an owner that has been issued a permit, or a design professional
acting on behalf of that owner, and an approved quality assurance agency listing the
types of construction and construction work required to be verified through a special
inspection process.

Quality system auditor means a person with the requisite knowledge, skill and experience to evaluate the
quality assurance and quality control operations of fabrication and manufacturing
facilities.

Recognized agency means a quality assurance agency (QAA) that maintains an accreditation through a
nationally recognized body.

Recognized fabricator/manufacturer means a facility that is listed or maintains an evaluation report through a nationally
recognized body. The evaluation report or listing is used by the building official
to determine the acceptability of the quality control and quality assurance operations
of the facility.

Recreational park trailer means a vehicle which is primarily designed to provide temporary living quarters
for recreational, camping or seasonal use.

Repair means the reconstruction or renewal of any part of an existing building, structure
or building service equipment for the purpose of maintenance or continued use, operation
or occupancy.

Residential code means that edition of the International Residential Code and amendments thereto adopted
by the City of Henderson and referenced in chapter 15.09 of the Henderson Municipal Code.

Ride means an amusement ride or transportation system (ATS) as defined in this chapter.

Sales trailer are those trailers which are intended to serve as temporary, office and sales space
for customer sales during the construction of a project.

Shall, as used in this chapter, is mandatory.

Special inspection means a process of inspection, testing and reporting by approved special inspectors
and quality assurance agencies to assure the building official that the construction
of structural elements, materials, and life safety systems is being performed in accordance
with the approved construction documents and applicable technical code.

Special inspection category means that collection of specialized inspection activities specified in chapter 17
